correspondence.imported-tractor-connecti.formal:
Let $[g]$ be the conformal class of the derived metric of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), on its invertible region. (i) $[g]$ carries a canonical connection on the rank-six tractor bundle, whose fibre is the vector space of $\Cl(2,4)$ and which on flat spacetime is the rotation-gauge field $D^{T}_{a} = a \cdot \nabla + \Omega_{T}(a)\times$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}; its expression in a scale $g$ is
\[
\nabla_a(\sigma, \mu_b, \rho) = \bigl(\nabla_a\sigma - \mu_a,\;\; \nabla_a\mu_b + g_{ab}\rho - \Sch_{ab}\sigma,\;\; \nabla_a\rho + \Sch_a{}^b\mu_b\bigr),
\]
with $\Sch$ the Schouten tensor. (ii) The conformal class likewise carries the classical bundle of conformal spinors (the \emph{local twistor} bundle), fibrewise the conformal spinor space $\CS = \Cl^+(2,4)P$, a $4$-dimensional module over the complex unit $I_6$, with the scale splitting $Z = (\omega^B, \pi_{B'})$ into the halves $\Som \oplus \Spi$, and its transport, the conformal spinor connection (local twistor transport),
\[
\nabla^{\mathrm{LT}}_a(\omega^B, \pi_{B'}) \;=\; \bigl(\nabla_a \omega^B + \varepsilon_A{}^B\,\pi_{A'}I_6,\;\; \nabla_a\pi_{B'} + \Sch_{AA'BB'}\,\omega^B I_6\bigr),
\]
in the index conventions of \cite[Vol.~2, Ch.~6]{PenroseRindler86}, where the complex unit of $\CS$, the source's imaginary unit, is right multiplication by the conformal pseudoscalar $I_6$; under conformal rescaling $\omega$ is invariant and $\pi$ shifts, so the $\pi$-plane $\{\omega = 0\}$ (the kernel in $\CS$ of the point's null vector) is the canonical subbundle. \emph{Provenance:} (i) \cite{BEG1994, CurryGover2018}, in the conventions of \cite[Fact 4.1, eq.~(3)]{ButlerT6}; (ii) \cite{PenroseMacCallum73, Dighton74}; the statement that (ii) is the spin representation of (i), that is, that the conformal spinor connection is the tractor connection acting on $\CS$, is standard in the tractor literature \cite{BEG1994, CurryGover2018}, and is \emph{proved} rather than imported below, since the proof is short in the present framework.
correspondence.imported-tractor-connecti.technical:
The conformal class of a gravitational field on flat spacetime carries two canonical connections. On the rank-six tractor bundle, whose fibre is the vector space of $\Cl(2,4)$ and on which the connection is the flat-space gauge field $\Omega_{T}$ built from $\Omega$, the frame and the Schouten map, the expression in a scale $g$ is $
abla_a(\sigma, \mu_b, ho) = (
abla_a\sigma - \mu_a,\ 
abla_a\mu_b + g_{ab}ho - \Sch_{ab}\sigma,\ 
abla_aho + \Sch_a{}^b\mu_b)$, with $\Sch$ the Schouten tensor. On the bundle of conformal spinors, fibrewise the $4$-dimensional spinor space $\CS$ of the even conformal algebra over the complex unit $I_6$ and split in a scale as $Z = (\omega^B, \pi_{B'})$, the conformal spinor connection is $
abla^{\mathrm{LT}}_a(\omega^B, \pi_{B'}) = (
abla_a\omega^B + \varepsilon_A{}^B\pi_{A'}I_6,\ 
abla_a\pi_{B'} + \Sch_{AA'BB'}\omega^B I_6)$ in Penrose-Rindler index conventions, with the unit $I_6$ acting on the right.

Under conformal rescaling $\omega$ is invariant and $\pi$ shifts, so the $\pi$-plane $\{\omega = 0\}$, the kernel of the point's null vector, is the canonical subbundle. Both connections are taken from the literature, the first in the series' own conventions; that the second is the first acting on conformal spinors (its spin representation) is proved in the series rather than imported.
correspondence.imported-tractor-connecti.lay: Gravity on flat spacetime determines a conformal geometry, which carries two standard ways of carrying data from point to point. One acts on the six-component vectors of the series' conformal model, called tractors, and on flat spacetime it is itself a gauge field built from gravity; the other acts on four-component spinors of the conformal geometry. This entry records both formulas, taken from the literature, in the conventions the series uses.

__notes__.note.correspondence.setting-setting-impo: Two dimension counts we use, $\dim_\R \Cl(2,4) = 2^6 = 64$ and $\dim_\C \Cl(2,4)_\C = 64$ for the complexification $\Cl(2,4)_\C = \Cl(2,4)\otimes_\R\C \cong \Cl_6(\C)$, the second of which is checked in the verification script (the first follows from it, since complexification doubles the real dimension); Remark \claimref{note.correspondence.dimensions-real-form} records where they place the algebra in the standard tables. Two letters are reused with the tractor literature's meanings wherever a tractor is written in its scale splitting (Facts \claimref{correspondence.imported-vacuum-equations-scale-tractor} and \claimref{correspondence.imported-tractor-connection-local-twistor-transport}, Corollary \claimref{correspondence.one-statement-three-languages}, Proposition \claimref{correspondence.local-twistor-transport-ascended-spinor-connection}): inside the tractor triple $(\sigma, \mu, \rho)$, $\sigma$ and $\rho$ are the top and bottom slots, and $\rho_g$ is the bottom slot of the scale tractor; outside a triple, $\rho$ is the spinor action and $\sigma$ the pairing of Proposition \claimref{correspondence.reality-conjugation-twistor-form-factor}, and $\sigma_a$ with a direction index is the soldering summand of Proposition \claimref{correspondence.local-twistor-transport-ascended-spinor-connection}. Throughout, ``twistor space'' means the module $\T$ constructed in Theorem \claimref{correspondence.spinor-identification}; no prior twistor formalism is assumed, and the contact with Penrose's conventions is made in the section “Incidence encodes the completion”. We fix once an orthonormal basis $a_1, a_2$ (norm $+1$), $b_1, \dots, b_4$ (norm $-1$) of $V$, with $\nO, \nInf$ in the span of $a_1, b_1$. The verification script works with $C(v) := c(v)/\sqrt2$, for which $\{C(u), C(v)\} = \ip{u}{v}$; every identity below is stated for $c$ and checked for $C$, the two differing only by powers of $\sqrt2$.
__notes__.note.correspondence.one-imported-convent: Proposition \claimref{correspondence.local-twistor-transport-ascended-spinor-connection}(3) proves the block form, the uniqueness of the summands up to two constants whose product is invariant, and the value of that invariant on the Clifford side. The remaining step, that Penrose's composite $-\varepsilon_A{}^B\mathrm{P}_{CC'DA'}\omega^D$ equals $\tfrac12 c(e_a)c(\mathrm{P}(e_c))$ under Levi-equivariant identifications, is the statement that the tensor written $\mathrm{P}_{ab}$ in \cite{PenroseRindler86} (there $\Phi_{ab} - \Lambda g_{ab}$) is the Schouten tensor of Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-tractor-connection-local-twistor-transport}(i) with a definite sign fixed by their curvature conventions. The paper imports this identification rather than re-deriving the curvature conventions of \cite{PenroseRindler86}; the algebraic side is proved and script-checked, and nothing later depends on the sign.
__notes__.note.correspondence.boundary-stated-plai: Facts \claimref{correspondence.imported-nonlinear-graviton} and Proposition \claimref{correspondence.no-real-lorentzian-vacuum-half-flat} together are the boundary of the correspondence: the nonlinear graviton globalises the completion's point space in the Euclidean and complexified sectors, where half-flatness is a nontrivial condition, and \emph{never} for a real Lorentzian black hole. Encoding the full, two-sided Einstein equations in data on the projective spinor space $\PCS$ (twistor data) is the googly problem, open in every formalism, including this one. What the transport framework does capture of the Lorentzian black hole's structure on the conformal spinor space (its twistorial nature) is the type-D structure: the Kerr conformal scale is the inverse cube of the Walker-Penrose Killing spinor \cite[Prop.~6.8]{ButlerT6}, a statement at the level of the section “Incidence encodes the completion”'s dictionary, not of Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-nonlinear-graviton}'s globalisation.
__notes__.note.hawking.setting-position-series:
This paper is T7 of the series. \emph{It relies on six predecessors:} the primer T0 \cite{ButlerT0} and the root paper T1 \cite{ButlerT1} for the completed-pair language and the transport principle; the tower paper T3 \cite{ButlerT3} for the CAR limit that makes the boundary modes an algebra (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-algebra-boundary-modes-car-algebra}); the singularity paper T5 \cite{ButlerT5} for modular descent under its premises (P) and (R), the bosonisation bridge under (Q), and the surface gravity $\kappa = 1/4M$ (Facts \claimref{hawking.imported-modular-descent-premises-geometric-normalisation} and \claimref{hawking.imported-s-wave-bosonic-sector}); the interior paper T6 \cite{ButlerT6} for the exterior exactness that greybody inheritance rests on (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-exterior-exactly-general-relativity}); and the twistor paper T9 \cite{ButlerT9} for the ordering shift from which Proposition \claimref{hawking.homogeneity-ordering-shift} is promoted.

\emph{Papers that rely on this one:} the entropy paper T8 \cite{ButlerT8} imports the single-mode modular structure, the quasi-free calculus, and the finite-window identities; the action paper T10 \cite{ButlerT10} imports the finite-window quantification of the current algebra; the standard-model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} imports the helicity identification of Proposition \claimref{hawking.homogeneity-ordering-shift}; and the capstone T17 \cite{ButlerT17} tabulates this paper's claims at their tiers.
__notes__.note.interior.setting-introduction:
T5 of this series \cite{ButlerT5} runs a six-step chain from the Schwarzschild gauge field to the Page curve, and at three of its links it defers to a companion geometry paper: for the detailed geometry of where and how division fails, for the covariant meaning of the ascent at the level of the field equations, and for the tests that decide whether the ascended description has physical content or is only a redescription. This is that paper.

The object under study is the gauge-theoretic formulation of general relativity in the spacetime algebra $\Cl(1,3)$, due to Lasenby, Doran and Gull \cite{LDG1998}: gravity as a position-dependent linear map $\hb$ on a flat background, with every metrical statement built from $\hb^{-1}$. The theory's geometric content exists exactly where $\hb$ is invertible, and the series' transport principle \cite{ButlerT1} is a general theory of the loci where it is not. Three questions arise the moment the principle is applied to a black hole, and they organise the paper's three parts.

\emph{Where, exactly, does division fail, and what is the algebraic character of the approach?} Part one (the section “Part one: where division fails”) answers with two exact factorisations. The Schwarzschild gauge trajectory is a ray in a one-parameter unipotent group: at every radius the field is a finite null-type shear of the identity, and the singularity is the divergence of the shear parameter (Proposition \claimref{interior.gauge-trajectory-unipotent-ray}). The curvature factorises exactly, at every radius, into a divergent conformal prefactor $-M/r^3$ times a fixed, mass-independent shape operator $S$ satisfying $S^2 + S = 2$ (Proposition \claimref{interior.exact-scale-decoupling}): the entire approach to the singularity is carried by a single conformal weight, and what survives the approach is conformal data.

\emph{Is the ascent $\Cl(1,3) \to \Cl(2,4)$ a property of the equations or something added to them?} Part two (the section “Part two: the vacuum equations as a parallel ideal point”) proves the strongest available answer: no limit is needed. The vacuum field equations are exactly equivalent, at every radius, to the covariant constancy of the distinguished null scale section of the rank-six ambient (tractor) bundle: a parallel ideal point of the fibre quadric (Theorem \claimref{interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equations}). The equations of vacuum gravity are natively a statement in the ascended description, and the familiar metric form is what that statement looks like after a scale is chosen. The cosmological constant enters at theorem level: for $\Lambda \neq 0$ the frozen point leaves the cone, its squared norm is $\Lambda/3$, and its stabiliser rotates from the parabolic Poincar\'e group to the reductive de Sitter or anti-de Sitter group (Theorem \claimref{interior.scale-tractor-leaves-cone}, Proposition \claimref{interior.stabiliser-rotates-parabolic-reductive}): $\Lambda$ measures precisely the failure of infinity to be parabolic.

\emph{Does the covariant description actually reach the singularity?} Part three answers in two halves. the section “Part three, first half: the approach” proves the weighted limit theorem: blowing up the interior along the singular locus with direction-dependent weights equal to the Kasner exponents $(-1/3, 2/3, 2/3)$, the Hubble-normalised connection and the parallel tractor extend continuously to the exceptional boundary, with explicit rates ($O(\tau^{2/3})$ in the boosts, $O(\tau^{1/3})$ in the rotations), and the values-level boundary holonomy algebra is exactly $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$, which for $\Lambda = 0$ is the Levi factor of the frozen point's parabolic stabiliser with no component in the nilradical, and for $\Lambda \neq 0$ a proper subalgebra of its reductive stabiliser (Theorem \claimref{interior.weighted-limit-theorem}). The theorem is proved in full for the Schwarzschild class, extends verbatim to Schwarzschild-de Sitter (Theorem \claimref{interior.schwarzschild-de-sitter-weighted-limit}), and carries a sharp delimiter: for generic mixmaster singularities the frame limit provably fails to exist, and the correct generic statement must be billiard-invariant (Remark \claimref{note.interior.generic-delimiter-mixmaster}). the section “Part three, second half: the Kerr tests” then runs the Kerr tests: the whole Kerr family is unipotent on a null shear (Proposition \claimref{interior.unipotency-across-kerr-family}); the curvature takes the Schwarzschild form with a complexified scale whose non-invertibility locus is exactly the ring, with the disc interior regular (Proposition \claimref{interior.complex-factorisation-location-ring}); the complex scale is the inverse cube of the Walker-Penrose Killing spinor, so the framework's scalar-plus-pseudoscalar scale is a hidden twistorial object (Proposition \claimref{interior.complex-scale-inverse-cube-killing-spinor}); and at the perturbed Cauchy horizon the imported PDE results establish survival by derivative level, point-level structure (metric and conformal alike) extending continuously while connection-level structure generically fails (proved in spherical symmetry, expected for Kerr), with the strict conformal-over-metric separation registered as the sharpest successor problem (the section “The perturbed Cauchy horizon”).
__notes__.note.interior.setting-prior-art: Each part of the paper relies on named prior art, and the boundaries are declared here once. \emph{Gauge theory gravity} is due to Lasenby, Doran and Gull \cite{LDG1998}, with the textbook treatment in \cite{DoranLasenby2003}; the field equations, the Newtonian (Painlev\'e-Gullstrand) gauge, and the Kerr-Schild forms used below are theirs, and the curvature computations we import are so marked. \emph{Tractor calculus} goes back to Thomas and was formalised by Bailey, Eastwood and Gover \cite{BEG1994}, with the modern treatment in Curry-Gover \cite{CurryGover2018}; the almost-Einstein characterisation (Einstein metrics as parallel scale tractors) is Gover's \cite{Gover2010}, and Theorem \claimref{interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equations} is that characterisation put to a new use: the reading of the GTG vacuum equations as the covariant constancy of an ideal point of the series' completion, and the identification of the parabolic stabiliser structure with the obstruction structure of \cite{ButlerT1}, are the contributions claimed, not tractor calculus itself. The \emph{Kasner} form of the Schwarzschild interior is classical (Kantowski-Sachs), and the velocity-dominated class descends from Eardley-Liang-Sachs \cite{ELS1972} and Isenberg-Moncrief \cite{IsenbergMoncrief1990}; BKL oscillations and the billiard description are \cite{BKL1970, DHN2003}; the weighted limit theorem and its holonomy identification are new. On the Kerr side, the Kerr-Schild form is \cite{KerrSchild1965}, the Killing spinor is Walker-Penrose \cite{WalkerPenrose1970} with Carter's constant \cite{Carter1968}; mass inflation is Poisson-Israel \cite{PoissonIsrael1990}, the $C^0$ stability of the Kerr Cauchy horizon with generic curvature blow-up is Dafermos-Luk \cite{DafermosLuk2017}, and the finiteness of tidal distortion is Ori \cite{Ori1991}. What part three adds is the reading: the location of the framework's own criteria inside these results, and the conclusion they jointly support about the ascent.
__notes__.note.interior.what-equation-now-says: In the flat model the parallel null tractor is the ideal point $\nInf$ of Proposition \claimref{interior.stabilisers-flat-model}: the point at infinity. Theorem \claimref{interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equations} therefore reads: \emph{the field equation of vacuum gravity literally asserts the covariant constancy of a distinguished point at infinity}. This is a statement not about metric components but about a preferred ideal point of the fibre quadric, parallel-transported without change over the whole of $M^\circ$. The space it lies in, the point space of the completion, is precisely where \cite[Thm.~4.10]{ButlerT1} located the resolution of division by zero, and precisely the structure that the no-go theorem showed cannot be replaced by any element-level classical assignment. The ascent is not notation added to the physics: the physics, in vacuum, is an assertion within the ascended description, and the familiar metric form of the equations is what that assertion looks like after a scale is chosen. The points of contact with established physics, kept in view as the series' practice requires: the bundle $\mathcal{T}$ is the standard conformal tractor bundle (Thomas; Bailey-Eastwood-Gover), the equivalence ``Einstein $\Leftrightarrow$ parallel scale tractor'' is the almost-Einstein characterisation of Gover \cite{Gover2010}, and the spinor module of the fibre algebra $\Cl(2,4)$, the conformal spinor space $\CS$, is Penrose's twistor space, whose development belongs to the series' correspondence paper.
__notes__.note.interior.setting-perturbed-cauchy-h: Exact Kerr was never the hard part of the test. Since Kerr is Ricci-flat, Theorem \claimref{interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equations} applies verbatim on the whole vacuum region, inner horizons included: the parallel null tractor exists globally, and exact Kerr passes the covariance test outright. The physical question is what survives perturbation, because the Cauchy horizon is known to be unstable. The established results are imported with provenance and then read.
__notes__.note.interior.setting-position-series: This paper is T6 of the series. It consumes four predecessors. From the primer T0 \cite{ButlerT0} it takes the working language of geometric algebra; from the root paper T1 \cite{ButlerT1} the zero-divisor taxonomy, the no-go theorem whose transvections reappear here as the nilradical of the frozen point's stabiliser, and the completion that fixes the ambient algebra $\Cl(2,4)$; from the sheaf paper T4 \cite{ButlerT4} the wall-level theory of degeneration whose codimension-two extension Conjecture \claimref{interior.duality-monodromy-fibration-over-ring} names; and from the singularity paper T5 \cite{ButlerT5} the curvature computation imported as Fact \claimref{interior.imported-schwarzschild-curvature-spectrum} and the six-step chain whose three geometric links this paper closes. It supplies, downstream: the Hawking paper T7 \cite{ButlerT7} imports the GTG equivalence and the vacuum theorem (Fact \claimref{interior.imported-equivalence-einstein-equations}, Theorem \claimref{interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equations}); the entropy paper T8 \cite{ButlerT8} builds on the Kasner form of the interior (Lemma \claimref{interior.kasner-form-interior}), the weighted-limit results of the section “Part three, first half: the approach”, and the duality-monodromy conjecture (Conjecture \claimref{interior.duality-monodromy-fibration-over-ring}); the twistor paper T9 \cite{ButlerT9} develops the flat-model dictionary of the section “Part two: the vacuum equations as a parallel ideal point”, the vacuum and $\Lambda$ theorems, and the Killing-spinor identification (Proposition \claimref{interior.complex-scale-inverse-cube-killing-spinor}); and the dark-energy paper T10 \cite{ButlerT10} takes the frozen point, its norm $\Lambda/3$, and the parabolic-to-reductive stabiliser rotation (Theorems \claimref{interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equations}, \claimref{interior.scale-tractor-leaves-cone}, Proposition \claimref{interior.stabiliser-rotates-parabolic-reductive}) as its kinematic base.
__notes__.note.interior.setting-exact-scale-decoup: Write $\sigma_r := \er\et$ for the unit radial spacetime bivector, so $\sigma_r^2 = \er\et\er\et = -\er^2\et^2 = +1$, and let $\Pi$ denote the projection of the six-dimensional bivector space onto the plane pair $\operatorname{span}\{\sigma_r, I\sigma_r\}$.
__notes__.note.interior.three-readings: First, the trace-free curvature is pure Weyl, as vacuum requires, and the Weyl part is precisely the conformally covariant part of curvature: what survives the approach is conformal data. Second, dilations emerge exactly, not asymptotically: normalise by the conformal prefactor and nothing along the trajectory changes at all, a rigidity peculiar to the type-D family and stronger than any generic BKL statement. Third, the spectrum exhibits the classic $2{:}1$ Coulombic tidal structure, stretching along the radial plane at twice the rate of the transverse compression; the ratio is an eigenvalue ratio of $S$, hence a conformal invariant of the approach. The singularity is approached with a fixed, scale-free curvature shape, and the divergence is carried entirely by a single conformal weight. The identity $S^2 + S = 2$, equivalently $(S-1)(S+2) = 0$, is the minimal-polynomial statement of this rigidity, and it is the algebraic identity that the complexified Kerr version in the section “Part three, second half: the Kerr tests” inherits unchanged, the scale alone becoming complex.
__notes__.note.interior.conclusion-two-cautions: Proposition \claimref{interior.filtration-cauchy-horizon-read-literature}(2) is a filtration statement, and it is read as exactly that: survival at the perturbed Cauchy horizon is ordered by derivative level, with the divergence in the nilpotent slots, which is the structure the framework predicts. What the literature does not supply is a strict separation of the conformal from the metric description at fixed derivative level: the framework's central claim, that the ascended description persists where the metric one fails, therefore rests at the Cauchy horizon on the open transport question of successor problem (1), not on a finished theorem. The Kerr test is passed at the level the imports reach, and no further. Two cautions make the conclusion more precise, both recorded as scope. First, generic perturbations destroy type-D rigidity: the exact shape factorisations of Propositions \claimref{interior.exact-scale-decoupling} and \claimref{interior.complex-factorisation-location-ring} are properties of the exact family, and robust statements off it must be made at the level of the boost-weight filtration rather than the fixed operator $S$. Second, what the framework most needs, a quantitative transport theorem (convergence of tractor parallel transport along causal curves crossing the Cauchy horizon), needs integrability of the connection along such curves: a property strictly between the established $C^0$ metric extension and the $C^1$ statement whose generic failure is proved in spherical symmetry and expected for Kerr, and not currently available in either direction. It is the sharpest open problem the test leaves, and it is registered in the section “Scope, and successor problems”.
__notes__.note.interior.setting-what-proved-what-i:

__notes__.note.interior.abstract: This paper is the mathematical-relativity companion to T5: the geometry of the ascent $\Cl(1,3) \to \Cl(2,4)$ at the black-hole singularity, in three parts. Part one, where division fails: the Schwarzschild gauge field is a ray in a one-parameter unipotent group, and the curvature factorises exactly, at every radius, into a divergent conformal scale times a fixed shape operator $S$ satisfying $S^2 + S = 2$. Part two, the covariant form: the vacuum field equations are exactly equivalent to the covariant constancy of the null scale section of the rank-six tractor bundle, a parallel ideal point; for $\Lambda \neq 0$ the point leaves the cone with squared norm $\Lambda/3$, and its stabiliser rotates from parabolic Poincar\'e to reductive (anti-)de Sitter. Part three, the approach and the tests: under a blow-up weighted by the Kasner exponents $(-\tfrac13, \tfrac23, \tfrac23)$ the tractor formulation extends to the singular locus for the Einstein velocity-dominated class, with values-level boundary holonomy exactly $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$, for $\Lambda = 0$ the Levi factor of the frozen point's parabolic stabiliser, and transport-level convergence along tangential curves of fixed Hubble-normalised length; and Kerr passes three tests: unipotency on a null shear, a complex factorisation locating the ring and leaving the disc regular, and the conformal scale as the inverse cube of the Walker-Penrose Killing spinor. At the perturbed Cauchy horizon point-level structure extends continuously while connection-level structure generically fails, proved in spherical symmetry and expected for Kerr; the conformal-over-metric separation is the sharpest open problem. Eighty-two checks verify the computational identities.
__notes__.note.interior.setting-contribution: At the standard of \cite{ButlerT1}, with each theorem carrying its own hypotheses and imports stated as Facts with provenance. (1) The exact algebra of the failure: the unipotent ray and the exact scale decoupling $S^2 + S = 2$ (the section “Part one: where division fails”). (2) The covariant form of the vacuum equations as a parallel ideal point, with a self-contained flat-model dictionary that fixes every sign, the $\Lambda \neq 0$ extension, and the parabolic-to-reductive stabiliser rotation proved outright (the section “Part two: the vacuum equations as a parallel ideal point”). (3) The weighted limit theorem for the Einstein velocity-dominated class, with explicit Kasner data, explicit convergence rate, the values-level boundary holonomy, the mixmaster delimiter, and the Schwarzschild-de Sitter extension, together with transport-level convergence along every tangential curve of fixed Hubble-normalised length for the whole admissible class and the explicit $\tau^{1/3}$ rate of the Schwarzschild $\varphi$-lines (the section “Part three, first half: the approach”, the section “Transport along tangential curves, and the $\varphi$-lines”). (4) The Kerr tests: unipotency across the family, the complex factorisation locating the ring, the Killing-spinor identification of the scale, the duality-monodromy conjecture, and the Cauchy-horizon filtration reading of the PDE literature (the section “Part three, second half: the Kerr tests”). (5) Machine verification of every computational identity in exact arithmetic \cite{ButlerVerifyT06}.
__notes__.note.interior.setting-setting-convention:
Spacetime algebra $\Cl(1,3)$ with orthonormal generators $\gamma_0, \gamma_1, \gamma_2, \gamma_3$, $\gamma_0^2 = +1$, $\gamma_i^2 = -1$; in the $(t,r)$ plane write $\et := \gamma_0$, $\er := \gamma_1$. The pseudoscalar is $I := \gamma_0\gamma_1\gamma_2\gamma_3$, with $I^2 = -1$; $I$ commutes with every even element and anticommutes with every vector. Units $G = c = 1$; metric signature $(+,-,-,-)$. Curvature conventions are those fixed by the Cartan structure equations exactly as in T5's appendix \cite[App.~A]{ButlerT5}; in these conventions de Sitter space has $\mathcal{R}(a) = \Lambda a$ on physical vectors and scalar curvature $\mathcal{R} = 4\Lambda$ (in components $\Ric_{ab} = \Lambda\, g_{ab}$, $R = 4\Lambda$), where $\mathcal{R}(B) = -R(\hb(B))$ is the curvature operator of Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields} in the store's sign.

In gauge theory gravity, gravity is a pair of gauge fields on the flat background: the position-dependent linear map $\hb(a)$ on vectors, gauging local frame rescalings, and the connection bivector $\Omega(a)$, gauging local Lorentz rotations. The covariant derivative and field strength are
\[
D_a M = a \cdot \nabla M + \Omega(a) \times M, \qquad
R(a \wedge b) = a\cdot\nabla\,\Omega(b) - b\cdot\nabla\,\Omega(a) + \Omega(a) \times \Omega(b),
\]
with $A \times B := \tfrac12(AB - BA)$, and the field equations are, in the store's curvature sign, $\mathcal{R}(a) - \tfrac12 a\,\mathcal{R} = -\kappa\, T(a)$ for $\mathcal{R}(B) = -R(\hb(B))$ (in the sign of \cite{LDG1998}, $R(a) - \tfrac12 a R = \kappa\, T(a)$), together with the vanishing of torsion, which determines $\Omega$ algebraically from $\hb$; the metric is $g(a,b) = \hb^{-1}(a) \cdot \hb^{-1}(b)$ \cite{LDG1998}. Every operation in these displays is interior to $\Cl(1,3)$: nothing invokes a curved manifold beyond the flat background. The theory is a field theory of an invertibility-demanding map, which is exactly the condition the transport principle addresses.
These are the only geometric imports of Part one; everything else in the section “Part one: where division fails” through the section “Part three, first half: the approach” is proved here.
__notes__.note.interior.setting-part-two-vacuum-eq: Part one located the failure of division and the conformal rigidity of the approach. This part proves that the ascent $\Cl(1,3) \to \Cl(2,4)$ is not an operation applied to the field equations from outside: the vacuum equations \emph{are}, exactly and at every radius, a single covariant statement about the rank-six ambient bundle whose fibre algebra is $\Cl(2,4)$. No limit is taken anywhere in this section.
__notes__.note.interior.setting-tractor-bundle-sca:
Let $M^\circ$ be a region where $\hb$ is invertible, $g$ the physical metric there, and $[g]$ its conformal class. The completion of the series assigns to $[g]$ the ambient (tractor) bundle: the rank-six vector bundle $\mathcal{T}$ which, in the chosen scale $g$, splits as
\[
\mathcal{T} \;\cong\; \R \,\oplus\, TM^\circ \,\oplus\, \R, \qquad \text{sections } (\sigma, \mu^b, \rho),
\]
carrying the tractor metric
\begin{equation}
Q((\sigma,\mu,\rho)) \;=\; g(\mu,\mu) \,+\, 2\sigma\rho .
\end{equation}
With $g$ of signature $(1,3)$ the form $\ip{(\sigma,\mu,\rho)}{(\sigma,\mu,\rho)} \;=\; g(\mu,\mu) \,+\, 2\sigma\rho$ has signature $(2,4)$: the $\mu$ block contributes $(1,3)$ and the hyperbolic $\sigma\rho$ pairing contributes $(1,1)$. The fibre Clifford algebra is $\Cl(2,4)$ and the structure algebra of the bundle is $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$, acting through the bivectors of $\Cl(2,4)$: this is the same completion that Rule 1 forces at the degenerate locus \cite{ButlerT1, ButlerT4}, here assembled over the regular region.
__notes__.note.interior.convention-note-sign-norm: In the labelling fixed here (tractor signature $(2,4)$ meaning two plus, four minus, forced by $\ip{(\sigma,\mu,\rho)}{(\sigma,\mu,\rho)} \;=\; g(\mu,\mu) \,+\, 2\sigma\rho$ with $g$ mostly minus), the norm of the frozen point is proportional to $+\Lambda$, and that sign is the series' convention throughout. It is not a free choice: the stabiliser of a \emph{negative}-norm vector in $O(2,4)$ is $O(2,3)$, the anti-de Sitter group, by Proposition \claimref{interior.non-null-stabilisers-section-they-act}(1), so a norm proportional to $-\Lambda$ could not carry the de Sitter stabiliser that Theorem \claimref{interior.scale-tractor-leaves-cone} and Proposition \claimref{interior.stabiliser-rotates-parabolic-reductive} establish for $\Lambda > 0$. The invariant content is what those two results prove: nullity exactly at $\Lambda = 0$, reductive rotation, and de Sitter for $\Lambda > 0$. The verification script checks the complement signatures exactly.
__notes__.note.interior.refining-not-contradicting: Two comments locate the result within the series. First, the parabolic structures of this paper are singularity phenomena, not infinity phenomena: the unipotent ray of Proposition \claimref{interior.gauge-trajectory-unipotent-ray} and the Levi boundary holonomy of Theorem \claimref{interior.weighted-limit-theorem} concern the approach to $r = 0$, and the section “Part three, first half: the approach” proves ($\Lambda$-robustness, Theorem \claimref{interior.schwarzschild-de-sitter-weighted-limit}) that they survive $\Lambda \neq 0$ unchanged: under the weighted blow-up the Weyl data is order one while the $\Lambda$ terms carry positive weight and vanish at the boundary. Second, the rotation of the stabiliser is itself series data: the passage from a parabolic to a reductive stabiliser is exactly the passage from the obstructed situation of the no-go theorem (null direction, transvections, no canonical complement) to the unobstructed one (non-null direction, orthogonal complement splits); the cosmological constant is, in this precise sense, the parameter that removes the obstruction at infinity while leaving the obstruction at the singularity intact.
__notes__.note.interior.what-two-ends-geometry-joi: The frozen point governs both ends of the geometry, in opposite algebraic ways. At infinity, its stabiliser is rotated from parabolic to reductive by $\Lambda$ (Proposition \claimref{interior.stabiliser-rotates-parabolic-reductive}): the obstruction structure at infinity is removed by the cosmological constant. At the singularity, the approach gives nonzero limiting values in the boost part of the Levi factor, which generates it, and zero in the nilradical, for $\Lambda = 0$ and $\Lambda \neq 0$ alike (Theorems \claimref{interior.weighted-limit-theorem}, \claimref{interior.schwarzschild-de-sitter-weighted-limit}): the obstruction structure at the singularity is intact, and the weighted limit resolves it by transporting the description, not by removing the obstruction. This division is the geometric instance of the series' one-way door: what is obstructed is never repaired in place, and what survives is the conformal, ascended data.

__notes__.note.interior.parabolic-structure-comple: The theorem completes the argument announced in Remark \claimref{note.interior.parabolic-structural-reason}. The stabiliser of the covariantly constant ideal point is the parabolic with Levi factor $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$ and nilradical $\R^4$ (Proposition \claimref{interior.stabilisers-flat-model}); the weighted limit gives nonzero limiting values in the boost part of the Levi factor, which generates it, and zero in the nilradical, which consists of the very shear directions whose transvection action obstructed the element-level completion in \cite[Thm.~4.2]{ButlerT1}. Three appearances of one structure are now related: the parabolic obstruction of the no-go theorem, the unipotent gauge trajectory of Proposition \claimref{interior.gauge-trajectory-unipotent-ray}, and the Levi boundary holonomy of Theorem \claimref{interior.weighted-limit-theorem}. At the singularity the limiting connection lies purely in the Levi factor of the stabiliser of a frozen ideal point.
__notes__.note.mass.abstract:
Mass enters a conformally invariant theory where scale does: as coupling to the frozen point, the parallel scale tractor of squared norm $\Lambda/3$. We prove the mass-weight dictionary: a density of conformal weight $w$ coupled to the frozen point through the Thomas operator obeys the Klein-Gordon equation with $m^{2} = -w(w+n-1)Q(I)$, in dimension four $m^{2} = -w(w+3)\Lambda/3$, the de Sitter formula $\Delta(3-\Delta)H^{2}$ with $\Delta = -w$, $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$. A real weight gives a nonnegative $m^{2}$ only on $w \in [-3,0]$, and there at most $m = 3H/2$; every known massive particle has complex weight $-\tfrac32 \pm I_4\nu$ (numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$) with $\nu \approx m/H$, about $3 \times 10^{38}$ for the electron. We prove the twistor counterpart, $m^{2} = 2|\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}|^{2}$ for a two-twistor composite, and compute its exact de Sitter extension: the composite's grip on the frozen point, $P = M(I_{\Lambda})$ with $M$ the conformal moment map, is its de Sitter momentum, with squared length
\[
m^{2} \;=\; 2\,|B_{\Lambda}|^{2} + Q(I_{\Lambda})\, C,
\]
where $B_{\Lambda} = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}} + (\Lambda/6)[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]$ is the composite's pairing against the frozen point and $C$ the internal $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ Casimir of the constituents' Gram matrix. Relative to the deformed bracket the correction is one term, with coefficient exactly $\Lambda/3$, and the massless locus is computed. The dictionary then assigns the composite its weight; it does not explain the observed masses but relocates the question: the hierarchy is the size of an imaginary weight. The paper is Tier B; every computational identity is verified in exact arithmetic by a deposited script.
__notes__.note.mass.setting-introduction:
The action paper of this series builds the internal vector of gravity's MacDowell-Mansouri functional from the completion's frozen point, the parallel scale tractor $I$ whose squared norm is $\Lambda/3$: the Stelle-West vector is $V = X - (3/\Lambda)I$, made from $I$ and the canonical tractor $X$ \cite{ButlerT10}. That is the framework's account of what gravity is. This paper asks what mass is, and finds the same object at the centre of the answer twice: mass is the strength of a field's grip on the frozen point, measured once as a conformal weight read against the frozen point's length, and once as the length of a composite's momentum, which is the composite's grip on the same point. The paper proves each formula at the series' standard, computes the composite's mass in de Sitter space exactly, with the correction to the flat-space formula derived rather than estimated, and says precisely how the two readings meet: the flat formula is the squared pairing of the composite against the frozen point, and the dictionary then assigns the composite its weight.

The results come in three steps. \emph{The dictionary} (the section “The mass-weight dictionary”): a density of conformal weight $w$ coupled to the frozen point through the Thomas operator obeys the Klein-Gordon equation with
\[
m^{2} = -w(w+n-1)\,Q(I),
\]
in dimension four $m^{2} = -w(w+3)\Lambda/3$. With $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$ and $\Delta = -w$ this is the de Sitter mass formula $m^{2} = \Delta(3-\Delta)H^{2}$, and it carries its own classification: masslessness is $w \in \{0, -3\}$, the conformally coupled scalar $w = -1$ has $m^{2} = 2H^{2}$, a real weight gives $m^{2} \ge 0$ only for $w \in [-3, 0]$ and then $m \le 3H/2$, and every heavier field has complex weight $w = -\tfrac32 \pm I_4\nu$ (numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$). Since $3H/2$ is about $10^{-33}\,\mathrm{eV}$, every known massive particle is of the last kind, with $\nu \approx m/H$, about $3 \times 10^{38}$ for the electron. The natural conjecture, that coupling to the frozen point explains the observed masses, fails: what the dictionary yields is the hierarchy problem restated as the size of an imaginary weight. \emph{The area} (the section “Mass as symplectic area”): a single twistor is massless; a two-twistor composite has $m^{2} = 2|\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}|^{2}$, the squared symplectic area between its constituents' spinor parts. \emph{The join} (the section “The exact join”): the de Sitter scale in the flat conformal chart is $\sigma = 1 - \Lambda Q/12$, and its frozen point in the twistor chart is $I_{\Lambda} = n_{\infty} + (\Lambda/6)\,n_{0}$, derived rather than assumed. The composite's grip on it, the ambient vector $P = M(I_{\Lambda})$ built from the conformal moment map, is the de Sitter momentum, and its squared length is computed in closed form:
\[
m^{2} \;=\; 2\,|B_{\Lambda}|^{2} + Q(I_{\Lambda})\,C, \qquad B_{\Lambda} = \ip{I_{\Lambda}}{Z^{1}\wedge Z^{2}} = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}],
\]
with $C$ the internal $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ Casimir of the two constituents. At $\Lambda = 0$ this is the area formula, now read as the squared pairing of the composite against the frozen point; for $\Lambda \neq 0$ the correction is a single term whose coefficient is the frozen point's norm. The composite's weight is then read off the dictionary: for every composite heavier than $3H/2$, $\mathrm{Re}\,w = -\tfrac32$ and $\mathrm{Im}\,w = m/H - \tfrac98 H/m + O((H/m)^{3})$. the section “What gravity is, and what remains” assembles the results with the action paper, at declared levels: mass is coupling to the frozen point, gravity is the action of the frozen point, and the universality of free fall reads as the statement that the theory contains one scale-giving object.
__notes__.note.mass.setting-prior-art: The tractor calculus and the Thomas operator are Thomas's, in the modern formulation of Bailey, Eastwood and Gover \cite{BEG1994}; the scale tractor and the almost-Einstein technology are Gover's \cite{Gover2010}; the identification of the parallel scale tractor with this series' frozen point, and the norm $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ in the series' conventions, are the geometry paper's \cite{ButlerT6}. The two-twistor description of massive particles is classical twistor theory: Penrose, Hughston, and the Oxford school \cite{PenroseRindler1986, Hughston1979}; the mass formula as a two-index contraction with the infinity twistor is standard there, as is the conformal moment map in twistor variables. The three series of unitary representations of $SO(1,4)$ are Dixmier's \cite{Dixmier1961}; the mass formula $\Delta(3-\Delta)H^{2}$ is their modern parametrisation, standard in the de Sitter literature. The identification of the ambient space with $\Lambda^{2}\T$, of the incidence chart with the completion, and of the frozen point with the infinity twistor, which the join relies on, is the twistor paper's \cite{ButlerT9}. What this paper claims as new is the dictionary read through the frozen point, so that mass and dark energy derive from a single object; the derivation of the de Sitter frozen point $I_{\Lambda}$ and its deformed bracket from the scale function of the flat chart; the closed-form mass of the two-twistor composite in de Sitter space, with the correction to the flat formula computed as one term; and the reading of the equivalence principle that the assembly with the action paper permits.
__notes__.note.mass.setting-contribution: (1) The mass-weight dictionary at theorem level in the series' conventions, with its three de Sitter series as a corollary (the section “The mass-weight dictionary”). (2) The two-twistor area formula, classical, reproved at theorem level because the join needs every sign, with the Fock-vacuum reading from the twistor paper (the section “Mass as symplectic area”). (3) The exact join: the de Sitter scale and frozen point in the flat chart, what the chart's nullity fixes and the real slice, the chart form of the spin isomorphism, the grip of a composite on the frozen point and its reality (the first half of the reality lemma being the chart form of a twistor-paper statement, the second this paper's), the closed-form mass with its one-term correction, the Casimir form of the result, the five broken generators, and the weight of a composite (the section “The exact join”). (4) The assembly with the action paper at declared levels, and the successor problems (the section “What gravity is, and what remains”). (5) Machine verification of every computational identity in exact arithmetic \cite{ButlerVerifyT11}.
__notes__.note.mass.conventions-sign: The dictionary is written in the conventions of Fact \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection}, where $Q(I) = +\Lambda/3$, and there it carries a minus sign in the invariant form. The physical content is convention-independent: $m^{2} = \Delta(3-\Delta)H^{2}$ with $\Delta = -w$ is the de Sitter mass formula of Fact \claimref{mass.imported-unitary-representations-de-sitter-group}, and the conformally coupled scalar of Corollary \claimref{mass.weight-polynomial-two-series}(2) fixes it. The sign in the invariant form and the sign of the norm are tied together by the computation of Theorem \claimref{mass.mass-weight-dictionary}, and neither carries content on its own. \cite[Rem.~4.9]{ButlerT6} records that the norm reads $+\Lambda$ in the present conventions, and why the opposite sign could not carry the de Sitter stabiliser; this paper's displays are all in the present conventions. What no convention changes is the statement that a positive mass above $3H/2$ requires a complex weight.
__notes__.note.mass.setting-grip-composite-frozen-: Three properties follow at once. First, $\ip{P}{I} = M_{I\wedge I} = 0$: the grip lies in $I^{\perp}$. Second, $m^{2}$ is invariant under the stabiliser of $I$: for $\gamma$ with $\gamma I = I$, $\ip{P(\gamma Z)}{U} = M_{U\wedge I}(\gamma Z) = M_{\gamma^{-1}(U\wedge I)}(Z) = M_{\gamma^{-1}U\wedge I}(Z) = \ip{P(Z)}{\gamma^{-1}U} = \ip{\gamma P(Z)}{U}$, so $P(\gamma Z) = \gamma P(Z)$ and $Q(P)$ is unchanged; for the frozen point of Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point} the stabiliser acts on the ambient space through $SO(1,4)$ (Fact \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection}; the Lie-algebra form of the surjection is Lemma \claimref{mass.five-broken-generators}), and $P$ is a de Sitter vector. Third, at $\Lambda = 0$, $I = n_{\infty}$ and $\ip{P}{x} = M_{x\wedge n_{\infty}}$ is, by Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism}(2), the value of the translation generator on the composite, that is, its total momentum in the direction $x$; the $x$-slot part of $P$ is therefore the momentum, the remaining part is $-d\,n_{\infty}$ with $d$ the dilation charge, and since $n_{\infty}$ is null and orthogonal to the $x$-slot, $m^{2}$ is the Poincar\'e Casimir $p^{2}$. Definition \claimref{obj.mass.grip-mass-composite} is the de Sitter extension of the mass of Proposition \claimref{mass.mass-symplectic-area-two-twistor-formula}: the composite's momentum is its grip on the point at infinity, and its mass is the length of that grip. Lemma \claimref{mass.five-broken-generators} below identifies the generators $A(e_{a}\wedge I)$, $e_{a} \in I^{\perp}$, whose charges are the components of $P$, with the five generators of $\mathfrak{su}(2,2)$ broken by $I$, the de Sitter translations, which is the representation-theoretic form of the same statement. That $P$ is a real vector, so that $Q(P)$ is a value of the real $(1,4)$ form on $I^{\perp}$, is the next lemma.

__notes__.note.mass.setting-machine-verification:
Every computational identity asserted in this paper has been verified in exact arithmetic by the script \texttt{verify\_T11.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT11}, which imports the series' shared library \texttt{GA.py}: exact rationals and Gaussian rationals, exact rank, rational functions in a formal variable, and exact truncated power series. No floating point is used anywhere; thirty-nine checks, all passing, organised in five parts keyed to statement tags.

\emph{Part A: the dictionary.} The pairing $I \cdot D\sigma$ is formed slot by slot from Facts \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection} and \claimref{mass.imported-thomas-operator}, with $\sigma$ and $\Box\sigma$ as formal coordinates, and $m^{2}$ is read off the resulting Klein-Gordon equation: $m^{2} = -w(w+n-1)Q(I)$ on a $144$-point rational grid in $(w, n, J)$, with a separate check that the opposite sign fails at every grid point where $m^{2} \neq 0$; in $n = 4$, $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, $\rho_{I} = \Lambda/6$ and $m^{2} = -w(w+3)\Lambda/3$ as rational-function identities in a formal $\Lambda$. Corollary \claimref{mass.weight-polynomial-two-series}: the conformally coupled scalar's $m^{2} = 2\Lambda/3$ from the pairing; the massless weights $w = 0$ and $w = 1-n$, and no others among four further test values; the shadow symmetry $m^{2}(w) = m^{2}(1-n-w)$ and the closed form $\tfrac{n(n-2)}{4}Q(I)$ at $w = 1 - n/2$ for four values of $n$; the completed square $-w(w+3) = \tfrac94 - (w+\tfrac32)^{2}$ as a polynomial identity, with $m^{2} \ge 0$ at six real weights inside $[-3,0]$ and $m^{2} < 0$ at six outside; and $w = -\tfrac32 \pm I_4\nu$ (numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$, the Gaussian rationals standing for $\mathbb{Q}(I_4)$) solving the dictionary in exact Gaussian rationals.

\emph{Part B: the area.} On exact Gaussian-rational spinor instances: a single twistor's momentum is null; $p^{2} = 2|\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}|^{2}$ on all ten pairs with the imaginary part identically zero; aligned spinors give a null composite.

\emph{Part C: the chart and the de Sitter scale.} The chart on $\Lambda^{2}\CS$, the exterior square of twistor space, which is the complexified conformal vector space; its unit commutes with every conformal vector and is the central pseudoscalar $I_7$ of the odd extension $\Cl(3,4)$ (\claimref{std-algebra.complexification-is-the-odd-extension}), not the $I_4$ of the weight in Part A: $\ip{n_{0}}{n_{\infty}} = +1$ with both null; $Q(x) = -2\det x$ and the orthogonality of the slots; $Q(X_{c}) = Q(1+2c)$ with $c$ undetermined (Remark \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes}). Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point}: every slot of the flat tractor connection on $(\sigma, \nabla\sigma, -\tfrac14\Box\sigma)$ vanishes and the norm is $\Lambda/3$, as rational-function identities in $\Lambda$ at rational points; $\ip{X(x)}{n_{\infty} + \lambda n_{0}} = 1 - \lambda Q/2$ at rational points and three values of $\lambda$, with the inverted order giving $\lambda - Q/2$, and the six point embeddings of the uniqueness argument of exact rank six; the ambient pairing of $n_{\infty} + \lambda n_{0}$ with itself formed and equal to $2\lambda$ at four values, with $2\lambda = \Lambda/3$, and the vector null, hence simple by Fact \claimref{mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-infinity}, exactly at $\lambda = 0$. Theorem \claimref{mass.exact-join}(1) and (4): both blocks of the deformed bracket on all ten twistor pairs, the assembled $B_{\Lambda}$ at $\Lambda = 3$, the point-supported factor $\sigma(x)$ at two points and two values of $\Lambda$, and the wedge identity $Z^{1}\wedge Z^{2} = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}X(x)$ for twistors built on the incidence line $\mu_{x}\pi + \pi$, at four points and two spinor pairs.

\emph{Part D: the grip theorem.} The spin isomorphism is solved exactly: for each rotation $R_{U\wedge V}$ the construction needs, the script finds the traceless $A$ whose action on every basis bivector equals that of the rotation. The nine rotations whose matrices Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism} displays (the grading, four translations, four special conformal generators) are compared with these solutions entry by entry. The moment map $M_{A}(Z^{1}, \dots, Z^{N}) := i\sum_{i=1}^{N} \bar{Z}^{i}\cdot(A Z^{i}), \qquad A \in \mathfrak{sl}(\T)$ and the grip of Definition \claimref{obj.mass.grip-mass-composite} are then built from these solutions, on ten twistor pairs: at $\Lambda = 0$, $Q(P) = 2|\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}|^{2}$ and $P \perp n_{\infty}$; the grip on $n_{0}$, $M(n_{0})$, has squared length $2|[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]|^{2}$; the cross term $\ip{P_{\infty}}{P_{0}}$ equals $p\cdot k - d^{2}$ with the three forms in the components of the proof, $\det t = \overline{\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}}[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]$, and equals $2\,\mathrm{Re}(\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}\overline{[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]}) + C$; and the theorem itself, $Q(P) = 2|B_{\Lambda}|^{2} + 2\lambda C$, as an identity in $\lambda$ (all three coefficients of the quadratic), with $m^{2}$ real, $P \perp I_{\Lambda}$, and $P_{\Lambda} = P_{\infty} + \lambda P_{0}$ recomputed independently at three values of $\lambda$. The identities for $C$ in the relation displayed with \claimref{mass.grip-real} and its nonnegativity. Lemma \claimref{mass.grip-real}: on four real points of the slice \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes}, every generator of a real pair (grading, translations, special conformal, Lorentz) has $\Sigma A$ anti-Hermitian, the commutator identity of the proof holds on all sixteen pairs of points, and the grip on $I_{\Lambda}$ has real pairing with $n_{\infty}$, $n_{0}$ and the four real vectors on all ten pairs, and the anti-Hermiticity condition on the eight real parameters of $x$ has rank four (Remark \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes}). The doubled composite's $m^{2} = 2\lambda(\bar{Z}\cdot Z)^{2}$ on all five twistors and the non-doubled massless pair of Theorem \claimref{mass.exact-join}(5). Proposition \claimref{mass.casimir-form-join}: both Casimirs formed from the exact moment components in adapted bases, the decomposition (1), the value (2) and the closed form (3) on four pairs, and $\tr\mathsf{E}^{2} = 1$ on the grading element. Lemma \claimref{mass.five-broken-generators}: the dimensions $10$, $6$, $5$ by exact rank, and the five matrices $A(e_{a}\wedge I_{\Lambda})$ traceless, independent, with $\Omega A$ antisymmetric.

\emph{Part E: the weight.} $\nu^{2} = 6|B_{\Lambda}|^{2}/\Lambda + C - \tfrac94$ on three pairs at two values of $\Lambda$, real and positive there; the expansion $\sqrt{1 - \tfrac94\epsilon^{2}} = 1 - \tfrac98\epsilon^{2} - \tfrac{81}{128}\epsilon^{4} + \cdots$, $\epsilon = H/m$, as an exact truncated power series.

What the script does not check: the conformal invariance of the Thomas operator (imported, Fact \claimref{mass.imported-thomas-operator}); the flat-model dictionary and the spin isomorphism as theorems (imported, Fact \claimref{mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-infinity}; the script solves the isomorphism on the basis but does not prove it is one); Schur's lemma behind Lemma \claimref{mass.invariant-forms-simple-lie-algebra} (imported); the de Sitter classification against which Corollary \claimref{mass.weight-polynomial-two-series} is read (imported, Fact \claimref{mass.imported-unitary-representations-de-sitter-group}); the ``only if'' of the massless locus in Theorem \claimref{mass.exact-join}(5), which is the positivity argument of the proof; the normalisation $1/\sqrt2$ of the real slice \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes}, which the script carries as a scalar; the identification of the real form in Lemma \claimref{mass.five-broken-generators} (that the stabiliser is $\mathfrak{so}(1,4)$, that the five are the de Sitter translations, and the match with the action paper's Goldstone count), the script working over the Gaussian rationals, with no real-form check beyond the anti-Hermiticity checks of Lemma \claimref{mass.grip-real}; the $N$-constituent formulas of successor problem (5); and Proposition \claimref{mass.casimir-form-join}(2) beyond $N = 2$.

__notes__.note.pairing.setting-two-claims-kill-con:
\textbf{Claim R2 (the pairing generator).} The framework's own connection, relative to the framework's own vacuum field, has a nonzero pairing class along some directions, and that class is fixed by data the framework supplies: the vacuum field selected by the curvature (the radial pair of Fact \claimref{pairing.imported-schwarzschild-connection-curvature}, its radial member by the sign of the square, and a null direction in it by the flag bit) and the connection. A pairing generator exists and is derived, not premised, up to the flag bit.

\begin{itemize}
\item[K2.1] (nothing pairs) If the pairing class vanishes for every direction at every radius, the connection preserves the vacuum field and the claim is dead.
\item[K2.2] (frame artefact) If the class is nonzero but is not the transverse derivative $\ip{\nabla_X \ell}{m}$ of the vacuum's null direction, it is a property of the frame and not of the vacuum field, and the result is a reading, not a derivation. Test: the identity must hold in $\Q(F)$, and the vanishing locus must be invariant under $\ell \mapsto \lambda\ell$.
\item[K2.3] (consistency with the singularity paper) If the class along $\partial_t$ or $\partial_r$ is nonzero, the diagonality of that paper's supplied class \cite[Prop.~7.31, Thm.~C.8]{ButlerT5} is contradicted at the pre-ascent level; this would kill that paper's statement, not the claim, and would be reported as such.
\item[K2.4] (intra-fibre only) If every class found acts within the fibre at one point, and no component of the connection pairs the ladder at $x$ with the ladder at $y \neq x$, the cross-point clause of (L$_E$) is untouched and the claim closes only in the intra-fibre sense. Parallel transport along a path identifies the fibre at $x$ with the fibre at $y$, so ``transport, then compare'' is the intra-fibre result along a path; the cross-point object is a generator in $\so(V_{x} \oplus V_{y})$ for the completion's independent ladders, which no connection supplies. This condition bounds the claim and was expected to trigger.
\end{itemize}
Predictions, as registered: the class vanishes along $\partial_t$ and $\partial_r$, is proportional to $\sqrt f/r$ in the transverse directions, vanishes at the horizon and changes sign across it (P2.1); it equals $\ip{\nabla_X\ell}{m}$ (P2.2); the mixed-plane curvature has ``nonzero pairing class in the $n$-$m$ planes and zero in the $\ell$-$m$ planes'', and the radial and angular planes have none (P2.3); in the flat conformal model the classes of a displacement $dx$ are $(\ip{dx}{\ell}, \ip{dx}{m}, 0)$ and vanish only along the ray (P2.4).
__notes__.note.pairing.setting-schwarzschild-exact: The framework's Schwarzschild vacuum is the radial one: the extreme curvature eigenvalue distinguishes the pair of the radial plane and its dual, the sign of the square selects the radial member (Fact \claimref{pairing.imported-schwarzschild-connection-curvature}), the flag bit picks the outgoing or the ingoing null direction in it, and the chirality bit picks $m$. The computations below take $\ell$ outgoing, and Proposition \claimref{pairing.regular-frame-class-vanishes-horizon-changes} records what the ingoing choice gives instead; they are exact in the field $\Q(F)$, $F = \sqrt f$, $r = 2M/(1 - F^{2})$, at $M = \tfrac12$ (the singularity paper's device for keeping every coefficient rational), and in $\Q(\beta)$, $r = 2M/\beta^{2}$, for the regular frame.
__notes__.note.pairing.reading-prior-art: Proposition \claimref{pairing.pairing-class-transverse-derivative-null-direction} is elementary once Proposition \claimref{pairing.stabiliser-parabolic-algebra-null-direction} is in hand, and its content is a dictionary: by Fact \claimref{pairing.imported-spin-coefficients-null-tetrad} the components of the pairing class on the null tetrad are, up to normalisation and sign convention, the spin coefficients $\kappa, \tau, \sigma, \rho$, so the pairing generator of the framework's vacuum is the transverse deformation of the vacuum's null congruence, the optical scalars of Sachs and Newman-Penrose: the vacuum is parallel along its own integral curve if $\ell$ is geodesic ($\kappa = 0$), along $n$ if $\tau = 0$, and along every transverse real direction if the congruence has neither expansion, twist nor shear ($\rho = \sigma = 0$). Under the series' rule this is an import with a framework reading. The reading is this. The stabiliser part of the connection, eight of the twelve spin coefficients, rescales $\ell$, rotates $m$ in its plane and tilts $n$ and $\mb$ by null rotations about $\ell$; it is what the singularity paper's hops, annihilations and Cartan elements do, and it cannot move the vacuum, and so cannot create entanglement from it (off the vacuum a hop does entangle, as that paper's own script exhibits \cite[Rem.~13.5]{ButlerT5}). The pairing part, the other four, tilts $\ell$ and is what the framework had said it did not supply. It supplies it wherever the congruence of its chosen null direction is not parallel.
__notes__.note.pairing.what-horizon-reading: The horizon is where the pairing generator of the outgoing vacuum vanishes in every direction. Along $\ell$ and along $n$ it vanishes at every radius, the congruence being geodesic and $\tau = 0$ throughout Schwarzschild; what singles out the horizon is the transverse class, which vanishes there and nowhere else because the expansion of the horizon generators is zero, a Killing-horizon fact (Fact \claimref{pairing.imported-spin-coefficients-null-tetrad}) that Proposition \claimref{pairing.regular-frame-class-vanishes-horizon-changes} exhibits exactly. In the trapped region the class has the opposite sign: transport tilts the outgoing null direction the other way. None of this uses the ascent; it is the pre-ascent geometry of the null direction the descent selects, and it is where the singularity paper's Step 4d premise is calibrated, at the fixed locus of the boost \cite[Prop.~7.25]{ButlerT5}. The evidence for the horizon statement is the regular-frame computation of Proposition \claimref{pairing.regular-frame-class-vanishes-horizon-changes}, not the static one: the static frame degenerates on the horizon and the rescaling between the two frames vanishes there, so Proposition \claimref{pairing.pairing-class-transverse-derivative-null-direction}'s invariance does not carry the static result across; that the static class $-\sqrt f/r$ also vanishes is consistent, not evidential.
__notes__.note.pairing.setting-machine-verificatio:
Every computational identity asserted in this note has been verified in exact arithmetic by the script \texttt{verify\_T05\_pairing.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT05pairing}, which imports the series' shared library \texttt{GA.py}: its basis-blade Clifford engine over the rationals, its Gaussian rationals for the complex Witt vectors, its rational functions in one variable for the two Schwarzschild frames, and its exact ranks and kernels. Identities in $\Q(F)$ or $\Q(\beta)$ are verified as identities where the text says so, and at rational sample points where the text says so. No floating point is used anywhere; the script exits nonzero on any failure. Fifty-three checks, all passing, in eight parts. On the $(t, r, \vartheta)$ and $(T, r, \vartheta)$ blocks the check covers, the connection forms of both frames are verified against the first structure equations, which with antisymmetry determines them there, the curvature forms are derived from them by the second structure equations, and the block one-forms are tied to the frame matrices that the classes are computed from. The pre-registration is deposited beside the script \cite{ButlerPreregT05pairing}.

\emph{Part A: the stabiliser.} The tetrad's pairings; the action $\tfrac12[e_{a}e_{b}, e_{c}] = \eta_{bc}e_{a} - \eta_{ac}e_{b}$ on all basis bivectors and vectors; the six values of $\pv$ with the two transverse images $e_{02}\cdot\ell = -e_{2}$, $e_{12}\cdot\ell = e_{2}$; the equivalence of $B\cdot W \subseteq W$ with $\pv(B) = 0$ on twenty random complex bivectors, none of which stabilises, with the projection $B + \pv(B)e_{12}$ always stabilising; the null rotations $\ell e_{2}$, $\ell e_{3}$ as bivectors fixing $\ell$; the rank two of $(\operatorname{Re}\pv, \operatorname{Im}\pv)$, the rank four of $\{e_{01}, e_{23}, \ell e_{2}, \ell e_{3}\}$ and the rank five with $e_{02}$ appended; the classes $2$, $2I_{5}$ of $ne_{2}$, $ne_{3}$ (values in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{5}\}$, the complexification of spacetime by the central $I_{5}$ of $\Cl(2,3)$, in which $m = e_{2} + I_{5}e_{3}$) and $0$, $4$ of $n m$, $n\mb$.

\emph{Part B: the Fock dictionary.} The Clifford relations of the four Jordan-Wigner operators; $c(\ell)$, $c(m)$ annihilating the vacuum and $c(n)$, $c(\mb)$ creating; $\bra{12}B\ket{0} = -\pv(B)$ on all six basis bivectors; the $2 \times 2$ structure of the even sector, including $a_{1}a_{2}\ket{12} = -\ket{0}$.

\emph{Part C: the witness.} $R\tilde R = 1$; $R\ket{0} = \tfrac35\ket{0} + \tfrac45\ket{12}$; $R\ell\tilde R$ with its nullity and its pairing $\tfrac{32}{25}$ with $\ell$; the rotated pair annihilating $R\ket{0}$; the boost rotor acting on $\ket{0}$ as $\tfrac13$.

\emph{Part D: the static frame.} $f'$ and $f''$ by differentiation in $\Q(F)$; the first structure equations on the $(t, r, \vartheta)$ block; the second structure equations giving the three curvature two-forms with their coefficients; the bivectors reproducing all sixteen frame derivatives; the block one-forms evaluated on the frame vectors equal to the frame matrices; the four classes; the scaling law with the derivative term $(e_{1}\lambda)\ell$ modelled and nonzero; the horizon zeros and the value $-\tfrac{48}{125}$; the tetrad components $(0, 0, 0, -2\sqrt f/r)$; the transverse expansion, its equality with $-\pv(\Omega(\mb))$, and $\nabla_{\ell}\ell = (f'/2\sqrt f)\ell$; $\Omega(e_{0}) \propto e_{01}$ and $\Omega(e_{1}) = 0$.

\emph{Part E: curvature.} The two eigenvalues from the derived block forms (the angular one is entered); the six classes; the null rotation $(M/r^{3})\ell e_{2}$ for the loop $(\ell, e_{2})$, the class $2M/r^{3}$ for $(n, e_{2})$, and the six complex loops, $(n, \mb)$ alone carrying $4M/r^{3}$; the Weyl dictionary: Ricci-flatness on all sixteen frame pairs, $\Psi_{0} = \Psi_{1} = 0$, $\Psi_{2} = -4M/r^{3}$, and the six loop classes equal to $(\Psi_{0}, 0, -\Psi_{1}, \Psi_{1}, 0, -\Psi_{2})$, in the adapted tetrad and again in a generic rational tetrad where $\Psi_{0}$ and $\Psi_{1}$ are nonzero.

\emph{Part F: the regular frame.} The first and second structure equations on the $(T, r, \vartheta)$ block as identities in $\Q(\beta)$, with $\beta' = -\beta^{3}/4M$ and the curvature coefficients equal to the static ones as functions of $r$; the bivectors against the frame derivatives; the block one-forms against the frame matrices; the four classes; the values $-\tfrac{16}{125}, 0, 4$ at $\beta = \tfrac45, 1, 2$; the ingoing vacuum's classes $+(1 + \beta)/r$ with the values $\tfrac{144}{125}, 2, 12$; the covariance factor $F/(1 + \beta)$ at five rational points of the circle; $\Omega(e_{0}) = 0$ and $\Omega(e_{1}) \propto e_{01}$; the transverse expansion $2(1 - \beta)/r$ with its sign on both sides and $\nabla_{\ell}\ell = (\beta^{3}/4M)\ell$; the $(n, e_{2})$ curvature class $2M/r^{3}$ in this frame, equal to the static value at three radii and to $1$ on the horizon.

\emph{Part G: gap 1.} $\Lambda^{\mathsf T}\eta\Lambda = \eta$, the images $\tfrac{F}{1 + \beta}\ell$ and $e_{2}$, and the identity on the circle at three rational points; the two Hawking states as vacua of rotated decompositions with the two distinct rational null directions.

\emph{Part H: the flat model.} $\nz$, $\ninf$; isotropy and rank of $W(x)$ at four points; the translation identity, the fixing of $\ninf$, the action on $\ell(x)$, and the second-order remainder of a finite displacement; the classes $(\ip{dx}{\ell}, \ip{dx}{m}, 0)$ at four points for twenty random real displacements; the four named real displacements and the complex $m$, $\mb$; incidence at three values of $s$; the rank three of the three functionals on the fifteen bivectors, their common kernel of dimension twelve, and its coincidence with the stabiliser on ten random kernel elements and on every basis bivector.

What the script does not check: the geometric identifications imported as Facts \claimref{pairing.imported-null-flags}, \claimref{pairing.imported-spin-coefficients-null-tetrad}, \claimref{pairing.imported-flat-conformal-model-twistor-incidence} and \claimref{pairing.imported-weyl-scalars-petrov-type-schwarzschild} (the note computes components and matches them to named quantities; it does not re-derive the formalisms), Lemma \claimref{pairing.loop-classes-are-weyl-components} beyond its Schwarzschild instance; the angular-plane curvature coefficient $(1 - f)/r^{2}$, which lies off the $(t, r, \vartheta)$ block and is taken from the singularity paper's verified appendix; and the $\hat3$ forms of both frames beyond the mirror symmetry, the $e_{23}$ term being in the stabiliser by Part A.
__notes__.note.singularity.abstract: In gauge theory gravity the Schwarzschild solution is carried by an invertibility-demanding linear map, and the singularity is where the theory divides by zero. The series' transport algorithm is run on that division. The gauge field is a unipotent ray at every radius, so the divergence lies in the connection bivector; at the centre the light cones fold onto a null direction, a type-N obstruction whose forced repair is the Witt completion $\Cl(1,3) \to \Cl(2,4)$. No classical value repairs the dying directions, by two no-go theorems; the completion installs canonical anticommutation relations, one fermionic mode per boundary point, and the curvature factorises exactly into $-M/r^3$ times a fixed shape operator, selecting the boost plane. Descent to the metric level is, mode by mode, the fermion parity average, so every physical state has thermal single-mode marginals, and one named premise, KMS at the Euclidean section's period, sets their temperature at Hawking's and leaves the joint state free. Bosonisation at s-wave scope gives the Planck sector from a named quasi-freeness premise. The descent's multi-mode cost is a relative entropy carried by inter-quanta correlations: on the pointwise-descent reading, information is lost in $\Cl(1,3)$ and preserved in $\Cl(2,4)$, a category error between levels. In a rate model with boundary-mode locality the radiation entropy is exactly the window's thermal content, giving the Page envelope without typicality. Inside, the modular flow is the $t$-line holonomy of the collar, at Hubble-normalised rate $1/3$; the premised locality's pairing part is the tangent of the vacuum orbit.
__notes__.note.singularity.setting-prior-art: The physics targets are classical: Hawking's flux and temperature \cite{Hawking1975}; Israel's thermofield-double reading of the eternal black hole \cite{Israel1976}; the identification of modular flow with the boost for wedge and horizon algebras by Bisognano-Wichmann and Sewell \cite{BW1976, Sewell1982}; Page's curve and typicality theorem \cite{Page1993}; the quantum-extremal-surface derivations of the Page curve \cite{Penington2020, AEMM2019}; the Hayden-Preskill mirror \cite{HP2007}; the interior-volume growth \cite{CR2015}. The algebraic inputs are this series': the no-go and minimal completion, the taxonomy, the pinching and one-way theorems, and the transport algorithm this paper instantiates, from T1 \cite{ButlerT1}; the tower and CAR limit, from T3 \cite{ButlerT3}; and the localisation of the ladder on the degenerate locus, from T4 \cite{ButlerT4}. GTG is \cite{LDG1998, DoranLasenby2003}; bosonisation and the boson-fermion correspondence are \cite{PressleySegal1986}, met from the physics side by the near-horizon two-dimensional reduction \cite{RW2005}; twistors are \cite{Penrose1967}. Klein's inequality, the single classical input of the deficit theorem, is standard \cite{NielsenChuang}. This paper is the chain's self-contained form, with the statuses argued inline, the imports replaced by citations to the series' proved papers, and the finite-mode model new.
__notes__.note.singularity.setting-step-1-locate-f: Conventions: spacetime algebra $\Cl(1,3)$ with $\gamma_0^2 = +1$, $\gamma_i^2 = -1$; in the $(t,r)$ plane write $\et := \gamma_0$, $\er := \gamma_1$, so $\et^2 = 1$, $\er^2 = -1$, $\et \cdot \er = 0$. Units $G = c = \hbar = 1$; the Einstein coupling in the field equations is written $8\pi$, the symbol $\kappa$ being reserved throughout for the surface gravity of Step 4b.
__notes__.note.singularity.setting-schwarzschild-c: This appendix computes the curvature spectrum and the surface gravity in the metric picture, by the Cartan structure equations in the static chart, where the computation is shortest. It plays two roles. It supplies the mixed- and angular-plane eigenvalues that the abelian radial computation of Proposition \claimref{singularity.solution-where-divergence-lies}(1) does not reach, completing the input to Theorem \claimref{singularity.curvature-gauge-field-exact-shape-decoupling}; and it is the independent cross-check, in a second formalism, of the gauge-theoretic the section “Step 1: locate the failure”: on the invertible region the two pictures agree by Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-equivalence-einstein-equations}, so any disagreement anywhere would falsify one of them. The computations are classical differential geometry, included in full per the series' standard of proof; the verification script checks every derivative identity and eigenvalue exactly, with $f$ handled as a rational function.

correspondence.imported-vacuum-equations.technical:
Where the position-gauge field $\hb$ is invertible, the vacuum field equations are exactly equivalent to $D^{T} I_g = 0$ for the scale tractor of the physical scale (null exactly when $\Lambda = 0$), $D^{T}$ being the tractor connection, which on flat spacetime is the $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field built from $\Omega$, the frame and the Schouten map. The scale tractor of a scale $g$ is $I_g = (1, 0, \rho_g) = \nInf + \rho_g\nO$ in the splitting of that scale, with $\rho_g$ fixed by the scalar curvature of $g$.

For an Einstein field with $\mathrm{Ric} = \Lambda g$ the scale tractor is parallel with $Q(I_g) = \Lambda/3$; conversely a parallel section of the form $(1, 0, \rho)$ forces $\rho$ constant and $g$ Einstein with $\Lambda = 6\rho$. The entry restates the series' covariant vacuum theorem and its cosmological-constant companion.
correspondence.imported-vacuum-equations.lay: Einstein's vacuum equations can be rewritten as the statement that one vector of the six-dimensional conformal model, attached to the choice of scale, does not change as the gravitational gauge fields carry it across flat spacetime. With a cosmological constant the same holds, and the squared length of that vector is a third of the constant. This entry restates both results from earlier in the series.

correspondence.imported-weyl-commutes-du.formal: For a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), at every point of its invertible region the Weyl map $\mathcal{W}$, the trace-free part of the curvature operator $\mathcal{R}$ on physical bivectors, commutes with duality: $\mathcal{W}(IB) = I\,\mathcal{W}(B)$ for every bivector $B$, where $I$ is the pseudoscalar of $\Cl(1,3)$ and multiplication by $I$ is, up to the sign convention of the star, the Hodge star on the two-forms of the derived metric. The statement is pointwise; equivalently, on an oriented Lorentzian $4$-manifold the Weyl curvature operator on $2$-forms commutes with the Hodge star. \emph{Provenance:} classical $4$-dimensional curvature decomposition; \cite{PenroseRindler86}.
correspondence.imported-weyl-commutes-du.technical: For a gravitational field on flat spacetime, let $\mathcal{W}$ be the Weyl part of its field strength, a linear map on bivectors, and let duality be multiplication by the pseudoscalar $I$, which is the Hodge star of the derived metric up to its sign convention. Then $\mathcal{W}(IB) = I\,\mathcal{W}(B)$ at every point where $\hb$ is invertible: in curved-spacetime language, on an oriented Lorentzian four-manifold the Weyl operator on two-forms commutes with the Hodge star, $\mathcal{W}\star = \star\mathcal{W}$. This is part of the classical decomposition of curvature in four dimensions, imported from Penrose and Rindler.
correspondence.imported-weyl-commutes-du.lay: In four dimensions, the part of the gravitational field strength responsible for tidal forces and gravitational waves respects a natural symmetry that exchanges electric-type and magnetic-type components. This is a standard result of relativity, imported here.

correspondence.imported-weyls-theorem.formal: A pseudo-Riemannian metric in dimension at least four is locally conformally flat if and only if its Weyl tensor vanishes. In Gauge Theory Gravity (the $d$-dimensional clause of Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}, $d \geq 4$): for a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat $\R^{p,q}$, its derived metric is locally conformally flat, that is, about each point of the invertible region there is a gauge in which $\hb^{-1}(a) = e^{\omega}a$ for a scalar function $\omega$, if and only if its Weyl curvature $\mathcal{W}(a \wedge b) = \mathcal{R}(a \wedge b) - \Sch(a) \wedge b - a \wedge \Sch(b)$ vanishes. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{Weyl1918}.
correspondence.imported-weyls-theorem.technical: For a pseudo-Riemannian metric $g$ in dimension $n \geq 4$: $g$ is locally conformally flat, that is locally of the form $e^{2\omega}\eta$ with $\eta$ flat, if and only if its Weyl tensor vanishes. For a gravitational field on flat $\R^{p,q}$ this says: locally there is a gauge with $\hb^{-1}(a) = e^{\omega}a$, a pure rescaling of the flat background, exactly when the trace-free part $\mathcal{W}$ of the field strength vanishes. Imported from Weyl (1918).
correspondence.imported-weyls-theorem.lay: In four or more dimensions, a gravitational field on flat spacetime amounts locally to nothing more than a change of scale exactly when one particular part of its strength, the Weyl curvature, is zero. This classical result is imported.

imported_from.citation: H. Weyl, Reine Infinitesimalgeometrie, Math. Z. 2 (1918), 384--411.
