synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise.formal:
\emph{Premise (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$).} Units $\hbar = c = 1$. Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), $p$ any point of its invertible region and $\ell$ any future physically null direction at $p$; let $\mathcal{H}_{p,\ell}$ be the local Rindler horizon through $p$ generated by $\ell$ (the null boundary of the past of a small spacelike two-surface element through $p$ orthogonal to $\ell$, with vanishing expansion and shear at $p$; in a normal gauge at $p$, $\hb(p) = 1$ and $\Omega(p) = 0$, it is at leading order a piece of the null hyperplane through $p$ orthogonal to $\ell$), with approximate boost flow of acceleration $a$. Everything is to leading order in the size of the patch, the order at which the boost flow is defined when the field strength $\mathcal{R}$ is nonzero. The patch's modes are the field on its generators' light rays: the continuum mode space of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}, one carrier per light ray, identified with the matter field on those light rays (the horizon modes and the matter crossing the patch are one field). Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(Loc)] \emph{(Entropy, integrated reading.)} The entropy of a cut $\Sigma$ of the patch's horizon is a functional of the cut, $S[\Sigma] = \int_{\Sigma}\eta\,dA$, where the density $\eta$ depends only on the patch's flat tangent data at each point (the null ray and the edge plane: a physical null vector up to scale and a physical bivector, compared with the flat product), and not on the curvature (the field strength $\mathcal{R}$), the matter stress tensor or the boost normalisation there. Horizon entropy contains no Euler (Jacobson-Myers) term, on local and on closed horizons alike; the Euler term stays in the action. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-entropy-clause-curvature-independent-density}(i) such a density is one universal constant, so $\delta S = \eta\,\delta A$; calibrated on the Schwarzschild family under the series' temperature premises it is $\eta = 1/4$ in Planck units, with no mode count (part (ii) there).
\item[(R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$)] \emph{(Temperature, before the crossing.)} Before matter crosses the patch, the state of the patch's modes on the past half of each generator (the half ending on the edge) is jointly KMS for the local boost future-directed there at rapidity period $2\pi$, on the patch's whole mode algebra. It is a condition on the state before the crossing: after a crossing with heat $\delta Q \neq 0$ the state departs from it at the order of the heat (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.clausius-is-window-first-law-plus-boost-charge-conservation}(2)). In Minkowski space (a vanishing field strength) this continuum form follows from Premise \claimref{synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state} (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(iii), case (c)), with the positivity of the null translations derived there from a nonnegative conformal energy (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-conformal-energy-gives-positive-null-translations}); for a gravitational field of nonzero field strength it follows from the local form of (N$_{+}$), argued at leading order. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.local-boost-temperature-is-local-regularity} the rapidity period $2\pi$ gives $T = a/2\pi$ in the proper time of the boost observers at leading order, the period at which the local boost's Euclidean section is regular.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Note (the Euler exclusion in normalisation form).} The exclusion of the Euler term in (Loc) has an equivalent normalisation form. With the geodesic-curvature edge term of a patch (the two-dimensional Gibbons-Hawking term), the Euler part of the Wald entropy of the series' action on every patch $P$ of a cut is the topological constant $2\pi\alpha\chi(P)$, $\alpha = -3/(4\Lambda)$, so it changes no entropy difference along a local horizon, and excluding it is the normalisation (Z) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.sds-clausius-fixes-area-constant} (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.euler-entropy-of-a-horizon-patch-is-an-edge-term}). The adopted reading is that horizon entropy is the entropy of (Loc), not the action's Wald entropy. This note records a reading of the clause; what the premise asserts is unchanged.

\emph{Note (status of the two clauses on the joint set with the gravitational action).} Suppose, besides this premise and the Clausius relation, that the field equations are those of the store's gravitational action on the field space, with one normalisation $G$ for every admissible field and $\Lambda \neq 0$, taken as a stated hypothesis. Then at a point where matter crosses (the stress is not a multiple of the metric) the Clausius relation at rapidity period $2\pi c$ holds on every patch exactly when $\eta = c/(4G)$, Jacobson's identification read with $G$ given by the action, and on matter-free regions it holds for every $\eta$ and $c$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.clausius-on-the-action-shell-ties-entropy-density-to-period}). So on that joint set, with the calibration $\eta = \tfrac14$ at the action's $G$ ($G = 1$ in the same units) taken as an independent input, the one-coupling clause of (Loc) and the period $2\pi$ of (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) imply each other where matter crosses (the direction from the period to the one coupling, $\eta = 1/(4G)$ on every field that carries matter, does not need the calibration), and the Clausius relation is then a constraint on the thermal data, not a derivation of the field equations, which the action supplies. This note records the status of the clauses on that joint set; the action is not a premise of (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$), and what the premise asserts is unchanged.

\emph{One mode set, per light ray.} On a hole's horizon the modes on each light ray and the modes premises (C1) and (C2) place at the curvature cutoff are one set described twice (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-is-a-second-placement-of-the-count}: independent placements would double the entropy, $G_{\mathrm{cl}} = 2G$, under the total-entropy reading). The counted windows of the cutoff placement, and the point-spectrum mode sets on which the series' thermal premises are worded, are discretisations of the per-light-ray carrier, recovered only for modes of vanishing Mellin width (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(iv)). The point-spectrum wording could not carry this clause: with a phase-acting flow the two local horizons of one edge admit (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) on modes they share only at zero weight (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.r-loc-needs-sheet-labelled-modes}), and (R) at the cutoff placement and (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) at the collar's points ask one mode set for different periods (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.collar-temperature-fixed-locally-by-r-loc}); on the per-light-ray carrier the past halves of the two sheets of an edge are different null half-planes and the edge is a null set carrying no mode. The cutoff premises (C1), (C2) and (IC) are read as a Schwarzschild calibration only: away from Schwarzschild the horizon placement with the flat-data density of (Loc) governs, since read with a horizon's modular period on a Schwarzschild-de Sitter hole the literal cutoff count is not a curvature-independent entropy per unit area (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cutoff-count-is-not-a-local-density-on-sds}).

\emph{Status of the clauses.} (Loc) is not derived on either reading of the entropy. On the differences reading of version 2 it is independent of the Clausius relation, of (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) and of every $\Lambda$-vacuum horizon datum of the store (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.loc-independent-of-clausius-and-killing-data}). On the integrated reading adopted here the Clausius relation on open patches forces $\eta$ to be constant along each gravitational field (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}(6)), and within the series' entropy family it admits the Euler term only where the field strength at the point is of constant-curvature type, $\mathcal{R}(B)$ a multiple of $B$, and forces the curvature-independent density (Theorems \claimref{synthesis.euler-entropy-first-order-rate-on-local-patches} and \claimref{synthesis.series-wald-entropy-changes-without-flux-on-local-horizons}); a density built from scalars of the field strength that is constant on each admissible gravitational field still escapes, and its failures are confined to fields with no calibrated vacuum point (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.loc-independent-of-clausius-and-killing-data}). The continuum form of (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) follows from (N$_{+}$) in Minkowski space and is argued for nonzero field strength; without (N$_{+}$), (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) with modes labelled by null direction is independent of the store's other premises, and what it fixes off Killing horizons is the matter coupling (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.r-loc-independent-sets-matter-coupling}).

\emph{What it delivers.} With the Clausius relation for the boost-energy flux of matter, a separate hypothesis and not a clause of this premise, and the geometric hypotheses stated there, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius} proves Einstein's equations, the field equations $\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a = -8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}\,T(a)$ of the gravitational field in the store's sign, with $\Lambda$ an integration constant and $G_{\mathrm{cl}} = 1/(4\eta)$ (Jacobson's argument, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-jacobson-clausius-1995}). With $\eta = 1/4$ from the Schwarzschild calibration this gives $G_{\mathrm{cl}} = G$, a consistency and not a determination of $G$, since the calibration contains $G$. What selects Einstein's equations over their Ricci-polynomial extensions on this route is the curvature-independence in (Loc), not locality. Toward the Clausius relation itself: with the horizon modes and the crossing matter one field on the light rays, the conservation of the patch's boost charge is an identity, and given Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-null-plane-modular-hamiltonian-first-law} the first law of the modes in the state of (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) holds on the continuum for entropy differences, so the Clausius relation at first order follows once the entropy change is read through (Loc), under the hypotheses of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.clausius-is-window-first-law-plus-boost-charge-conservation}.

\emph{Not part of this premise.} Two readings of version 1 are recorded as what Jacobson's 2016 small-diamond route (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-jacobson-entanglement-equilibrium-2016}) would additionally need: the mode-count reading of the entropy, $\eta = 4\pi\nu\langle s\rangle$ at the epoch density of Theorem \claimref{scrambling.epoch-modular-period-two-unknowns-become}, and the geometric reading of the modular flow on nested sub-patches, which contradicts a point-spectrum mode set (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-modular-clause-moves-no-nested-patch}) and is not established on the continuum carrier. Version 1 stated the premise as three clauses, (i) count, (ii) temperature, (iii) modular flow, on local Rindler horizons and small diamonds; version 2 read the entropy as differences only and posed (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) on the point-spectrum windows; the results that analyse those versions refer to them.

\emph{Refutation condition.} The premise is false if any of the following is established: (a) a result showing that the entropy of the cuts of some class of local horizons is not a universal constant times the area at leading order, for example that its density depends on the acceleration, on the matter crossing the patch or on the field strength at the point, or that horizon entropy carries an Euler term; the literal counts of the cutoff placement for spinning holes (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kerr-ring-count-misses-area-law}) and on Schwarzschild-de Sitter holes (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cutoff-count-is-not-a-local-density-on-sds}) are counts on the cutoff placement read away from Schwarzschild, in conflict with the horizon area law, and count against that placement, not against (Loc); (b) a result showing that no state of the patch's per-light-ray modes is jointly KMS for the local boost at rapidity period $2\pi$ at leading order before matter crosses; (c) a confirmed departure from Einstein's equations with a cosmological constant in a regime where local horizons are defined, since the premise with the Clausius relation gives those equations and nothing else (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.black-hole-data-do-not-fix-field-equations} shows the Killing-horizon data alone cannot exclude Ricci-polynomial corrections, and the curvature-independence in (Loc) is what does).
synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise.technical:
The series places its boundary modes, their temperature and their entropy on Killing horizons: the Schwarzschild horizon and the de Sitter cosmological horizon. This premise extends them to local Rindler horizons through every point, at leading order in the patch size, in the two forms Jacobson's 1995 argument uses, with the modes taken as the field running along each light ray of the patch and identified with the matter field there. (Loc): the entropy of a cut of the horizon is the integral of a density $\eta$ that depends only on the flat tangent data and not on the field strength (curvature) or matter; such a density is one universal constant, fixed at $1/4$ by the Schwarzschild calibration without counting modes, and horizon entropy carries no Euler term (that term stays in the action); equivalently, since with the patch's edge term the Euler part adds only a topological constant per patch, excluding it is a normalisation, and horizon entropy is read as the entropy of (Loc), not the action's Wald entropy. If the store's gravitational action with one coupling $G$ and $\Lambda \neq 0$ is also in force, the Clausius relation where matter crosses reduces to $\eta = c/(4G)$ at period $2\pi c$, so, given the calibration $\eta = \tfrac14$ at the action's $G$, the one-coupling part of (Loc) and the period of (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) imply each other there and the Clausius relation becomes a constraint on the thermal data rather than a derivation of the field equations (a status note; the premise is unchanged). (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$): before matter crosses, the modes on the light rays ending on the edge are jointly thermal for the local boost at rapidity period $2\pi$, which gives the temperature $a/2\pi$. In Minkowski space this follows from the null ground-state premise (N$_{+}$), which has no temperature in it; for a nonzero gravitational field strength it follows from that premise's local form, argued at leading order.

The modes on a hole's horizon and the cutoff modes are one set, now per light ray; the counted windows are discretisations of it. On point-spectrum windows the temperature clause could not stand (the two sheets of an edge would share modes only at zero weight, and the cutoff and collar placements would ask one mode set for two periods), and the continuum carrier removes both conflicts. The cutoff premises are a Schwarzschild calibration only, since on a Schwarzschild-de Sitter hole the literal cutoff count is not a local area density. (Loc) is not derived on either reading of the entropy: on the differences reading an explicit model shows it independent; on the integrated reading Clausius forces the density to be constant on each gravitational field and, within the series' family, excludes the Euler term, but a density constant on each field and varying between fields with no calibrated vacuum point still escapes.

With the Clausius relation for matter's boost energy, kept as a separate hypothesis, the store proves Einstein's equations from this premise, with $\Lambda$ an integration constant and $G_{\mathrm{cl}} = 1/(4\eta)$; $G_{\mathrm{cl}} = G$ is a consistency check, since the calibration of $\eta$ contains $G$. With the horizon modes and the matter one field, the boost-charge conservation behind Clausius is an identity, and given an imported fact on null-plane modular Hamiltonians the first law of the modes gives the Clausius relation at first order once the entropy change is read through (Loc). It is a Tier C premise, refuted by an entropy density on local horizons that depends on the field strength, matter or acceleration or carries an Euler term, by the absence of a jointly thermal state for the local boost before matter crosses, or by an observed departure from Einstein's equations where local horizons make sense. The literal Kerr and Schwarzschild-de Sitter counts are not refutations: they count against the cutoff placement away from Schwarzschild.
synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise.lay: The series computes a temperature and an entropy for the edges of black holes and of the universe's horizon, using quantum modes it places on those edges. Jacobson showed in 1995 that Einstein's equations of gravity follow if every small piece of horizon around every point, including the horizon seen by an accelerating observer, has a temperature set by the acceleration and an entropy proportional to its area, by the same amount everywhere. This assumption says exactly that, with the quantum modes running continuously along the light rays of each small horizon and being the same field as the matter that falls through it. It has two parts: the entropy of a slice of the horizon is its area times a fixed number that does not depend on how strong the gravitational field is there, and before matter falls through, the modes are thermal at the accelerating observer's temperature. Where there is no gravitational field the second part now follows from a simpler assumption with no temperature in it; the first part is still assumed. With it, the store proves Einstein's equations, with the strength of gravity set by the entropy per area and the cosmological constant left free. The assumption would fail if the entropy per area turned out to depend on the strength of the gravitational field or on matter, or if gravity were found to deviate from Einstein's equations.

synthesis.c-loc-modular-clause-moves-no-.formal:
Let $\mathfrak{A}$ be the boundary-mode algebra of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics}, the CAR algebra over a countable mode set with window algebras $\mathfrak{A}_{F}$, and let $(\tau_{t})_{t \in \R}$ be any one-parameter group of $*$-automorphisms that multiplies each generating mode by a phase, $\tau_{t}(a_{j}) = e^{-J\omega_{j}t}a_{j}$ with real $\omega_{j}$, as the Definition's boost dynamics does. Numbers on $\mathfrak{A}$ and on its GNS spaces are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$, $J = e_{2}e_{3}$ the complex unit of the radial atom from which the boundary modes descend, which commutes with the mode operators (\claimref{synthesis.transverse-bivector-is-the-complex-unit-of-the-radial-atom}).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Recurrence.)} Every $x \in \mathfrak{A}$ has a relatively compact $\tau$-orbit, and for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and $S > 0$ there are $T \ge S$ and $T' \le -S$ with $\|\tau_{T}(x) - x\| < \varepsilon$ and $\|\tau_{T'}(x) - x\| < \varepsilon$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(No proper semigroup invariance.)} If $\mathcal{B} \subseteq \mathfrak{A}$ is a norm-closed subspace with $\tau_{t}(\mathcal{B}) \subseteq \mathcal{B}$ for all $t \ge 0$, or for all $t \le 0$, then $\tau_{t}(\mathcal{B}) = \mathcal{B}$ for every $t \in \R$. The same holds in the GNS representation $(\mathcal{H}, \pi, \Omega)$ of any $\tau$-invariant state, with $V_{t}$ the unitaries implementing $\tau$: $V_{t}$ has pure point spectrum, and every $\sigma$-weakly closed subspace $\mathcal{B}$ of $\pi(\mathfrak{A})''$ with $V_{t}\mathcal{B}V_{t}^{*} \subseteq \mathcal{B}$ for all $t$ of one sign satisfies $V_{t}\mathcal{B}V_{t}^{*} = \mathcal{B}$ for all $t$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Consequence for the local-horizon premise.)} Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a local Rindler horizon carrying $\mathfrak{A}$ as clause (i) of version 1 of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise} asserts (clauses (i), (ii), (iii) below are those of version 1: count, temperature, modular flow; the current version keeps the temperature clause as (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) and records the other two under ``Not part of this premise''), with affine parameter $\lambda$ on its generators and bifurcation cut at $\lambda = 0$, and let $\mathcal{N}_{c} = \{\lambda > c\}$, $c > 0$. Assume (P): the local boost acts on the patch's modes as the Definition's boost dynamics, so that the modular flow, which clause (iii) identifies with the local boost, is $\tau$ up to a nonzero rescaling of its parameter (clause (i) cites the algebra; that its phase dynamics is the local boost is this hypothesis). Consider the geometric reading (G) of clause (iii): the modes on $\mathcal{N}_{c}$ generate C$^{*}$-subalgebras $\mathfrak{A}_{c} \subseteq \mathfrak{A}$ (or von Neumann subalgebras of $\pi(\mathfrak{A})''$ in the GNS representation of the selected state) with $\mathfrak{A}_{c} \subseteq \mathfrak{A}_{c'}$ for $c \ge c'$, and the modular flow carries $\mathfrak{A}_{c}$ onto $\mathfrak{A}_{e^{\mp 2\pi s}c}$ at modular parameter $s$, the way the boost moves $\mathcal{N}_{c}$. Then, under (P), $\mathfrak{A}_{c} = \mathfrak{A}_{c'}$ for all $c, c' > 0$. So (G) with properly nested sub-patch algebras contradicts clause (i) as worded, given (P); the same holds for nested diamonds sharing a tip, moved monotonically by the conformal Killing flow of the larger one.
\end{enumerate}
Hence, given (P), clause (iii) is consistent with clause (i) only as a statement about the boost dynamics acting on the patch's mode algebra as a whole, which is how the flow acts at a Killing horizon, where the modes sit on the fixed locus of the boost; for a faithful state this is the KMS condition of clause (ii) restated (on windows, part (ii) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.local-boost-temperature-is-local-regularity}). The geometric reading, the one the Bisognano-Wichmann and Hislop-Longo flows realise for a quantum field and the one the small-diamond route uses, needs a mode space on which the boost has continuous spectrum, such as Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}, which clause (i) does not cite.
synthesis.c-loc-modular-clause-moves-no-.technical: Clause (i) of the local-horizon premise puts on every local horizon the series' boundary-mode algebra, on which the boost multiplies each mode by a phase. Such a flow is almost periodic: every orbit is relatively compact, so every element returns arbitrarily close to itself at arbitrarily late and early times. It follows that a closed subspace mapped into itself by the flow for all positive times (or all negative times) is mapped onto itself for all times: the flow cannot push a subalgebra properly inside itself. The same holds for weakly closed subalgebras in the GNS representation of any boost-invariant state, since the implementing unitaries have pure point spectrum and generate a compact group, in which a closed semigroup is a group. A boost acting geometrically does exactly that to the algebras of the future parts of the generators, $\lambda > c$, which it carries to $\lambda > e^{\mp 2\pi s}c$; this is the half-sided structure behind the Bisognano-Wichmann and Hislop-Longo theorems, and the stored no-go on half-sided translations is its translation-side counterpart. So, if the local boost acts on the patch's modes as the cited boost dynamics, clause (iii) cannot mean that the modular flow moves nested sub-patch algebras, unless those algebras all coincide. Read as the boost dynamics acting on the patch's algebra as a whole, as at a Killing horizon where the modes sit on the fixed locus, clause (iii) is consistent, and for a faithful state it says no more than the KMS condition of clause (ii). The exact checks illustrate the theorem and do not test (ii) or (iii), which are proved in the proof text: they verify the canonical anticommutation relations and the phase action on a two-mode window with the non-periodic phase $(3 + 4J)/5$ (numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$, $J = e_{2}e_{3}$ the boundary modes' complex unit), that this phase is no root of unity up to order $200$ while returning within $10^{-3}$ of $1$ (squared distance) at order $61$, and, in contrast, that the bilateral shift never returns and maps its half-space properly into itself.
synthesis.c-loc-modular-clause-moves-no-.lay: The new assumption needed for Einstein's equations has three parts: small horizons carry the series' quantum modes, those modes are at the right temperature, and their natural time flow is the geometric flow of the horizon. This result shows that the third part can only be meant in a weak sense. The series' modes evolve by simple rotations of phases, and such an evolution always comes back close to where it started. A genuinely geometric flow would instead push the modes of a smaller piece of horizon ever deeper into a larger piece, never returning. The two cannot both hold. So the third part must be read as a statement about the modes of the whole patch, where it adds nothing beyond the temperature part; the stronger geometric reading would need a continuous family of modes, which the assumption does not name.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i)} Each window $\mathfrak{A}_{F}$ is finite-dimensional and $\tau$-invariant, and on it $\tau_{t}$ acts through the phases $e^{-J\omega_{j}t}$, $j \in F$, so the orbit of any $x \in \mathfrak{A}_{F}$ is the continuous image of a subset of a compact torus and is relatively compact (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.point-spectrum-boost-admits-no-half-sided-translations}(i)). The union of the windows is dense in $\mathfrak{A}$ (Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics}: $\mathfrak{A}$ is their C$^{*}$-inductive limit). Given $x \in \mathfrak{A}$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, pick $x'$ in a window with $\|x - x'\| < \varepsilon/3$; since every $\tau_{t}$ is isometric, $\|\tau_{t}(x) - \tau_{t}(x')\| < \varepsilon/3$ for all $t$, and finitely many balls of radius $\varepsilon/3$ cover the orbit of $x'$, so finitely many balls of radius $\varepsilon$ cover the orbit of $x$. The orbit is totally bounded, hence relatively compact in the Banach space $\mathfrak{A}$. For recurrence, fix $S > 0$ and consider $\tau_{nS}(x)$, $n = 1, 2, \dots$; they lie in a compact set, so two of them, $n < m$, satisfy $\|\tau_{mS}(x) - \tau_{nS}(x)\| < \varepsilon$, and applying the isometry $\tau_{-nS}$ gives $\|\tau_{(m - n)S}(x) - x\| < \varepsilon$ with $T = (m - n)S \ge S$. The points $\tau_{-nS}(x)$ give $T' \le -S$ in the same way.

\emph{(ii)} Suppose $\tau_{t}(\mathcal{B}) \subseteq \mathcal{B}$ for $t \ge 0$. Let $x \in \mathcal{B}$, $s > 0$ and $y = \tau_{-s}(x)$. For $\varepsilon > 0$, (i) gives $T \ge s$ with $\|\tau_{T}(y) - y\| < \varepsilon$, and $\tau_{T}(y) = \tau_{T - s}(x) \in \mathcal{B}$ because $T - s \ge 0$. So $y$ lies within $\varepsilon$ of $\mathcal{B}$ for every $\varepsilon$, and $y \in \mathcal{B}$ since $\mathcal{B}$ is closed. Thus $\tau_{-s}(\mathcal{B}) \subseteq \mathcal{B}$ for all $s > 0$, so $\tau_{t}(\mathcal{B}) \subseteq \mathcal{B}$ for every real $t$, and applying this to $t$ and $-t$ gives $\tau_{t}(\mathcal{B}) = \mathcal{B}$. The case $t \le 0$ is the same with $T' \le -s$. \emph{The GNS version.} Let $\omega$ be $\tau$-invariant with GNS triple $(\mathcal{H}, \pi, \Omega)$ and $V_{t}\pi(x)\Omega = \pi(\tau_{t}(x))\Omega$. Each $\pi(\mathfrak{A}_{F})\Omega$ is a finite-dimensional $V$-invariant subspace, and their union is dense, so $\mathcal{H}$ is spanned by eigenvectors of $V$: $V_{t} = \sum_{\mu}e^{-J\mu t}P_{\mu}$ with $\sum_{\mu}P_{\mu} = 1$, pure point spectrum. On unitaries of this form the strong topology is the product topology on the phases $(e^{-J\mu t})_{\mu}$, so the strong closure $K$ of $\{V_{t}\}$ is a closed subgroup of a product of circles, a compact abelian group. The strong closure of $\{V_{t} : t \ge 0\}$ is a closed subsemigroup of $K$, and a closed subsemigroup of a compact group is a subgroup; so for $s > 0$ there is a net $t_{\alpha} \ge 0$ with $V_{t_{\alpha}} \to V_{-s}$ strongly, hence strongly with adjoints (inversion is continuous on the unitary group in the strong topology). For $x \in \mathcal{B}$, $V_{t_{\alpha}}xV_{t_{\alpha}}^{*} \in \mathcal{B}$ is a bounded net converging strongly to $V_{-s}xV_{-s}^{*}$; on bounded sets the weak and $\sigma$-weak topologies agree, and a $\sigma$-weakly closed subspace meets every ball in a weakly closed set (Krein-Smulian; this and the subsemigroup fact are standard, cited from memory), so the limit lies in $\mathcal{B}$. The rest is as above.

\emph{(iii)} Under (G) and (P) the modular group is $\sigma_{s} = \tau_{\gamma s}$ for some real $\gamma \ne 0$ (clause (i) supplies the algebra and its boost dynamics $\tau$, (P) says that $\tau$ is how the local boost acts on the patch's modes, clause (iii) identifies the modular flow with that boost; the rescaling of the parameter, fixed in clause (ii) by the temperature, does not matter here; in the GNS form $\Delta^{Js} = V_{\gamma s}$ and the GNS version of (ii) is used), and $\sigma_{s}(\mathfrak{A}_{c}) = \mathfrak{A}_{e^{\mp 2\pi s}c}$. Take the sign so that this is $\mathfrak{A}_{e^{-2\pi s}c}$ (the other is the same argument with $s$ replaced by $-s$). For $s \le 0$, $e^{-2\pi s}c \ge c$, so $\sigma_{s}(\mathfrak{A}_{c}) = \mathfrak{A}_{e^{-2\pi s}c} \subseteq \mathfrak{A}_{c}$ by the nesting. So $\mathcal{B} = \mathfrak{A}_{c}$, norm-closed as a C$^{*}$-subalgebra, is mapped into itself by $\tau_{t}$ for all $t$ of one sign, and (ii) gives $\sigma_{s}(\mathfrak{A}_{c}) = \mathfrak{A}_{c}$ for all $s$, that is $\mathfrak{A}_{e^{-2\pi s}c} = \mathfrak{A}_{c}$ for all $s$; as $s$ ranges over $\R$, $e^{-2\pi s}c$ ranges over all $c' > 0$. For nested diamonds $D_{c} \subseteq D$ sharing the future tip of $D$, the conformal Killing flow of $D$ moves the family monotonically (the conformal map from the wedge to the diamond carries the half null planes $\mathcal{N}_{c}$ to them, as in Hislop and Longo's treatment, cited from memory), so the same argument applies with $\mathfrak{A}_{c}$ the algebra of $D_{c}$. Only the phase action of $\tau$ is used: no property of the state enters.

\emph{The reading.} At a Killing horizon the store's modes sit on the fixed locus of the boost (Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics}: one ladder pair per point of the blown-up singular boundary, with the boost acting by phases), so the flow acts on the algebra as a whole and moves no sub-patch; clause (iii) read that way is consistent with clause (i), and for a faithful state the modular group being $\tau_{-\beta s}$ is the $(\tau, \beta)$-KMS condition of clause (ii) (on windows this equivalence is part (ii) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.local-boost-temperature-is-local-regularity}). The contrast in the check is the bilateral shift $S e_{k} = e_{k + 1}$ on $\ell^{2}(\mathbb{Z})$, unitary with Lebesgue spectrum, the model to which the dilations of the half line are unitarily equivalent: $\|S^{n}e_{0} - e_{0}\|^{2} = 2$ for every $n \ge 1$, and $S$ maps the closed span of $\{e_{k}\}_{k \ge 0}$ onto that of $\{e_{k}\}_{k \ge 1}$, a proper subspace, exactly the behaviour (ii) excludes for phase flows. The check illustrates and does not test (ii) or (iii): it verifies, on a two-mode window in the Jordan-Wigner representation, the canonical anticommutation relations and $\tau(a_{j}) = \bar z^{\omega_{j}}a_{j}$ for the step $z = (3 + 4J)/5$ with weights $(1, 2)$; $z = (2 + J)/(2 - J)$ is a quotient of non-associate Gaussian primes, so $z^{n} = 1$ would give $(2 + J)^{n} = (2 - J)^{n}$, impossible by unique factorisation in $\mathbb{Z}[J] = \mathrm{span}_{\mathbb{Z}}\{1, J\}$, and the flow is not periodic; still $|z^{61} - 1|^{2} < 10^{-3}$, the recurrence of (i) seen in exact arithmetic.

synthesis.clausius-heat-exceeds-created-.technical: One route to the Clausius hypothesis of the Einstein derivation is to let matter hand its boost energy to the horizon's boundary modes, conserve energy, and use the first law of entanglement to turn the energy into entropy. This result tests that route against the temperature clause of the local-horizon premise, which says the boundary modes are in a KMS state for the local boost. A finite window has exactly one KMS state at a given temperature, so if the clause holds at every instant and the window and its weights are fixed, the window's entropy and energy cannot change at all. The horizon entropy can then grow only by adding modes, which is the area-count picture. A mode added in its thermal state brings entropy $s(x)$ but Killing energy only $\omega n(x)$, and the Clausius relation asks for heat $T s(x)$; the difference, $T\ln(1 + e^{-x})$ per mode, is positive for every weight. So the three statements, Clausius, the temperature clause at every instant with fixed weights, and conservation of boost energy between matter and the modes' Killing energy, cannot all hold when heat crosses: some third carrier must take that energy. At zero weight, where the registered calibration residue sits in its one-mode-per-unit reading, the modes carry no Killing energy and the third carrier takes all the heat: this is, locally, the same tension as the hole's mass sitting on a c-number label rather than in the counted modes, and the label's energy is fed at $T\ln 2$ per created mode. The gap is the created mode's free energy with opposite sign, $-F = T\ln Z$ per mode, a chemical potential $\mu = -T\ln(1 + e^{-x})$ for mode creation in $T\,dS = dE - \mu\,dN$; that much is standard thermodynamics, and the content here is that the series' premises supply no carrier for it. Weights that moved with the heat could balance the ledger instead, but the boundary-mode Definition fixes them as labels and provides no such dynamics. If instead the temperature clause is only required before the crossing, the reading Jacobson-type arguments use, energy can flow into a fixed window and the first law gives the right entropy at first order (the route filed alongside, synthesis.clausius-is-window-first-law-plus-boost-charge-conservation), but the window then leaves its KMS state; an exact resonant exchange shows the occupation moving from $1/4$ to $73/100$. This result prices the every-instant reading. The checks verify KMS uniqueness on a two-mode window (a one-dimensional solution space of the KMS equations), the exchange model, the factorisation of the Gibbs state when a mode is added, and the per-mode ledger at $e^{x} = 3$ and at zero weight with exact logarithms of rationals. The result does not decide which reading of the premise is right; it says what each reading costs.
synthesis.clausius-heat-exceeds-created-.lay: One hope for deriving Einstein's equations in the series is this: when matter falls across a horizon, it hands its energy to the horizon's quantum modes, and the standard thermodynamic law then turns that energy into the entropy that the horizon's area measures. This result checks the hope against the series' own assumption that those horizon modes are always at the horizon's temperature. A fixed set of modes at a fixed temperature has only one possible state, so it cannot soak up energy and stay at that temperature. The horizon can then gain entropy only by gaining modes. But a new mode at the horizon's temperature carries less energy than the heat the thermodynamic law requires for the entropy it brings, and at the special value the series' calibration uses it carries none at all. So the energy has to go somewhere other than the matter or the modes' own energy: something like the extra mass label the series already needed for black holes. The alternative is to let the modes leave their temperature while heat flows in, which gives up the assumption the hope started from.

proofs.main:
\emph{(1)} A window algebra is $\End(\Lambda^\bullet\C^F)$, a matrix factor over $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$, $J = e_2e_3$ the complex unit of the radial atom from which the boundary modes descend (\claimref{synthesis.transverse-bivector-is-the-complex-unit-of-the-radial-atom}), and its boost dynamics is $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{JtH_F})$. By Theorem \claimref{singularity.kms-uniqueness-factor} its only KMS state at $\beta$ is $\varrho_I = e^{-\beta H_F}/Z_F$. If (R$_{\mathrm{inst}}$) holds at two instants with the same window $F$ and the same weights, the window's state is $\varrho_I$ at both, so $S(\varrho)$ and $\Tr(\varrho H_F)$ agree. (The check solves the KMS equations directly on a two-mode window: with $G = e^{\beta H}$, the condition $\Tr(\varrho\,A\,e^{-\beta H}Be^{\beta H}) = \Tr(\varrho BA)$ for all $A, B$ is, by cyclicity, $G\varrho A G^{-1} = A\varrho$ for all $A$; over the sixteen matrix units this has a one-dimensional solution space spanned by $e^{-\beta H}$.)

\emph{(2)} $e^{-\beta H_{F'}} = e^{-\beta H_F}\otimes e^{-\beta\omega_j N_j}$ for $F' = F \cup \{j\}$ (the boost Hamiltonian is a sum of commuting number terms), so the KMS state of the larger window is the product of the smaller window's KMS state and the new mode's marginal $\mathrm{diag}(1 - n(x_j), n(x_j))$; von Neumann entropy and the expectation of a sum of number operators are additive on product states. Repeating, a window $F$ at the later instant and $F_0$ at the earlier, with $F \setminus F_0 = C$ and $F_0 \setminus F = D$ and the common modes in the same state by (1), have $\delta S = \sum_C s(x_j) - \sum_D s(x_j)$ and $\delta E = \sum_C\omega_j n(x_j) - \sum_D\omega_j n(x_j) = T(\sum_C x_j n(x_j) - \sum_D x_j n(x_j))$. The marginal entropy is $s(x) = \ln(1 + e^{-x}) + x\,n(x)$ by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boundary-mode-thermal-entropy}.

\emph{(3)} By (Cl), $\delta Q = T\,\delta S$, so $\delta Q - \delta E = T\sum_C(s - xn)(x_j) - T\sum_D(s - xn)(x_j)$ with $s(x) - x\,n(x) = \ln(1 + e^{-x}) > 0$ for every real $x$. At a common weight $x$ with net number $\delta m = |C| - |D|$, $\delta S = s(x)\delta m$, so $\delta Q \neq 0$ forces $\delta m \neq 0$ and then $\delta Q - \delta E = T\ln(1 + e^{-x})\,\delta m \neq 0$; the ratio $\delta E/\delta Q = x\,n(x)/s(x)$ is below $1$ because $\ln(1 + e^{-x}) > 0$, and it is $0$ at $x = 0$, where $s(0) = \ln 2$ and $\delta Q = T\ln 2\,\delta m$. If $D = \emptyset$ and $\delta Q \neq 0$, then $\delta S \neq 0$, so $C \neq \emptyset$ and $\delta Q - \delta E = T\sum_C\ln(1 + e^{-x_j}) > 0$. In both settings (E), $\delta Q = \delta E$, fails.

\emph{Why the weights are held fixed.} If the weights of kept modes could move, a mode moving from $x$ to $x + \delta x$ changes its entropy by $s'(x)\delta x = -x\,n(1 - n)\delta x$ and its Killing energy by $T\,\delta(x n) = T(n - x\,n(1 - n))\delta x$, so $T\delta S - \delta E$ changes by $-T\,n\,\delta x$, and a suitable increase of weights could offset the deficit of created modes. The boundary-mode Definition fixes the weights as mode labels, and the statement assumes it; a dynamics that moved them in response to matter would be a further structure of the same kind as the one the conclusion names.

\emph{(4)} If (R$_{\mathrm{inst}}$) holds only at the earlier instant, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boundary-mode-first-law-of-entanglement}(i)-(ii) gives the entropy gain $\beta\,\delta E$ of a fixed window at first order, short by $\rel{\varrho}{\varrho_{I}}$ at second order; that route to Clausius is the one treated in the result filed alongside, synthesis.clausius-is-window-first-law-plus-boost-charge-conservation, and is not repeated here. What (1) adds is that $\delta E \neq 0$ forces $\varrho \neq \varrho_I$, so the new state is not KMS at $\beta$. In the example, the basis is $|n_w n_m\rangle$, the initial state is $\mathrm{diag}(0, 0, 3/4, 1/4)$ on $(|00\rangle, |10\rangle, |01\rangle, |11\rangle)$ (window mode thermal with $n = 1/4$, matter mode occupied), and the exchange is the rotation of $(|10\rangle, |01\rangle)$ by $\cos\theta = 3/5$, $\sin\theta = 4/5$, the identity on $|00\rangle$ and $|11\rangle$; it commutes with the total number. The window's occupation becomes $\sin^2\theta\cdot\tfrac34 + \tfrac14 = \tfrac{73}{100}$, total occupation stays $\tfrac54$, the window's reduced state stays diagonal, and $\tfrac{73}{100}$ is not $n(x) = \tfrac14$.

\emph{Conclusion.} Under (R$_{\mathrm{inst}}$) with fixed weights, (H1) can hold only if boost energy $\delta Q - \delta E \neq 0$ goes to a carrier other than matter and the boundary modes' Killing energy, together with a rule creating modes as heat arrives ($\delta m = \delta Q/(T s(x))$ at a common weight). Per mode the gap is $T\ln(1 + e^{-x}) = T\ln Z_{\mathrm{mode}} = -F_{\mathrm{mode}}$, minus the free energy of a mode created in its Gibbs state: in $T\,dS = dE - \mu\,dN$ it is the chemical-potential term with $\mu = -T\ln(1 + e^{-x})$, standard thermodynamics. If the weights may move, the computation above shows the ledger can balance, so a dynamics of the weights is a third way out, which the boundary-mode Definition does not provide; if (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) is weakened to the earlier instant, a fixed window can absorb the heat, at the price of leaving its KMS state at first order. At zero weight the carrier takes $T\ln 2$ per created mode, the whole heat; this is the per-mode form of the c-number label that carries a hole's mass in the model of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.central-label-carries-mass-at-zero-weight} and that the Gibbs reading forces in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.hole-mass-is-ground-energy-label}. Those results are cited for comparison only; the argument does not use them.

\emph{The check.} Exact rational arithmetic, with logarithms of rationals written as exact coefficient vectors over $\ln 2, \ln 3, \ln 5$: the KMS equations on a two-mode window with $e^{-\beta\omega} = 1/3, 1/5$ (rank $15$ on sixteen unknowns, kernel $e^{-\beta H}$); the exchange example; the factorisation of the Gibbs state of a window plus one created mode; and the per-mode ledger at $e^{x} = 3$ (entropy $2\ln 2 - \tfrac34\ln 3$, Killing energy over $T$ equal to $\tfrac14\ln 3$, difference $\ln\tfrac43 > 0$) and at $x = 0$ (entropy $\ln 2$, Killing energy $0$), and the common-weight deficit $\delta m\ln\tfrac43$ for $\delta m = 2, -1, 0$.

synthesis.clausius-is-window-first-law-p.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$. Let $F$ be a window of the boundary-mode algebra with its boost dynamics (Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics}), $H_{F} = \sum_{j \in F}\omega_{j}N_{j}$ in the time of a boost field $\chi$ of surface gravity $\kappa$, $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$, and $\rho_{I}$ the restriction to $F$ of the state of Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state}, the Gibbs state of $\beta H_{F}$ (the state that the temperature clause (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) of the local-horizon premise prescribes for a patch's window before matter crosses). Let the matter be a second-quantised field over a finite-dimensional one-particle space $\mathfrak{h}_{m}$ (finitely many matter modes crossing the patch) with self-adjoint one-particle boost generator $k$, so that its boost charge is $d\Gamma(k)$, the $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ part of $\Psi^{*}k\Psi$ (Theorem \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(3)). A \emph{process} is a unitary $U$ on the joint Fock space applied to $\rho_{I} \otimes \rho_{m}$, $\rho_{m}$ any matter state; write $\rho'$ for the result, $\rho_{F}'$ and $\rho_{m}'$ for its marginals, $\delta Q := \Tr(\rho_{m}\,d\Gamma(k)) - \Tr(\rho_{m}'\,d\Gamma(k))$ for the boost energy the matter loses, $\Delta S_{F} := S(\rho_{F}') - S(\rho_{I})$, and $S(\cdot\,\|\,\cdot)$ for relative entropy. Consider the hypothesis
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(J)] \emph{(Boost-charge conservation.)} $U$ commutes with $H_{F}\otimes 1 + 1\otimes d\Gamma(k)$.
\end{enumerate}
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Conservation is a one-particle condition.)} $[d\Gamma(a), d\Gamma(b)] = d\Gamma([a, b])$, so a quadratic coupling $d\Gamma(v)$ on $\mathfrak{h}_{F} \oplus \mathfrak{h}_{m}$, with $H_{F} = d\Gamma(w)$, conserves the total boost charge if and only if $[v, w \oplus k] = 0$: it couples only modes of equal boost weight.
\item \emph{(Clausius from the first law.)} Under (J), $\Delta S_{F} = \beta\,\delta Q - S(\rho_{F}'\,\|\,\rho_{I})$ exactly. The defect is nonnegative, vanishes only for $\rho_{F}' = \rho_{I}$, and is of second order in $\rho_{F}' - \rho_{I}$. Hence $\Delta S_{F} = \delta Q/T_{\chi}$, $T_{\chi} = \kappa/2\pi$, at first order in the change of the window's state, and $\Delta S_{F} \le \delta Q/T_{\chi}$ always. (This is the standard first-law identity of a Gibbs state, combined with (J).)
\item \emph{(The matter's modular Hamiltonian reading.)} For every process, with or without (J), $\Delta S_{F} = \beta\,\delta Q + I(F{:}m)_{\rho'} + S(\rho_{m}'\,\|\,\sigma_{m}) - S(\rho_{m}\,\|\,\sigma_{m})$, where $\sigma_{m}$ is the Gibbs state of $\beta\,d\Gamma(k)$, whose modular Hamiltonian is $\beta\,d\Gamma(k)$ up to a constant (the boost-KMS state of the matter on the patch, when it exists), and $I(F{:}m)_{\rho'}$ is the mutual information created. Under (J) the defects balance: $S(\rho_{F}'\,\|\,\rho_{I}) + I(F{:}m)_{\rho'} = S(\rho_{m}\,\|\,\sigma_{m}) - S(\rho_{m}'\,\|\,\sigma_{m})$. (This is the standard entropy-production identity of a system coupled unitarily to a thermal state, with the window and the matter in the roles stated.)
\item \emph{(Without (J) the relation fails.)} For a window mode of weight $\omega_{F}$ coupled by number-conserving hopping to a matter mode of weight $\omega_{m} \neq \omega_{F}$, the first-order coefficients of $\Delta S_{F}$ and $\beta\,\delta Q$ are $\beta\omega_{F}\,\delta n$ and $\beta\omega_{m}\,\delta n$, $\delta n \neq 0$ the occupation transferred: the window's first law and its state hold, and (H1) fails. So (J) does not follow from the window's state and its first law.
\item \emph{(Zero weight.)} If every mode of $F$ has zero weight (a limit outside the windows of the Definition, whose weights are positive, admitted here because one realisation of the registered residue sits there), the case in which each counted unit is one mode carrying $\ln 2$ and the residue takes its registered value (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}; under the weight clause of version 3 of Premise (Q), $\omega_{k} = \kappa(k + \tfrac12)$, the registered value is also realised by two arrays per counted unit at nonzero weight, to which this clause does not apply), then $H_{F} = 0$, under (J) $\delta Q = 0$ for every process, and $\Delta S_{F} = -S(\rho_{F}'\,\|\,\rho_{I}) \le 0$: a fixed window of zero-weight modes absorbs no boost energy and its entropy can only fall. On that reading a nonzero heat can raise the horizon entropy only by changing the window's mode set, not through the first law of a fixed window.
\item \emph{(The boost charge on a generator.)} On a horizon generator with affine parameter $v$ and $\chi = \kappa v\,\partial_{v}$, a chiral mode $\psi(v)$ supported in the patch, with $T_{vv} = \tfrac{I_{4}}{2}(\bar\psi\psi' - \bar\psi'\psi)$ (the mode space's complex unit is the field theory's unit $I_{4}$, numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$), has $\int \chi^{v}T_{vv}\,dv = \kappa\ip{\psi}{I_{4}(v\partial_{v} + \tfrac12)\psi}$: the boost flux through the generator is the expectation of the one-particle generator of dilations of $v$, whose second quantisation is the boost charge $d\Gamma(k)$ above.
\item \emph{(The continuum carrier: (J) as an identity; the first law there given the imported Fact.)} Let the patch's modes on a generator be the continuum mode space (Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}) over $L^{2}(\R_{+}, du)\otimes K$, the half of the generator beyond the edge with affine parameter $u$ and $\chi = \kappa u\,\partial_{u}$, the boost acting as $\psi(u) \mapsto e^{\kappa t/2}\psi(e^{\kappa t}u)$ with one-particle generator $h = \kappa\,I_{4}(u\partial_{u} + \tfrac12)$ (eigenvalue $-\kappa w$ on $u^{-1/2 + I_{4}w}$), in the continuum I-state at $\beta$ (Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state-continuum}). If the patch's modes and the matter crossing the patch are one field on these generators, then by the polarised form of (6) the window's boost Hamiltonian and the matter's boost charge are one quadratic form, $d\Gamma(h) = \int\chi^{u}T_{uu}\,du$, on modes vanishing at the edge, so (J) holds identically (proved). That the first law (2) then holds for that field's entropy differences on the continuum follows given the imported Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-null-plane-modular-hamiltonian-first-law}: $h$ has purely continuous spectrum, so the continuum carrier has no Gibbs windows of the Definition (and a point-spectrum discretisation replaces $h$ by an operator whose second quantisation is no longer the boost flux), and the statement is Araki's relative-entropy form with the null-plane modular Hamiltonian $\beta\,d\Gamma(h) = 2\pi\int u\,T_{uu}\,du$, which by that Fact gives $\Delta S_{F} = \beta\,\delta Q - S(\rho_{F}'\,\|\,\rho_{I})$ for entropy differences, hence (2), on the type III algebra of the half-generator. This is the series' form of the known statement that the null-plane modular Hamiltonian is the boost charge of the field on the horizon. On modes shared by both sheets of an edge the temperature clause for both sheets forces zero weight, and then (5) applies instead.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Consequence for the Einstein derivation.} If the patch's window is in the state above before matter crosses, (J) holds, the window's state changes at the order of the heat (so the defect of (2) is of order $\delta Q^{2}$, that is $\lambda_{0}^{4}$ in the patch of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}, two orders beyond the balance), and the window's entropy change is the horizon's, $\eta\,\delta A$, then the Clausius hypothesis (H1) of that theorem holds at the order it is used, with $\delta Q$ the boost flux of the matter. The temperature clause is used here as a condition on the window's state before the crossing: by (2) and Klein's inequality the window's state after a process with $\delta Q \neq 0$ is not $\rho_{I}$, so the clause read as a condition at every instant on a fixed window is incompatible with (2).
synthesis.clausius-is-window-first-law-p.technical: Jacobson's Clausius relation, hypothesis (H1) of the stored derivation of Einstein's equations, is the step at which matter enters gravity. This result asks what the series' own objects supply toward it. The boundary-mode window of a local patch, in the state the temperature clause prescribes, is a Gibbs state of the boost Hamiltonian at inverse temperature $2\pi/\kappa$, so its modular Hamiltonian is $\beta H_{F}$ plus a constant and its entropy obeys the first law: the entropy change equals $\beta$ times the change of its boost energy, up to a relative-entropy defect of second order. The matter field is second-quantised, and its boost charge is the second quantisation of the one-particle boost generator; on a horizon generator this is exactly the boost flux $\int\chi^{v}T_{vv}\,dv$ of a chiral mode. The missing link is that the boost energy the matter loses is the boost energy the window gains. That is the hypothesis (J), and the reduction holds with the temperature clause read as the window's state before the crossing: the joint dynamics of matter and window conserves the total boost charge. Because second quantisation turns commutators of one-particle operators into commutators of their second quantisations, (J) for a quadratic coupling is a one-particle condition: the coupling joins only modes of equal boost weight. Given (J), the first law of the window, a standard identity of Gibbs states, is the Clausius relation at first order; (H1) itself then follows once the window's entropy change is read as $\eta\,\delta A$. Without (J) it fails: an exact two-mode model with a detuned coupling keeps the window's state and first law and breaks the relation at first order. A second reading puts the matter's stress tensor into a modular Hamiltonian: if the matter on the patch has a boost-KMS state, its modular Hamiltonian is $\beta$ times its boost charge, and for any process the window's entropy change is $\beta\,\delta Q$ plus the mutual information created plus the change of the matter's distance from that state; with (J) these defects balance exactly (the standard entropy-production identity of quantum thermodynamics). The zero-weight case, where one mode per counted unit sits at the registered residue (under the weight clause of (Q) version 3 the residue is also realised by two arrays at nonzero weight, which this case does not cover), is degenerate: the window's boost Hamiltonian vanishes, (J) then lets no boost energy in, and the window's entropy can only fall, so there the first-law route to (H1) is closed on a fixed window and heat can raise the horizon entropy only by changing the mode set (zero-weight windows are a limit outside the Definition's windows; the energy ledger of such a change, under the reading of the temperature clause at every instant, is the subject of synthesis.clausius-heat-exceeds-created-modes-killing-energy, filed alongside). On the continuum carrier of a generator, where the horizon modes and the crossing matter are one field, the window's boost Hamiltonian is the matter's boost charge, $d\Gamma(h) = \int\chi^{u}T_{uu}\,du$ as quadratic forms, so (J) is an identity there (proved; the series' form of the known statement that the null-plane modular Hamiltonian is the horizon boost charge). That the first law then holds for that field's entropy differences, leaving only the identification of the entropy change with $\eta\,\delta A$, follows given the imported Fact on the null-plane modular Hamiltonian and Araki's relative entropy (Wall; Casini, Teste and Torroba; Faulkner et al.): the dilation generator has no point spectrum, so there are no Gibbs windows on the continuum, and the first law there is the relative-entropy form that Fact supplies. The identities are checked exactly in two-mode models with rational Boltzmann factors and occupations, logarithms reduced to prime exponents. Transport-absent.
synthesis.clausius-is-window-first-law-p.lay: In Jacobson's derivation of Einstein's equations, the step where matter enters gravity is the assumption that the energy of matter falling across a small horizon raises the horizon's entropy by that energy divided by the temperature. This result asks whether the series' own quantum objects explain that step. The horizon's quantum modes, in the thermal state the series assumes, obey a standard law: their entropy rises by their energy gain divided by the temperature, up to a small correction. So the step follows if the energy matter loses is exactly the energy the horizon modes gain, that is, if the coupling between matter and horizon conserves the relevant energy (the boost energy). That conservation is the one extra ingredient, and an explicit small model shows it does not follow from the rest: a coupling that does not conserve it breaks the relation. If the horizon modes and the infalling matter are the same quantum field living on the horizon's light rays, the conservation is automatic, because the two energies are then one quantity; that the entropy law then carries over to that continuous setting follows given an imported fact of quantum field theory on light-like surfaces. Where the series' registered counting sits in its one-mode-per-unit reading, with horizon modes of zero energy, the route closes: such modes are already at maximum entropy and cannot absorb energy, so infalling matter can raise the horizon entropy only by adding new modes, which this mechanism does not describe.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} The window and its boost dynamics are those of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics}. On the window, $\rho_{I} = e^{-\beta H_{F}}/Z_{F}$ (Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state}), and Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boundary-mode-first-law-of-entanglement}(ii) gives, for every state $\rho$ of $F$,
\[
S(\rho) - \beta\Tr(\rho H_{F}) = \ln Z_{F} - S(\rho\,\|\,\rho_{I}). \tag{$*$}
\]
The same identity holds for any finite system and any Gibbs state $\sigma = e^{-\beta K}/Z$: $S(\rho\,\|\,\sigma) = \Tr\rho\ln\rho - \Tr\rho\ln\sigma = -S(\rho) + \beta\Tr(\rho K) + \ln Z$.

\emph{(1)} The CAR give $[a_{i}^{*}a_{j}, a_{k}^{*}a_{l}] = \delta_{jk}a_{i}^{*}a_{l} - \delta_{il}a_{k}^{*}a_{j}$, so with $d\Gamma(A) = \sum_{ij}A_{ij}a_{i}^{*}a_{j}$,
\[
[d\Gamma(A), d\Gamma(B)] = \sum_{i,l}(AB)_{il}a_{i}^{*}a_{l} - \sum_{k,j}(BA)_{kj}a_{k}^{*}a_{j} = d\Gamma([A, B]).
\]
The map $d\Gamma$ is injective on one-particle operators, since $d\Gamma(A)a_{j}^{*}|0\rangle = \sum_{i}A_{ij}a_{i}^{*}|0\rangle$. With $H_{F} \otimes 1 + 1 \otimes d\Gamma(k) = d\Gamma(w \oplus k)$ on the joint Fock space (Theorem \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(3) for the span$\{1, I_{4}\}$ part), $[d\Gamma(v), d\Gamma(w \oplus k)] = d\Gamma([v, w \oplus k])$ vanishes if and only if $[v, w \oplus k] = 0$, and then every $U = \exp(-I_{4}t\,d\Gamma(v))$ satisfies (J). In a basis of boost eigenmodes with weights $\omega_{i}$, $[v, \mathrm{diag}(\omega)]_{ij} = v_{ij}(\omega_{j} - \omega_{i})$, so the condition is that $v$ joins only modes of equal weight.

\emph{(2)} Apply $(*)$ to $\rho_{F}'$ and to $\rho_{I}$ (for which the relative entropy vanishes) and subtract: $\Delta S_{F} = \beta\,\Delta\langle H_{F}\rangle - S(\rho_{F}'\,\|\,\rho_{I})$, where $\Delta\langle H_{F}\rangle = \Tr(\rho_{F}'H_{F}) - \Tr(\rho_{I}H_{F})$. Under (J) the expectation of $H_{F}\otimes 1 + 1\otimes d\Gamma(k)$ is the same in $\rho'$ and in $\rho_{I}\otimes\rho_{m}$, and the expectation of $H_{F}\otimes 1$ (of $1\otimes d\Gamma(k)$) depends only on the window (matter) marginal, so $\Delta\langle H_{F}\rangle = \delta Q$. The relative entropy is nonnegative and vanishes only at $\rho_{F}' = \rho_{I}$ (Klein's inequality; Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boundary-mode-first-law-of-entanglement}(ii)), and along a differentiable family $\rho_{t}$ with $\rho_{0} = \rho_{I}$ its first derivative at $t = 0$ is $\Tr(\dot\rho\ln\rho_{I}) - \Tr(\dot\rho\ln\rho_{I}) + \Tr\dot\rho = 0$, so it is of second order. Hence $\Delta S_{F} = \beta\,\delta Q$ at first order and $\Delta S_{F} \le \beta\,\delta Q$, with $\beta = 1/T_{\chi}$, $T_{\chi} = \kappa/2\pi$. This is the standard first-law identity of a Gibbs state combined with (J).

\emph{(3)} The joint entropy is invariant under $U$ and additive on the product $\rho_{I}\otimes\rho_{m}$; after the process $S(\rho') = S(\rho_{F}') + S(\rho_{m}') - I(F{:}m)_{\rho'}$. So $\Delta S_{F} = -\Delta S_{m} + I(F{:}m)_{\rho'}$. The identity below $(*)$ for $\sigma_{m} = e^{-\beta d\Gamma(k)}/Z_{m}$ gives $\Delta S_{m} = \beta\big(\Tr(\rho_{m}'d\Gamma(k)) - \Tr(\rho_{m}d\Gamma(k))\big) - \big(S(\rho_{m}'\,\|\,\sigma_{m}) - S(\rho_{m}\,\|\,\sigma_{m})\big) = -\beta\,\delta Q - \Delta D_{m}$. Hence $\Delta S_{F} = \beta\,\delta Q + I(F{:}m)_{\rho'} + \Delta D_{m}$, with no use of (J). This is the standard entropy-production identity of quantum thermodynamics for a system coupled unitarily to a thermal state (Esposito, Lindenberg and Van den Broeck 2010; Reeb and Wolf 2014; cited from memory), with the window and the matter in the roles stated. The modular Hamiltonian of $\sigma_{m}$ is $-\ln\sigma_{m} = \beta\,d\Gamma(k) + \ln Z_{m}$: the matter's boost charge. Under (J), comparing with (2): $-S(\rho_{F}'\,\|\,\rho_{I}) = I(F{:}m)_{\rho'} + \Delta D_{m}$, which is the stated balance. (It is also the invariance of $S(\rho\,\|\,\rho_{I}\otimes\sigma_{m})$ under a $U$ that commutes with $\rho_{I}\otimes\sigma_{m}$, split by the chain rule $S(\rho'\,\|\,\rho_{I}\otimes\sigma_{m}) = S(\rho_{F}'\,\|\,\rho_{I}) + S(\rho_{m}'\,\|\,\sigma_{m}) + I(F{:}m)_{\rho'}$.)

\emph{(4)} Take one window mode $b$ of weight $\omega_{F}$ at its Gibbs occupation $n_{I} = (1 + r_{F})^{-1}$, $r_{F} = e^{\beta\omega_{F}}$, and one matter mode $a$ of weight $\omega_{m}$ at occupation $p \neq n_{I}$, in the diagonal product state, and the number-conserving hopping $U$ that rotates $(a, b)$ by $\begin{pmatrix} c & -s\\ s & c\end{pmatrix}$ on the one-particle space (and is the identity on the empty and doubly occupied states, the determinant being $1$). On the occupation basis the one-particle block $\mathrm{diag}(p(1 - n_{I}), (1 - p)n_{I})$ is rotated and the doubly occupied weight $pn_{I}$ is unchanged, so $n_{b}' = s^{2}p + c^{2}n_{I} = n_{I} + \delta n$ and $n_{a}' = p - \delta n$ with $\delta n = s^{2}(p - n_{I})$. The window's marginal is diagonal, so $\Delta S_{F} = h(n_{I} + \delta n) - h(n_{I})$ with $h(q) = -q\ln q - (1 - q)\ln(1 - q)$, whose first-order term is $h'(n_{I})\,\delta n = \ln\frac{1 - n_{I}}{n_{I}}\,\delta n = \beta\omega_{F}\,\delta n$, while $\beta\,\delta Q = \beta\omega_{m}(p - n_{a}') = \beta\omega_{m}\,\delta n$. For $\omega_{m} \neq \omega_{F}$ these differ at first order in $s^{2}$, while the window's state before the process and its first law $(*)$ are as in (2). The coupling $v$ joins modes of different weight, so by (1) it violates (J).

\emph{(5)} The windows of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics} have positive weights; zero weight is the limit at which the registered residue sits when each counted unit is one mode, admitted here as such (under (Q) version 3 the residue is also realised by two arrays at nonzero weight, outside this clause). If $\omega_{j} = 0$ on $F$ then $H_{F} = 0$ and (J) says $U$ commutes with $1\otimes d\Gamma(k)$, so $\delta Q = 0$; then (2) gives $\Delta S_{F} = -S(\rho_{F}'\,\|\,\rho_{I}) \le 0$, with $\rho_{I}$ the tracial state of entropy $\ln 2$ per mode (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boundary-mode-thermal-entropy} at $\omega = 0$), the maximum, which is the zero-weight case of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy} in which the residue takes its registered value. Without (J), (4) with $\omega_{F} = 0$ shows the window's entropy has zero first-order change while the matter loses $\omega_{m}\,\delta n$. Either way a fixed zero-weight window cannot satisfy $\Delta S_{F} = \beta\,\delta Q$ with $\delta Q \ne 0$ at first order.

\emph{(6)} For $\psi$ smooth with support in the patch, integration by parts gives $-\int v\bar\psi'\psi\,dv = \int\bar\psi\,(v\psi)'\,dv = \int\bar\psi\psi\,dv + \int v\bar\psi\psi'\,dv$, so $\int v(\bar\psi\psi' - \bar\psi'\psi)\,dv = 2\ip{\psi}{(v\partial_{v} + \tfrac12)\psi}$, and multiplying by $\tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\kappa$ gives the claim. The operator $I_{4}(v\partial_{v} + \tfrac12)$ is symmetric, since $(v\partial_{v})^{*} = -v\partial_{v} - 1$. With the unit $I_{4}$ (Theorem \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(4)), its second quantisation is the boost charge of the chiral field on the generator, and its expectation is the boost flux $\int T_{ab}\chi^{a}k^{b}\,d\lambda$ of (H1) per generator. For a general field the identification of $d\Gamma(k)$ with $\int T_{ab}\chi^{a}d\Sigma^{b}$ is the Noether charge of the Killing field $\chi$, cited from memory and not proved here.

\emph{(7)} On $u^{a}$, $I_{4}(u\partial_{u} + \tfrac12)u^{a} = I_{4}(a + \tfrac12)u^{a}$, which for $a = -\tfrac12 + I_{4}w$ is $-w\,u^{a}$; so $h$ is the generator of the dilation $\psi(u) \mapsto e^{\kappa t/2}\psi(e^{\kappa t}u)$ with the Mellin eigenvalues $-\kappa w$, and the continuum I-state of Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state-continuum} for this $h$ has symbol $(1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1}$. For modes $f, g$ vanishing at $u = 0$ (and at the far end of the patch) the integration by parts of (6), applied to $\bar f g$, gives $\int\kappa u\,\tfrac{I_{4}}{2}(\bar f g' - \bar f' g)\,du = \ip{f}{hg}$. Expanding $\psi(u) = \sum_{i}e_{i}(u)a_{i}$ in an orthonormal basis of such modes, $\int\chi^{u}T_{uu}\,du = \sum_{ij}\ip{e_{i}}{he_{j}}a_{i}^{*}a_{j} = d\Gamma(h)$ as quadratic forms on the finite-particle domain (with the unit $I_{4}$, the span$\{1, I_{4}\}$ part of $\Psi^{*}h\Psi$, Theorem \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(3)). In the I-state the expectation of $d\Gamma(h)$ is not finite, and $\delta Q$ is the difference of expectations, finite for perturbations of finite boost energy. If the window's modes and the crossing matter are one field, the operator in (J) is $d\Gamma(h)$ alone and (J) is the statement that a unitary commuting with $d\Gamma(h)$ conserves it, while $\delta Q$, the boost energy deposited, is $\Delta\langle d\Gamma(h)\rangle$ by definition; so no separate conservation hypothesis remains. This proves (J) as an identity of quadratic forms. The first law on this carrier is not the window theorem: $h$ has purely continuous spectrum and no finite-dimensional invariant subspace, so the restriction of the I-state to a finite subspace with projection $P$ has symbol $P(1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1}P$, which is not the Gibbs symbol of $PhP$, and Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state-continuum}(1) gives the window theorem only for pure point spectrum; replacing $h$ by a point-spectrum discretisation $h_{d}$ makes (2) available but $d\Gamma(h_{d})$ is then no longer $\int\chi^{u}T_{uu}\,du$, so (J) stops being an identity exactly where (2) applies. The continuum statement is supplied by Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-null-plane-modular-hamiltonian-first-law}: Araki's relative-entropy identity $S(\rho\,\|\,\omega) = \Delta\langle\beta\,d\Gamma(h)\rangle - \Delta S$ for the half-generator algebra, read for entropy differences on a type III algebra, with the null-plane modular Hamiltonian $\beta\,d\Gamma(h) = 2\pi\int u\,T_{uu}\,du$ (at $\kappa$ normalised as here, since $\beta\kappa = 2\pi$; the Fact's $2\pi K(0)$ on one generator). The restriction of the I-state to the half-generator is KMS at $\beta$ for $h$ (Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state-continuum}), so its modular Hamiltonian is $\beta\,d\Gamma(h)$, and clause (iii) of the Fact gives $\Delta S_{F} = \beta\,\Delta\langle d\Gamma(h)\rangle - S(\rho_{F}'\,\|\,\rho_{I}) = \beta\,\delta Q - S(\rho_{F}'\,\|\,\rho_{I})$ with $\delta Q = \Delta\langle d\Gamma(h)\rangle$ as above: this is (2) on the continuum, for entropy differences, given the imported Fact. If the modes at the edge were shared by its two sheets, whose future boosts are $\chi$ and $-\chi$, the KMS conditions at $\beta$ for $h$ and for $-h$ hold together only for $h = 0$ on each window, and (5) applies.

\emph{Consequence.} In the patch of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}, $\delta Q = \tfrac{\kappa}{2}T(k,k)\lambda_{0}^{2} + O(\lambda_{0}^{3})$ per unit area; if $\rho_{F}' - \rho_{I} = O(\delta Q)$ the defect of (2) is $O(\lambda_{0}^{4})$, so (2) is the balance (H1) requires at order $\lambda_{0}^{2}$, once the window's entropy change is read as $\eta\,\delta A$.

\emph{The check.} Exact arithmetic throughout; every logarithm is that of a positive rational and is stored as its vector of prime exponents, which decides identities exactly. In GA, the ascent pairs of $\Cl(3,3)$ satisfy the CAR, $[d\Gamma(A), d\Gamma(B)] = d\Gamma([A,B])$ on rational matrices, and a resonant coupling commutes with the boost charge while a detuned one does not, in agreement with the one-particle criterion. On the two-mode model at three rational Boltzmann factors and rotations ($(3/5, 4/5)$, $(5/13, 12/13)$, $(8/17, 15/17)$), from the explicit $4\times 4$ density matrix: the conservation $n_{a}' + n_{b}' = p + n_{I}$, the window identity of (2), the joint identity of (3) (also for a detuned pair, with $\sigma_{m}$ at the matter's own weight), the balance of the defects, and a nonzero defect at finite rotation; the Gibbs ratio $\frac{1 - n_{I}}{n_{I}} = r$ (which makes the first-order coefficient of (2) $\ln r$); the detuned failure of (4); the zero-weight statements of (5); (6) for two Gaussian-rational polynomial modes times $(1 - v^{2})^{2}$ on $[-1, 1]$, by exact integration; and (7): the Mellin eigenvalue $-w$ at three rational $w$, and the polarised identity $\int\kappa u\,\tfrac{I_{4}}{2}(\bar f g' - \bar f' g)\,du = \ip{f}{hg}$ with its Hermitian symmetry for three modes times $u^{2}(1 - u)^{2}$ on $[0, 1]$, with pinned values, and the normalisation of the modular Hamiltonian, $\beta$ times the flux at $\kappa = \tfrac14, \tfrac23, 3$ equal to $2\pi$ times the flux at $\kappa = 1$ (the Fact's $2\pi K(0)$, with $2\pi$ a formal symbol).
