synthesis.clausius-on-the-action-shell-t.formal:
Units $\hbar = 1$ and the speed of light one, signature $(1,3)$, the store's curvature sign, $t = 2\pi T$ for a stress tensor $T$ and $\tau$ its trace. Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) with zero torsion. The joint premise set is: (A) the field equations of the gravitational action on the field space of Postulate \claimref{synthesis.field-space-premise-parallel-frozen-point} with the Einstein-Cartan matter coupling (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-einstein-cartan-matter-coupling}), $\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a + 8\pi G\,T(a) = 0$ with one normalisation $G$ for every admissible field and $\Lambda \neq 0$, the range in which that theorem states the functional (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.macdowell-mansouri-principle-fixes-the-trace-free-part}(iv)); (A) is a hypothesis of this result, not a premise it derives; (B) the Clausius hypothesis (H1) with (H2) to (H4) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius} on every local patch through every point $p$, at the local temperature of rapidity period $2\pi c(p)$ ($c = 1$ is (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$); $c \neq 1$ as in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.r-loc-independent-sets-matter-coupling}), with $\delta S = \eta\,\delta A$, $\eta$ constant along each field (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}(6)). Call $p$ matter-crossed if $T$ at $p$ is not a multiple of the metric.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The relation; proved.)} A symmetric $t$ with $t(k,k) = 0$ for every null $k$ ($Q(k) = 0$) is a multiple of the metric. Under (A) the Clausius defect on the pencil about $k$ at $p$ is $t(k,k)\,(1 - 4G\eta/c)$ for every null $k$, whatever the Weyl part. So at a matter-crossed point the Clausius relation holds on every patch through $p$ if and only if $\eta = c(p)/(4G)$ (at $c = 1$ this is Jacobson's identification $G = 1/(4\eta)$, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-jacobson-clausius-1995}, read with $G$ given by (A)), and at a point where $T$ is a multiple of the metric it holds for every $\eta$ and $c$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The one-coupling clause from the period; proved.)} If $c = 1$ at a matter-crossed point of an admissible field (for example, at leading order, where its modes are locally normal to the null vacuum: the local form of (N$_{+}$) there, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.local-normality-at-the-edge-gives-the-null-ground-state}, gives (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$)'s period at leading order), then $\eta = 1/(4G)$ on that whole field: on the joint set every admissible field carrying matter has the same density, and a density that depends on the matter fails the joint set at such a point. The witness of the clause's independence in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.integrated-loc-curvature-clause-forced-matter-clause-independent}, the Einstein static universe of radius $2$ with dust $t = \tfrac14$ and $\eta = \tfrac12$, solves (A) only with $G = \tfrac12$; at $G = 1$ its spatial equations force $\Lambda = \tfrac14$ for every dust density and the radius-$2$ universe then carries $t = \tfrac18$ with $\eta = \tfrac14$. If moreover the density is a continuous function of local data as in (i) of that theorem, a flat dust Friedmann field with $\Lambda > 0$ (matter-crossed and asymptotically de Sitter) has $\eta = \tfrac14$, so $G = 1$ in the Planck units of the calibration: the action's free normalisation is the calibrated one.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The period from (Loc), given the calibration; proved.)} If $\eta = \tfrac14$ and $G = 1$, the calibration with the action's $G$ in the same units taken as an independent input, then $c = 1$ at every matter-crossed point: the model of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.r-loc-independent-sets-matter-coupling}(i), which keeps $\eta = \tfrac14$, fails the joint set wherever matter crosses its region $U$. Without that input the joint set fixes only $\eta/c = 1/(4G)$: a period model with $\eta = c/(4G)$ satisfies it at matter-crossed points where $c$ is constant. So the converse of (ii) needs the calibration; (ii) itself does not.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Matter-free regions; proved.)} Where $T$ is a multiple of the metric, in vacuum with $\Lambda \neq 0$ and with any Weyl part, the Clausius relation holds at leading order for every $\eta$ and $c$. So the period model with $U$ in a matter-free region off every Killing horizon (the region between the horizons of a Schwarzschild-de Sitter hole, away from both, a solution of (A)) satisfies the joint set, and (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$)'s period there remains independent of it; and the joint set fixes no value of $\eta$ on a field with no matter-crossed point.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} On the joint set the Clausius relation does not derive the field equations, which the action supplies; it is one relation, $\eta = c/(4G)$, between the entropy density and the local period factor. The two independent thermal data of the Clausius route, (Loc)'s one coupling and (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$)'s period, become one independent datum wherever matter crosses: either gives the other. What supplies the one coupling is the single normalisation of the action, so the clause has been moved into (A), not derived from transport. At $c = 1$ the value $1/(4G)$ is the density of the Einstein-Hilbert part of the action's Wald entropy, whose Euler part changes no entropy difference on open patches with the edge term of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.euler-entropy-of-a-horizon-patch-is-an-edge-term}: at matter-crossed points (ii) is that agreement, obtained from the Clausius relation and not assumed. The stored independence of the one-coupling clause (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.integrated-loc-curvature-clause-forced-matter-clause-independent}) and of the period (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.r-loc-independent-sets-matter-coupling}) hold relative to the thermal premises; this result does not change them there. The gap that (iv) leaves, the period at matter-free points, would close if a state condition that excludes the period model were imposed at every point of every generator: the period-$2\pi c$ state fails the generator analogue of the Hadamard condition and local normality at the patch edge (the microlocal result \claimref{synthesis.microlocal-condition-on-a-generator-gives-the-local-null-ground-state}), and the closed-generator normality result (\claimref{synthesis.normality-on-the-closed-generator-gives-the-vacuum-folium-not-the-ground-state}) excludes it too; either, imposed at every point, would be a new premise, not a derivation. Imposed at matter-crossed points, the microlocal condition gives $c = 1$ there at leading order, and then (ii) gives $\eta = 1/(4G)$ on every field that carries matter.
synthesis.clausius-on-the-action-shell-t.technical:
The store reaches Einstein's equations by two routes and keeps both: the Clausius route, which needs the entropy clause (Loc) and the temperature clause (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) on local horizons, and the gravitational action on the field space of the frozen-point postulate, whose normalisation $G$ is a free constant. On the Clausius route alone two independence results are stored: a density that depends on the matter can be $\tfrac14$ on every Einstein field at the calibrated coupling and $\tfrac12$ on an Einstein static universe where the Clausius relation still holds, now with coupling $\tfrac12$; and a rapidity period $2\pi c$ on local horizons off Killing horizons gives Einstein's equations with coupling $c/(4\eta)$.

Both models change the coupling of matter at the points where matter crosses. With the action's field equation at coupling $G$, the Ricci part on a null direction is $-4G\,t(k,k)$ in the store's sign, so the Clausius defect at period $2\pi c$, $t(k,k) + (\eta/c)\,k \cdot \mathcal{R}(k)$, is $t(k,k)(1 - 4G\eta/c)$. A stress that is not a multiple of the metric has $t(k,k) \neq 0$ for some null $k$ (the null-cone values have rank $9$ on the ten symmetric maps), so there the relation is $\eta = c/(4G)$. Given the period ($c = 1$), the density is $1/(4G)$ on every field that carries matter; given (Loc) with the calibration ($\eta = \tfrac14$, $G = 1$, an independent input identifying the action's $G$ with the calibration's), the period is $2\pi$ wherever matter crosses. The relation itself is Jacobson's identification of the area density with $1/(4G)$, read in reverse with $G$ supplied by the action; what is new is its use against the two stored independence models. The stored one-coupling witness is a solution of the action only at $G = \tfrac12$. Where the stress is a multiple of the metric both sides of the Clausius relation vanish at leading order, so nothing is fixed there, and the period model placed in a vacuum region (between the horizons of a Schwarzschild-de Sitter hole) survives. The action is stated for $\Lambda \neq 0$, so the vacuum examples carry a cosmological constant.

What this does and does not settle. It answers the problem's first attack line on the joint set: the one-coupling clause follows from the period and the action, and a matter-dependent density is not a model of all present premises once the action is among them. It does not derive the clause from transport, since the action's one coupling carries the same content, and it says nothing on fields with no matter (the curvature clause off calibrated paths there is untouched) or about local normality at the edge, which is a premise on the state, not on the coupling.
synthesis.clausius-on-the-action-shell-t.lay: The series has two ways of getting Einstein's equations for gravity. One borrows a standard action principle with a single strength of gravity. The other uses horizon thermodynamics: entropy proportional to area, a temperature set by acceleration, and heat flowing in as energy crosses a horizon. On the thermodynamic route alone, two ingredients were known to be independent assumptions: that the entropy per unit area does not depend on what matter is present, and the exact temperature of small horizons. This result asks what happens when both routes are kept, as the series now does. Wherever matter crosses a horizon, the heat balance then becomes a single equation tying the entropy per area to the temperature factor and the strength of gravity. Once the entropy per area is fixed at its standard value in the same units as the strength of gravity, either assumption gives the other there, and the known counterexamples stop working. The core equation is Jacobson's 1995 link between horizon entropy and the strength of gravity. In empty regions the equation says nothing, and the temperature remains a separate assumption there.

proofs.main:
Read in Gauge Theory Gravity, the Ricci curvature, the local boost field and the field equations below are those of the gravitational field on flat spacetime through its derived metric and field strength (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}). Write $\mathcal{R}(a)$ for the Ricci map in the store's sign and $t = 2\pi T$, so $8\pi G\,T = 4G\,t$.

\emph{The action's Ricci part.} By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.macdowell-mansouri-principle-fixes-the-trace-free-part}(iv), on the field space of Postulate \claimref{synthesis.field-space-premise-parallel-frozen-point} with the matter coupling of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-einstein-cartan-matter-coupling}, every admissible torsion-free field satisfies $\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a + 4G\,t(a) = 0$, $\mathcal{G}(a) = \mathcal{R}(a) - \tfrac12 a\,\mathcal{R}$, with one normalisation $G$. Taking the trace in four dimensions, $-\mathcal{R} + 4\Lambda + 4G\tau = 0$, so $\mathcal{R} = 4\Lambda + 4G\tau$ and
\[
\mathcal{R}(a) = (\Lambda + 2G\tau)\,a - 4G\,t(a).
\]
For a null $k$, $Q(k) = 0$, hence $k \cdot \mathcal{R}(k) = -4G\,t(k,k)$, whatever the Weyl part of the field strength (the Weyl part does not enter the Ricci map).

\emph{(i).} By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.r-loc-independent-sets-matter-coupling}(ii), at the temperature of rapidity period $2\pi c$ the Clausius defect on a thin pencil about the generator through $p$ with tangent $k$ is $\tfrac{\kappa}{2}\big(T(k,k) - \tfrac{\eta}{2\pi c}\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}(k,k)\big)\lambda_{0}^{2}$ at leading order; on a null $k$ the trace-free part and the full Ricci tensor agree, and in the store's sign and with $t = 2\pi T$ the bracket is $\tfrac{1}{2\pi}\big(t(k,k) + \tfrac{\eta}{c}\,k \cdot \mathcal{R}(k)\big)$, the defect of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.integrated-loc-curvature-clause-forced-matter-clause-independent} at $c = 1$. Substituting the action's Ricci part gives $t(k,k)\,(1 - 4G\eta/c)$. The Clausius hypothesis (H1) on every patch through $p$ asks the defect to vanish for every null $k$. The map from symmetric $t$ to the function $k \mapsto t(k,k)$ on the null cone has kernel the multiples of the metric: the metric is in the kernel since $Q(k) = 0$, and the check computes rank $9$ on the ten-dimensional space of symmetric maps from twelve rational null directions, so the kernel is one-dimensional. Hence at a matter-crossed point some null $k$ has $t(k,k) \neq 0$, and the defect vanishes for all $k$ exactly when $1 - 4G\eta/c = 0$, that is $\eta = c/(4G)$. At $c = 1$ this is Jacobson's identification $G = 1/(4\eta)$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-jacobson-clausius-1995}), here with $G$ given by (A) and read as a condition on $\eta$; where $t = \mu g$ every $t(k,k) = \mu Q(k) = 0$ and the defect vanishes for all $\eta$, $c$.

\emph{(ii).} With $c = 1$ at a matter-crossed point $p$, (i) gives $\eta(p) = 1/(4G)$. Under the integrated reading the Clausius relation on open patches forces $\eta$ constant along the field (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}(6)), so $\eta = 1/(4G)$ on the whole field; $G$ is the same for every admissible field by (A), so every admissible field with a matter-crossed point has this one density, which is the one-coupling clause there. A density that is not $1/(4G)$ at a matter-crossed point of an admissible field violates (H1) there by (i). The local form of (N$_{+}$) gives $c = 1$ at leading order (the passage from it to (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$)'s period is the stored leading-order argument) at points where the modes are locally normal to the null vacuum (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.local-normality-at-the-edge-gives-the-null-ground-state}); that is one way the hypothesis $c = 1$ is met, not used otherwise.

For the stored witness: the Einstein static universe of radius $A$ has, in its rest frame, the spatial Einstein equation $\mathcal{G}(\gamma_{i}) + \Lambda\gamma_{i} = 0$ for dust ($t(\gamma_{i}) = 0$), which the check evaluates on the stereographic field of radius $2$ and which fixes $\Lambda = \tfrac14 = 1/A^{2}$ independently of the dust density and of $G$. The time equation then reads $4G\,t_{00} = 2/A^{2} = \tfrac12$. With $t_{00} = \tfrac14$ it holds at $G = \tfrac12$ and fails at $G = 1$ for every $\Lambda$ (the check also confirms that no $\Lambda$ in a sample satisfies all four equations, as the spatial equation already fixes it); at $G = 1$ it needs $t_{00} = \tfrac18$, and then the Clausius defect vanishes at $\eta = \tfrac14$ and not at $\eta = \tfrac12$. So the witness is a solution of the action with a different normalisation, and on the joint set with $G = 1$ the same geometry carries $\eta = \tfrac14$, as (i) requires.

Continuity: by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.integrated-loc-curvature-clause-forced-matter-clause-independent}(i), a density that is a continuous function of local data is $\tfrac14$ on every admissible field whose local data approach calibrated data, and by its part (ii) a flat dust Friedmann field with $\Lambda > 0$ is such a field (its data tend to de Sitter data). It solves (A) at coupling $G$ (the Friedmann relations with $8\pi G\rho$ in place of $\kappa\rho$) and is matter-crossed at every instant (dust is not a multiple of the metric). So (i) at $c = 1$ gives $\tfrac14 = 1/(4G)$, $G = 1$ in the Planck units in which the calibration $\eta = \tfrac14$ is stated.

\emph{(iii).} Take $\eta = \tfrac14$ and $G = 1$ as an independent input (the calibration, with the action's $G$ in the calibration's units; (ii) derives $G = 1$ only from $c = 1$, so using that derivation here would be circular). Then (i) at a matter-crossed point gives $c = 4G\eta = 1$. Without the input, (i) fixes only $\eta/c = 1/(4G)$, and a period model with $\eta = c/(4G)$ passes at matter-crossed points where $c$ is constant. The model of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.r-loc-independent-sets-matter-coupling}(i) has $c \neq 1$ on a region $U$; at a matter-crossed point of $U$ its Clausius relation returns the coupling $c/(4\eta) = c \neq 1$, which contradicts (A). The check verifies on a flat dust Friedmann-$\Lambda$ instant on the shell of (A) at $G = 1$ (expansion rate $1$, $\kappa\rho = \tfrac32$, $\Lambda = \tfrac32$, deceleration term $\tfrac14$) that with $\eta = \tfrac14$ the defect vanishes at every sampled null $k$ only for $c = 1$ among $c \in \{\tfrac12, 1, \tfrac32, 2, 3\}$.

\emph{(iv).} Where $T = \mu g$, $t(k,k) = 0$ and, by the action's Ricci part, $\mathcal{R}(a) = (\Lambda + 2G\tau - 4G\mu)\,a$, so $k \cdot \mathcal{R}(k) = 0$ for null $k$ and the defect vanishes for every $\eta$, $c$; the check confirms this on de Sitter and on vacuum fields with $\Lambda \in \{\tfrac12, \tfrac35, 2\}$ and nonzero type-D Weyl parts. The model of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.r-loc-independent-sets-matter-coupling}(i) changes only the state of local-horizon modes at points of $U$; with $U$ in a matter-free region off every Killing horizon (for example the static region of a Schwarzschild-de Sitter hole away from both horizons, a vacuum solution of (A) with $\Lambda > 0$; (A) is stated for $\Lambda \neq 0$) the Clausius relation there holds for its $c$, so it satisfies (A) and (B), and (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$)'s period at those points remains independent of the joint set. On a field with no matter-crossed point (B) imposes only the constancy of $\eta$, and (i) fixes no value. In particular a density depending on the field strength alone, as in the models of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.loc-independent-of-clausius-and-killing-data}, is constrained on vacuum fields by the joint set no more than by (B) alone.

\emph{The reading.} At $c = 1$, $1/(4G)$ is the coefficient of the area in the Wald entropy of the Einstein-Hilbert part of the action, and with the edge term of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.euler-entropy-of-a-horizon-patch-is-an-edge-term} the Euler part changes no entropy difference on open patches; so at matter-crossed points the (Loc) density agrees with the action's Wald density for differences. This is a remark on the comparison, not a step in (i) to (iv).

synthesis.curvature-only-tractor-actions.formal:
Work in $\Cl(2,4)$ with $\nO = \tfrac12(e_{4} + e_{5})$, $\nInf = e_{4} - e_{5}$ as in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}, $\Lambda \neq 0$, frozen point $I = \nInf + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\nO$ with $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, canonical tractor $X = \nO$ and Stelle-West vector $V = X - \tfrac{3}{\Lambda}I$ with $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$, $\ip{I}{V} = 0$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}); $W = \{I, V\}^{\perp}$, a copy of the spacetime vectors. A gauge field $A$ is a bivector-valued one-form on flat spacetime with values in a Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ of bivectors, $F = dA + \tfrac12[A, A]$ its field strength (commutator product), $F \wedge G$ the wedge of forms with the values multiplied. Call a four-form density $L$ \emph{admissible} if (P) it is a polynomial in the components of the fields, formed with wedge products only (no inverse frame, so no Hodge dual and no contraction with $\hb$); (C) it depends on $A$ only through $F$ and on the data $I$, $X$ (or $V$) algebraically; (G) it is invariant under $\mathfrak{g}$ acting on all values at once. Then $L = B(F \wedge F)$ for a $\mathfrak{g}$-invariant symmetric bilinear form $B$ on the values. For $w \in W$ the \emph{internal reflection} acts on the values by $u \mapsto wuw^{-1}$ with the spacetime orientation fixed; since the integral of a four-form changes sign under orientation reversal, a density odd under the internal reflection is even under the \emph{combined parity} (orientation reversal with the internal reflection, the frame identifying the two), under which Einstein-Hilbert is even and the Holst term odd. With $i_{6}$ the unit pseudoscalar:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Pure transport and one datum; proved.)} For $\mathfrak{g} = \so(2,4)$ with no datum, and for the parabolic algebra of the line of $X$, the invariant forms are the multiples of $K(F, G) = \langle FG\rangle_{0}$: $L$ is the Chern-Weil density $\langle F \wedge F\rangle_{0}$, closed, with identically vanishing Euler-Lagrange derivative. With $X$ alone, invariance under the stabiliser of $X$ and the field strength unrestricted (forms on all bivectors), there are two invariant forms and none is odd under the internal reflection. On $\Lambda^{2}(X^{\perp})$ (the values of the field strength of a connection valued in the stabiliser of $X$, and of the normal torsion-free tractor connection) there are two invariant forms, exactly one internally odd, $\epsilon_{X}$; for a connection valued in the stabiliser of $X$ both are Chern-Weil, while on the normal tractor connection $\epsilon(I, X, F, F)$ is the Weyl square (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-integrand-on-tractor-transport-is-weyl-squared}(iii)).
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The frozen point alone; proved.)} For $A$ valued in the stabiliser of $I$ ($\so(1,4)$ for $\Lambda > 0$, $\so(2,3)$ for $\Lambda < 0$; this is $\Lambda^{2}(I^{\perp})$), the invariant forms are again the multiples of $K$: topological.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Frozen point and canonical tractor; proved.)} For $A$ in the stabiliser of $I$ and invariance under it acting on $(A, V)$ (equivalently, at $V$ fixed, under the Lorentz algebra stabilising $I$ and $V$), the invariant forms are a three-dimensional space with basis $K$, $H(F, G) = \langle (F \wedge I \wedge V)(G \wedge I \wedge V)\rangle_{0}$ and $M(F, G) = \langle (F \wedge G \wedge I \wedge V)\,i_{6}\rangle_{0} = \epsilon(I, V, F, G) = \epsilon(I, X, F, G)$. Under the internal reflection in a vector of $W$, $K$ and $H$ are even and $M$ is odd; the internally odd invariant forms are the multiples of $M$. So under the combined parity $M$ is even and $K$, $H$ are odd. Of the three only $K$ is invariant under the whole stabiliser of $I$, so only $K$ is a Chern-Weil density.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Field equations; proved.)} In the gauge $V$ constant the general connection preserving $I$ is $A(a) = \Omega(a) + \hb^{-1}(a) \wedge V/Q(V)$, the field variable for every field (on Einstein fields it is the connection of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}(v)). The frame variation of $\int M(F \wedge F)$ is, as a linear map of the curvature at a point, of rank $10$ on the algebraic curvature tensors with kernel the Weyl part (the frame equation of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.macdowell-mansouri-principle-fixes-the-trace-free-part}); the frame variation of $\int H(F \wedge F)$ vanishes on every curvature obeying the first Bianchi identity (torsion zero) and has rank $16$ on general curvature two-forms. So $H$ is not topological but changes no frame equation without torsion.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Consequence.)} An admissible action on the series' data is $\kappa M + \kappa' H + \kappa'' K$; invariant under the combined parity it is $\kappa\,\epsilon(I, X, F, F)$, the frozen-point MacDowell-Mansouri functional $Q(I)^{-1}\int\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$ of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west} up to the free normalisation $\kappa$. Without the parity hypothesis uniqueness is equivalent to torsion-free coupling: on torsion-free fields the frame equation is that of $\kappa M$ (that torsion-free fields still solve the connection equation without spin is the Holst result, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-lovelock-cartan-four-forms-and-holst-term}(b), not checked here), but under the Einstein-Cartan coupling of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-einstein-cartan-matter-coupling} torsion is proportional to the spin density, so with spinning matter $\kappa'$ is physical (it enters the spin-spin contact term, as the Barbero-Immirzi parameter; the readings recorded in Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-lovelock-cartan-four-forms-and-holst-term}). Writing the Lorentz block $F_{W} = -R + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}e \wedge e$, $Q(I)^{-1}M(F_{W}, F_{W}) = \tfrac{3}{\Lambda}M(R, R) - 2M(R, e \wedge e) + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}M(e \wedge e, e \wedge e)$: Euler, Einstein-Hilbert and volume terms in fixed ratio, so the cosmological constant of the field equations is the frozen point's and the Euler term is present; since $M$ spans the internally odd admissible densities, no admissible counterterm removes it inside the class (the Lorentz Euler density $M(R, R)$ depends on $DV$ through $R$, so it is not admissible under (C)).
\item[(vi)] \emph{(Which hypotheses do the work; proved, the slot step argued by degree counting and proved under (T) in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.inverse-frame-free-tractor-gauge-field-preserves-a-frozen-point}(i).)} Dropping (C), so that $V$ also enters through $DV$ (the soldering form), adds two invariants $B'(e \wedge e, F)$ (Einstein-Hilbert and Holst type) and one $e^{4}$ (volume): six in all, and the Euler, Einstein-Hilbert and volume coefficients become independent. Dropping the reduction (letting $F$ range over all bivectors with $I$, $V$ algebraic) gives six invariant forms. Hypothesis (P) forces the reduction for slots that are functions of $(\hb, \Omega)$, that is under the premise (T) that the tractor gauge field is assembled from $(\hb, \Omega)$ and no further field: the only polynomial, Lorentz-covariant, inverse-frame-free special-conformal slot built from them is $\rho\,\hb^{-1}(a)$ with $\rho$ constant (the Lorentz commutant on $W$ is one-dimensional), and with it $\nInf + \rho\nO$ is parallel: the reduction datum is a frozen point with $\Lambda = 6\rho$, and the normal tractor connection, whose slot is the Schouten map, lies outside (P). Without (T) the forcing fails: a special-conformal slot that is a field of its own also satisfies (P) and preserves no tractor (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.inverse-frame-free-tractor-gauge-field-preserves-a-frozen-point}(iv)). So the field space of connections preserving $I$, not the integrand, is what (P) supplies under (T); in invariant form that field space is Premise \claimref{synthesis.field-space-premise-parallel-frozen-point}.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.curvature-only-tractor-actions.technical:
The open problem asks whether transport fixes the frozen-point MacDowell-Mansouri functional among the invariant four-forms of the $\Cl(2,4)$ tractor gauge field. This result answers it as a classification, with the hypotheses stated. Admissible densities are polynomial, use no inverse frame (no Hodge dual), depend on the gauge field only through its field strength $F$, take the frozen point $I$ and the canonical tractor $X$ algebraically, and are gauge invariant. In four dimensions they are $B(F \wedge F)$ for an invariant symmetric form $B$, and the invariant forms are computed in exact arithmetic. Parity below means the combined spacetime and internal parity, under which Einstein-Hilbert is even and the Holst term odd; at the level of the forms it is oddness under the internal reflection alone.

Pure transport (all of $\so(2,4)$, or the parabolic algebra of $X$) and the frozen point alone each admit only the Killing form, whose density is the Chern-Weil form, closed and without field equations. With the canonical tractor alone and the field strength unrestricted there is no internally odd density; on the subspace where the field strength annihilates $X$ there is one, which on the normal tractor connection is the Weyl square. With the connection reduced by $I$ and both data present the space is three-dimensional: the Chern-Weil form, a Holst-type form $H$ built from the Lorentz block, and $\epsilon(I, X, F, F)$, which equals $\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$. Only the last is parity-invariant. Its frame equation is the stored Einstein equation with cosmological constant (rank 10, Weyl kernel). The Holst-type form is not topological, but its frame equation vanishes whenever the curvature obeys the first Bianchi identity, so it changes nothing without torsion; under the Einstein-Cartan coupling spinning matter sources torsion and its coefficient becomes physical.

So, inside the curvature-only class with the reduction by $I$, parity selects the MacDowell-Mansouri functional up to its normalisation, which stays free; without parity, uniqueness holds exactly when the coupling is torsion-free. Inside the class its Euler, Einstein-Hilbert and volume terms come in fixed ratio: the field equations' $\Lambda$ is the frozen point's, and the Euler term cannot be cancelled. Allowing the soldering form $DV$ as a separate ingredient adds three invariants and frees those ratios. Not reducing by $I$ gives six invariant forms. No inverse frame forces the reduction for slots built from the two gauge fields $(\hb, \Omega)$ alone (an independent special-conformal field would also be inverse-frame-free), since the only admissible special-conformal slot built from them is a constant multiple of the frame, which makes a constant scale tractor, a frozen point, parallel.
synthesis.curvature-only-tractor-actions.lay: The series borrows a formula for the action of gravity, the rule from which Einstein's equations follow. This result asks which rules of the same general kind could be built from the series' own ingredients: its six-dimensional connection, its frozen point and its canonical direction. Rules built from the connection alone, or with the frozen point alone, have no effect on the equations. With the connection tied to the frozen point and the canonical direction added, there are exactly two rules with effect. One is the borrowed formula. The other has no effect unless matter spins. Requiring the rule to respect mirror symmetry of space and of the internal directions together keeps only the borrowed formula, up to its overall strength, which is still not fixed.

proofs.main:
\emph{Reduction to quadratic forms.} Under (P) and (C) an admissible density is a polynomial in the field strength $F$ whose coefficients are polynomials in the algebraic data $I$, $X$ (or $V$), formed with wedge products and no background form (a fixed coordinate four-form is not a field of the series). A product of $k$ factors $F$ is a $2k$-form, so a four-form on four-dimensional spacetime is homogeneous of degree two in $F$; two-forms commute under the wedge product, so $L = B(F \wedge F)$ for a symmetric bilinear form $B$ on the values of $F$, depending on the data. A gauge transformation acts on the values by $F \mapsto UF\tilde{U}$ with $U$ a rotor of the gauge group, and on the data by $V \mapsto UV\tilde{U}$; (G) is invariance under these. With $V$ ranging over its orbit $\{Q(V) = -3/\Lambda,\ \ip{V}{I} = 0\}$ under the stabiliser of $I$, the form $B_{V}$ is fixed by $B_{V_{0}}$ at one point $V_{0}$, which must be invariant under the stabiliser of $(I, V_{0})$; conversely the three forms $K$, $H$, $M$ below are polynomial in $V$, so each invariant $B_{V_{0}}$ extends polynomially. The problem is therefore the finite one of computing the invariant symmetric bilinear forms of a Lie algebra of bivectors on a space of bivectors.

\emph{The counts (i) to (iii).} The infinitesimal invariance condition $B([\xi, u], v) + B(u, [\xi, v]) = 0$ for $\xi$ in a spanning set of the algebra is a homogeneous linear system on the coefficients of $B$; the check solves it exactly over the rationals, with the stabilisers computed as the bivectors $\xi$ with $\xi \times I = 0$ (and $\xi \times V = 0$), dimensions $10$ and $6$, at $\Lambda \in \{3, -3, \tfrac97\}$. Results: $\so(2,4)$ on all bivectors, $1$; its parabolic algebra of the line of $X$ (the stabiliser of $X$ with the dilation $\nO \wedge \nInf$, which maps $X$ to itself), $1$; the stabiliser of $X$ alone on all bivectors, $2$, with no form odd under the internal reflection in $e_{1}$ (which fixes $X$); the stabiliser of $X$ on $\Lambda^{2}(X^{\perp})$, which is the stabiliser of $X$ as a space, $2$, exactly one of them internally odd (on this subspace $\epsilon(I, X, F, G)$ depends on $I$ only through $\ip{X}{I}$; it is not the restriction of an invariant form on all bivectors, since those restrict to even forms); the stabiliser of $I$ on $\Lambda^{2}(I^{\perp})$, $1$; the stabiliser of $(I, V)$ on $\Lambda^{2}(I^{\perp})$, $3$; on all bivectors, $6$. These agree with the representation count: $\so(2,4)$, $\so(1,4)$ and $\so(2,3)$ are simple, so their invariant symmetric forms are the multiples of the Killing form, while under the Lorentz algebra $\Lambda^{2}(I^{\perp}) = \Lambda^{2}W \oplus (W \wedge V)$, with two invariant forms on $\Lambda^{2}W$ (the scalar and pseudoscalar contractions) and one on $W \wedge V$, and no cross term since $\Lambda^{2}W$ and $W$ share no irreducible summand. The check confirms that $K$, $H$ and $M$ lie in the three-dimensional space and are independent, that $M$ computed with $X$ in place of $V$ is the same form (because $V - X = -\tfrac{3}{\Lambda}I$ and $I \wedge I = 0$), that the internal reflection $u \mapsto e_{1}ue_{1}^{-1}$, which fixes $I$ and $V$, fixes $K$ and $H$ and reverses $M$, that the odd subspace is exactly the multiples of $M$ and the even one is spanned by $K$ and $H$, and that of the three only $K$ is invariant under the whole stabiliser of $I$.

\emph{Chern-Weil forms are topological.} If $B$ is invariant under the algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ in which $A$ takes values, then $dB(F \wedge F) = 2B(DF \wedge F) = 0$ by the Bianchi identity $DF = 0$, the density is locally $d$ of the Chern-Simons form of $A$, and its Euler-Lagrange derivative vanishes identically (Chern-Weil theory and Chern and Simons 1974, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-chern-weil-and-chern-simons-forms}(a), (b)). This gives the topological statements of (i), (ii) and the $K$ part of (iii); for a connection valued in the stabiliser of $X$ it makes both invariant forms on $\Lambda^{2}(X^{\perp})$ Chern-Weil. On the normal tractor connection, which is not valued in the stabiliser of $X$ although its field strength annihilates $X$ when the torsion vanishes, the odd form is not topological: it is the Weyl square (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-integrand-on-tractor-transport-is-weyl-squared}(iii)).

\emph{Parity.} The internal reflection acts on the values only, with the spacetime orientation fixed. The integral of a four-form changes sign under reversal of the spacetime orientation, so under the combined parity (orientation reversal together with the internal reflection, the frame identifying the two) a density odd under the internal reflection is invariant and an internally even one changes sign. Hence $M$ (and its Euler, Einstein-Hilbert and volume parts) is even under the combined parity and $K$, $H$ (Pontryagin and Holst type) are odd, the usual assignment.

\emph{Field equations (iv).} Let $B$ be invariant only under the Lorentz algebra $\mathfrak{h}$ of $(I, V)$ and write $A = \omega + \theta$ with $\omega$ in $\mathfrak{h}$ and $\theta(a) = \hb^{-1}(a) \wedge V/Q(V)$ in the complement $W \wedge V$: in the gauge $V$ constant this is the general connection preserving $I$, the field variable for every field (on Einstein fields it is the connection of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}(v)). Then $dB(P \wedge R) = B(D_{\omega}P \wedge R) \pm B(P \wedge D_{\omega}R)$, $D_{A} = D_{\omega} + [\theta, \cdot\,]$, and $D_{\omega}F = -[\theta, F]$ by the Bianchi identity, so for a variation $\delta A$,
\[
\delta B(F \wedge F) = 2\,dB(\delta A \wedge F) + 2B([\theta, \delta A] \wedge F) - 2B(\delta A \wedge [\theta, F]) .
\]
For $H$ and $M$, which see only the $\Lambda^{2}W$ block, and a frame variation $\delta A = \delta\hb^{-1} \wedge V/Q(V)$ in $W \wedge V$, the last term vanishes and $[\theta, \delta A]$ is a nonzero multiple of $\hb^{-1} \wedge \delta\hb^{-1}$ in $\Lambda^{2}W$, so the frame equation is the three-form $B(e \wedge \delta e \wedge F_{W})$ with $e = \hb^{-1}$ and $F_{W} = -R + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}e \wedge e$ the Lorentz block (the store's sign, vanishing on the de Sitter field). At a point, with the frame the identity and $R$ any of the $36$ curvature two-forms with values in $\Lambda^{2}W$, the check evaluates the sixteen components $E_{B}(d, u) = \sum\epsilon^{d\nu\rho\sigma}B(u \wedge e_{\nu}, F_{W}(\rho, \sigma))$. The first Bianchi identity (the cyclic sum of $R(\rho\sigma) \cdot e_{\tau}$, which is $DT$ in Cartan's structure equations, a labelled reading) cuts out a $20$-dimensional space, the algebraic curvature tensors. For $M$ the map has rank $10$ there (the Weyl kernel of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.macdowell-mansouri-principle-fixes-the-trace-free-part}(ii)) and rank $16$ on all $36$, it vanishes on the de Sitter curvature $R(\rho\sigma) = \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}e_{\rho} \wedge e_{\sigma}$ and not at three times it, and its value at $R = 0$ (the volume term) is nonzero. For $H$ the map is zero on the $20$ algebraic curvatures, rank $16$ on all $36$, and its value at $R = 0$ is zero. So $M$ and $H$ are not topological (their frame equations do not vanish identically), $H$ is fed only by the non-cyclic part, which is the torsion's derivative, and by the connection equation of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-einstein-cartan-matter-coupling} the torsion vanishes without spin density. With spinning matter the same Fact makes the torsion proportional to the spin density, so $H$ then changes the field equations (through the spin-spin contact term, the readings recorded in Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-lovelock-cartan-four-forms-and-holst-term}): without the parity hypothesis, uniqueness of $\kappa M$ is equivalent to a torsion-free coupling. $H$ is the Holst term up to a Pontryagin density: on $\Lambda^{2}W$ it is the scalar contraction, and $H(F_{W}, F_{W}) = H(R, R) - \tfrac{2\Lambda}{3}H(R, e \wedge e)$ because $H(e \wedge e, e \wedge e) = 0$ (Holst 1996, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-lovelock-cartan-four-forms-and-holst-term}(b), which also gives that without spin the connection equation with $H$ added still forces zero torsion).

\emph{(v).} By (iii) an admissible action is $\kappa M + \kappa' H + \kappa'' K$, and invariance under the combined parity leaves $\kappa M$; $M = \epsilon(I, V, F, F) = \epsilon(I, X, F, F)$, and $Q(I)^{-1}\kappa M$ is the frozen-point functional of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}, whose split into Gauss-Bonnet, Einstein-Cartan and cosmological terms is Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west}. The split stated is bilinearity of $M$ in $F_{W} = -R + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}e \wedge e$ with $Q(I)^{-1} = 3/\Lambda$. No invariance fixes $\kappa$. Any admissible internally odd density is a multiple of $M$, and the Lorentz Euler density $M(R, R)$ is not admissible because $R = -F_{W} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}e \wedge e$ involves $e$, a multiple of $DV$, so adding one rescales all three terms together: the Euler term cannot be removed inside the class, and the volume-to-Einstein-Hilbert ratio, hence the field equations' $\Lambda$, is the frozen point's.

\emph{(vi).} If $V$ may also enter through $DV$, then in the gauge $V$ constant $DV = [\theta, V]$ is a nonzero multiple of the soldering form $e$, a $W$-valued one-form ($\ip{V}{DV} = 0$ since $Q(V)$ is constant, $\ip{I}{DV} = 0$ since $I$ is parallel and $\ip{I}{V} = 0$). The additional four-forms are $B'(e \wedge e \wedge F)$ with $B'$ a Lorentz-invariant bilinear form on $\Lambda^{2}W \times \Lambda^{2}(I^{\perp})$, of which the check finds $2$ (the pseudoscalar contraction, Einstein-Hilbert, and the scalar one, Holst), and $e^{4}$, a multiple of the one invariant of $\Lambda^{4}W$ (volume): $3 + 2 + 1 = 6$, comparable with the Lovelock-Cartan classification in four dimensions (Mardones and Zanelli 1991, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-lovelock-cartan-four-forms-and-holst-term}(a); their list also has torsion-squared and exact terms, so the comparison is not term by term). Their coefficients are independent, so the Euler term can then be subtracted, $\Lambda$ in the field equations is a free coefficient, and the frozen point fixes only the constraint data. Without the reduction ($F$ any bivector two-form, invariance under the Lorentz algebra of $(I, V)$) the check finds $6$ invariant forms. Finally, under (T), that the special-conformal slot of the tractor gauge field is a function of $(\hb, \Omega)$ and involves no further field, it must be a $W$-valued one-form built from them, covariant, polynomial and inverse-frame-free (this step is proved as clause (i) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.inverse-frame-free-tractor-gauge-field-preserves-a-frozen-point}, and without (T) an independent slot field also satisfies (P), part (iv) there). Under (P) the covariant forms available are $e$ (degree one), the curvature and torsion (degree two) and their covariant derivatives; with no inverse frame no contraction lowers the degree and no non-constant scalar zero-form can be built, so the slot is linear in $e$ with a constant coefficient, $e \mapsto S(e)$ a Lorentz-equivariant map of $W$. The check finds the Lorentz commutant on $W$ one-dimensional, so $S = \rho\,\mathrm{id}$; then $\Theta(A) \times (\nInf + \rho\nO) = \rho A - S(A) = 0$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}(ii)), checked exactly, and not for the slot $2\rho\,\mathrm{id}$. The parallel datum is a frozen point with $\Lambda = 6\rho$. The Schouten slot of the normal tractor connection is a contraction of the curvature with the inverse frame, so the normal connection is not admissible.

\emph{Scope.} Proved: the classification within (P), (C), (G) at the stated algebras, and the field-equation ranks at a point. Imported: Chern-Weil closedness (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-chern-weil-and-chern-simons-forms}), the absence of torsion without spin (the imported coupling, with the Holst term inert by Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-lovelock-cartan-four-forms-and-holst-term}(b)), and the value of $\epsilon(I, X, F, F)$ on the normal tractor connection (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-integrand-on-tractor-transport-is-weyl-squared}); the Lovelock-Cartan comparison and the Barbero-Immirzi readings are cited, not used. Not addressed: why there should be a local action at all, and the matter coupling.

synthesis.cutoff-count-is-not-a-local-de.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = G = 1$. For $\Lambda > 0$ and $0 < M < 1/(3\sqrt{\Lambda})$ let $f(r) = 1 - 2M/r - \Lambda r^{2}/3$ be the metric function of the Schwarzschild-de Sitter field on flat spacetime, in the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand gauge $\hb = 1 - \beta P$, $P(a) = (a \cdot e_{t})\,e_{r}$, $\beta^{2} = 2M/r + \Lambda r^{2}/3 = 1 - f(r)$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), with black-hole horizon $r_{b}$ and cosmological horizon $r_{c}$, $2M < r_{b} < 3M < r_{c}$, surface gravities $\kappa_{b} = f'(r_{b})/2 = (3M - r_{b})/r_{b}^{2}$ and $\kappa_{c} = -f'(r_{c})/2$ for the Killing field $\partial_{t}$, the physical vector field $K = \hb^{-1}(e_{t})$, $A_{b} = 4\pi r_{b}^{2}$, $u = 2M/r_{b} \in (\tfrac23, 1)$, and $w_{h} = 2M/r_{b}^{3}$ the radial eigenvalue of the electric part of the Weyl tensor at the horizon, the eigenvalue of the Weyl map $\mathcal{W}$ of the field strength on the radial plane $\sigma_{r}$ in the store's sign. The interior near $r = 0$ has the Kasner wall, exponents and boundary data of the Schwarzschild interior (Theorem \claimref{interior.schwarzschild-de-sitter-weighted-limit}), so the count rules read verbatim on it.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The cutoff does not see $\Lambda$.)} The measure of the exceptional set (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.exceptional-boundary-measure-one-calibration}(ii)) is $\mu_{E} = \lim_{\tau\to0}V(\tau)/\tau = 12\pi M$ per unit Killing time for every $\Lambda$; $\Lambda$ enters $V$ and $\tau$ only at relative order $\Lambda r^{3}/M$. On the slice $r_{c}^{3} = 2M$ of (C1) (Proposition \claimref{singularity.stretched-singularity-count}) the volume rate is $8\pi M\sqrt{1 - r_{c}/2M + \Lambda/3}$ exactly, so $8\pi M$ at leading order in $(2M)^{-2/3}$ and $\Lambda$ (Planck units; $\Lambda M^{2}$ may stay finite).
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The count over the hole's period.)} Let the counted epoch be the hole's modular period $2\pi/\kappa_{b}$: this reads (IC), which the store states for Schwarzschild, with a horizon's modular period, as it gives at $\Lambda = 0$ (Theorem \claimref{scrambling.epoch-modular-period-two-unknowns-become}), and the density be fixed by the area law at $\Lambda = 0$ ($\nu' = 1/24\pi$ in the 1-nat convention for (C2$'$), equivalently the registered density for (C1) and (C2)). Then the count $N$ and its entropy at mean mode entropy $\langle s\rangle_{0}$ satisfy, exactly for (C2$'$) and at leading order for (C1) and (C2),
\[
\frac{N\langle s\rangle_{0}}{A_{b}/4} \;=\; \frac{M}{\kappa_{b}r_{b}^{2}} \;=\; \frac{u}{3u - 2} \;=\; \frac{1}{1 - 2\Lambda/(3w_{h})} ,
\]
equal to $1$ at $\Lambda = 0$, strictly larger for $\Lambda > 0$, increasing in $\Lambda M^{2}$ and unbounded as $9\Lambda M^{2} \to 1$ (the Nariai limit, $\kappa_{b} \to 0$). Read as an entropy per unit horizon area, the count gives $\tfrac14/(1 - 2\Lambda/3w_{h})$. On this one-parameter family every quantity is a function of $u$; this is that function written through the Ricci curvature ($\Lambda$, the Ricci map $\mathcal{R}(a) = \Lambda a$) and the radial Weyl eigenvalue ($w_{h}$) of the field strength at the horizon, a relabelling which shows that the ratio is not one constant, not that the count is a local density.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(No horizon period gives the area law.)} $N\langle s\rangle_{0} = A_{b}/4$ holds exactly for the epoch $2\pi r_{b}^{2}/M$, the period of $M/r_{b}^{2}$, the part of the surface gravity without $\Lambda$. For $\Lambda > 0$, $\kappa_{c} < \kappa_{b} < M/r_{b}^{2}$, so either horizon's modular period gives a count above $A_{b}/4$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Consequences.)} Under the identification of the hole's horizon modes with its cutoff modes (one mode set, Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise}), the literal count assigns the hole's horizon the entropy $(A_{b}/4)\,u/(3u - 2)$, while the Clausius relation along the family with the series' temperatures and zero entropy at zero mass gives $A_{b}/4$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.sds-clausius-fixes-area-constant}); the two disagree for every $\Lambda > 0$. Under the area-law hypothesis of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy} (the counted modes carry $A_{b}/4$), the mean entropy per counted mode is $\langle s\rangle = \langle s\rangle_{0}(3u - 2)/u < \langle s\rangle_{0} \le \ln 2$, so the counted modes' Killing weights in units of $\kappa_{b}$ must grow with $\Lambda/w_{h}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boundary-mode-thermal-entropy}): no weight law fixed in units of the surface gravity, such as $\omega_{k} = \kappa k$, reconciles the count with the area law on this family, and at the registered zero-weight value for $\Lambda = 0$ every $\Lambda > 0$ needs nonzero weights. Every weight law the store states is of that kind (zero weight, the registered residue's case with one mode per counted unit; $\kappa k$ of version 2 of Premise (Q); $\kappa(k + \tfrac12)$, the offset of its version 3; $0$ or $\pm\kappa$ under the unadopted clock hypothesis (K)), so under one mode set the literal count contradicts $A_{b}/4$ for each of them. Under Premise (Q) no assignment escapes. Without its weight clause (Q-w), an affine law $\omega_{k} = ck + d$ with $c$ depending on $\Lambda/w_{h}$, in the class characterised by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.q-splits-maximum-entropy-affine-weights}(ii), would escape; no stored result adopts one, and on modes shared by the two sheets of an edge, where (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) forces zero weight (filed alongside, synthesis.r-loc-needs-sheet-labelled-modes), that escape is closed as well.
\item[(v)] \emph{(For clause (Loc).)} The cutoff count per unit horizon area per modular period is curvature-independent on the $\Lambda = 0$ family only. So clause (Loc) of the local-horizon premise is not a consequence of (C1), (C2) and (IC), read with a horizon's modular period, with one mode set: the count reading $\eta = 4\pi\nu\langle s\rangle$ fails to be a curvature-independent density on Schwarzschild-de Sitter, and a curvature-independent density can come only from a placement of the modes on the horizon with a density fixed by flat data, which restates (Loc). As with the literal Kerr count, the disagreement counts against the literal cutoff placement and (IC) away from $\Lambda = 0$, not against (Loc).
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.cutoff-count-is-not-a-local-de.technical: Clause (Loc) of the local-horizon premise says the entropy per unit area of a small horizon does not depend on the curvature (the gravitational field strength) or the matter at the point. The constructive hope is that this follows from what the counted modes are: if the series' boundary modes, placed at the curvature cutoff inside a hole and counted over one modular period, always add up to a fixed multiple of the horizon area, the density they define would be universal. This result tests that hope on the one family beyond Schwarzschild where the store's count rules apply verbatim, Schwarzschild-de Sitter, whose singularity is the same Kasner wall. The cutoff's volume rate does not feel the cosmological constant at all ($12\pi M$ on the exceptional set), but the hole's modular period does: the surface gravity drops from $M/r_{b}^{2}$ to $(3M - r_{b})/r_{b}^{2}$. So with the density calibrated on Schwarzschild, the count over one period exceeds the area law by the factor $u/(3u - 2)$, which, written through the field strength at the horizon, is $1/(1 - 2\Lambda/3w_{h})$ ($w_{h}$ the radial Weyl eigenvalue): an entropy per unit area that is not one constant, and diverging as the hole approaches the Nariai limit. Neither horizon's period fixes it; only the period of the $\Lambda$-free part of the surface gravity would. Hence the count does not supply (Loc); under the identification of horizon and cutoff modes it contradicts the hole's Clausius entropy $A_{b}/4$ for every positive $\Lambda$, as the literal Kerr count does for every spin; and if the counted modes are to carry $A_{b}/4$, their mean entropy, and so their weights, must depend on the curvature ratio. For physical holes the discrepancy is tiny, of relative size $\tfrac83\Lambda M^{2}$, but it is exact and grows without bound towards Nariai.
synthesis.cutoff-count-is-not-a-local-de.lay: The local-horizon assumption says that every small piece of horizon carries the same entropy per unit area, whatever the strength of the gravitational field there. One might hope to derive this from the series' own way of counting a black hole's quantum modes, which sit deep inside the hole near the singularity and are counted over one tick of the horizon's thermal clock. For an ordinary black hole this count gives exactly a quarter of the horizon area. In a universe with a cosmological constant, the black hole's thermal clock slows down while the region near the singularity is unchanged, so the same counting gives more than a quarter of the area, and much more for the largest holes a positive cosmological constant allows. Measured per unit of horizon area, the count's entropy changes from hole to hole as the cosmological constant's share of the gravitational field strength at the horizon changes. So the counting rule cannot be the reason the entropy per area is universal; that has to be assumed or come from modes placed on the horizon itself.

proofs.main:
Read in Gauge Theory Gravity, $f$ below is the metric function of the Schwarzschild-de Sitter field in the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand gauge, $\beta^{2} = 1 - f$, its Killing field is $K = \hb^{-1}(e_{t})$ and the curvature is the field strength (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}, clauses (iv) and (vi)). \emph{Setting.} Units $\hbar = c = G = 1$ and $f(r) = 1 - 2M/r - \Lambda r^{2}/3$. For $\Lambda > 0$ and $9\Lambda M^{2} < 1$, $f$ has two positive zeros $r_{b} < r_{c}$ and a negative one $-(r_{b} + r_{c})$; by Vieta, $\Lambda/3 = 1/(r_{b}^{2} + r_{b}r_{c} + r_{c}^{2})$ and $2M = (\Lambda/3)\,r_{b}r_{c}(r_{b} + r_{c})$, and $f(r_{b}) = 0$ gives $\Lambda r_{b}^{2}/3 = 1 - u$ with $u = 2M/r_{b}$. Since $f(2M) = -4\Lambda M^{2}/3 < 0$ and $f$ is negative below $r_{b}$, $r_{b} > 2M$; and $f'(r_{b}) > 0$ gives $\kappa_{b} = M/r_{b}^{2} - \Lambda r_{b}/3 = (3M - r_{b})/r_{b}^{2} > 0$, so $r_{b} < 3M$ and $u \in (\tfrac23, 1)$. Inside $r_{b}$ near $r = 0$ the region is the interior of Theorem \claimref{interior.schwarzschild-de-sitter-weighted-limit}: same Kasner exponents, boundary data and wall as Schwarzschild, with corrections of relative order $\Lambda r^{3}/M$. So the placement rules (C1), (C2), and their leading-order form (C2$'$) on the exceptional set (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.exceptional-boundary-measure-one-calibration}), apply on this family as written.

\emph{(i)} Write $A(r) = -f(r) = (2M/r)\,U(r)$ with $U = 1 - r/2M + \Lambda r^{3}/6M$. The proper time to the wall is $\tau(r) = \int_{0}^{r}A^{-1/2}\,dr'$ and the three-volume per unit Killing time of the slice at $r$ is $V = 4\pi r^{2}\sqrt{A}$. With $r = \rho^{2}$, $\tau = (2M)^{-1/2}\int_{0}^{\rho}2\rho'^{2}U^{-1/2}\,d\rho'$ and $V = 4\pi(2M)^{1/2}\rho^{3}U^{1/2}$; both are power series in $\rho$ starting at $\rho^{3}$, with leading coefficients $\tfrac23(2M)^{-1/2}$ and $4\pi(2M)^{1/2}$, so $\mu_{E} = \lim V/\tau = 12\pi M$. $\Lambda$ appears in $U$ only through $\rho^{6} = r^{3}$, hence in $V$ and $\tau$ only from relative order $\Lambda r^{3}/M$, and not in $\mu_{E}$. On the slice $r_{c}^{3} = 2M$, $(4\pi r_{c}^{2})^{2}A(r_{c}) = 16\pi^{2}r_{c}^{4}(2M/r_{c})(1 - r_{c}/2M + \Lambda r_{c}^{3}/6M) = 64\pi^{2}M^{2}(1 - r_{c}/2M + \Lambda/3)$, using $r_{c}^{3} = 2M$, which is the stated rate; Proposition \claimref{singularity.stretched-singularity-count} is its $\Lambda = 0$ case. In Planck units the corrections are $O((2M)^{-2/3})$ and $O(\Lambda)$; both vanish in the limit $M \to \infty$, $\Lambda \to 0$ at fixed $\Lambda M^{2}$, in which $u$ stays fixed.

\emph{(ii)} With the epoch $\Delta t$ and $\nu'$ modes per Planck area of $\mu_{E}$, $N = \nu'\mu_{E}\Delta t = 12\pi\nu' M\,\Delta t$, exactly for (C2$'$); for (C1) and (C2), $N = 8\pi\nu M\,\Delta t$ at leading order, the same number with $\nu = \tfrac32\nu'$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.exceptional-boundary-measure-one-calibration}(iii)). The products below do not depend on the normalisation of $\partial_{t}$, since $\mu_{E}$ is per unit $t$ and the periods are in $t$. At $\Lambda = 0$, Theorem \claimref{scrambling.epoch-modular-period-two-unknowns-become} gives the epoch $8\pi M$ under (IC) and the area law fixes the density: $\nu'\langle s\rangle_{0}\cdot 12\pi M\cdot 8\pi M = 4\pi M^{2}$, so $\nu'\langle s\rangle_{0} = 1/24\pi$ (in the 1-nat convention, $\langle s\rangle_{0} = 1$, $\nu' = 1/24\pi$; in the capacity convention $\langle s\rangle_{0} = \ln 2$). With the hole's period $\Delta t = 2\pi/\kappa_{b}$,
\[
\frac{N\langle s\rangle_{0}}{\pi r_{b}^{2}} = \frac{1}{24\pi}\cdot\frac{12\pi M\cdot 2\pi}{\kappa_{b}\,\pi r_{b}^{2}} = \frac{M}{\kappa_{b}r_{b}^{2}} = \frac{M}{3M - r_{b}} = \frac{u}{3u - 2} .
\]
With $w_{h} = 2M/r_{b}^{3}$, the radial eigenvalue of the electric part of the Weyl tensor, $2\Lambda/(3w_{h}) = \Lambda r_{b}^{3}/3M = (1 - u)\,r_{b}/M = 2(1 - u)/u$, so $1 - 2\Lambda/3w_{h} = (3u - 2)/u$ and the ratio is $1/(1 - 2\Lambda/3w_{h})$. It equals $1$ at $u = 1$ ($\Lambda = 0$); its derivative in $u$ is $-2/(3u - 2)^{2} < 0$, and $u$ decreases as $\Lambda M^{2}$ grows ($r_{b}$ increases with $\Lambda$ at fixed $M$, since $\partial_{\Lambda}f < 0$ and $f'(r_{b}) > 0$), so the ratio increases, and it diverges as $u \to \tfrac23$, $r_{b} \to 3M$, $9\Lambda M^{2} \to 1$, where $\kappa_{b} \to 0$. For small $\Lambda M^{2}$, $u = 1 - \tfrac43\Lambda M^{2} + O(\Lambda^{2}M^{4})$ and the ratio is $1 + \tfrac83\Lambda M^{2} + O(\Lambda^{2}M^{4})$. Dividing the count's entropy by $A_{b} = 4\pi r_{b}^{2}$ gives $\eta_{\mathrm{count}} = \tfrac14/(1 - 2\Lambda/3w_{h})$; $\Lambda = \tfrac14 R$ is the Ricci part and $w_{h}$ the Weyl eigenvalue of the curvature at every point of the horizon.

\emph{(iii)} $N\langle s\rangle_{0} = \pi r_{b}^{2}$ requires $12\pi M\Delta t/24\pi = \pi r_{b}^{2}$, that is $\Delta t = 2\pi r_{b}^{2}/M$. Since $r_{b} > 2M$, $\kappa_{b} = M/r_{b}^{2} - \Lambda r_{b}/3 < M/r_{b}^{2}$. For the cosmological horizon, scale $r_{b} = 1$ and write $x = r_{c} > 1$: then $\Lambda/3 = 1/(1 + x + x^{2})$, $M = x(1 + x)/(2(1 + x + x^{2}))$ and $\kappa_{c} = \Lambda r_{c}/3 - M/r_{c}^{2} = (2x^{2} - x - 1)/(2x(1 + x + x^{2}))$, so $\kappa_{c} < M$ is $2x^{2} - x - 1 < x^{2}(1 + x)$, that is $x^{3} - x^{2} + x + 1 > 0$, true for $x \ge 1$ since $x^{3} - x^{2} \ge 0$. With $\kappa_{c} < \kappa_{b}$ (the check verifies it on five rational families with both horizons rational; it is not needed for the conclusion, which uses only $\kappa_{c}, \kappa_{b} < M/r_{b}^{2}$), both periods exceed $2\pi r_{b}^{2}/M$ and both counts exceed $A_{b}/4$.

\emph{(iv)} Under one mode set, the hole's horizon modes are its cutoff modes, so the count's entropy $N\langle s\rangle$ is the hole's horizon entropy. Theorem \claimref{synthesis.sds-clausius-fixes-area-constant}(i),(ii) gives $S_{b} = A_{b}/4$ under the series' temperatures, the Clausius relation along the family and $S_{b} \to 0$ as $M \to 0$. With $\langle s\rangle = \langle s\rangle_{0}$ the two disagree by the factor of (ii) for every $\Lambda > 0$. If instead the counted modes are required to carry $A_{b}/4$ (the area-law hypothesis of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}), then $N\langle s\rangle = A_{b}/4$ with $N$ as in (ii) gives $\langle s\rangle = \langle s\rangle_{0}(3u - 2)/u$. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boundary-mode-thermal-entropy}, $s(x)$ is even, strictly decreasing in $|x|$ and at most $\ln 2$, with $x = 2\pi\omega/\kappa_{b}$; a smaller mean entropy needs larger $|x|$ for some counted modes. So the weights in units of $\kappa_{b}$ cannot be the same on all members of the family, and if they are all zero at $\Lambda = 0$ (the registered value, the equality case of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}(ii)) they are not all zero for any $\Lambda > 0$. A law $\omega_{k} = \kappa_{b}k$ fixes every $x_{k} = 2\pi k$ and hence $\langle s\rangle$, so it cannot follow $(3u - 2)/u$. The same holds for every weight law the store states: the zero weight of the registered residue (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}(ii)), $\kappa k$, $\kappa(k + \tfrac12)$ and the values $0, \pm\kappa$ of the unadopted clock hypothesis are all fixed multiples of the surface gravity, each fixing $\langle s\rangle$ on the family (by a search of the store's weight assignments; none involves $\Lambda$ except through $\kappa$). Under Premise (Q), whose clause (Q-w) sets the slope $c = \kappa$, no assignment escapes. The affine class $\omega_{k} = ck + d$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.q-splits-maximum-entropy-affine-weights}(ii) leaves $c$ free, so without (Q-w) a slope depending on $\Lambda/w_{h}$ could follow $(3u - 2)/u$; no stored result adopts one, and on modes shared by the two sheets of an edge (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) forces zero weight (filed alongside, synthesis.r-loc-needs-sheet-labelled-modes).

\emph{(v)} By (ii) the count, read as an entropy per unit area of the hole's horizon, depends on $\Lambda/w_{h}$, so it is not one constant (on a one-parameter family this curvature form is a relabelling of the dependence on $u$; what matters is that the ratio varies), and in particular not a density depending only on the flat tangent data. A derivation of (Loc) from (C1), (C2) and (IC), read with a horizon's modular period, with one mode set would have to make the count a fixed multiple of the area on every family to which these rules apply; Schwarzschild-de Sitter is such a family and the multiple varies. A curvature-independent density is obtained by placing modes on the horizon with a density fixed by flat data (per unit area and unit rapidity), which is (Loc) restated in the language of modes. (IC) is stated in the store for Schwarzschild (epoch $8\pi M$); reading it on this family with a horizon's modular period is the assumption of (ii), and (iii) shows that no horizon period removes the disagreement. As for the literal Kerr count (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kerr-ring-count-misses-area-law}, cited as a parallel and not used), the conflict is between the cutoff count and $A_{b}/4$, and it bears on the literal cutoff placement and on (IC) with a horizon period away from $\Lambda = 0$, not on (Loc), whose value $\tfrac14$ agrees with $A_{b}/4$.

\emph{Remarks.} (a) The physical size is small: for a hole of the mass of the Sun in Planck units ($M \sim 10^{38}$) and the observed $\Lambda \sim 10^{-122}$, $\tfrac83\Lambda M^{2} \sim 10^{-46}$; the result is structural, not observational. (b) The statement uses the cosmological constant only as a Ricci curvature at the horizon; it does not use any premise about the frozen point. (c) The cosmological horizon carries its own modes in the store (with an unfixed count), and is not part of this comparison.

\emph{The check.} Exact power series (GA.ps\_pow\_rat, GA.ps\_int) for $\tau$ and $V$ in $\rho$ give $\mu_{E} = 12\pi M$ for four masses with $2M$ a square and four values of $\Lambda$ (including $0$ and a negative one), and show that $\Lambda$ first moves the series at relative order $\rho^{6}$; the (C1) volume identity is checked at three rational $r_{c}$ and three $\Lambda$. The ratio of (ii) is computed from $\nu' = 1/24\pi$, $\mu_{E}$ and $2\pi/\kappa_{b}$, with $f(r_{b}) = 0$ and $\kappa_{b} = f'(r_{b})/2$ checked, on five rational $r_{b}$ from $2M$ towards $3M$ (values $1, \tfrac{10}{9}, 2, 10, 100$), and compared with $u/(3u - 2)$ and $1/(1 - 2\Lambda/3w_{h})$; towards Nariai it exceeds $10^{j}/3$ at $r_{b} = 3M - M/10^{j}$. On five rational families with both horizons rational the needed epoch is $2\pi r_{b}^{2}/M$ and $0 < \kappa_{c} < \kappa_{b} < M/r_{b}^{2}$; the polynomial inequality of (iii) is checked on $192$ ratios. The forced mean entropy $(3u - 2)/u$ is checked on four members.

synthesis.duality-complex-structure-does.formal:
Work in $\Cl(2,4)$ in the chart of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection} with $X = \nO$ and $I = \nInf + \rho\nO$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector} for $\rho = \Lambda/6 \neq 0$). Let $I_{4} = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}$ and $J(B) = I_{4}B$ on spacetime bivectors (here $J$ is this Hodge star, not the unit $J = e_{2}e_{3}$ of the radial atom), the Hodge star of Lemma \claimref{correspondence.lorentzian-duality-complex-structure}. For a Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ of bivectors (commutator product) its commutant is the set of linear maps $T$ of $\mathfrak{g}$ with $T[x, y] = [x, Ty]$ for all $x, y$; a complex structure on $\mathfrak{g}$ making it a complex Lie algebra lies in it.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Duality is the Lorentz commutant; proved, standard.)} The commutant of $\so(1,3)$ is spanned by $\id$ and $J$, with $J^{2} = -\id$. The commutant of the stabiliser of $I$ (ten-dimensional) is $\mathbb{R}\,\id$ for every $\rho$, of de Sitter, anti-de Sitter and Poincar\'e type, and so are those of the parabolic algebra stabilising the line of $X$ (eleven-dimensional, the algebra that gauges the tractor field) and of $\so(2,4)$. Hence none of these carries a complex structure commuting with its bracket, and $J$ preserves neither the stabiliser of $I$ nor the parabolic algebra. This is the standard fact that $\so(1,3)$, with $J$ as its complex unit, is a complex Lie algebra (the complex Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ over $\mathrm{span}\{\id, J\}$) and the others are not.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The frozen-point pairing is the duality pairing; proved.)} On spacetime bivectors $\epsilon_{X}(B, B') := \epsilon(I, X, B, B') = -\langle B\,I_{4}\,B'\rangle_{0} = -K(B, JB')$ with $K(B, B') = \langle BB'\rangle_{0}$, for every $\rho$. With the central unit $I_{7}$ of the odd extension $\Cl(3,4)$ of $\Cl(2,4)$ (conventions, U3: it commutes with every element of $\Cl(2,4)$, so the slots may be complexified by it; it is a scalar unit for the pairings and is not identified with the Hodge star $J$), $I_{7}^{2} = -1$, the pairings $\epsilon_{X} + \tau K$ at $\tau = \pm I_{7}$ are $\pm I_{7} K(B, (1 \pm I_{7}J)B')$, the self-dual and anti-self-dual pairings.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Slot Hessian of the chiral family; proved.)} Vary the special-conformal slot $S$ of the unreduced field $\Omega - \nInf \wedge \hb^{-1} + \nO \wedge S$ (frame components, $\hb = 1$ at a point), whose spacetime block is $-\mathcal{R} + T_{S}$. The Hessian of $K(T_{S} \wedge T_{S})$ vanishes on the symmetric slot (lowered indices), the symmetric and antisymmetric slots decouple for both pairings, the Hessian of $\epsilon_{X}$ has rank sixteen, and on the antisymmetric slot $\det(H_{\epsilon} + \tau H_{K}) = -4096\,(1 + \tau^{2})^{3}$. So the slot Hessian of $\epsilon_{X} + \tau K$ is nondegenerate for every real $\tau$ and degenerate exactly at the chiral values $\tau = \pm I_{7}$, with a complex kernel of dimension three in the antisymmetric slot.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Every chirality returns the Schouten slot; proved, standard in content.)} At $\tau = 0$ the Schouten slot is the unique stationary slot of $\epsilon_{X}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-reduces-the-connection-only-when-infinitely-stiff}(iii)); the extension claimed here is to the chiral family. For torsion-free $\Omega$ the slot gradient of $K(F \wedge F)$ also vanishes at the Schouten slot $S = \Sch$. Hence $\Sch$ is a stationary slot of $\epsilon_{X} + \tau K$ for every $\tau$: the only one for real $\tau$, and at $\tau = \pm I_{7}$ the only one up to a free antisymmetric slot in the kernel of (iii), which leaves the density and its equations unchanged (the connection, not the equations, is undetermined there). At $\Sch$ the spacetime block is $-\mathcal{W}$ and the density is $\tfrac14 W_{abcd}W^{abcd} + \tau K(\mathcal{W} \wedge \mathcal{W})$, the Weyl square plus $\tau$ times the Pontryagin-type density of the Weyl curvature, the standard statement that the chiral Weyl square is the Weyl square plus a Pontryagin term. With torsion the $K$ gradient at the corresponding Schouten slot does not vanish.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} Self-dual (Ashtekar, Plebanski) field spaces are built from a self-dual projection of a Lorentz connection, with an independent Lorentz connection and frame (or two-forms reducing to one) as input: they take the first-order field space as given rather than derive it, and their simplicity and reality conditions are not analysed here. In the series the projection is the stored Hodge star, and by (i) it acts only on the Lorentz algebra, which is present in the normal tractor setting and in the reduced one alike, so it distinguishes neither the parabolic (normal tractor) field space nor the connections preserving $I$. Applied to the frozen-point integrand with the slot varied, every chirality returns the normal tractor slot, (iv): the duality complex structure does not supply the reduction by the frozen point, which the store records as Premise \claimref{synthesis.field-space-premise-parallel-frozen-point}. The result is transport-absent: the series' objects enter only as notation for standard Lie-theoretic and curvature facts.
synthesis.duality-complex-structure-does.technical:
Self-dual formulations of gravity (Ashtekar's variables, Plebanski's action) pick their field space by projecting a Lorentz connection onto its self-dual half. The series has the needed complex structure: the Hodge star on spacetime bivectors is multiplication by the spacetime pseudoscalar $I_{4}$, with square $-1$. Could it act on the larger algebras where the frozen point lives, or select the connections that preserve $I$?

It cannot. The maps commuting with the bracket of $\so(1,3)$ are spanned by the identity and $J$; for the ten-dimensional stabiliser of the frozen point (de Sitter, anti-de Sitter or Poincar\'e type), for the eleven-dimensional parabolic algebra that gauges the tractor field and for $\so(2,4)$ they are only the multiples of the identity, so no complex structure exists there (standard: only the Lorentz algebra is complex). The duality therefore lives on the Lorentz algebra, common to the normal and the reduced field spaces, and distinguishes neither. On the Lorentz block the frozen-point pairing is $\epsilon_{X} = -K(\cdot, J\,\cdot)$, so its self-dual version is the pairing $\epsilon_{X} + \tau K$ at $\tau = \pm I_{7}$. With the special-conformal slot varied, the Killing part is blind to the symmetric slot, the antisymmetric slot has determinant $-4096(1 + \tau^{2})^{3}$, and on torsion-free fields the Schouten map is stationary for every $\tau$. So the self-dual integrand gives conformal gravity plus a Pontryagin-type term, as the real one does; at the chiral values three complex antisymmetric slot components are left free without changing the equations. Plebanski's and Ashtekar's formulations take an independent Lorentz connection and frame as input, the first-order field space, so they adopt it rather than derive it. Transport-absent: standard facts in the series' notation.
synthesis.duality-complex-structure-does.lay: A popular reformulation of gravity splits the field into two mirror-image halves using an operation that, applied twice, gives minus one, like multiplying by the imaginary unit. The series has exactly that operation. This result asks whether it could explain which version of the gravitational field the series' action should be applied to. It finds that the operation only makes sense for ordinary spacetime rotations, which every candidate version contains, not for the larger symmetries that tell the versions apart, and that using the mirror-image half of the action changes nothing about the choice: the action still prefers the series' own transport, which gives a different theory (conformal gravity) rather than Einstein's.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} As in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-integrand-on-tractor-transport-is-weyl-squared}: generators $e_{0}, \dots, e_{5}$ with squares $(+,-,-,-,+,-)$, $\nO = \tfrac12(e_{4} + e_{5})$, $\nInf = e_{4} - e_{5}$, $I_{6} = e_{0}\cdots e_{5}$, commutator product $x \times y = \tfrac12(xy - yx)$, four-form value of a pairing $\beta$ on two-forms $\tfrac14\sum_{p}\sgn(p)\beta(F_{p_{0}p_{1}}, G_{p_{2}p_{3}})$.

\emph{(i) Commutants.} $J$ is the Hodge star of Lemma \claimref{correspondence.lorentzian-duality-complex-structure}: $I_{4}^{2} = -1$ and $I_{4}$ commutes with every even element of $\Cl(1,3)$, so $J(B) = I_{4}B$ maps spacetime bivectors to spacetime bivectors, $J^{2} = -\id$ and $J[x, B] = [x, JB]$ for $x \in \so(1,3)$: $J$ is in the commutant. The commutant is computed as the null space of the linear conditions $T\,\mathrm{ad}_{x} = \mathrm{ad}_{x}T$ for $x$ running over a basis (structure constants from the commutator product, exact over the rationals): dimension two for $\so(1,3)$ (containing $\id$ and $J$), one for $\so(2,4)$. The stabiliser of $I = \nInf + \rho\nO$ (for $\rho \neq 0$ the frozen point of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}, of de Sitter or anti-de Sitter type) is the null space of $B \mapsto B \times I$ on the fifteen bivectors, of dimension ten; its commutant has dimension one at $\rho = \tfrac37$, $-\tfrac25$ and $0$. These three values cover every case: the boost $\exp(\tfrac{\theta}{2}\nO\wedge\nInf)$ rescales $\nInf$ and $\nO$ by inverse factors, so it maps $I_{\rho}$ to a multiple of $I_{\rho e^{\mp 2\theta}}$ and conjugates the stabilisers of all $\rho$ of one sign; $\rho = 0$ is the null case. A complex structure $T$ with $T[x, y] = [x, Ty]$ lies in the commutant and squares to $-\id$, impossible in $\mathbb{R}\,\id$. The parabolic algebra (bivectors $B$ with $B \times X$ a multiple of $X$, eleven-dimensional) also has a one-dimensional commutant. In the computed bases, four of the ten elements of the stabiliser and five of the eleven of the parabolic algebra are sent by $I_{4}$ outside the bivectors, so $J$ acts on neither. This is the algebraic statement that $\so(1,3)$, with $J$ as its complex unit, is a complex Lie algebra ($\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ over $\mathrm{span}\{\id, J\}$) while the de Sitter, anti-de Sitter and Poincar\'e algebras and $\so(2,4)$ are not.

\emph{(ii) Pairings.} The check computes the Gram matrices of $\epsilon(I, X, B, B')$ and $\langle B I_{4} B'\rangle_{0}$ on the six spacetime blades at two values of $\rho$ and finds them opposite; since $I \wedge X = \nInf \wedge \nO$ does not depend on $\rho$, neither does $\epsilon_{X}$ (as in the stored theorem (ii)). Then $\epsilon_{X}(B, B') = -K(B, JB')$, and with the central unit $I_{7}$ of $\Cl(3,4)$, $I_{7}^{2} = -1$, commuting with $J$, $\epsilon_{X} + I_{7}K = I_{7}K(B, (1 + I_{7}J)B')$ and $\epsilon_{X} - I_{7}K = -I_{7}K(B, (1 - I_{7}J)B')$; $(1 \pm I_{7}J)/2$ are complementary projectors because $(I_{7}J)^{2} = \id$.

\emph{(iii) The slot Hessian.} The spacetime block of the field strength is $-\mathcal{R} + T_{S}$ with $T_{S}$ linear in $S$ (proof of the stored GTG tractor theorem (iv), slot left free). For each pairing the Hessian in $S$ is the Gram matrix of $T$ on the sixteen matrix units. In the basis of lowered-index symmetric (ten) and antisymmetric (six) slots, the check finds the $K$ Hessian zero on symmetric slots and the cross blocks of both Hessians zero; the $\epsilon_{X}$ Hessian has rank sixteen and the $K$ Hessian rank six. On the antisymmetric block $\det(H_{\epsilon} + \tau H_{K})$ is a polynomial of degree at most six in $\tau$; it equals $-4096(1 + \tau^{2})^{3}$ at the eight integers $-3, \dots, 4$, hence identically. It has no real zero, and its zeros are $\tau = \pm I_{7}$, each of multiplicity three. At $\tau = \pm I_{7}$ the complex Hessian $H_{\epsilon} \pm I_{7}H_{K}$ is represented by the real $32 \times 32$ matrix $\begin{pmatrix} H_{\epsilon} & \mp H_{K} \\ \pm H_{K} & H_{\epsilon}\end{pmatrix}$, of rank twenty-six (thirty-two at $\tau = 2I_{7}$), so the complex kernel has dimension three, in the antisymmetric slot.

\emph{(iv) Stationarity at the Schouten slot.} At $S = \Sch$ the spacetime block of a torsion-free field is $-\mathcal{W}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}(iv)). The slot gradients are $2\beta(-\mathcal{W}, T_{\delta})$ for each pairing $\beta$ and slot direction $\delta$, linear in the curvature. The algebraic curvature tensors are spanned by the one hundred Kulkarni-Nomizu products of the ten basis symmetric matrices; on each the check forms the Schouten slot and finds both gradients zero in all sixteen directions, so they vanish for every torsion-free curvature (complete). With a curvature antisymmetric in each pair only (the curvature of a rotation gauge with torsion) the $\epsilon_{X}$ gradient still vanishes at the Schouten slot of the transposed Ricci contraction, while the $K$ gradient does not. So for torsion-free fields $\Sch$ is stationary for $\epsilon_{X} + \tau K$ for every $\tau$, unique by (iii) for real $\tau$ and unique up to the three-dimensional kernel at $\tau = \pm I_{7}$, which lies in the antisymmetric slot and does not change the symmetric part. The value there is $\epsilon_{X}(\mathcal{W} \wedge \mathcal{W}) + \tau K(\mathcal{W} \wedge \mathcal{W}) = \tfrac14 W_{abcd}W^{abcd} + \tau K(\mathcal{W} \wedge \mathcal{W})$ by the stored theorem (iii); $K(F \wedge F)$ is the Chern form there (stored theorem (iv)), here evaluated on the Weyl block, the Pontryagin-type density. The real case $\tau = 0$ with the slot eliminated is the conformal-gauge construction of conformal gravity (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-conformal-gravity-bach-equations-and-conformal-gauge-form}(b)), proved in the series as Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-reduces-the-connection-only-when-infinitely-stiff}(iii); (iv) extends it to the whole chiral family. At $\tau = \pm I_{7}$ the kernel directions change neither the density nor its equations (they lie in the kernel of the Hessian and the gradient is zero there), so the equations are those of the Schouten slot while the slot itself is fixed only up to that kernel.

\emph{Scope.} Nothing here concerns the simplicity constraints of Plebanski's action or the reality conditions of Ashtekar's variables (cited from memory); those formulations take an independent Lorentz connection and frame as input, the first-order field space, so they adopt it rather than derive it.
