synthesis.einstein-condition-is-infinity.formal:
Let $g$ be the derived metric, of signature $(1,3)$, of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), write tractors in its splitting as $(\sigma, \mu_b, \rho)$, the vectors $\sigma\nInf + \mu + \rho\nO$ of $\Cl(2,4)$, with the connection of Fact \claimref{interior.imported-tractor-connection} (on flat spacetime the $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field $\Omega_{T}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}), and let $I_g = (1, 0, 0)$ be the pure-scale tractor and $X = (0, 0, 1)$ the canonical tractor, so $Q(I_g) = Q(X) = 0$ and $\ip{X}{I_g} = 1$. Call a maximal totally isotropic subspace $W$ (dimension three) of the complexified tractor space $\mathcal{T}_x \oplus \mathcal{T}_x I_{7}$, the span of the $V + I_{7}V'$ with $V, V' \in \mathcal{T}_x$ and numbers in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{7}\}$, $I_{7} = I_{6}e'$ the central unit of the odd extension $\Cl(3,4)$ (conventions U3; \claimref{std-algebra.complexification-is-the-odd-extension}), an \emph{infinity vacuum} at $x$ if $I_g \in W$ and a \emph{point vacuum} if $X \in W$; maximal isotropic subspaces come in two families, and by Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-pure-spinors-incidence-chart} the infinity (respectively point) vacua of the family attached to the conformal spinor space $\CS$ are the Fock vacua $u \in \CS$ with $c(I_g)u = 0$ (respectively $c(X)u = 0$); the other family is attached in the same way to the other half of the Fock module. For a field $W$ of such subspaces and $v \in T_xM$, a physical vector at $x$, the pairing classes of $W$ along $v$ are the values $\omega_v(w, w') := \ip{\nabla_v w}{w'}$ for $w, w' \in W$. The content is a translation of the standard equivalence ``$g$ is Einstein if and only if $\Sch(\ell,\ell) = 0$ for every null $\ell$'' into this language, not a derivation of it. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Shape.)} Every infinity vacuum is $W = \mathrm{span}(I_g, \ell, m)$ with $\ell, m$ in the $\mu$ slot spanning a totally null plane $A_W$ of the $\mu$ slot $T_xM \oplus T_xM\,I_{7}$ of that space, the complexified tangent space with the same unit $I_{7}$ (not the spacetime unit $I_{5}$ of U3); $A_W$ contains exactly one real null direction $\ell_W$, and every real null direction lies in exactly two infinity vacua. The same holds for point vacua with $X$ in place of $I_g$.
\item \emph{(Classes.)} For $w \in W$, $\omega_v(I_g, w) = -\Sch(v, w)$ for infinity vacua and $\omega_v(X, w) = g(v, w)$ for point vacua; both depend only on $W$ at $x$, not on its extension. For $W$ in the family of $\CS$, its Fock vacuum $u_W$ is annihilated by $c(\nabla_v I_g)$ if and only if $\omega_v(I_g, \cdot) = 0$ on $W$.
\item \emph{(Point vacua, in every metric.)} Every point vacuum has $\omega_{\ell_W}(X, \cdot) = 0$ on $W$: point vacua are unexcited along their own real null direction whatever $g$ is.
\item \emph{(Einstein with a free constant.)} The following are equivalent at $x$: (a) every infinity vacuum has $\omega_{\ell_W}(I_g, \ell_W) = 0$; (b) every infinity vacuum has $\omega_{\ell_W}(I_g, \cdot) = 0$ on $W$; (c) $\Sch = \tfrac{J}{4}\, g$ at $x$, that is $\Ric = \tfrac{R}{4}\, g$. If (c) holds on a connected region, $R$ is constant there (contracted Bianchi identity, Schur's argument in dimension four), and with $\Lambda := R/4$ the classes along a general direction are $\omega_v(I_g, w) = -\tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\, g(v, w)$.
\item \emph{(Ricci-flat.)} Every infinity vacuum has $\omega_v(I_g, \cdot) = 0$ on $W$ for every $v$ if and only if $\Sch = 0$, if and only if $\Ric = 0$, if and only if $\nabla I_g = 0$ (Theorem \claimref{interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equations}).
\item \emph{(One vacuum field: pure radiation.)} For a single infinity vacuum $W$ at $x$, $\omega_v(I_g, \cdot) = 0$ on $W$ for every $v$ if and only if $\Sch = c\, \ell_W^\flat \otimes \ell_W^\flat$ with $c$ real; then $J = 0$ and $\Ric = 2c\, \ell_W^\flat \otimes \ell_W^\flat$.
\item \emph{(Matter.)} For a real symmetric tensor $T$ at $x$ and a constant $G$, $\omega_{\ell_W}(I_g, \ell_W) = 4\pi G\, T(\ell_W, \ell_W)$ for every infinity vacuum if and only if $\Ric + 8\pi G\, T = h\, g$ at $x$ for some number $h$. If this holds on a connected region with $\nabla^a T_{ab} = 0$, then $h - 4\pi G\, g^{ab}T_{ab} =: \Lambda$ is constant there, and $\Ric + 8\pi G\,T = (\Lambda + 4\pi G\,g^{ab}T_{ab})\,g$ is the Einstein equation with source $T$ and cosmological constant $\Lambda$ in the store's curvature convention ($\Ric = \Lambda g$ for de Sitter space in signature $(1,3)$, so that $\Ric$ is minus the Ricci tensor of the convention in which the round sphere has positive Ricci curvature).
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.einstein-condition-is-infinity.technical: This is a translation, not a derivation: the standard equivalence ``Einstein if and only if the Schouten tensor vanishes on null directions'' is rewritten in the language of Fock vacua. For a gravitational field on flat spacetime with derived metric $g$, the stored vacuum equations say $\nabla_a I_g = (0, -\Sch_{ab}, 0)$ for the tractor gauge field. On the CAR side, the null tractor $I_g$ is a nilpotent mode operator $c(I_g)$ whose kernel on the eight-dimensional Fock module is four-dimensional: it is spanned by the Fock vacua for which the infinity mode is an annihilator, the infinity vacua. Each infinity vacuum is $\mathrm{span}(I_g, \ell, m)$ with $\mathrm{span}(\ell, m)$ a totally null plane of the complexified tangent space, which contains exactly one real null direction (a signature argument), so infinity vacua are labelled by the celestial sphere, two per direction. The pairing classes of $I_g$ against the vacuum are $-\Sch(v, \cdot)$ on $W$, and they are exactly the single-mode excitation amplitudes of the vacuum by $c(\nabla_v I_g)$. The point vacua (those containing the canonical tractor $X$) have classes $g(v, \cdot)$, which vanish along the vacuum's own null direction in every metric: this is the twistor incidence relation, and it is kinematic. Asking the infinity vacua to obey the same incidence, unexcited along their own null generators, is equivalent to $\Sch = (J/4)g$, the Einstein condition with an undetermined constant; the contracted Bianchi identity then makes the constant constant. Asking them to be unexcited in every direction is Ricci-flatness, and the classes of an Einstein metric along a transverse direction are the universal amplitude $-(\Lambda/6)g(v, w)$. One infinity-vacuum field left unexcited in every direction forces $\Ric = 2c\,\ell\otimes\ell$, pure null radiation along its generator. The matter clause is pointwise algebra: equating the own-ray class with $4\pi G\,T(\ell, \ell)$ for every null $\ell$ is $\Ric + 8\pi G T = h g$ in the store's sign convention, which is the null-null content of the Einstein equations; under the null energy condition the own-ray class is non-negative. With a conserved $T$ on a connected region, the trace and the contracted Bianchi identity give $dh = 4\pi G\,d(g^{ab}T_{ab})$, so $h = \Lambda + 4\pi G\,g^{ab}T_{ab}$ with $\Lambda$ an integration constant. All of this is the Einstein condition rewritten in the vacuum language: nothing here supplies a quantum principle that forces the classes to vanish, nor a CAR-side definition of $T$. The exact checks verify the class formulas, the rank-nine own-ray system with kernel spanned by $g$, the one-vacuum kernel spanned by $\ell^\flat\otimes\ell^\flat$, the Fock-module annihilation criterion, the real-direction count on sample planes, and, for the matter clause, the own-ray classes of the store-convention Einstein tensor with a rational source together with the linear algebra of the Bianchi step.
synthesis.einstein-condition-is-infinity.lay: A known way of stating Einstein's condition on empty space is that the curvature felt along every light ray has no part of a certain kind. This result translates that known statement into the series' language of quantum vacua; it does not derive it. In the series, every point of spacetime carries a small family of quantum vacuum states, and so does the point at infinity that a choice of scale singles out. Each such vacuum is attached to one light-ray direction. The vacua of an ordinary point are never disturbed when you move along their own light ray, in any spacetime: that is pure geometry. This result shows that asking the same of the vacua at infinity, that moving along their own light ray never disturbs them, is exactly Einstein's condition on the curvature, with the cosmological constant left free. Asking that they are never disturbed in any direction gives empty space with no cosmological constant, and asking it of one vacuum only gives a beam of pure radiation. With matter present, the disturbance along each light ray equals the matter's energy flowing along it exactly when Einstein's equations hold, the cosmological constant appearing as a free constant. These are equivalences: the result translates Einstein's condition into the language of vacua and does not explain why nature would impose it.

synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$, signature $(1,3)$. Write $\Ric^{\circ}$ for the Ricci tensor of the convention in which the round sphere has positive Ricci curvature (the one in the Raychaudhuri equation); the store's $\Ric$ is $-\Ric^{\circ}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-condition-is-infinity-vacuum-incidence}(7)). Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a gravitational field on four-dimensional flat spacetime whose derived metric $g$ is $C^{3}$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), let $U$ be a connected open part of its invertible region, and assume Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise}, clauses (Loc) and (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$): every local Rindler horizon $\mathcal{H}_{p,k}$ through $p \in U$ generated by a future physically null $k$ (the null boundary of the past of a small spacelike two-surface element through $p$, with vanishing expansion and shear at $p$) changes its entropy as $\delta S = \eta\,\delta A$ with $\eta$ one universal constant, and its selected state is at temperature $a/2\pi$ in the proper time of the boost observers of acceleration $a$. The Raychaudhuri equation for the generators enters through hypothesis (c) of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-jacobson-clausius-1995}; its explicit form and the shear equation are Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-raychaudhuri-null-congruence}. Assume further the hypotheses of Jacobson's argument that the premise does not supply:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(H1)] \emph{(Clausius.)} For every $p \in U$, every future null $k$ at $p$ and every small patch of $\mathcal{H}_{p,k}$ (generators with affine parameter $\lambda$, $\lambda = 0$ at $p$, $\lambda \in [\lambda_{0}, 0]$), the boost energy of matter crossing it, $\delta Q = \int T_{ab}\chi^{a}k^{b}\,d\lambda\,d\mathcal{A} = \int \chi \cdot T(k)\,d\lambda\,d\mathcal{A}$ with $\chi$ the approximate boost Killing field of surface gravity $\kappa$, equals $T_{\chi}\,\delta S$, with $T_{\chi}$ the temperature in the time of $\chi$ and $\delta S$ the change of the horizon's entropy alone, read as differences: $\delta S = \eta\,\delta A$, with $\eta$ the density at $p$.
\item[(H2)] \emph{(Patch.)} $\chi = -\kappa\lambda k$ on $\mathcal{H}_{p,k}$ up to $O(\lambda^{2})$; the balance (H1) is taken per unit cross-section area in the limit of a thin pencil about the generator through $p$ (the cross-section shrunk to zero before $\lambda_{0}$), and is required at leading order in $\lambda_{0}$. (The generators of a null hypersurface have zero twist.)
\item[(H3)] \emph{(Matter.)} $T$ is a given real symmetric linear map $a \mapsto T(a)$ on physical vectors, $C^{1}$ on $U$ (components $T_{ab}$; classical, or a renormalised expectation value), covariantly conserved, $\nabla^{a}T_{ab} = 0$ with $\nabla$ the covariant derivative $D$.
\item[(H4)] \emph{(Dimension.)} Spacetime is four-dimensional (the flat background is that of $\Cl(1,3)$).
\end{enumerate}
Then, with $G_{\mathrm{cl}} := 1/(4\eta)$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Temperature.)} Clause (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) gives $T_{\chi} = \kappa/2\pi$: on the orbit of $\chi$ at proper distance $\rho$ from the edge, $a = 1/\rho$ and $|\chi| = \kappa\rho$, and $T_{\chi} = (a/2\pi)\,|\chi|$. Nothing below depends on $\kappa$.
\item \emph{(Focusing at leading order.)} $\theta(\lambda) = -\lambda\,\Ric^{\circ}(k,k)|_{p} + O(\lambda^{2})$, and per unit cross-section area at $p$
\[
\delta Q - T_{\chi}\,\eta\,\delta A \;=\; \frac{\kappa}{2}\Big(T(k,k) - \frac{\eta}{2\pi}\Ric^{\circ}(k,k)\Big)\Big|_{p}\,\lambda_{0}^{2} + O(\lambda_{0}^{3}),
\]
where the gradients of $\Ric^{\circ}(k,k)$ and $T(k,k)$ along the generator and the $O(\lambda^{2})$ error of $\chi$ enter at $O(\lambda_{0}^{3})$, and the shear and $\theta^{2}$ at $O(\lambda_{0}^{4})$. A shear $s_{0} = |\sigma|^{2}(p) \neq 0$ would replace $\Ric^{\circ}(k,k)$ by $\Ric^{\circ}(k,k) + s_{0}$, and an expansion $\theta_{0} \neq 0$ at $p$ gives a defect $\kappa\eta\theta_{0}\lambda_{0}/2\pi$ at first order, so (H1) forces $\theta_{0} = 0$. Hence (H1) gives $\Ric^{\circ}(k,k) = (2\pi/\eta)\,T(k,k)$, that is $-k \cdot \mathcal{R}(k) = (2\pi/\eta)\,k \cdot T(k)$, for every physical null $k$ at every $p \in U$.
\item \emph{(Restatement in the store's language.)} The leading defect equals $\kappa\,\tfrac{\eta}{2\pi}\big(4\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}\,T(k,k) - \omega_{k}(I_{g},k)\big)\lambda_{0}^{2}$, with $\omega_{k}(I_{g},k) = -\Sch(k,k) = \tfrac12\Ric^{\circ}(k,k)$ the own-ray class of the infinity vacua through $k$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-condition-is-infinity-vacuum-incidence}(2)). This identity is a relabelling of $\Ric^{\circ}(k,k)$ and adds no content: the Clausius balance in the direction $k$ is the own-ray incidence condition of that theorem's clause (7).
\item \emph{(Einstein's equations.)} On $U$,
\[
\Ric + 8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}\,T = (\Lambda + 4\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}\,\tau)\,g, \qquad \tau = g^{ab}T_{ab},
\]
with $\Lambda$ a constant, that is, for the gravitational field, $\mathcal{R}(a) + 8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}\,T(a) = (\Lambda + 4\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}\,\tau)\,a$, or $\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a = -8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}\,T(a)$, with the store's curvature operator; equivalently $\Ric^{\circ} - \tfrac12 R^{\circ}g - \Lambda g = 8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}\,T$ in signature $(1,3)$, which is $G_{ab} + \Lambda g_{ab} = 8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}T_{ab}$ in signature $(3,1)$. $\Lambda$ is an integration constant: (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) and (H1) to (H4) leave its value free.
\item \emph{(Newton's constant.)} $8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}} = 2\pi/\eta$, so $G_{\mathrm{cl}} = 1/(4\eta)$, and in the mode-count reading of version 1 of the premise, $\eta = 4\pi\nu\langle s\rangle/G$, $G_{\mathrm{cl}} = G/(16\pi\nu\langle s\rangle)$, $G$ the constant that defines the Planck cell.
\item \emph{(Where the universality of $\eta$ is used.)} On the differences reading of (H1), if $\eta$ were a function on $U$, steps (1) to (3) would still give $\Ric + \gamma T = h\,g$ with $\gamma = 2\pi/\eta$, and the contracted Bianchi identity with $\nabla^{a}T_{ab} = 0$ would give $d(h - \tfrac12\gamma\tau) = -T(\nabla\gamma, \cdot)$: the cosmological term is constant only where $T(\nabla\eta, \cdot) = 0$, so universality is used at the Bianchi step. On the integrated reading $S = \int\eta\,dA$ instead, a varying $\eta$ already gives a first-order defect $(\kappa/2\pi)(k\cdot\nabla\eta)\lambda_{0}$ at step (2), and (H1) forces $\nabla\eta = 0$ there.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Note (entropy reading).} Version 3 of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise} reads (Loc) on the integrated reading $S = \int\eta\,dA$, where this result was first stated with the differences reading. The conclusions do not depend on the change: with $\eta$ one universal constant the integrated reading gives $\delta S = \eta\,\delta A$, which is the entropy change (H1) uses, so items (1) to (5) hold as stated; item (6) treats both readings, and on the integrated reading the universality is used already at the focusing step. The remark in the proof that the store takes the differences reading refers to version 2 of the premise.

\emph{Note (heat tensor and Hilbert stress).} The source $T$ of item (4) is the heat tensor of (H1), the boost-energy flux of matter, whatever functional the matter has. If the matter equations are the Euler-Lagrange equations of a local functional $S_{m}$, the coupled system (item (4) with those equations) is the Euler-Lagrange system of one local functional exactly when $T$ is the Hilbert stress of $S_{m}$, up to a term independent of the matter (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.inverse-problem-for-the-clausius-route}(v)). The route does not impose this identification; it is the condition under which the route's equations have a variational form with matter.

\emph{Note (the whole-stress clause; added 1 November).} Item (2) uses (H1) for every physical null $k$ at every point, so the route takes the null-null component $T(k,k)$ of the whole stress map as the source in every null direction; since a symmetric map vanishing on every null vector is a multiple of the metric, these components fix $T$ up to such a multiple, and the Bianchi step of item (4) fixes the multiple up to the constant $\Lambda$. This is the clause that the whole stress map is the source, a clause of any field-theory route to Einstein's equations: consistency conditions alone do not supply it, since on twistor-flat fields Nordstr\"om's equations, sourced by the trace alone, satisfy the Bianchi identities, the conservation of the stress and the Newtonian limit (\claimref{synthesis.twistor-flat-fields-give-nordstrom-not-einstein}). The Clausius route assumes the clause through (H1); it does not derive it.
synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-.technical: This writes out, inside the store, the conditional derivation of Einstein's equations from the local-horizon premise (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) and Jacobson's 1995 Clausius argument, and names every hypothesis the argument needs beyond the premise. The premise supplies two of Jacobson's inputs: an entropy density $\eta$ per unit area, one universal constant (clause (Loc)), and the temperature $a/2\pi$ of the boost observers (clause (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$)), which in the time of a boost Killing field of surface gravity $\kappa$ is $\kappa/2\pi$. The modular-flow clause of version 1 is not used. The further hypotheses are: the Clausius relation, with heat the boost energy of matter crossing the horizon, no entropy other than the horizon's, and entropy changes read as $\eta\,\delta A$; the patch (the approximate boost field, balance per unit area in a thin pencil about one generator, at leading order in the patch length); a given $C^{1}$ conserved stress tensor on a gravitational field whose derived metric is $C^{3}$; and four dimensions. Vanishing expansion and shear at the point are the premise's own construction of the horizon. The Raychaudhuri focusing comes with Jacobson's Fact; the explicit Raychaudhuri and shear equations are imported as a Fact. Under these, the proof integrates the Raychaudhuri equation along a generator in exact power series: the area change and the heat both start at second order in the patch length, with coefficients $\Ric^{\circ}(k,k)/2$ and $\kappa T(k,k)/2$, while the gradients and the error of the Killing field enter one order later and the shear two orders later, so the Clausius relation at leading order is the pointwise null-null equation $\Ric^{\circ}(k,k) = (2\pi/\eta)T(k,k)$; the normalisation $\kappa$ cancels. A shear or an expansion at the point would spoil this. In the store's language, as a restatement, the Clausius defect is the gap between the matter's null energy and the own-ray class of the infinity vacua; this is a relabelling, not new content. The store's theorem on the Einstein condition (polarisation, valid in any dimension, then the contracted Bianchi identity, where four dimensions fix the coefficient $4\pi G\tau$) turns the null-null equation into Einstein's equations, the field equations $\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a = -8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}\,T(a)$ of the gravitational field on flat spacetime, with $\Lambda$ an integration constant and $G_{\mathrm{cl}} = 1/(4\eta)$, that is $G/(16\pi\nu\langle s\rangle)$ in the mode-count reading. The universality of $\eta$ is used at the Bianchi step on the differences reading (a varying $\eta$ would make the cosmological term vary wherever matter flows along its gradient), and already at the focusing step on the integrated reading $S = \int\eta\,dA$. What selects Einstein's equations over their Ricci-polynomial extensions is the assumption that the density does not depend on curvature. $G_{\mathrm{cl}} = G$ holds at the area-law condition only if the horizon modes and the cutoff modes are one set. With matter, the field equations and the matter's own equations come from one action exactly when the heat tensor is the matter's Hilbert stress (the stress obtained by varying the matter action with respect to the metric); the route itself does not impose this. The derivation is Jacobson's, transport-absent; it is conditional on the premise and on the Clausius relation, and it says nothing about the value of $\Lambda$.
synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-.lay: In 1995 Ted Jacobson showed that Einstein's equations of gravity follow if every small patch of horizon, as seen by an accelerating observer, has a temperature set by the acceleration and an entropy proportional to its area, and if heat crossing the patch raises its entropy by heat divided by temperature. The series assumes, as a premise, that its own horizon quantum modes give that temperature and that entropy on all such small horizons. This result writes the argument out step by step under that premise and checks each algebraic step exactly. It also lists everything else the argument needs: that the heat is the energy carried by matter and nothing else changes the entropy, that the horizon patch is momentarily neither expanding nor shearing, that matter is described by an ordinary conserved energy tensor, that the gravitational field is smooth enough, and that space-time has four dimensions. Given all that, Einstein's equations follow, with the strength of gravity fixed by the entropy per area and the cosmological constant left free. What singles out Einstein's equations, rather than more complicated versions of them, is that the entropy per area is the same everywhere and does not depend on the strength of the gravitational field there. The derivation is conditional: it shows what the premise would deliver, not that the premise holds.

proofs.main:
Read in Gauge Theory Gravity, the metric, Ricci tensor and covariant derivatives below are the derived metric, the contractions of the field strength (with $\Ric = \mathcal{R}$ as a map on physical vectors in the store's sign) and $D$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}, clauses (i), (ii) and (iv)). \emph{Inputs.} From Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise} only clause (Loc) (density $\eta$ per unit area, one universal constant) and clause (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) ($a/2\pi$ in the proper time of the boost observers) are used, together with its construction of $\mathcal{H}_{p,k}$ (vanishing expansion and shear at $p$). From Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-jacobson-clausius-1995} we take the setting (local Rindler horizons through every point in every null direction, the approximate boost field $\chi$, the heat as boost energy of matter) and its hypothesis (c), which is (H1) here and which carries the focusing of the generators through the Raychaudhuri equation; we do not use the Fact's conclusion as a black box but rederive it from (H1) to (H4), so that every step is visible. The explicit equations are Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-raychaudhuri-null-congruence}: for a twist-free congruence of null geodesics with tangent $k$ and affine parameter $\lambda$, the Raychaudhuri equation $d	heta/d\lambda = -	frac12	heta^{2} - |\sigma|^{2} - \Ric^{\circ}(k,k)$ with $|\sigma|^{2} \geq 0$ the squared shear, and the shear equation $d\sigma/d\lambda = -	heta\sigma - C(\cdot,k,\cdot,k)$ on the screen space, so that $\sigma(0) = 0$ gives $\sigma = O(\lambda)$ and $|\sigma|^{2} = O(\lambda^{2})$. The shear equation is the one step that is not inside the Fact. Both $\Ric^{\circ}(k,k)$ and $	heta$ are unchanged under $g \mapsto -g$, so they hold as written in signature $(1,3)$. The generators of the null hypersurface $\mathcal{H}_{p,k}$ are twist-free.

\emph{(1) Temperature.} In the flat tangent model at $p$ with coordinates $(t,x)$ in the plane of the boost, $\chi = \kappa(x\partial_{t} + t\partial_{x})$. Its orbit $x^{2} - t^{2} = ho^{2}$, parametrised rationally by $t = 	frac{ho}{2}(u - u^{-1})$, $x = 	frac{ho}{2}(u + u^{-1})$, has $\dot t^{2} - \dot x^{2} = ho^{2}/u^{2}$, unit velocity $U = 	frac{u}{ho}(\dot t, \dot x)$ and acceleration $	frac{u}{ho}\dot U$ of square $-1/ho^{2}$, so $a = 1/ho$; and $g(\chi,\chi) = \kappa^{2}(x^{2} - t^{2}) = \kappa^{2}ho^{2}$. The time of $\chi$ runs at $1/|\chi|$ times proper time, so energies and temperatures in it are $|\chi|$ times the proper ones: by (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$), $T_{\chi} = (a/2\pi)|\chi| = (1/2\piho)\,\kappaho = \kappa/2\pi$, the same on every orbit. On the past horizon $x = -t$ of the wedge, with $k = \partial_{t} - \partial_{x}$ and $\lambda = t < 0$, $\chi = \kappa(-\lambda\,\partial_{t} + \lambda\,\partial_{x}) = -\kappa\lambda k$, future-directed for $\lambda < 0$; for a field of nonvanishing field strength this holds up to $O(\lambda^{2})$ (H2), and curvature corrections to the flat tangent model are of higher order in the patch size, the order (H2) discards.

\emph{(2) Focusing.} Write $r(\lambda) = \Ric^{\circ}(k,k)$ and $t(\lambda) = T(k,k)$ along the generator through $p$, $r = r_{0} + r_{1}\lambda + \dots$, $t = t_{0} + t_{1}\lambda + \dots$ (Taylor expansions with remainders $O(\lambda^{2})$, since the metric is $C^{3}$ and $T$ is $C^{1}$), $|\sigma|^{2} = s_{2}\lambda^{2} + \dots$ (by the construction of $\mathcal{H}_{p,k}$ and the shear equation), and $\chi = -\kappa(\lambda + e_{2}\lambda^{2} + \dots)k$. The Raychaudhuri equation with $	heta(0) = 0$ gives $	heta = -r_{0}\lambda - 	frac12 r_{1}\lambda^{2} + O(\lambda^{3})$, the terms $	heta^{2}$ and $|\sigma|^{2}$ first entering $	heta$ at $\lambda^{3}$. Per (H2) we work per unit cross-section area in a thin pencil about this generator, the cross-section shrunk to zero before $\lambda_{0}$ (neighbouring generators of a finite element have expansion $O(\epsilon)$ at $\lambda = 0$ for an element of size $\epsilon$). The cross-section area obeys $dA/d\lambda = 	heta A$, so $A(\lambda)/A(0) = \exp\int_{0}^{\lambda}	heta = 1 - 	frac12 r_{0}\lambda^{2} + O(\lambda^{3})$ and the area gained between $\lambda_{0}$ and $p$ is, per unit area at $p$, $\delta A = A(0) - A(\lambda_{0}) = 	frac12 r_{0}\lambda_{0}^{2} + O(\lambda_{0}^{3})$. The heat is $\delta Q = \int_{\lambda_{0}}^{0} T(\chi,k)\,(A(\lambda)/A(0))\,d\lambda = -\kappa\int_{\lambda_{0}}^{0}(\lambda + e_{2}\lambda^{2})\,t(\lambda)\,(1 + O(\lambda^{2}))\,d\lambda = 	frac12\kappa t_{0}\lambda_{0}^{2} + O(\lambda_{0}^{3})$. With $T_{\chi}\,\delta S = (\kappa/2\pi)\,\eta\,\delta A$ by (1), (Loc) and the differences reading of (H1),
\[
\delta Q - T_{\chi}\eta\,\delta A = 	frac{\kappa}{2} ig(t_{0} - 	frac{\eta}{2\pi}r_{0} ig)\lambda_{0}^{2} + O(\lambda_{0}^{3}),
\]
with no terms of order $\lambda_{0}^{0}$ or $\lambda_{0}^{1}$; $r_{1}, t_{1}, e_{2}$ first appear at $\lambda_{0}^{3}$ and $s_{2}$ at $\lambda_{0}^{4}$. Since (H1) holds at leading order for every small patch, the coefficient vanishes: $t_{0} = (\eta/2\pi)r_{0}$, and $\kappa 
eq 0$ drops out. The conditions at $p$ are needed: if $|\sigma|^{2}(p) = s_{0} 
eq 0$, the same computation gives $	heta = -(r_{0} + s_{0})\lambda + \dots$ and the coefficient $	frac{\kappa}{2}(t_{0} - 	frac{\eta}{2\pi}(r_{0} + s_{0}))$; if $	heta(0) = 	heta_{0} 
eq 0$, then $\delta A = -	heta_{0}\lambda_{0} + O(\lambda_{0}^{2})$ while $\delta Q = O(\lambda_{0}^{2})$, a first-order defect $\kappa\eta	heta_{0}\lambda_{0}/2\pi$, so (H1) forces $	heta_{0} = 0$. As $k$ and $p$ are arbitrary, $\Ric^{\circ}(k,k) = (2\pi/\eta)T(k,k)$ for every null $k$ on $U$.

\emph{(3) Restatement in the store's language.} For null $k$, $\Sch(k,k) = 	frac12\Ric(k,k) = -	frac12\Ric^{\circ}(k,k)$, so the own-ray class of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-condition-is-infinity-vacuum-incidence}(2) is $\omega_{k}(I_{g},k) = -\Sch(k,k) = 	frac12 r_{0}$. With $4\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}} = \pi/\eta$, $	frac{\kappa}{2}(t_{0} - 	frac{\eta}{2\pi}r_{0}) = \kappa	frac{\eta}{2\pi}(	frac{\pi}{\eta}t_{0} - 	frac12 r_{0}) = \kappa	frac{\eta}{2\pi}(4\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}\,T(k,k) - \omega_{k}(I_{g},k))$. synthesis.euler-entropy-first-order-rate.formal:
Signature $(-,+,+,+)$ in this statement and its proof, units $\hbar = c = 1$; under the change to the store's $(+,-,-,-)$, $g \mapsto -g$, inner products change sign while $\Ric^{\circ}$, the Ricci tensor (with two lower indices) of the convention in which the round sphere has positive Ricci curvature, is unchanged, its mixed components and its scalar changing sign; the store's sign is $\Ric = -\Ric^{\circ}$ in either signature. Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a gravitational field on four-dimensional flat spacetime whose derived metric $g$ is $C^{3}$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), $p$ a point of its invertible region, $k$ a future null physical vector at $p$ ($g$ on physical vectors is the flat product), and $\Sigma$ a small spacelike two-surface element through $p$ orthogonal to $k$, with null normals $k$, $l$ normalised by $g(k,l) = -1$ and extended along the generators of the null hypersurface $\mathcal{H}$ that $\Sigma$ emits in the direction $k$, affinely parametrised by $\lambda$ with $\Sigma$ at $\lambda = 0$; let $\Sigma_{\lambda}$ be the cuts at constant $\lambda$, $h$ their induced metric, $e_{a}$ a frame of $T\Sigma$ dragged along the generators, $B^{(k)}_{ab} = g(\nabla_{e_{a}}k, e_{b})$ and $B^{(l)}_{ab} = g(\nabla_{e_{a}}l, e_{b})$, with $\nabla_{e_{a}} = e_{a} \cdot D$ the covariant derivative, the two null second fundamental forms, $\theta_{k}, \theta_{l}$ their traces and $\sigma_{k}, \sigma_{l}$ their trace-free parts, $\omega_{a} = -g(l, \nabla_{e_{a}}k)$ the normal connection, $C$ the Weyl tensor, $\widehat{C}_{k}(e_{a}, e_{b}) = C(e_{a}, k, e_{b}, k)$, and $Z_{b} = h^{ac}R(e_{a}, k, e_{c}, e_{b})$, the Riemann and Weyl tensors being read from the field strength $\mathcal{R}$ and its Weyl map $\mathcal{W}$ in the convention of the proof (Riemann positive on spheres). Call $\Sigma$ \emph{admissible} if $B^{(k)} = 0$ at $p$ ($\theta_{k} = \sigma_{k} = 0$ there), the condition defining the local Rindler patches of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-jacobson-clausius-1995} and hypothesis (H1) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}. Write ${}^{(2)}\!R$ for the scalar curvature of $h$ and $P = h^{ac}h^{bd}R_{abcd}$ for the projected curvature. Then, on an admissible element:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Rates.)} At $p$,
\[
\frac{d}{d\lambda}\Big(\sqrt{h}\,{}^{(2)}\!R\Big)\Big|_{0} = \theta_{l}\,\Ric^{\circ}(k,k) - 2\,\sigma_{l}^{ab}\widehat{C}_{k\,ab} + 4\,\omega^{b}Z_{b} + (\nabla_{k}R)(e_{a},e_{b},e^{a},e^{b}),
\qquad
\frac{d}{d\lambda}\Big(\sqrt{h}\,P\Big)\Big|_{0} = 4\,\omega^{b}Z_{b} + (\nabla_{k}R)(e_{a},e_{b},e^{a},e^{b}),
\]
per unit area, where the last term equals $2\,(\nabla_{e^{b}}R)(e_{a},k,e^{a},e_{b})$ by the second Bianchi identity; the difference of the two rates is the derivative of the extrinsic term of the Gauss equation. Data of the element beyond its second fundamental forms and normal connection at $p$ do not enter. Given $p$ and $k$, every symmetric $B^{(l)}(p)$ and every covector $\omega(p)$ is realised by some admissible element.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The Clausius relation at first order.)} Take as the entropy of a patch the Jacobson-Myers functional $S = \frac{1}{4G}\int(1 + 2\alpha\,{}^{(2)}\!R)\,dA$ of the series' Lagrangian $(R - 2\Lambda + \alpha E_{4})/16\pi G$, $\alpha = -3/(4\Lambda)$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.euler-term-horizon-entropy-shift}, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-wald-noether-charge-entropy}(c)), or its projected form with $P$ in place of ${}^{(2)}\!R$, and take the Clausius relation (H1) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius} on every open admissible element, with $\delta S$ the change of this functional (entropy read as a functional of the cut), in the thin-pencil limit (H2). Per unit cross-section area the defect $\delta Q - T_{\chi}\,\delta S$ is $(\kappa/2\pi)(\alpha/2G)\,r\,\lambda_{0} + O(\lambda_{0}^{2})$, with $r$ the rate of (i), while the heat and the area change start at $\lambda_{0}^{2}$. So (H1) on every admissible element through $p$ requires $r = 0$ for all of them. For the Jacobson-Myers form this requires $\Ric^{\circ}(k,k) = 0$ and $\widehat{C}_{k} = 0$ for every null $k$ at $p$, that is the trace-free Ricci tensor and the Weyl tensor vanish at $p$ (then $Z = 0$ at $p$), and the gradient term to vanish; at every point of a connected region it holds if and only if the region has constant curvature, $\mathcal{R}(B) = cB$ with $c$ constant (Schur's lemma). For the projected form it requires $Z_{b} = 0$ and $(\nabla_{k}R)(e_{a},e_{b},e^{a},e^{b}) = 0$ for every null $k$ and every screen. On flat elements ($B^{(l)} = 0$, $\omega = 0$ at $p$) both forms reduce to the gradient term, which is nonzero in vacuum: for the vacuum plane-wave field $\hb^{-1}(a) = a + \tfrac12(x^{3} - 3xy^{2})\,(a\cdot e_{v})\,e_{v}$ on the background frame $e_{u}, e_{v}, e_{x}, e_{y}$ of the labels ($e_{u}$, $e_{v}$ null with $e_{u}\cdot e_{v} = -1$; derived metric, in components, $-2\,du\,dv + (x^{3} - 3xy^{2})\,du^{2} + dx^{2} + dy^{2}$) it is $6$ at the origin for the null direction $e_{u} + \tfrac12 e_{v} + e_{x}$; on radial generators of Schwarzschild-de Sitter the formula reduces to this term, whose value there is computed in the result filed alongside on the vacuum side.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Consequences.)} With $\alpha \neq 0$, the Clausius relation on every admissible patch through every point of a region holds for the Jacobson-Myers form only if the region has constant curvature; if Einstein's equations hold there, $\Ric^{\circ}(k,k) = 8\pi G\,T(k,k)$, so no null energy crosses and no Weyl curvature is present. Hence on the Einstein route the entropy of open patches cannot contain the Euler term of the series' action, in either form, and the entropy functional within the family $\frac{1}{4G}\int(\eta' + \beta\,{}^{(2)}\!R)\,dA$ or with $P$ is forced to $\beta = 0$: the curvature-independent area density of clause (Loc) of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise}. Together with clause (iv) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-entropy-clause-curvature-independent-density} (a density varying over spacetime is excluded at first order), the Clausius relation derives (Loc) for every density of the form $\eta(x) + \beta\,{}^{(2)}\!R$ or $\eta(x) + \beta P$; it does not derive (Loc) for arbitrary curvature-dependent densities. All of (iii) concerns entropies that are functionals of the cut, the reading under which a Wald entropy is defined; on the differences reading $\delta S = \eta\,\delta A$ that the premise adopts, an $\eta$ depending on curvature scalars at the point produces no first-order term and is not excluded by (H1) (filed alongside, synthesis.loc-independent-of-clausius-and-killing-data).
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.euler-entropy-first-order-rate.technical: The series' action contains, besides the Einstein-Cartan term, an Euler (Gauss-Bonnet) term with coefficient $\alpha = -3/(4\Lambda)$. Its Wald entropy adds to the area term the integral of the intrinsic curvature of the horizon cut; on closed cuts that is a topological constant, invisible to every first law, and the store left open whether it matters on the small open patches of a local Clausius argument. It does, and at the leading order. Along the generators of a Jacobson patch (an element whose expansion and shear vanish at the point), in a gravitational field on flat spacetime whose field strength plays the part of curvature, the Euler density changes at first order in the affine extent, by an amount fixed by the Ricci curvature times the element's other expansion, the Weyl curvature times its other shear, a normal-connection term and a curvature gradient. The heat and the area change start one order later, so the Clausius relation forces this rate to vanish on every patch. Since the element's other expansion, shear and normal connection can be chosen freely, that happens only where the trace-free Ricci and Weyl tensors vanish: in regions of constant curvature, with no null energy if Einstein's equations hold. The projected form of the Wald entropy loses the first two terms but keeps the gradient term, which is already nonzero in vacuum (an exact plane wave; radial generators of Schwarzschild-de Sitter, treated in a result filed alongside). Both conclusions use two readings, stated here: the Clausius relation is imposed on every open patch (the Euler change is a divergence on the cut and cancels on closed cuts, so closed-cut relations do not see it), and the entropy is a functional of the cut. So the Euler term cannot be part of the entropy on the Einstein route, and within the family of entropies the series' action supplies, the Clausius relation selects the pure area density: the curvature-independence that clause (Loc) of the local-horizon premise assumes. This derives (Loc) from the Clausius relation within that family (and, with a stored result, for densities varying over spacetime); it does not exclude every conceivable curvature-dependent density, and on the differences reading $\delta S = \eta\,\delta A$, with $\eta$ evaluated at the point, a density depending on curvature scalars escapes it, so there (Loc) is not derived.
synthesis.euler-entropy-first-order-rate.lay: The series' description of gravity has an extra term in its action that does not change the equations of motion but would, by the standard formula for black-hole entropy, add a curvature term to the entropy of a horizon. For whole horizons that term is a constant and cancels from every comparison. This result looks at the small pieces of horizon used in Jacobson's thermodynamic derivation of Einstein's equations. On those pieces the extra entropy changes at once, as soon as the piece moves along its light rays, whereas the heat carried in by matter and the growth of the area only appear one step later. The balance between heat and entropy that the derivation needs therefore fails unless the gravitational field strength at that point is perfectly uniform, the same in every direction, with no matter flowing and no gravitational waves. So on the thermodynamic route to Einstein's equations, if the entropy of a piece of horizon is computed from the shape of that piece, it must be the area term alone, and within the kinds of entropy the series' action supplies this is exactly the assumption that the entropy per area does not depend on curvature. For whole, closed horizons the extra term cancels again, so the conclusion concerns the small open pieces only.

proofs.main:
Read in Gauge Theory Gravity, the metric below is the derived metric, $\nabla$ is the covariant derivative $D$ on physical vectors, and the Riemann and Weyl tensors are read from the field strength and its Weyl map (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}, clauses (i), (ii), (iv) and (v)). \emph{Conventions.} Signature $(-,+,+,+)$; $R^{a}{}_{bcd} = \partial_{c}\Gamma^{a}_{db} - \partial_{d}\Gamma^{a}_{cb} + \Gamma^{a}_{ce}\Gamma^{e}_{db} - \Gamma^{a}_{de}\Gamma^{e}_{cb}$, so that $R(e_{1},e_{2},e_{1},e_{2})$ is the sectional curvature of an orthonormal plane and $\Ric^{\circ}_{bd} = R^{a}{}_{bad}$ is positive on round spheres; this $\Ric^{\circ}$ is the one in the Raychaudhuri equation of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-raychaudhuri-null-congruence}. The element $\Sigma$, its null normals $k$, $l$ with $g(k,l) = -1$, the generators of $\mathcal{H}$ with affine parameter $\lambda$, the cuts $\Sigma_{\lambda}$, the frame $e_{a}$ (Lie-dragged along $k$, so $\nabla_{k}e_{a} = \nabla_{e_{a}}k$), $B^{(k)}$, $B^{(l)}$, $\omega$, $\widehat{C}_{k}$, $Z$ and $P$ are as in the statement; screen indices are raised with $h$. The generators of a null hypersurface are twist-free.

\emph{Step 1 (Gauss equation).} The normal part of $\nabla_{e_{a}}e_{b}$ is $K_{ab} = B^{(l)}_{ab}\,k + B^{(k)}_{ab}\,l$: indeed $g(K_{ab}, k) = g(\nabla_{e_{a}}e_{b}, k) = -g(e_{b}, \nabla_{e_{a}}k) = -B^{(k)}_{ab}$, which is $g(B^{(k)}_{ab}\,l, k)$ since $g(l,k) = -1$, and likewise with $k$ and $l$ exchanged; both forms are symmetric because $[e_{a}, e_{b}]$ is tangent to $\Sigma$. The Gauss equation ${}^{(2)}\!R_{abcd} = R_{abcd} + g(K_{ac},K_{bd}) - g(K_{ad},K_{bc})$ (standard, cited from memory) with $g(K_{ac},K_{bd}) = -(B^{(l)}_{ac}B^{(k)}_{bd} + B^{(k)}_{ac}B^{(l)}_{bd})$, contracted with $h^{ac}h^{bd}$, gives
\[
{}^{(2)}\!R = P - 2\,\theta_{k}\theta_{l} + 2\,B^{(k)}_{ab}B^{(l)ab} .
\]

\emph{Step 2 (the projected part).} Along the generator through $p$, $\partial_{\lambda}h_{ab} = 2B^{(k)}_{(ab)} = 0$ at $p$ and $\partial_{\lambda}\sqrt{h} = \theta_{k}\sqrt{h} = 0$ at $p$, so only the curvature and the frame move at first order. Since $g(\nabla_{e_{a}}k, k) = 0$ and $g(\nabla_{e_{a}}k, l) = -\omega_{a}$, $\nabla_{e_{a}}k = B^{(k)}{}_{a}{}^{b}e_{b} + \omega_{a}k$, which is $\omega_{a}k$ at $p$. Hence at $p$
\[
\frac{dP}{d\lambda} = (\nabla_{k}R)(e_{a},e_{b},e^{a},e^{b}) + h^{ac}h^{bd}\big(\omega_{a}R(k,e_{b},e_{c},e_{d}) + \omega_{b}R(e_{a},k,e_{c},e_{d}) + \omega_{c}R(e_{a},e_{b},k,e_{d}) + \omega_{d}R(e_{a},e_{b},e_{c},k)\big),
\]
and the pair symmetry and antisymmetries of $R$ make the four frame terms equal, each $\omega^{a}h^{bd}R(k,e_{b},e_{a},e_{d}) = \omega^{a}Z_{a}$ (since $R(k,e_{b},e_{a},e_{b}) = R(e_{b},k,e_{b},e_{a})$). This is the second formula of (i). The second Bianchi identity $\nabla_{k}R_{abab} + \nabla_{a}R_{abbk} + \nabla_{b}R_{abka} = 0$, summed over the screen indices, gives $(\nabla_{k}R)(e_{a},e_{b},e^{a},e^{b}) = 2(\nabla_{e^{b}}R)(e_{a},k,e^{a},e_{b})$, the divergence form of the gradient term.

\emph{Step 3 (the extrinsic part).} At $p$, $B^{(k)} = 0$, so the derivative of $-2\theta_{k}\theta_{l} + 2B^{(k)}_{ab}B^{(l)ab}$ needs only $dB^{(k)}/d\lambda$ at $p$, not $dB^{(l)}/d\lambda$. By Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-raychaudhuri-null-congruence}, at $p$ (where $\theta_{k} = \sigma_{k} = 0$) $d\theta_{k}/d\lambda = -\Ric^{\circ}(k,k)$ and $d\sigma_{k}/d\lambda = -\widehat{C}_{k}$, so $dB^{(k)}/d\lambda = -\widehat{C}_{k} - \tfrac12\Ric^{\circ}(k,k)\,h$. Therefore
\[
\frac{d}{d\lambda}\big(-2\theta_{k}\theta_{l} + 2B^{(k)}_{ab}B^{(l)ab}\big) = 2\Ric^{\circ}(k,k)\theta_{l} - 2\widehat{C}_{k\,ab}B^{(l)ab} - \Ric^{\circ}(k,k)\theta_{l} = \theta_{l}\Ric^{\circ}(k,k) - 2\sigma_{l}^{ab}\widehat{C}_{k\,ab},
\]
using that $\widehat{C}_{k}$ is trace-free on the screen. With Steps 1 and 2 and $\partial_{\lambda}\sqrt{h} = 0$ at $p$ this is the first formula of (i). Only $B^{(k)}$, $B^{(l)}$ and $\omega$ at $p$ and the curvature and its first derivatives at $p$ enter; third- and higher-order data of the embedding of $\Sigma$, and the normalisation of $k$ beyond its first derivative, do not.

\emph{Step 4 (free data).} In coordinates in which $p = 0$, the metric is $-2\,du\,dv + dx^{2} + dy^{2}$ at $p$ with vanishing first derivatives, $k = \partial_{u}$ and $l = \partial_{v}$ at $p$, an element $X(s_{1},s_{2}) = (u(s), v(s), s_{1} + \dots, s_{2} + \dots)$ has $B^{(k)}_{ab}(p) = \partial_{a}\partial_{b}v(0)$ and $B^{(l)}_{ab}(p) = \partial_{a}\partial_{b}u(0)$. So $v$ without quadratic terms makes the element admissible, and the quadratic part of $u$ prescribes any symmetric $B^{(l)}(p)$. Rescaling $k \mapsto e^{f}k$ by a function on $\Sigma$ constant along the generators, with $f(p) = 0$, keeps the generators affinely parametrised, keeps $B^{(k)}(p) = 0$ and $B^{(l)}(p)$ (with $l \mapsto e^{-f}l$), and changes $\omega$ to $\omega + df$, so every covector $\omega(p)$ is realised. This proves the last sentence of (i).

\emph{Step 5 (Clausius at first order).} In the setting of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-jacobson-clausius-1995}, per unit cross-section area in the thin-pencil limit (H2), with the patch $\lambda \in [\lambda_{0}, 0]$ and $\chi = -\kappa\lambda k$ up to $O(\lambda^{2})$, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}(2) gives the heat $\delta Q = \tfrac12\kappa T(k,k)\lambda_{0}^{2} + O(\lambda_{0}^{3})$ and the area change $\delta A = \tfrac12\Ric^{\circ}(k,k)\lambda_{0}^{2} + O(\lambda_{0}^{3})$, both without a term of order $\lambda_{0}$. The Euler part of the Jacobson-Myers entropy (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-wald-noether-charge-entropy}(c)), $\frac{\alpha}{2G}\int{}^{(2)}\!R\,dA$, changes per unit area by $\frac{\alpha}{2G}\big[\sqrt{h}\,{}^{(2)}\!R\big]_{\lambda_{0}}^{0}/\sqrt{h}(0) = -\frac{\alpha}{2G}\,r\,\lambda_{0} + O(\lambda_{0}^{2})$, with $r$ the first rate of (i); likewise with $P$ and the second rate. With $T_{\chi} = \kappa/2\pi$,
\[
\delta Q - T_{\chi}\,\delta S = \frac{\kappa}{2\pi}\,\frac{\alpha}{2G}\,r\,\lambda_{0} + O(\lambda_{0}^{2}) .
\]
(H1) holds at leading order on every admissible patch, so $\alpha r = 0$, and $\alpha = -3/(4\Lambda) \neq 0$ forces $r = 0$ for every admissible element through $p$.

\emph{Step 6 (what $r = 0$ for all elements means).} For the Jacobson-Myers form, $r$ is affine in the free data $(\theta_{l}, \sigma_{l}, \omega)$ of Step 4, with coefficients $\Ric^{\circ}(k,k)$, $-2\widehat{C}_{k}$ and $4Z$ and constant term the gradient term. It vanishes for all data if and only if all four vanish. $\Ric^{\circ}(k,k) = 0$ for every null $k$ is the vanishing of the trace-free Ricci tensor (a symmetric form vanishing on the null cone is a multiple of $g$; the check confirms rank nine on eleven rational null vectors). $\widehat{C}_{k} = 0$ for every null $k$ and its screen is the vanishing of the Weyl tensor (the check builds the ten-dimensional space of Weyl tensors as the trace-free part of the span of Kulkarni-Nomizu products and finds the map to these components injective, rank ten). Then the curvature at $p$ is $K(g_{ac}g_{bd} - g_{ad}g_{bc})$, for which $Z_{b} = K(h^{ac}g_{ac}g(k,e_{b}) - h^{ac}g(e_{a},e_{b})g(k,e_{c})) = 0$. If this holds at every point of a connected region, the contracted Bianchi identity makes $K$ constant (Schur's lemma, standard, cited from memory), so $\nabla R = 0$ and the gradient term vanishes as well; conversely in constant curvature all four coefficients vanish. For the projected form, $r = 4\omega\cdot Z + (\nabla_{k}R)(e,e,e,e)$, and $r = 0$ for all $\omega$ requires $Z = 0$ and the gradient term to vanish, for every null $k$ and screen.

\emph{Step 7 (examples).} In the plane waves, the gravitational fields $\hb^{-1}(a) = a + \tfrac12 H\,(a\cdot e_{v})\,e_{v}$ ($e_{v}$ null, $e_{u}\cdot e_{v} = -1$) with derived metric $-2\,du\,dv + H\,du^{2} + dx^{2} + dy^{2}$, the only curvature components are $R_{uiuj} = -\tfrac12\partial_{i}\partial_{j}H$. For $k = \partial_{u}$, $Z = 0$, and for $H$ quadratic the gradient vanishes, so $r = \theta_{l}\Ric^{\circ}(k,k) - 2\sigma_{l}\!:\!\widehat{C}_{k}$: for the vacuum wave $H = 3x^{2} - 3y^{2} + 2xy$ an element with $\sigma_{l} \neq 0$ gives $r \neq 0$ ($32$ in the check), so the Jacobson-Myers form fails (H1) in vacuum; for the null dust $H = x^{2} - 5y^{2} + 2xy$, $\Ric^{\circ}(k,k) = 4$ and an isotropic element with $\theta_{l} = 4$ gives $r = 16$. For the vacuum wave $H = x^{3} - 3xy^{2}$, the null direction $k = \partial_{u} + \tfrac12\partial_{v} + \partial_{x}$, the flat element spanned by $e_{1} = \partial_{u} + \tfrac32\partial_{v} + 2\partial_{x}$ and $e_{2} = \partial_{y}$ (orthonormal, orthogonal to $k$ and to $l = \tfrac12\partial_{u} + \tfrac94\partial_{v} + \tfrac32\partial_{x}$, with $g(k,l) = -1$), and $k^{u} = 1$ along the element, $B^{(k)} = B^{(l)} = 0$ and $\omega = 0$ at $p$, and $R(e_{1},e_{2},e_{1},e_{2}) = R_{uyuy} = 3x$, so both rates equal $2\,k(3x) = 6$. On a radial generator of the Schwarzschild-de Sitter metric, a flat element tangent to the sphere has $\theta_{l} = \sigma_{l} = 0$, $\omega = 0$, $\Ric^{\circ}(k,k) = 0$ and $\widehat{C}_{k} = 0$ (a radial null direction is a repeated principal null direction) and $Z = 0$ by spherical symmetry, so (i) reduces to the gradient term; its value there, a change of the Euler entropy with no heat and no area change, is computed in the result filed alongside, synthesis.series-wald-entropy-changes-without-flux-on-local-horizons, and is not recomputed here.

\emph{Step 8 (consequences).} By Step 6, with $\alpha \neq 0$ the Clausius relation holds on every admissible patch through every point of a connected region, for the Jacobson-Myers form, only if the region has constant curvature; if Einstein's equations hold there, $8\pi G\,T(k,k) = \Ric^{\circ}(k,k) = 0$ and $C = 0$: no null energy and no Weyl curvature. The examples of Step 7 show the projected form fails in vacuum too. So the entropy that (H1) can use on the Einstein route does not contain the Euler term in either form. If (H1) were imposed only on flat elements ($B^{(l)} = 0$ and $\omega = 0$ at $p$), Step 6 would not apply and the constant-curvature conclusion would not follow, but $\beta = 0$ would: the gradient term alone is nonzero on the vacuum plane wave of Step 7 and on radial Schwarzschild-de Sitter generators, so the Euler coefficient must vanish already there. For the family $\frac{1}{4G}\int(\eta' + \beta\,{}^{(2)}\!R)\,dA$ (or with $P$), the Euler part contributes $\frac{\beta}{4G}r$ at first order and the area part nothing, so (H1) on a region that is not of constant curvature forces $\beta = 0$; with clause (iv) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-entropy-clause-curvature-independent-density}, $\eta'$ is constant. This is clause (Loc) of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise} for that family: the density depends on no curvature at the point. Densities built from other curvature components (for example $\Ric^{\circ}(k,k)$ or $R$, as in Ricci-polynomial extensions) are not treated, and (Loc) is not derived for them here. The argument needs the entropy to be a functional of the cut, so that its change between $\lambda_{0}$ and $0$ includes the change of the density; on the differences reading $\delta S = \eta\,\delta A$ with $\eta$ evaluated at $p$ there is no such term, and a curvature-dependent $\eta$ is consistent with (H1) (filed alongside, synthesis.loc-independent-of-clausius-and-killing-data).

\emph{Remarks.} (a) The rate is a total divergence on the cut: in two dimensions $\int\sqrt{h}\,{}^{(2)}\!R$ is topological, and its first variation under $\delta h_{ab} = 2B^{(k)}_{ab}\,\delta\lambda$ is $\sqrt{h}\,(2D^{a}D^{b}\sigma^{(k)}_{ab} - D^{2}\theta_{k})\,\delta\lambda$ (first variation of the two-dimensional Einstein-Hilbert density, cited from memory). So on closed cuts it integrates to zero, as Theorem \claimref{synthesis.euler-term-horizon-entropy-shift}(ii) states; on an open patch in the thin-pencil limit it does not, and the formula of (i) evaluates it at $p$ through the Codazzi equation, whose trace carries the Weyl component $C(l,k,k,e_{b})$ as well as $\Ric^{\circ}(k,e_{b})$. (b) The two forms of the Wald entropy differ off bifurcation surfaces by the extrinsic term of the Gauss equation, one of the ambiguities of Jacobson, Kang and Myers \cite{JacobsonKangMyers1994}; both fail. Clausius derivations of Lovelock equations with the Jacobson-Myers entropy exist under extra conditions on the patch (Guedens, Jacobson and Sarkar 2012; Parikh and Svesko 2018, both cited from memory and not used): as recalled here, the latter uses closed spherical cuts of a stretched light cone, on which the Euler rate integrates to zero by Remark (a), and the former restricts the local horizon beyond vanishing expansion and shear at the point. Either restriction removes some of the freedom in $\theta_{l}$, $\sigma_{l}$, $\omega$ used in Step 6, or closes the cut, so they do not conflict with this result, which concerns (H1) as the store states it: every admissible open element. In four dimensions the Euler term leaves the field equations Einstein's, and the obstruction found here is in the entropy, not in the equations. (c) Nothing here bears on the de Sitter or Schwarzschild-de Sitter entropies of closed horizons, which Theorem \claimref{synthesis.sds-clausius-fixes-area-constant} already ties to the area law with zero constant.

\emph{The check.} Exact truncated power series in $(s_{1}, s_{2}, \lambda)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$: the null normal of a polynomial element is solved as a series with prescribed $k^{u}$, the generators $X + \lambda k$ give the induced metric, its scalar curvature is computed from Christoffel symbols with series inverses and square roots, and the $\lambda$-coefficient of $\sqrt{h}\,{}^{(2)}\!R$ at $s = 0$ is the rate. The Riemann tensor of the polynomial metric and its first derivatives at $p$ are computed independently, and the projected rate is computed from the dragged frame $e_{a} + \lambda\,\partial_{a}k$. On three polynomial metrics with generic rational quadratic and cubic terms in every component, and elements with generic $B^{(l)}$, normalisation gradient and cubic data, both formulas of (i) hold exactly, every term is nonzero in some case, and the Bianchi form of the gradient term agrees. The plane-wave cases of Step 7, flat space (rate $0$ for a curved element), the independence of third- and fourth-order element data and of the normalisation where $Z = 0$, the rank statements of Step 6, and the order counting of Step 5 for three values of $\Lambda$ (including a negative one) are checked separately.
