synthesis.euler-entropy-of-a-horizon-pat.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = G = 1$; $\Lambda \neq 0$ and $\alpha = -3/(4\Lambda)$, the Euler coefficient of the series' Lagrangian $(R - 2\Lambda + \alpha E_{4})/16\pi$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.euler-term-horizon-entropy-shift}(i)). Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), $\Sigma$ a spacelike two-surface element (a cut of a local horizon) with its Riemannian induced metric, Gauss curvature $K$ (${}^{(2)}\!R = 2K$) and area element $dA$, and for a compact patch $P \subset \Sigma$ with piecewise smooth edge let $S[P] = \tfrac14\int_{P}(1 + 2\alpha\,{}^{(2)}\!R)\,dA = A(P)/4 + S_{E}[P]$, $S_{E}[P] = \alpha\int_{P}K\,dA$, be the Jacobson-Myers functional of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-wald-noether-charge-entropy}(c) evaluated on the patch, as in (W$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.series-wald-entropy-changes-without-flux-on-local-horizons}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Transgression on the cut.)} For every orthonormal frame $(e_{2}, e_{3})$ tangent to $\Sigma$ on an open set $U$, with $\Omega_{\Sigma} = -\omega_{\Sigma}J$, $J = e_{2}e_{3}$, the rotation-gauge field of the cut in that frame and $\omega_{\Sigma}$ its Cartan connection form (conventions C10; in components the $e_{2}\wedge e_{3}$ component of the connection one-form, $de^{2} = -\omega_{\Sigma}\wedge e^{3}$, $de^{3} = \omega_{\Sigma}\wedge e^{2}$), the field strength of the cut is $\mathcal{R}_{\Sigma}(J) = K\,J$, that is $d\omega_{\Sigma} = K\,e^{2}\wedge e^{3}$. Hence on every patch $P \subset U$ on which the frame is smooth, $S_{E}[P] = \alpha\oint_{\partial P}\omega_{\Sigma}$, $\alpha$ times the holonomy angle of the cut's own rotation-gauge field (its Levi-Civita connection) around the edge, measured against the frame smooth on $P$; under a rotation of the frame by $\theta$, $\omega_{\Sigma} \mapsto \omega_{\Sigma} - d\theta$, so the edge integral is unchanged for $\theta$ smooth on $P$ and shifts by $-2\pi w$ for winding $w$ along the edge, $S_{E}$ by $-2\pi\alpha w$. (Reading.) In a frame adapted to the cut this edge term is the wall counterterm one dimension down, a reading supported by the following exact identities: the Chern-Simons form $Q(\omega)$ of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.wall-counterterm} has gauge variation $\delta_{\lambda}Q = d\bigl(\epsilon_{abcd}\lambda^{ab}d\omega^{cd}\bigr)$ (for $\delta\omega = D\lambda$), whose two-form $\epsilon_{abcd}\lambda^{ab}d\omega^{cd}$ is $4\,d\omega^{23}$ for $\lambda$ the binormal $e_{0}\wedge e_{1}$ of the cut, and on the cut $R^{23} - d\omega^{23} = -(b_{2}\wedge a_{3} + a_{2}\wedge b_{3})$ with $a_{A} = \omega^{A0} - \omega^{A1}$ and $b_{A} = \tfrac12(\omega^{A0} + \omega^{A1})$ the extrinsic forms along the null normals $k = e_{0} + e_{1}$ and $l$, which vanishes on admissible cuts ($a = 0$, the local Rindler cuts of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}).
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The edge term.)} By Gauss-Bonnet with edge and corners (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gauss-bonnet-with-corners-poincare-hopf-and-edge-term}(a)), for every patch $P$, with $k_{g}$ the geodesic curvature of its edge in $\Sigma$ (the rate at which the edge tangent turns against the cut's own parallel transport along the edge) and $\varepsilon_{j}$ the turning angles at its corners,
\[
S_{E}[P] + \alpha\Bigl(\oint_{\partial P}k_{g}\,ds + \sum_{j}\varepsilon_{j}\Bigr) \;=\; 2\pi\alpha\,\chi(P) \;=\; -\frac{3\pi\,\chi(P)}{2\Lambda} .
\]
So with the edge term $E[\partial P] = \alpha(\oint k_{g}\,ds + \sum_{j}\varepsilon_{j})$ added (the two-dimensional Gibbons-Hawking term of the Euler functional, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gauss-bonnet-with-corners-poincare-hopf-and-edge-term}(c); on open patches the Noether charge is fixed only up to edge terms, and choosing this one is argued, not derived), the Euler part of the entropy of every patch is a constant fixed by its topology, $-3\pi/(2\Lambda)$ for a disk. Along the generators of any local horizon, patches keep their topology, so the entropy $S'[P] = S[P] + E[\partial P] = A(P)/4 + 2\pi\alpha\chi(P)$ changes as $\delta A/4$: on the radial generators of every Schwarzschild-de Sitter hole, where the bare density $-3M/(2\Lambda r^{3})$ varies with no area change and no flux, $\delta S' = 0 = \delta Q$, and on every admissible element the first-order defect of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.euler-entropy-first-order-rate-on-local-patches}(ii) is absent; the Clausius relation (H1) holds for $S'$ on every open patch on which it holds for $A/4$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(What no edge term removes.)} No edge term that is additive under gluing (equal and opposite on the two orientations of a shared edge) and determined by the field and the cut alone makes $S_{E}$ vanish on every patch: cutting a closed cut along a circle into two disks, the edge terms cancel while $\alpha\int_{\Sigma}K\,dA = 2\pi\alpha\chi(\Sigma) \neq 0$ for a sphere. The geodesic-curvature term of (ii) leaves $2\pi\alpha\chi(P)$ on each patch (its corner turns are not additive); the frame-relative term of (i) is additive but needs a frame smooth on each patch, and on a sphere the frames smooth on two complementary caps differ along the common edge by a rotation of winding $2 = \chi$ (the clutching number, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gauss-bonnet-with-corners-poincare-hopf-and-edge-term}(b)), which carries the same $2\pi\alpha\chi$. On closed cuts every choice leaves $2\pi\alpha\chi = -3\pi\chi/(2\Lambda)$, the shift of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.euler-term-horizon-entropy-shift}(ii), equal to $-\chi/2$ times the de Sitter entropy $3\pi/\Lambda$; it is removed by the normalisation (Z) or by nonnegativity (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.sds-clausius-fixes-area-constant}(v)), not by an edge term. On open patches the constant is not negligible: for $\Lambda > 0$, $S'[P] = A(P)/4 - 3\pi/(2\Lambda)$ on every disk patch, negative whenever $A(P) < 6\pi/\Lambda$, half the de Sitter horizon area $12\pi/\Lambda$; $S'$ is non-additive and is usable as an entropy only after the normalisation.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The two routes.)} Read with the edge term of (ii), the Wald (Jacobson-Myers) entropy of the series' action and the entropy of the Clausius route agree on every entropy change of an open patch and differ on values by the topological constant $2\pi\alpha\chi(P)$ alone. The open-patch disagreement of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.series-wald-entropy-changes-without-flux-on-local-horizons} is therefore the bare functional's missing edge term, and the remaining disagreement is one constant on open patches and closed cuts alike. Since $A(P)/4 + 2\pi\alpha\chi(P)$ is not the integral of a density, the integrated reading of (Loc) excludes the constant, and so excludes the Euler term from horizon entropy; on the differences reading it is invisible. Transport fixes neither: the exclusion of the Euler term stays a decision (the normalisation (Z), with horizon entropy read as (Loc) rather than the action's Wald entropy), not a consequence of the series' objects; nothing in (i) to (iii) uses the series' objects beyond the value of $\alpha$.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.euler-entropy-of-a-horizon-pat.technical:
Take the series' Lagrangian $(R - 2\Lambda + \alpha E_{4})/16\pi$, $\alpha = -3/(4\Lambda)$, and read the entropy of a patch $P$ of a cut as the Jacobson-Myers functional, $A(P)/4$ plus the Euler part $S_{E}[P] = \alpha\int_{P}K\,dA$. On a cut, $K\,dA$ is exact: $K\,e^{2}\wedge e^{3} = d\omega_{\Sigma}$ with $\omega_{\Sigma}$ the Cartan form of the cut's rotation-gauge field $\Omega_{\Sigma} = -\omega_{\Sigma}J$ in any tangent frame ($\mathcal{R}_{\Sigma}(J) = KJ$). So $S_{E}[P]$ is an edge quantity, $\alpha$ times the holonomy angle of the cut's own rotation-gauge field around the edge, measured against a frame smooth on $P$, unchanged by smooth frame rotations and shifted by $-2\pi\alpha w$ for a frame winding $w$ times along the edge. As a reading, in an adapted frame this is the Chern-Simons wall counterterm one dimension down: the gauge variation of $Q(\omega)$ under the cut's binormal is $4\,d\omega^{23}$, and on admissible cuts $R^{23} = d\omega^{23}$ there.

By Gauss-Bonnet, $S_{E}[P] + \alpha(\oint k_{g}\,ds + \sum\varepsilon_{j}) = 2\pi\alpha\chi(P)$. With this geodesic-curvature edge term added (the two-dimensional Gibbons-Hawking term, a choice within the edge ambiguity of the Noether charge on open patches, argued not derived), the Euler part of every patch is the constant $-3\pi\chi(P)/(2\Lambda)$, so entropy changes along a local horizon are $\delta A/4$: on radial Schwarzschild-de Sitter generators the change is zero, matching the zero heat flux, where the bare density changes as $-3M/(2\Lambda r^{3})$. No additive edge term built from the field and the cut removes the constant (on a sphere cut into two disks the edge terms cancel and $4\pi\alpha$ is left); a frame-relative edge term moves it into the clutching winding $\chi$ of the cap frames. On closed cuts every choice leaves the stored shift $-3\pi\chi/(2\Lambda)$, which the normalisation (Z) or nonnegativity removes; on open patches, for $\Lambda > 0$, it makes the edge-corrected entropy negative on every disk patch of area below $6\pi/\Lambda$. So, with that edge term, the action and Clausius routes agree on entropy changes and differ by one topological constant; the integrated reading of (Loc) excludes it, transport does not. Transport-absent: the series supplies only $\alpha$.
synthesis.euler-entropy-of-a-horizon-pat.lay: The series' gravitational action contains an extra term (the Euler term) which leaves Einstein's equations unchanged but, in the standard recipe, adds a curvature-dependent piece to the entropy of a horizon. A stored result showed that this piece changes along small patches of a horizon with no heat flowing, which clashes with the heat-balance route to Einstein's equations. This result shows that the troublesome piece of a patch is really a property of the patch's edge: it equals a fixed multiple of the angle by which a direction carried around the edge within the patch's own surface turns. Adding the standard edge correction (how sharply the edge bends), which is a natural choice rather than one forced by the action, turns the piece into a fixed number set only by the patch's shape type, the same for every disk-shaped patch. Then the entropy changes exactly as the heat-balance route requires. What is left is a constant that no edge correction can remove; it is the same constant already known for closed horizons, and it is removed by the existing normalisation, not by anything in the series' objects. Without that normalisation the constant would even make the entropy of small patches negative.

proofs.main:
Everything is read in Gauge Theory Gravity on one flat chart (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}). The cut $\Sigma$ is a two-surface of the background; its induced derived metric is that of a two-dimensional gauge field $(\hb_{\Sigma}, \Omega_{\Sigma})$ on a flat Riemannian plane, with a constant orthonormal physical frame $e_{2}, e_{3}$ ($Q(e_{2}) = Q(e_{3}) = -1$) and unit bivector $J = e_{2}e_{3}$, $J^{2} = -1$; its field strength gives $\mathcal{R}_{\Sigma}(J) = K\,J$, $K$ the Gauss curvature. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.euler-term-horizon-entropy-shift}(i) and Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-wald-noether-charge-entropy}(c) the Jacobson-Myers density is $\tfrac14(1 + 2\alpha\,{}^{(2)}\!R) = \tfrac14 + \alpha K$, so $S[P] = A(P)/4 + \alpha\int_{P}K\,dA$; this is (W$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.series-wald-entropy-changes-without-flux-on-local-horizons}.

\emph{(i)} In two dimensions the bivectors are the multiples of $J$, so the rotation-gauge field of the cut is $\Omega_{\Sigma}(a) = -\omega_{\Sigma}(a)\,J$ with $\omega_{\Sigma}$ a scalar-valued linear function of $a$ (the minus sign is the Cartan convention of the statement's structure equations, dictionary C10), and its field strength has no commutator term, $\Omega_{\Sigma}(a)\times\Omega_{\Sigma}(b) = 0$:
\[
R_{\Sigma}(a\wedge b) = a\cdot\nabla\Omega_{\Sigma}(b) - b\cdot\nabla\Omega_{\Sigma}(a) = -(d\omega_{\Sigma})(a, b)\,J ,
\]
the exterior derivative written $d\omega_{\Sigma} = \nabla\wedge\omega_{\Sigma}$ for the gradient vector of $\omega_{\Sigma}$. With $\mathcal{R}_{\Sigma}(B) = -R_{\Sigma}(\hb_{\Sigma}(B))$ and $\mathcal{R}_{\Sigma}(J) = KJ$ this is $d\omega_{\Sigma} = K\,e^{2}\wedge e^{3}$, the two-dimensional transgression: the Euler form of the cut is the exterior derivative of its Chern-Simons form, which in two dimensions is the connection itself (the torsion equation $\hb_{\Sigma}^{T}(\nabla\wedge f^{A}) = \sum_{B}e^{B}\wedge(\Omega_{\Sigma}(e_{B})\cdot e^{A})$ is, in components, the structure equations $de^{2} = -\omega_{\Sigma}\wedge e^{3}$, $de^{3} = \omega_{\Sigma}\wedge e^{2}$ of the statement). Stokes' theorem on a patch $P$ on which the frame is smooth gives $\int_{P}K\,dA = \oint_{\partial P}\omega_{\Sigma}$. Parallel transport around the edge is the rotor $U$ with $dU/d\lambda = -\Omega_{\Sigma}(x')U/2$, $U = \exp(\tfrac12 J\oint_{\partial P}\omega_{\Sigma})$ against the frame, so $\oint_{\partial P}\omega_{\Sigma}$ is the holonomy angle of the cut's own rotation-gauge field (its Levi-Civita connection) around the edge, measured against the frame; this is the cut's intrinsic parallel transport, not the series' tractor transport. A rotation by $\theta$ of the tangent frame of the statement, which is the frame map $E_{A} = \hb_{\Sigma}(e_{A})$, $E_{2}' = \cos\theta\,E_{2} + \sin\theta\,E_{3}$, is the rotation gauge transformation $\hb_{\Sigma}^{-1} \mapsto R\,\hb_{\Sigma}^{-1}\tilde R$ with the rotor $R = e^{-J\theta/2}$ (then $\hb_{\Sigma}'(e_{2}) = \hb_{\Sigma}(\tilde R e_{2}R)$ and $\tilde R e_{2}R = \cos\theta\,e_{2} + \sin\theta\,e_{3}$); by the law of the definition, $\Omega_{\Sigma}' = R\Omega_{\Sigma}\tilde R - 2(a\cdot\nabla R)\tilde R = \Omega_{\Sigma} + (a\cdot\nabla\theta)J$ ($R$ commutes with $J$), that is $\omega_{\Sigma}' = \omega_{\Sigma} - d\theta$, so the edge integral changes by $-\oint d\theta$: zero when $\theta$ is a function on $P$, $-2\pi w$ when $\theta$ winds $w$ times along the edge. The GTG check builds the cut $ds^{2} + \rho(s)^{2}d\phi^{2}$ as the gauge field $\hb_{\Sigma}^{-1}(e_{s}) = e_{2}$, $\hb_{\Sigma}^{-1}(e_{\phi}) = \rho\,e_{3}$ for five polynomial profiles $\rho$ at three points, solves the torsion equation, and finds $\Omega_{\Sigma}(e_{s}) = 0$, $\Omega_{\Sigma}(e_{\phi}) = \rho' J$ (so $\omega_{\Sigma} = -\rho'\,d\phi$), no commutator term, field strength $\rho''J$ and $\mathcal{R}_{\Sigma}(J) = KJ$ with $K = -\rho''/\rho$; with the frame rotated by $\theta$, $\cos\theta = (1 - t^{2})/(1 + t^{2})$, $\sin\theta = 2t/(1 + t^{2})$ for three polynomials $t(s)$, it finds $\Omega_{\Sigma}'(e_{s}) = \theta' J$ with $\theta' = 2t'/(1 + t^{2})$ and $\Omega_{\Sigma}'(e_{\phi})$ unchanged. The earlier check computes the same from the Christoffel symbols and confirms the equality of area and edge integrals on rectangles $[s_{1}, s_{2}]\times[0, \phi_{0}]$.

For the link with the wall counterterm: for $Q = \epsilon_{abcd}(\omega^{ab}\wedge d\omega^{cd} + \tfrac23\omega^{ab}\wedge\omega^{c}{}_{e}\wedge\omega^{ed})$ and $\delta\omega = D\lambda$, the first variation is $\delta Q = 2\epsilon(\delta\omega, R) - d\,\epsilon(\omega, \delta\omega)$, and with $\epsilon(D\lambda, R) = d\,\epsilon(\lambda, R)$ (Bianchi identity and invariance of $\epsilon$) this is $d\,\epsilon(\lambda, d\omega)$, the standard gauge variation of a Chern-Simons form (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-chern-weil-and-chern-simons-forms}(c)); the check confirms $\delta_{\lambda}Q = d\,\epsilon(\lambda, d\omega)$ exactly as an identity of forms for a polynomial $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$ connection with legs in all four directions and a polynomial parameter, with $\epsilon_{abcd}$ read from $e_{a}e_{b}e_{c}e_{d} = \epsilon_{abcd}I$ in $\Cl(1,3)$. In GA the contraction is $\epsilon_{abcd}X^{ab}Y^{cd} = 4\langle X I^{-1}Y\rangle$ for bivectors $X = \tfrac12 X^{ab}e_{a}\wedge e_{b}$, $Y$ (the form of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.wall-counterterm}); for the binormal $\lambda = e_{0}\wedge e_{1}$, $\lambda I^{-1} = -e_{2}e_{3}$, so $4\langle\lambda I^{-1}Y\rangle = 4\,Y^{23}$ and $\epsilon_{abcd}\lambda^{ab}d\omega^{cd} = 4\,d\omega^{23}$ (the GTG check confirms $4\langle\lambda I^{-1}Y\rangle = 4Y^{23}$ on three bivectors). On the cut $x_{0} = x_{1} = 0$ in a frame with $e_{2}, e_{3}$ tangent, $R^{23} - d\omega^{23} = \omega^{2}{}_{0}\wedge\omega^{03} + \omega^{2}{}_{1}\wedge\omega^{13} = -\omega^{20}\wedge\omega^{30} + \omega^{21}\wedge\omega^{31}$, and substituting $\omega^{A0} = b_{A} + a_{A}/2$, $\omega^{A1} = b_{A} - a_{A}/2$ gives $-(b_{2}\wedge a_{3} + a_{2}\wedge b_{3})$; with $\eta_{11} = -1$, $a_{A}$ is (up to sign) the second fundamental form along $k = e_{0} + e_{1}$, so on an admissible cut $R^{23} = d\omega^{23}$ there (the Gauss equation; the check confirms the identity on a generic connection and that the defect is nonzero when $a \neq 0$). So, as a reading supported by these identities, in an adapted frame on admissible cuts the frame-relative edge term of (i) is the wall counterterm's gauge variation under the cut's binormal, as the wall counterterm is the primitive of the Euler term on a wall: in both cases a transgression of a topological density, defined relative to a frame, with a topological residual.

\emph{(ii)} Gauss-Bonnet for a compact surface with piecewise smooth boundary (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gauss-bonnet-with-corners-poincare-hopf-and-edge-term}(a)): $\int_{P}K\,dA + \oint_{\partial P}k_{g}\,ds + \sum_{j}\varepsilon_{j} = 2\pi\chi(P)$, with $k_{g}$ taken with respect to the inward normal and $\varepsilon_{j}$ the turning angles at corners. Multiplying by $\alpha$ gives the displayed identity, and $2\pi\alpha = -3\pi/(2\Lambda)$. In GTG the geodesic curvature of an edge with unit tangent $T$ and unit normal $N$ in the cut is $k_{g} = -((T\cdot D)T)\cdot N$ (the induced metric is minus the flat product on the Riemannian cut); for the circles $s = \mathrm{const}$, $(e_{3}\cdot D)e_{3} = \Omega_{\Sigma}(e_{\phi})\cdot e_{3}/\rho = -(\rho'/\rho)\,e_{2}$, so $k_{g} = \mp\rho'/\rho$ for $N = \pm e_{2}$ (the GTG check computes this from the solved gauge field; the earlier check computes $k_{g}$ as $g(\nabla_{T}T, N)$ from the Christoffel symbols), verifies that the meridians are geodesics, and confirms the identity in units of $2\pi$ on rectangles (four right corners, total turn one), polar caps (no corners) and annuli ($\chi = 0$) for every profile. A local horizon moves its cuts along generators by a smooth deformation, so a patch keeps its topology and $\delta(2\pi\alpha\chi(P)) = 0$; hence $\delta S' = \delta A/4$. On the radial generators of a Schwarzschild-de Sitter hole, by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.series-wald-entropy-changes-without-flux-on-local-horizons}(ii), $K = 2M/r^{3} + \Lambda/3$ on the admissible cuts, $\delta A = 0$ and $\delta Q = 0$, while the bare density is $-3M/(2\Lambda r^{3})$; the check confirms $K = (1 - f)/r^{2}$, the bare density, the nonzero two-signed bare change, and that $\tfrac14 + \alpha K - \alpha K = \tfrac14$ at five points along each generator for three holes, both signs and two patch lengths. In the thin-pencil limit (H2) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius} the constant $2\pi\alpha\chi(P)$ is the same at both ends of the pencil, so it drops out of $\delta S'$ at every $a_{0}$; the first-order rate of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.euler-entropy-first-order-rate-on-local-patches}(i) is the $\lambda$-derivative of $\alpha\int K\,dA$, which by Gauss-Bonnet is minus the derivative of the edge term, so it is absent from $S'$ and the defect of (ii) of that theorem vanishes for every admissible element.

\emph{(iii)} Suppose $Y$ assigns to each oriented edge a number, with $Y(-c) = -Y(c)$, determined by the field and the cut, and $S_{E}[P] = -Y(\partial P)$ for every disk patch. Cut a closed cut $\Sigma$ of genus zero along a circle $c$ into disks $P_{1}, P_{2}$; then $S_{E}[\Sigma] = -Y(c) - Y(-c) = 0$, while $S_{E}[\Sigma] = \alpha\int_{\Sigma}K\,dA = 4\pi\alpha \neq 0$ (the check confirms $\int K\,dA = 4\pi$ on three closed profiles $\rho = s(L - s)(1 + c\,s(L - s))/L$, $\rho'(0) = 1$, $\rho'(L) = -1$, positive inside). So no such $Y$ exists. The geodesic-curvature term is additive on smooth edges but its corner turns are not (two rectangles glued along a full edge have eight right corners, their union four), which is where $2\pi\chi(P)$ sits. The frame term $\oint\omega_{\Sigma}$ is additive for one frame, but no tangent frame is smooth on a sphere (Poincar\'e-Hopf, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gauss-bonnet-with-corners-poincare-hopf-and-edge-term}(b)): on the caps $s < s_{e}$ and $s > s_{e}$ the frames rotated by $\mp\phi$ from the polar frame are smooth, with $\omega_{N} = (1 - \rho')\,d\phi$ and $\omega_{S} = (-1 - \rho')\,d\phi$ vanishing at their poles, and along every separating circle $\omega_{N} - \omega_{S} = 2\,d\phi$, winding $2 = \chi(S^{2})$ (the clutching number, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gauss-bonnet-with-corners-poincare-hopf-and-edge-term}(b)); the check confirms both cap integrals as edge integrals and their sum $4\pi$ at three separating circles of three closed profiles. Hence on a closed cut every choice leaves $2\pi\alpha\chi = -3\pi\chi/(2\Lambda)$, which is the shift of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.euler-term-horizon-entropy-shift}(ii) ($-3\pi/\Lambda$ on spheres) and, with $3\pi/\Lambda$ the de Sitter entropy, $-\chi/2$ times it; Theorem \claimref{synthesis.sds-clausius-fixes-area-constant}(v) excludes it under (Z) or nonnegativity. On a disk patch, $S'[P] = A(P)/4 + 2\pi\alpha = A(P)/4 - 3\pi/(2\Lambda)$, so for $\Lambda > 0$, $S'[P] < 0$ exactly when $A(P) < 6\pi/\Lambda$, half the de Sitter horizon area $4\pi\cdot 3/\Lambda$ (the check confirms the threshold and the sign at three values of $\Lambda$); for $\Lambda < 0$ the constant is positive. Two disks glued along an edge have $S'$ summing to $A/4 - 3\pi/\Lambda$ against $A/4 - 3\pi/(2\Lambda)$ for their union, so $S'$ is not additive.

\emph{(iv)} By (ii), with the edge term, entropy changes of open patches are $\delta A/4$ for both readings, so (H1) holds for $S'$ exactly where it holds for $A/4$, and the bare functional's open-patch defect is the variation of the omitted edge term. By (iii) the remaining difference, $2\pi\alpha\chi(P)$ on every patch and $2\pi\alpha\chi$ on closed cuts, is one topological constant that no additive edge term removes. Under the integrated reading of (Loc) in Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise} the entropy of a patch is $\int\eta\,dA$, which $A(P)/4 + 2\pi\alpha\chi(P)$ is not for $\alpha \neq 0$ (the constant does not scale with the patch), so that reading excludes the constant; on the differences reading the constant does not enter. Nothing in (i) to (iii) uses a property of the frozen point, the canonical tractor or the tractor gauge field beyond the value of $\alpha$, so transport does not fix the constant: the exclusion of the Euler term from horizon entropy remains the adopted decision. Whether the edge term of (ii) is the one the action prescribes on open patches is argued, not proved: it is the Gibbons-Hawking term of the two-dimensional Euler functional (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gauss-bonnet-with-corners-poincare-hopf-and-edge-term}(c)), the term that makes its variation with the edge metric held fixed well posed, and Wald's Noether charge is fixed only up to closed forms, which on an open patch are edge terms; the Iyer-Wald and Jacobson-Kang-Myers rules (cited from memory) fix that freedom only on closed cuts.


\emph{Remark (argued, not used above).} In the BF variables of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-action-is-bf-transport-broken-by-the-blade-i-wedge-x}, the on-shell two-form field is proportional to the pseudoscalar dual of the Lorentz block of the Cartan curvature, and the pseudoscalar maps the cut's tangent bivector $e_{2}\wedge e_{3}$ to the binormal $e_{0}\wedge e_{1}$ up to sign; so the Jacobson-Myers density $-\tfrac{3}{4\Lambda}F(e_{2}, e_{3}, e_{2}, e_{3})$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.series-wald-entropy-changes-without-flux-on-local-horizons}(i) is, up to a constant whose sign is not fixed here, the flux of that field through the cut (the usual reading of the Wald entropy of a BF-type action, cited from memory). Splitting the Cartan curvature $F_{abcd}$ of that Theorem (minus the Lorentz block $R + \ell^{-2}e\wedge e$ of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west}, the Riemann tensor taken positive on spheres) into its Lorentz part and its soldering part $-\tfrac{\Lambda}{3}e\wedge e$, the soldering part gives $-\tfrac{3}{4\Lambda}\cdot(-\tfrac{\Lambda}{3}) = \tfrac14$, the area density, and the Lorentz part gives the Euler part treated in (i) to (iii). The adopted reading of horizon entropy as (Loc) keeps the flux of the soldering part only.

\emph{In components} (a labelled reading). In the coframe $e^{2} = ds$, $e^{3} = \rho\,d\phi$ the torsion equation is $de^{2} = -\omega_{\Sigma}\wedge e^{3}$, $de^{3} = \omega_{\Sigma}\wedge e^{2}$, solved by $\omega_{\Sigma} = -\rho'\,d\phi$, and $d\omega_{\Sigma} = -\rho''\,ds\wedge d\phi = K\rho\,ds\wedge d\phi$; the earlier check computes $K$ from the Christoffel symbols and the Riemann tensor of $ds^{2} + \rho^{2}d\phi^{2}$ as rational functions of $s$ and confirms these identities, the frame rotation law, and the Chern-Simons variation and the Gauss-equation identity of (i) as identities of forms on a generic polynomial connection.

synthesis.field-space-premise-parallel-f.formal:
\emph{Premise (FS), the field space of the gravitational action.} Work in $\Cl(2,4)$ in the chart of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}, $\nO = \tfrac12(e_{4} + e_{5})$, $\nInf = e_{4} - e_{5}$, $\ip{\nO}{\nInf} = 1$, with canonical tractor $X = \nO$. Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) on its invertible region, with derived metric $g$, and work in the scale $g$ (the physical scale). The \emph{varied gravitational connection} is the $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field $A$ (a bivector-valued one-form on flat spacetime, $D_{a}V = a \cdot \nabla V + A(a) \times V$) on which the gravitational action is varied; its soldering $a \mapsto A(a) \times X$ is nondegenerate (in the gauges below it is $\hb^{-1}(a)$). The premise: \emph{the varied gravitational connection admits a tractor field $I$ with $D_{a}I = 0$ for every $a$ and $\ip{X}{I} = 1$.} Since $A$ is bivector-valued, $Q(I) = 2\rho$ is then constant; $\Lambda := 6\rho$, so $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ as for the frozen point (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}). The value of $\rho$ is not fixed by (FS); the registered input $N$ fixes it. In the sense of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-holonomy-reductions-of-cartan-geometries}(a), $I$ is a holonomy reduction of $A$ to the stabiliser of $I$ (of de Sitter type for $\rho > 0$, anti-de Sitter type for $\rho < 0$); since $\ip{X}{I} = 1$ nowhere vanishes each connected region is a single open curved orbit, modelled on the stabiliser of $I$ with the Lorentz group as structure group (part (b) there and its reading). A special-conformal rotor, which fixes $X$, carries $I$ to the constant $I_{\rho} = \nInf + \rho\,\nO$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.inverse-frame-free-tractor-gauge-field-preserves-a-frozen-point}(vi)); in that gauge $A$ is valued in the stabiliser of $I_{\rho}$ and is $A_{\rho} = \Omega - (\nInf - \rho\,\nO) \wedge \hb^{-1}$ for a unique pair $(\hb, \Omega)$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-field-space-is-the-gtg-pair-and-its-omega-equation-is-the-torsion-equation}(ii)). (FS) is a condition on the connection that is varied, not on a solution: it is imposed for every configuration, Einstein or not, matter included.

\emph{What it is for.} With (FS) the frozen-point MacDowell-Mansouri functional $Q(I)^{-1}\int\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$ (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west}, Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}) has the frame equation $2(\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a)I = 0$, Einstein's equations with $\Lambda = 6\rho$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.macdowell-mansouri-principle-fixes-the-trace-free-part}), and its $\Omega$-equation is the torsion equation (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-field-space-is-the-gtg-pair-and-its-omega-equation-is-the-torsion-equation}(i)). Without it, the same integrand on the series' transport (the normal tractor connection of a torsion-free field) is a quarter of the Weyl square, with the Bach equations (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-integrand-on-tractor-transport-is-weyl-squared}), and on torsion-free conformal Cartan connections with the special-conformal slot varied it returns that connection and the same Weyl square (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-integrand-gives-einstein-only-with-the-symmetric-slot-frozen}(ii)). So the store's gravitational action is the imported functional plus (FS); what carries Einstein's equations is (FS), not the integrand. The registration condition of the $w = -1$ prediction assumes it (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition}(iii)).

\emph{Equivalent readings} (each at the strength proved there).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(R1)] \emph{(Assembly from the gauge-theory-gravity pair.)} Under the gauge group of gauge theory gravity (rotations and affine displacements, not the parabolic group), a $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field assembled from $(\hb, \Omega)$ and no further field (T), covariant (G), soldered (S), and either polynomial with no inverse frame (P) or built without derivatives (O), is $A_{\rho}$ with $\rho$ constant, and conversely every connection obeying (FS) is such a field in the gauge where $I$ is constant (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.inverse-frame-free-tractor-gauge-field-preserves-a-frozen-point}(i), (ii), (vi)); the field space is then exactly the pair $(\hb, \Omega)$ with a constant tractor (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-field-space-is-the-gtg-pair-and-its-omega-equation-is-the-torsion-equation}(ii)). Neither (P) nor (O) suffices without (T).
\item[(R2)] \emph{(The special-conformal slot frozen.)} In the gauge where $I$ is constant, (FS) says that the special-conformal slot is $\rho\,\id$ and the dilation vanishes, with $\rho$ constant (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.parallel-frozen-point-on-matter-regions-is-the-field-space-premise}(i)). As a statement about field equations, on torsion-free fields the frozen-point integrand gives Einstein's equations with $\Lambda = 6\rho$ exactly when the symmetric part of the slot is frozen at $\rho\,\id$, $\rho \neq 0$; the dilation and the antisymmetric slot are inert, so this reading fixes the equations, not the connection in those inert directions (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-integrand-gives-einstein-only-with-the-symmetric-slot-frozen}(iii)-(v)).
\item[(R3)] \emph{(Infinite stiffness.)} Read as a Higgs field on the unreduced connection, the frozen point reduces the connection, for the stored Stelle-West family and any curvature-independent slot potential, only in the infinitely stiff limit of the polynomial stiffness penalty, where its broken components vanish; finite stiffness adds a Weyl square, and a multiplier imposing $DI = 0$ is (FS) written into the action (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-reduces-the-connection-only-when-infinitely-stiff}). Equivalently, the gauge group of the varied field is the stabiliser of $I$, not the parabolic group of the line of $X$.
\item[(R4)] \emph{(Parallel on matter regions in the physical scale.)} In the physical scale the frozen point is parallel for a soldered connection exactly when the slot is $\tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\id$ with no dilation, for every field, matter included; adopting (FS) implies the registration condition of the $w = -1$ prediction, and that condition read kinematically (as fixing which connection carries the frozen point) is (FS) restated; read only of solutions it is weaker (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.parallel-frozen-point-on-matter-regions-is-the-field-space-premise}; forward and kinematic directions only).
\end{enumerate}

\emph{Not supplied by the series' other structures.} \emph{Transport:} for the normal tractor connection, preserving a tractor in the physical scale is the Einstein condition (Theorem \claimref{interior.scale-tractor-leaves-cone}, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}(ii)); the series' transport satisfies (T), (G), (S) and violates (P) and (O), in the special-conformal slot only (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.inverse-frame-free-tractor-gauge-field-preserves-a-frozen-point}(iii)), and on shell with matter it differs from $A_{\rho}$ by $4\pi G(T - \tfrac{\tau}{3}g)$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.parallel-frozen-point-on-matter-regions-is-the-field-space-premise}(ii)). \emph{The descent and a fixed frozen point:} a constant frozen point with the connection unrestricted is the unitary gauge of the Higgs reading, which gives conformal gravity at zero stiffness and reduces the connection only when infinitely stiff (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-reduces-the-connection-only-when-infinitely-stiff}); so freezing one $I$, as the descent's single frozen point does (Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}), does not restrict the connection. \emph{Topology:} sections of every norm and sign exist on every region with a scale, so neither the reduction nor the sign of $\Lambda$ is constrained (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.parallel-frozen-point-on-matter-regions-is-the-field-space-premise}(iv)). \emph{The duality structure:} the duality complex structure acts only on the Lorentz algebra, shared by every field space, and every chirality of the integrand returns the Schouten slot (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.duality-complex-structure-does-not-reach-the-frozen-point}). \emph{The independence of $\hb$ and $\Omega$:} on the reduced field space it decides exactly the torsion equation, not the frozen point (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-field-space-is-the-gtg-pair-and-its-omega-equation-is-the-torsion-equation}(i)). \emph{No inverse frame alone:} (P) admits an independent slot field and every row of the slot lattice (Theorems \claimref{synthesis.inverse-frame-free-tractor-gauge-field-preserves-a-frozen-point}(iv), \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-integrand-gives-einstein-only-with-the-symmetric-slot-frozen}(v)). Transport-convenient, not transport-essential: the chart, $X$ and the frozen point are the series' objects, and the premise is not derived from them.

\emph{What it does not give.} It does not fix $\rho$ (the registered input $N$ does), the normalisation of the action (Newton's constant), or the spin part of the matter coupling (torsion-free versus Einstein-Cartan). On the reduced field space $\rho$ is constant, so $\Lambda$ is a constant parameter and $w = -1$ is the $\Lambda$CDM equation of state: a confirmed $w = -1$ supports $\Lambda$CDM with a frozen point and is not evidence for (FS) independent of $\Lambda$CDM.

\emph{Refutation condition.} The premise is false if any of the following is established: (a) a confirmed detection of $w \neq -1$ at any epoch, with dark energy read as the norm of the frozen point (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition}(iii)), since on the reduced field space that norm, $\Lambda/3$, is constant (this refutes $\Lambda$CDM as well, so it does not discriminate (FS) from it); (b) with the imported functional, a confirmed departure of the gravitational field equations from Einstein's with a constant $\Lambda$ in a regime where the action applies, in particular a fourth-order (Weyl-square, Bach-type) term, which the reduced field space does not have and finite stiffness would add; (c) a derivation from the series' premises that the gravitational connection carries no parallel tractor of unit pairing with $X$ off the Einstein region, for example that its special-conformal slot is an independent field or the Schouten map, so that the frozen-point integrand gives the Bach equations rather than Einstein's.
synthesis.field-space-premise-parallel-f.technical:
The store reaches Einstein's equations from the frozen-point MacDowell-Mansouri functional only when it is varied over a particular field space, and no route through the series derives that field space; this premise records it. In invariant form: the $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field that is varied, with nondegenerate soldering, admits a parallel tractor $I$ whose pairing with the canonical tractor is one, that is, in the physical scale of the gravitational field. Its norm $Q(I) = 2ho$ is then constant and gives $\Lambda = 6ho$; in the language of Cap, Gover and Hammerl it is a holonomy reduction of the connection to the stabiliser of $I$, de Sitter or anti-de Sitter type, and the whole region is one open curved orbit. In the gauge where $I$ is the constant $
Inf + ho
O$ the connection is $\Omega - (
Inf - ho
O) \wedge \hb^{-1}$ for a unique gauge-theory-gravity pair. With it the functional's frame equation is Einstein's with that $\Lambda$ and its $\Omega$-equation the torsion equation; without it, on the series' transport or with the special-conformal slot free, the same integrand is the Weyl square and gives the Bach equations.

Four readings are proved equivalent at their stated strengths: building the connection from $(\hb, \Omega)$ alone, covariantly and soldered, with no inverse frame or no derivatives; the special-conformal slot frozen at $ho$ times the identity (as a statement about the field equations, only its symmetric part matters); the frozen point infinitely stiff, so that the gauge group of the varied field is the stabiliser of $I$ rather than the parabolic group; and the frozen point parallel on matter regions in the physical scale (forward and kinematic directions). Transport does not supply it (for the normal tractor connection preserving $I$ is the Einstein condition), nor does a fixed frozen point with the connection unrestricted, topology, the duality complex structure, the independence of $\hb$ and $\Omega$, or the no-inverse-frame hypothesis alone. It leaves $\Lambda$'s value, Newton's constant and the spin part of the matter coupling open, and with it $w = -1$ is the $\Lambda$CDM equation of state, not separate evidence. It would be refuted by a confirmed $w 
eq -1$, by a confirmed departure from Einstein's equations with constant $\Lambda$ (for example a Weyl-square term) where the action applies, or by a derivation that the gravitational connection has no such parallel tractor off the Einstein region.
synthesis.field-space-premise-parallel-f.lay: The series borrows a rule, an action, from which the equations of gravity follow, and that rule gives Einstein's equations only if one decides in advance which shapes of the gravitational field are allowed to vary: those that keep one special fixed direction, the frozen point, unchanged everywhere, measured in the actual scale of the spacetime. Without that decision the same rule gives a different theory, conformal gravity. Several attempts to derive the decision from the series' own structures failed; each turned out to be the same assumption in another form. So it is recorded as an assumption of its own. It explains why the cosmological constant is a fixed number, but for the same reason a measurement that dark energy never changes would not count as separate evidence for it. It would be refuted if dark energy were found to change, or if gravity were found to deviate from Einstein's equations where the rule applies.

synthesis.frozen-point-action-is-bf-tran.formal:
Let $\Lambda \neq 0$ and work on the Einstein region of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), with the frozen point $I$, $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, the canonical tractor $X$ and the Stelle-West vector $V = X - (3/\Lambda)I$ of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector} and Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.stelle-west-vector-frozen-point}; in the flat chart $I = \ninf + (\Lambda/6)\nO$, $X = \nO$. The chart is that of the stored frozen-point check: generators $e_{0}$ ($+1$), $e_{1}, e_{2}, e_{3}$ ($-1$), $e_{+}$ ($+1$), $e_{-}$ ($-1$), $\nO = (e_{+} + e_{-})/2$, $\ninf = e_{+} - e_{-}$, pseudoscalar $I_{6} = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}e_{+}e_{-}$, and a four-form is read by its coefficient as the sum over the six coordinate planes, $B \wedge C = \sum_{P,Q}\omega(P,Q)B_{P}C_{Q}\,d^{4}x$; in this orientation $\epsilon(I, V, e\wedge e, e\wedge e) = +6\det(\hb^{-1})$, and the opposite orientation of the pair $(\ninf, \nO)$ reverses $I \wedge V$ and every sign of $\epsilon(I, V, \cdot, \cdot)$. Let $\iota := (I \wedge V)\,I_{6}$, the unit pseudoscalar of $\{I, V\}^{\perp}$ (in the flat chart $\iota = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}$), so $\iota^{2} = -1$. The field space is that of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(iii): connections $A$ of the ambient bundle preserving $I$, with field strength $F$, a bivector-valued two-form with values in $\Lambda^{2}I^{\perp}$, whose Lorentz block $F_{L}$ (values in $\Lambda^{2}\{I, V\}^{\perp}$) is $R + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\,e\wedge e$ in the store's sign and whose translational block (values in $V \wedge \{I, V\}^{\perp}$) carries the torsion $De$. For a bivector-valued two-form $B$ with values in $\Lambda^{2}I^{\perp}$ (the de Sitter or anti-de Sitter algebra) and real $a, b$ with $a^{2} + b^{2} \neq 0$ and $c \neq 0$ set
\[
S_{a,b}[A, B] = \int \langle B \wedge F\rangle_{0} - \tfrac14 \int \langle B \wedge (a\iota + b) B_{L}\rangle_{0}, \qquad S_{a,b,c} = S_{a,b} - \tfrac{c}{4}\int\langle B_{V}\wedge B_{V}\rangle_{0},
\]
$B_{L}$ and $B_{V}$ the Lorentz and translational blocks of $B$ and the wedge that of two-forms ($S_{a,b}$ has its breaking supported on the Lorentz block). At $a = b = 0$ it is the BF functional of the reduced connection.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The breaking term lives on the blade $I \wedge X$; proved.)} For every $\Lambda \neq 0$, $I \wedge V = I \wedge X = \ninf \wedge \nO$, with $(I \wedge V)^{2} = 1$ and $\iota = (I\wedge V)I_{6}$; on bivectors $\epsilon(I, V, B, B') = -\langle B\,\iota\,B'\rangle_{0}$, a symmetric form invariant under the stabiliser of $(I, V)$ and odd under the internal reflection in a vector of $\{I, V\}^{\perp}$ (as spacetime densities after elimination, the $\epsilon$ terms are even under ordinary parity and the Pontryagin term odd). The breaking term $\epsilon(I, V, B, B)$ therefore needs the second vector (the slot count of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(iii)) and depends on the pair only through a unit blade independent of $\Lambda$, so $\Lambda$ enters $S_{a,b}$ only through the connection and the coefficient $a$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Eliminating $B$; proved.)} At each point $S_{a,b}$ has a stationary point in $B$ exactly when the translational block of $F$ vanishes, that is when the torsion vanishes; there $B_{L} = 2(b - a\iota)F_{L}/(a^{2} + b^{2})$ is unique, the other blocks of $B$ are free multipliers, and the value is
\[
S_{a,b} = \frac{1}{a^{2} + b^{2}}\Big(a\int\epsilon(I, V, F, F) + b\int\langle F \wedge F\rangle_{0}\Big).
\]
At $b = 0$, $a = \alpha$ this is $\alpha^{-1}\int\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$, the frozen-point integrand of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(iii) with $1/\alpha$ in place of its prefactor. On torsion-free fields $\langle F \wedge F\rangle_{0} = \langle R \wedge R\rangle_{0}$: the cross term $\langle R \wedge e \wedge e\rangle_{0}$ vanishes by the first Bianchi identity and $\langle e\wedge e \wedge e \wedge e\rangle_{0}$ vanishes identically, so $b$ adds only the Pontryagin density, and at $a = 0$ the reduced theory is topological.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Same vacuum solutions; proved.)} The vacuum connection equation of $\int\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$, the map $T \mapsto \epsilon(I, V, \cdot, T \wedge e)$ on the $24$ torsion components, has rank $24$, so it is equivalent to zero torsion. Hence in vacuum the multiplier constraint of (ii) is already a field equation of the frozen-point functional, the same rank forces the translational multiplier to vanish, and the stationary points of $S_{\alpha, 0}$ are exactly those of the frozen-point functional with $B_{L} = -(2/\alpha)\,\iota F_{L}$. With a matter source coupled to the connection the same rank-$24$ map solves $B_{V}$ for the spin density while the torsion stays zero, so off vacuum $S_{\alpha, 0}$ and the stored functional with the Einstein-Cartan coupling of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-einstein-cartan-matter-coupling} differ.
\item[(iii$'$)] \emph{(The translational term; proved.)} The symmetric form $\langle B_{V}\, B'_{V}\rangle_{0}$ is invariant under the stabiliser of $(I, V)$. For $S_{a,b,c}$ the stationary point in $B$ exists for every $F$: $B_{L}$ as in (ii) and $B_{V} = 2F_{V}/c$, with value $S_{a,b} + \tfrac1c\int\langle F_{V}\wedge F_{V}\rangle_{0}$, a torsion-squared term in place of the zero-torsion constraint, which tends to zero as $c \to \infty$ and leaves the frozen-point functional, whose connection equation with spinning matter is that of the Einstein-Cartan coupling. The zero-torsion coupling of (iii) is therefore a property of the Lorentz-block restriction, not of the BF form.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The BF sector is pure transport; proved.)} At $a = b = 0$ the field equations are $F = 0$ and $DB = 0$; for the store's tractor gauge field on the Einstein region $F = 0$ exactly where the Weyl part $W$ vanishes (its algebraic field strength is $-W$, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}), that is on the locally de Sitter ($\Lambda > 0$) or anti-de Sitter ($\Lambda < 0$) fields, where transport is path-independent. With $a = \alpha$, $b = 0$, on a vacuum Einstein field $B_{L} = (2/\alpha)\,\iota W$: $B$ vanishes exactly on the pure-transport fields, annihilates $I$ and $V$, and measures the Weyl part.
\item[(v)] \emph{(The coupling; proved, given the stored normalisation.)} For torsion-free fields, in the orientation stated, $\frac{1}{Q(I)}\epsilon(I, V, F, F) = -(\mathcal{R} - 2\Lambda)\det(\hb^{-1})\,d^{4}x + \frac{3}{\Lambda}\epsilon(I, V, R, R)$, with $\mathcal{R}$ the store-sign scalar curvature ($\mathcal{R} = 4\Lambda$ on de Sitter). With the functional normalised as in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.macdowell-mansouri-principle-fixes-the-trace-free-part}(iv) (frame equation $\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a + 8\pi G\,T(a) = 0$, so the coefficient of $\int\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$ has magnitude $1/(16\pi G\,|Q(I)|)$) and $N^{2} = 1/(G\,Q(I))$ for $\Lambda > 0$ (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-frozen-point-dictionary}, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-entropy-pi-n-squared}), matching (ii) gives $|a|/(a^{2} + b^{2}) = N^{2}/(16\pi)$, so
\[
|a|\,N^{2} = 16\pi\,\frac{a^{2}}{a^{2} + b^{2}}, \qquad |\alpha| = 16\pi G\,Q(I) = \frac{16\pi}{N^{2}} \ \text{ at } b = 0,\ a = \alpha .
\]
With coefficient $\lambda$ on $\langle B \wedge F\rangle_{0}$ the effective value is $\lambda^{2}$ times that at coefficient $1$, the same as coefficient $1$ with breaking $(a, b)/\lambda^{2}$; so $\alpha N^{2}$ is fixed by the normalisation of the BF term (and by $b$), not by the series: it is the definition of $N$ re-expressed, not a relation.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.frozen-point-action-is-bf-tran.technical:
Freidel and Starodubtsev (cited from memory) read MacDowell-Mansouri gravity as topological BF theory of the de Sitter group broken by a quadratic term in $B$ with a tiny dimensionless coupling. This result tests that reading on the series' objects. The frozen point plays two parts: it reduces the ambient group to its stabiliser, the de Sitter or anti-de Sitter group, and its norm sets the coupling. It is not the breaking datum: the breaking term $\epsilon(I, V, B, B)$, odd under the internal reflection, needs a second vector, and it depends only on the blade $I \wedge X$ spanned by the frozen point and the canonical tractor, a unit blade the same for every $\Lambda$. A breaking even under that reflection leaves the reduced theory topological.

With the breaking on the Lorentz block, eliminating $B$ returns exactly the frozen-point integrand $\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$, with $1/\alpha$ as prefactor, plus a Pontryagin term for any even part of the breaking; the translational components of $B$ are multipliers that set the torsion to zero. In vacuum that constraint costs nothing, because the functional's own connection equation already forces zero torsion (a rank-$24$ map), so the BF form and the stored functional agree in vacuum. With spinning matter they differ: the BF form keeps the torsion zero and puts the spin into the multiplier, giving the torsion-free coupling with the Hilbert source, while the stored functional carries the Einstein-Cartan coupling. Adding the invariant translational term $c\langle B_{V}\wedge B_{V}\rangle_{0}$ trades the constraint for a torsion-squared term that vanishes as $c \to \infty$, returning the Einstein-Cartan case, so the matter coupling is decided by where the breaking is supported, not by the BF form (the even term of Freidel and Starodubtsev may include this translational piece; from memory). With no breaking the field equations say the reduced connection is flat: for the tractor gauge field this is the vanishing of the Weyl part, the locally de Sitter field, on which transport is path-independent. With breaking, on a vacuum field the multiplier $B$ is $2/\alpha$ times the dual Weyl curvature, so it vanishes exactly on pure transport.

The coupling in the store's normalisation is $16\pi G\,Q(I) = 16\pi/N^{2}$, about $10^{-120}$. The pre-registered test was whether this ties $\alpha$ to $N$ without a free factor. It does not: rescaling $B$ changes $\alpha$ at fixed physics, and the factor is $16\pi$ in the Clifford scalar-part normalisation and $1$ in the normalisation Freidel and Starodubtsev quote, so $\alpha N^{2}$ is a convention and the coupling is $N$ re-expressed.

For the three imports of the open problem: the action principle is not removed (the BF form with its breaking is still an action); the MacDowell-Mansouri form is rewritten, not reduced, as the choice of a quadratic breaking on the blade of the pair (frozen point, canonical tractor), which is the same choice as $\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$ because elimination inverts the quadratic form, on the same field space of connections preserving the frozen point; the Einstein-Cartan coupling is not supplied, since the breaking's support decides it. The Euler term comes out together with the Einstein-Hilbert and cosmological terms, so the BF form does not remove it. Transport-convenient: the topological sector is pure transport and gravity is its breaking, but the dynamics is still imported. All algebra is checked exactly in $\Cl(2,4)$, at $\Lambda = 3/4, -3/2, 12$, on de Sitter, Bianchi I and Kasner samples.
synthesis.frozen-point-action-is-bf-tran.lay: One way physicists have rewritten Einstein's gravity treats it as a broken version of a much simpler theory, one with no local dynamics at all, in which only the global shape of things matters. The breaking is controlled by a single tiny number. This result checks that rewriting against the series' own objects. The simple, unbroken theory turns out to be exactly the series' idea of pure transport: moving things around with no dependence on the path taken, which the series has in a universe of pure cosmological constant. Gravity is the breaking of it. But the series' frozen point cannot do the breaking alone: it needs a second object, the canonical tractor, and only the plane the two span matters. The tiny controlling number comes out as $16\pi$ divided by the square of the series' large number $N$, about $10^{-120}$, but the $16\pi$ is a choice of bookkeeping, so this is not a new prediction. Without spinning matter the rewriting and the series' action agree; with it they can differ, depending on a choice the rewriting leaves open. The rewriting still assumes an action, and it does not explain how spinning matter couples to gravity.

synthesis.frozen-point-field-space-is-th.technical:
The question is whether the field space on which the frozen-point MacDowell-Mansouri integrand gives Einstein's equations, the $\Cl(2,4)$ connections preserving the frozen point $I$, is Gauge Theory Gravity's gauge principle: two independent gauge fields, $\hb$ for displacements and $\Omega$ for rotations.

The new content is a comparison. On the gauge fields preserving a constant tractor $I_{\rho}$, the $\Omega$-equation of the frozen-point functional is exactly the torsion equation (the standard first-order fact with an invertible frame, written in the series' chart: only the torsion block of the field strength enters, through an invertible map). So restricting to torsion-free fields, one field $\hb$ as for the normal tractor connection, still gives Einstein's equations with $\Lambda = 6\rho$ for $\rho \neq 0$. The normal tractor connection of the same torsion-free field has the same rotation-gauge field and soldering and differs only in the special-conformal slot, the Schouten map instead of $\rho$ times the frame; there the integrand gives the Bach equations. The slot, not the independence of the two gauge fields, carries Einstein's equations; the independence decides only the torsion (spin) equation.

The second clause records the field space in GTG terms, again a standard Cartan-geometric fact in the series' chart: the bivectors annihilating $I_{\rho} = \nInf + \rho\nO$ split uniquely into the Lorentz bivectors and $u_{\rho} \wedge W$, so $\Omega - u_{\rho} \wedge \hb^{-1}$ is a bijection from pairs onto $I$-preserving gauge fields, equivariant under GTG's rotation and displacement gauges, with field strength the shifted curvature $R + 2\rho\,E \wedge E$ plus the torsion. At $\rho = 0$ the algebra is the Poincar\'e algebra. Why the varied field is this one is not derived: it remains a premise.
synthesis.frozen-point-field-space-is-th.lay: In the series, gravity is described by two fields on flat spacetime, one recording how rulers are laid down and one recording how directions turn. A borrowed rule for gravity's equations works only if a larger six-dimensional connection built from these fields keeps one special direction, the frozen point, fixed. This result shows that treating the two fields as independent is not what makes the rule produce Einstein's equations: tying the second field to the first changes nothing in empty space. One specific slot of the larger connection does the work. It also confirms that the two fields plus a fixed special direction are exactly such connections. Why the connection has that form is an assumption, not something the series derives.

synthesis.frozen-point-integrand-gives-e.technical:
The open problem asks why the gravitational action should be varied over $\Cl(2,4)$ connections that preserve the frozen point, since on the series' own transport, the normal tractor connection, the same integrand is the Weyl square. This result compares the natural field spaces directly. Write a $\Cl(2,4)$ connection with nondegenerate soldering as rotation gauge field, coframe, special-conformal slot $S$ and dilation. The frozen-point integrand sees only the Lorentz block of the field strength, curvature plus $a \wedge S(b) + S(a) \wedge b$, and does not see the dilation or $\Lambda$. Split $S$ into trace, antisymmetric and trace-free symmetric parts and freeze or vary each. Varied parts appear algebraically and are eliminated by their equations.

On torsion-free fields, varying the whole slot returns $S$ equal to the Schouten map, so the unconstrained field space lands on the normal tractor connection and the Weyl square (conformal gravity, the Bach equations). Freezing the trace and the trace-free part at $\rho$ times the identity, with $\rho$ a nonzero constant, gives the Euler density plus Einstein-Hilbert with $\Lambda = 6\rho$. Varying only the trace removes the Einstein-Hilbert term and leaves the Euler density with an $R^{2}$ term; varying only the trace-free part adds a Ricci-squared term. Those remainders are not variationally trivial, so only the frozen rows give Einstein's equations. The antisymmetric part and the dilation make no difference without torsion, so preserving a tractor is necessary only up to those inert directions.

Every row satisfies the no-inverse-frame hypothesis, because the slot is itself a field; in the all-varied row the inverse frame comes back through the solution of the slot equation. So no-inverse-frame excludes the normal tractor connection only when the slot is required to be built from the frame and rotation gauge field. The field space therefore rests on a premise the hypothesis does not supply: the symmetric part of the slot is not an independent field, so the gauge content is the ten components of the de Sitter or anti-de Sitter algebra rather than the fifteen of the conformal algebra. In gauge-invariant form this is the statement that the varied connection admits a parallel tractor; freezing the slot is that statement in the gauge where the tractor is constant. None of this presupposes Einstein's equations.
synthesis.frozen-point-integrand-gives-e.lay: The series borrows a rule, the action, from which the equations of gravity follow. The same formula gives Einstein's equations or a different theory, conformal gravity, depending on which shapes of the six-dimensional connection one is allowed to vary. This result tries every natural choice. If the extra part of the connection is left free, the rule hands back the series' own transport and conformal gravity. Einstein's equations come out only when that extra part is fixed to be a nonzero constant multiple of the basic frame, with the constant giving the cosmological constant. The rule that forbids dividing by the frame does not make that choice, because a free extra part obeys the rule too. So the choice is a separate assumption.

Its closed product of two spheres and the integrals over it are global: no single gravitational field on flat spacetime carries them, so that part is read on the curved manifold.
synthesis.frozen-point-integrand-on-trac.lay: The series writes its gravitational action as a squared curvature seen from a special fixed point, the frozen point. This result asks what that action becomes when it is fed the series' own notion of transport, the connection that carries the conformal geometry of spacetime. The answer is that the frozen point drops out except as an overall factor, and what remains is the action of a different theory, conformal gravity, which only measures tidal distortion and whose equations are of fourth order. With only the series' transport and its canonical marker, this is the one action of its kind that is not purely topological. Einstein's equations appear only when the action is varied over a larger family of connections that keep the frozen point fixed. So the frozen point's job in the action is to choose which fields are varied, not to shape the formula.

synthesis.frozen-point-reduces-the-conne.formal:
Work in $\Cl(2,4)$ with the chart of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection} ($\nO \cdot \nInf = 1$, both null), unit pseudoscalar $i_{6} = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}e_{4}e_{5}$, $\epsilon(\dots)$ the coefficient of $i_{6}$ in the wedge, canonical tractor $X = \nO$, $\Lambda = 6\rho \neq 0$, frozen point $I = \nInf + \rho\nO$ ($Q(I) = 2\rho = \Lambda/3$) and Stelle-West vector $V = X - I/(2\rho)$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}). The \emph{unreduced field} is
\[
\Omega_{T}(a) = \Omega(a) - \nInf \wedge \hb^{-1}(a) + \nO \wedge S(a) + \beta(a)\,\nInf \wedge \nO,
\]
with $\hb$ (invertible), $\Omega$, the special-conformal slot $S$ (a vector-valued one-form) and the dilation $\beta$ (a scalar one-form) independent; $D Y = \Omega_{T} \times Y$. It contains the normal tractor connection ($S = \Sch\,\hb^{-1}$, $\beta = 0$, $\Omega$ torsion-free) and the connections preserving $I$, and no field equation enters its definition. With $I$ and $X$ held as fixed data, the densities below are invariant only under their joint stabiliser, the Lorentz rotations; holding $I$ constant is the unitary gauge of the Higgs reading (a special-conformal rotor of the parabolic group that gauges the tractor field moves $I$). The four-form densities are $L_{1} = \epsilon(I, V, F, F)$, $L_{3} = \epsilon(I, V, DV, DV, F)$, $L_{5} = \epsilon(I, V, DV, DV, DV, DV)$ (the family of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.stelle-west-norm-is-no-local-output}) and the stiffness $St = \epsilon(I, X, DI, DI, DX, DX)$, all polynomial with no inverse frame. At a point, in an orthonormal physical frame with $\hb = 1$ there, write $M$ for a linear map of physical vectors, $\tr M = \partial_{a} \cdot M(a)$, $Q_{2}(M) = 2\bigl((\tr M)^{2} - \tr(M^{2})\bigr)$ times the volume form; $\mathcal{R}(A \wedge B)$ for the store-sign curvature operator of $\Omega$ (without pair symmetry when $\Omega$ has torsion), $\mathcal{R}(b) = \partial_{a} \cdot \mathcal{R}(a \wedge b)$ its Ricci contraction (index reading $R_{bd} = \sum_{a}\eta^{aa}R_{adab}$), $\mathcal{R} = \partial_{a} \cdot \mathcal{R}(a)$, $\mathcal{G}(a) = \mathcal{R}(a) - \tfrac12 a\,\mathcal{R}$ its Einstein map, $\Sch_{*}(a) = \tfrac12\bigl(\mathcal{R}(a) - \tfrac16 a\,\mathcal{R}\bigr)$ its Schouten map (for torsion-free $\Omega$ the stored Schouten map), and $\mathcal{W}(a \wedge b) = \mathcal{R}(a \wedge b) - \Sch_{*}(a) \wedge b - a \wedge \Sch_{*}(b)$ its Weyl part (for torsion-free $\Omega$, where alone it is used below, the index reading $\mathcal{R} - \mathrm{KN}(\Sch_{*})$).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Broken components; proved.)} $DI(a) = \rho\,\hb^{-1}(a) - S(a) + \beta(a)(\nInf - \rho\nO)$ and $DX(a) = \hb^{-1}(a) - \beta(a)\nO$. Relative to the stabiliser of $I$ the broken components are therefore $S - \rho\,\hb^{-1}$ and $\beta$ (that $\Omega_{T}$ preserves $I$ exactly when both vanish is the slot lemma of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.parallel-frozen-point-on-matter-regions-is-the-field-space-premise}(i), and is not claimed here).
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The Stelle-West family does not freeze the slot; computed, general by equivariance.)} With $S$ varied, the slot derivative of $c_{1}L_{1} + c_{3}L_{3} + c_{5}L_{5}$ at the frozen value $S = \rho\,\hb^{-1}$ is, for torsion-free $\Omega$,
\[
\bigl(2c_{1} + c_{3}/\rho\bigr)\,\mathcal{G} + \bigl(2c_{1}\Lambda + 2c_{3}\Lambda/\rho + 12c_{5}/\rho\bigr)\id .
\]
So when $2c_{1} + c_{3}/\rho \neq 0$ the frozen slot solves its own equation only where $\mathcal{G} = -\Lambda_{\mathrm{eff}}\id$, an Einstein condition; for every curvature it does so only on the line $c_{3} = -2\rho c_{1}$, $c_{5} = \rho^{2}c_{1}$, where the density at the frozen slot is $c_{1}$ times the Euler form $\epsilon(I, X, \mathcal{R}, \mathcal{R})$ of $\Omega$ (also with torsion), which has no field equations, while the density still depends on $S$ away from it. More generally, adding to $c_{1}L_{1}$ ($c_{1} \neq 0$) any slot potential that does not involve the curvature leaves the frozen slot stationary only where $2c_{1}(\mathcal{G} + \Lambda\,\id)$ equals a fixed map, again an Einstein condition.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Stiffness is the slot Hessian; proved.)} $St = Q_{2}(S - \rho\,\hb^{-1})$, independent of $\beta$ and $\Omega$, and the same nondegenerate form is the slot Hessian of the frozen-point integrand: $L_{1}(S) = L_{1}(\Sch_{*}) + Q_{2}(S - \Sch_{*})$ for every curvature, where $\Sch_{*}$, the unique stationary slot of $L_{1}$, is the Schouten map of the slot elimination (for torsion-free $\Omega$ the stored Schouten map, with $L_{1}(\Sch_{*}) = \tfrac12\langle\mathcal{W}(a \wedge b)\,\mathcal{W}(\partial_{b} \wedge \partial_{a})\rangle_{0}$, in components $\tfrac14 W_{abcd}W^{abcd}$; the elimination itself is the conformal-gauge step of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-conformal-gravity-bach-equations-and-conformal-gauge-form}(b), and is not claimed here).
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Interpolation; proved.)} For $\mu \neq -1$ the slot equation of $L_{1} + \mu\,St$ has the unique solution $S_{\mu} = (\Sch_{*} + \mu\rho\,\id)/(1 + \mu)$ and the density there is $L_{1}(\Sch_{*}) + t\,Q_{2}(\rho\,\id - \Sch_{*})$ with $t = \mu/(1 + \mu)$; for torsion-free $\Omega$,
\[
(1 - t)\,\tfrac12\langle\mathcal{W}(a \wedge b)\,\mathcal{W}(\partial_{b} \wedge \partial_{a})\rangle_{0} + t\Bigl(\tfrac14 E - \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}(\mathcal{R} - 2\Lambda)\Bigr), \qquad E = 2\langle\mathcal{R}(a \wedge b)\,\mathcal{R}(\partial_{b} \wedge \partial_{a})\rangle_{0} - 4\,\mathcal{R}(\partial_{a}) \cdot \mathcal{R}(a) + \mathcal{R}^{2},
\]
in index reading $(1 - t)\,\tfrac14 W_{abcd}W^{abcd} + t\bigl(\tfrac14(R_{abcd}R^{abcd} - 4R_{ab}R^{ab} + R^{2}) - \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}(R - 2\Lambda)\bigr)$.
At $\mu = 0$ this is the Weyl square (the normal tractor slot, conformal gravity); as $\mu \to \infty$ it is the frozen-point density with the slot frozen; for finite $\mu \neq 0$ it is $t$ times the frozen-point density plus $\tfrac{1-t}{2}\langle\mathcal{W}(a \wedge b)\,\mathcal{W}(\partial_{b} \wedge \partial_{a})\rangle_{0}$ (in components $\tfrac{1-t}{4}W_{abcd}W^{abcd}$): the frozen-point functional with Newton's constant rescaled by $1/t$, plus a Weyl square whose coefficient relative to the Einstein-Hilbert term has magnitude $3/(4\mu\Lambda)$, so with $\Lambda$ as small as observed the Weyl-square scale $(\mu\Lambda)^{-1/2}$ stays unobservable only for enormous $\mu$. $Q_{2}$ is indefinite and $S$ enters without derivatives, so $St$ is a penalty on an auxiliary field, not a mass for propagating fields.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Einstein's equation is the frozen slot's equation; proved.)} The slot derivative of $L_{1}$ at $S = \rho\,\hb^{-1}$ is $2(\mathcal{G} + \Lambda\,\id)$. With $\Omega$ fixed and the slot tied to the frame ($S = \rho\,\hb^{-1}$), the frame derivative of $L_{1}$ is $2\rho$ times it, and divided by $Q(I) = 2\rho$ it is the frame equation $2(\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a)$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.macdowell-mansouri-principle-fixes-the-trace-free-part}.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} In the Stelle-West mechanism the Higgs vector's covariant derivative is the frame, which must be nondegenerate. Read the same way for the first step, from $\so(2,4)$ to the stabiliser of $I$, the field space of the frozen-point functional asks for the opposite: the broken components $DI$ must vanish. No member of the stored constant-coupling family, and no curvature-independent slot potential, imposes that off the Einstein locus; the stiffness penalty imposes it only in the limit $\mu \to \infty$. A Lagrange multiplier three-form paired with $DI$ (polynomial, inverse-frame free) imposes $DI = 0$ at finite coupling, but adding it is the same premise written into the action. The connections preserving $I$ are therefore the infinitely stiff frozen point, an equivalent reading of the field-space premise (Premise \claimref{synthesis.field-space-premise-parallel-frozen-point}), not a derivation of it. With the slot free the same integrand gives conformal gravity.
synthesis.frozen-point-reduces-the-conne.technical:
Write the $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field with all its parts independent: rotation gauge $\Omega$, frame $\hb^{-1}$, special-conformal slot $S$ and dilation $\beta$. This space holds both the normal tractor connection and the connections preserving the frozen point $I = \nInf + \rho\nO$, and assumes no field equation. The covariant derivative of $I$ is $DI = \rho\,\hb^{-1} - S$ plus a dilation part, so the parts that the frozen point "breaks" are $S - \rho\,\hb^{-1}$ and $\beta$. Holding $I$ constant is the unitary gauge; the densities are then invariant only under Lorentz rotations.

Three facts follow, all by exact computation. First, the stored Stelle-West family $c_{1}L_{1} + c_{3}L_{3} + c_{5}L_{5}$ does not hold the slot at its frozen value: there the slot equation reads $(2c_{1} + c_{3}/\rho)\mathcal{G}$ plus a multiple of the identity, which vanishes only on Einstein fields, and the same holds for any slot potential not involving the curvature. The one exception is a single line of couplings, and on it the frozen value of the density is the Euler form, with no field equations. Second, the stiffness term $\epsilon(I, X, DI, DI, DX, DX)$, a polynomial with no inverse frame, is exactly $Q_{2}(S - \rho\,\id)$, $Q_{2}(M) = 2((\tr M)^{2} - \tr M^{2})$, the same quadratic form as the slot Hessian of the frozen-point integrand, which is $\tfrac14 W\cdot W + Q_{2}(S - \Sch)$. Adding $\mu$ times the stiffness gives the slot $S_{\mu} = (\Sch + \mu\rho)/(1 + \mu)$ and the density $(1 - t)\tfrac14 W\cdot W + t\,(\text{frozen-point density})$, $t = \mu/(1 + \mu)$: Einstein gravity with rescaled Newton's constant plus a Weyl square of relative size $3/(4\mu\Lambda)$. Since $S$ has no derivatives and $Q_{2}$ is indefinite, this is a penalty on an auxiliary field, not a mass term. Third, at the frozen value the slot equation is $2(\mathcal{G} + \Lambda)$, and the frame equation of the reduced theory is the same expression: Einstein's equation is the equation the frozen slot would have obeyed.

So the Higgs reading does not supply the field space: it supplies conformal gravity at zero stiffness and the frozen-point functional only in the limit of infinite stiffness, where the broken components vanish. A multiplier imposing $DI = 0$ does it at finite coupling but is the premise itself. Infinite stiffness is thus an equivalent reading of the field-space premise. Transport-convenient.
synthesis.frozen-point-reduces-the-conne.lay: Einstein's equations come out of the series' gravitational action only if one particular part of the gravitational field is held fixed rather than allowed to vary. A standard way physicists fix such parts is a Higgs mechanism, in which a field settles into a preferred value. This result tries that idea on the series' fixed point. It finds that the usual terms do not hold the part fixed, except in situations that already obey Einstein's equations. A natural extra penalty term can hold it, but only in the limit where its coefficient is infinite; a term that simply forces the part to stay fixed works too, but that is the assumption itself. With zero strength one gets a different theory, conformal gravity; with finite strength one gets Einstein's theory plus an extra higher-derivative piece. So holding the part fixed remains an assumption, now stated as infinite stiffness.

synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reprod.lay: The series uses a construction called the tractor connection, which normally lives on a curved spacetime. This result shows that it can equally be written on flat spacetime, as a field that turns directions in a six-dimensional extension of spacetime from point to point, built from the gravitational fields themselves. Written this way it reproduces the stored formulas exactly, picks out the same special direction (the frozen point) for spacetimes with a cosmological constant, and its strength is the part of curvature that is unchanged by rescaling lengths.

synthesis.imported-chern-gauss-bonnet.formal:
Let $\chi$ denote the Euler characteristic.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] (Two dimensions.) For a closed (compact, boundaryless) Riemannian surface $\Sigma$ with Gaussian curvature $K$ and scalar curvature ${}^{(2)}\!R = 2K$, $\int_{\Sigma}K\,dA = 2\pi\chi(\Sigma)$, so $\int_{\Sigma}{}^{(2)}\!R\,dA = 4\pi\chi(\Sigma)$. In particular this holds for a closed spacelike two-surface lying in the invertible region of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), such as a cross-section of a horizon locus, with the Riemannian metric $-h$, where $h$ is the (negative-definite) metric that the derived metric, of signature $(+,-,-,-)$, induces.
\item[(b)] (Four dimensions.) For a closed Riemannian four-manifold $M$,
\[
\int_{M}\bigl(R_{abcd}R^{abcd} - 4R_{ab}R^{ab} + R^{2}\bigr)\,dV \;=\; 32\pi^{2}\chi(M).
\]
The integrand is the Euler density of the curvature operator $\mathcal{R}$ on bivectors, $E = 2\langle\mathcal{R}(a \wedge b)\,\mathcal{R}(\partial_{b} \wedge \partial_{a})\rangle - 4\,\mathcal{R}(\partial_{a}) \cdot \mathcal{R}(a) + \mathcal{R}^{2}$, independent of the sign convention of $\mathcal{R}$.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Provenance:} \cite{Chern1944, AllendoerferWeil1943}; the two-dimensional case is classical \cite[Sec.~4-5]{doCarmo1976}.

\emph{Beyond one flat chart.} The Euler characteristic of the closed four-manifold in (b) is global and is not carried by a single gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime; the Euler density above is in Gauge Theory Gravity on the invertible region, where its integral is a boundary term, and the Euler characteristic is read on the manifold assembled from the derived metric's charts.
synthesis.imported-chern-gauss-bonnet.technical: The Gauss-Bonnet-Chern theorem expresses the Euler characteristic of a closed Riemannian manifold as the integral of a curvature density. For a closed surface the total Gaussian curvature is $2\pi\chi$, so the integral of the scalar curvature $2K$ is $4\pi\chi$; for a closed four-manifold the integral of the Euler density $R_{abcd}R^{abcd} - 4R_{ab}R^{ab} + R^{2}$, a quadratic expression in the curvature operator on bivectors, is $32\pi^{2}\chi$. In particular the integral does not change under any deformation of the metric. The two-dimensional case applies directly to a closed horizon cross-section of a gravitational field on flat spacetime. The four-dimensional Euler characteristic is global: no single gravitational field on flat spacetime carries it, so that part is read on several charts of flat spacetime (charts of Euclidean $\R^{4}$), each carrying its own gravitational field, glued on overlaps by displacement and rotation gauge transformations.
synthesis.imported-chern-gauss-bonnet.lay: However a closed surface is bent or stretched, its total curvature stays the same, fixed by how many holes it has: a sphere always gives the same total, a doughnut always zero. Chern proved the analogue in higher dimensions, where a particular combination of curvatures integrates to a number fixed by the overall shape of the space. These are classical theorems of geometry taken from the literature.

imported_from.citation: S.-S. Chern, A simple intrinsic proof of the Gauss-Bonnet formula for closed Riemannian manifolds, Ann. of Math. (2) 45 (1944), 747--752.
C. B. Allendoerfer and A. Weil, The Gauss-Bonnet theorem for Riemannian polyhedra, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 53 (1943), 101--129.
M. P. do Carmo, Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces, Prentice-Hall, Englewood Cliffs (1976).

synthesis.imported-chern-weil-and-chern-.formal:
Let $A$ be a connection (a gauge field, a one-form) on an $n$-dimensional region with values in a Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ of bivectors, with field strength $F = dA + A \times A$ in the convention of the citing result ($\times$ the commutator product of the values, wedged as forms), and let $P$ be a symmetric $k$-linear form on $\mathfrak{g}$ invariant under $\mathfrak{g}$ (an invariant polynomial). Write $P(F^{k})$ for the $2k$-form $P(F \wedge \cdots \wedge F)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] (Chern-Weil.) $d\,P(F^{k}) = k\,P(DF \wedge F^{k-1}) = 0$ by the Bianchi identity $DF = 0$; for a variation $\delta A$, $\delta P(F^{k}) = k\,d\,P(\delta A \wedge F^{k-1})$, so with $2k = n$ the integral of $P(F^{k})$ has identically vanishing Euler-Lagrange derivative (it is a topological density, with no field equations).
\item[(b)] (Transgression.) For two connections $A_{0}$, $A_{1}$ with values in $\mathfrak{g}$, put $A_{t} = A_{0} + t(A_{1} - A_{0})$ with field strength $F_{t}$; then $P(F_{1}^{k}) - P(F_{0}^{k}) = d\,\bigl(k\int_{0}^{1}P((A_{1} - A_{0}) \wedge F_{t}^{k-1})\,dt\bigr)$. With $A_{0} = 0$ this is $P(F^{k}) = d\,\mathrm{CS}_{P}(A)$, the Chern-Simons form $\mathrm{CS}_{P}(A) = k\int_{0}^{1}P(A \wedge F_{t}^{k-1})\,dt$, $F_{t} = t\,dA + t^{2}A \times A$; so $P(F^{k})$ is locally exact.
\item[(c)] (Variation and gauge change.) $\delta\,\mathrm{CS}_{P}(A) = k\,P(\delta A \wedge F^{k-1})$ up to an exact form, so the field equations of $\int\mathrm{CS}_{P}$ in odd dimension $2k - 1$ are $P(J \wedge F^{k-1}) = 0$ for every $J$ in $\mathfrak{g}$. Under a gauge transformation $\mathrm{CS}_{P}$ changes by an exact form plus a closed form whose integral over a closed manifold is a topological (winding) number; under an infinitesimal one, $\delta_{\lambda}A = D\lambda$, it changes by an exact form.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Beyond one flat chart.} The winding in (c) is the degree of a gauge transformation over a closed manifold, read on several charts of flat spacetime glued by gauge transformations; (a), (b) and the infinitesimal clause of (c) are local.

\emph{Provenance:} \cite{ChernSimons1974}; Chern-Weil theory as in \cite[Ch.~XII]{KobayashiNomizu1969}.
synthesis.imported-chern-weil-and-chern-.technical: For any gauge field, the invariant polynomials of its field strength (traces of powers, Pfaffians, the Killing form) are closed forms by the Bianchi identity, and their variation is a total derivative, so integrated over a region of matching dimension they give no field equations: they are topological. Chern and Simons showed that each such form is locally the exterior derivative of a form built from the gauge field itself, the Chern-Simons form, obtained by integrating along the straight line of connections from zero (transgression); its variation gives the field equations of Chern-Simons theory in odd dimensions, and under a gauge transformation it changes by a total derivative plus a winding term whose integral is topological. Taken from the literature; the field strength's sign and normalisation follow the citing result.
synthesis.imported-chern-weil-and-chern-.lay: Some combinations of a force field's strength never change when the field is deformed a little: their total over a region depends only on the field at the edge, or on the shape of space. Chern and Simons showed how to write each of them as the change of another quantity built from the field, which in odd dimensions becomes an action of its own. These are classical theorems taken from the literature.

imported_from.citation: S.-S. Chern and J. Simons, Characteristic forms and geometric invariants, Ann. of Math. (2) 99 (1974), 48--69.
S. Kobayashi and K. Nomizu, Foundations of Differential Geometry, Vol. II, Interscience, New York (1969).
