synthesis.inverse-problem-for-the-clausi.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$, signature $(1,3)$, the store's curvature sign. Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) with derived metric $g$ and zero torsion, the setting of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}, which under the premise (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) and its hypotheses (H1) to (H4) delivers the solution set of $\mathcal{R}(a) + 8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}T(a) = (\Lambda + 4\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}\tau)a$, $\Lambda$ an integration constant, $G_{\mathrm{cl}} = 1/(4\eta)$, $T$ the heat tensor of (H1) and (H3). For a symmetric linear function $S(a)$ and rational $\beta$ put $M_{\beta}S(a) = S(a) + \beta\,\tr(S)\,a$, built from $g$ alone. The route's form is $M_{-1/2}$ of the Einstein form $\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a + 8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}T(a)$, and $M_{-1/4}$ of it is the trace-free form $\mathcal{R}^{\circ}(a) + 8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}T^{\circ}(a)$, free of $\Lambda$. An operator is an Euler-Lagrange expression of a local functional of a field only if its Fr\'echet derivative in that field is self-adjoint (the Helmholtz condition: the second variation is symmetric). Principal symbols are read at a point in a normal gauge, $d_{a} \to p_{a}$, on symmetric $h_{ab} = \delta g_{ab}$ with $\ip{k}{h} = k_{ab}h^{ab}$; the Lorentz-covariant second-order symbols are spanned by $A_{1} = p_{a}p_{b}\tr h$, $A_{2} = \eta_{ab}\,p\cdot h\cdot p$, $A_{3} = \eta_{ab}p^{2}\tr h$, $A_{4} = p^{2}h_{ab}$, $A_{5} = p_{a}(hp)_{b} + p_{b}(hp)_{a}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(With the metric as the varied field, the Helmholtz condition selects the Einstein form; proved.)} With $g$ (equivalently the frame) varied and the pairing above, $M_{\beta}(\mathcal{G} + \Lambda)$ is the Euler-Lagrange expression of a local functional only if $\beta = 0$, and for $\beta = 0$ it is one: the metric Euler-Lagrange expression of the Einstein-Hilbert functional with $\Lambda$, and the frame equation of the stored functional (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.macdowell-mansouri-principle-fixes-the-trace-free-part}(i)). On principal symbols the self-adjoint covariant ones form a space of dimension $4$; the Einstein symbol $-\tfrac12(A_{1} + A_{2} - A_{3} + A_{4} - A_{5})$ lies in it, and the asymmetry of $M_{\beta}\mathcal{G}$ is $\beta$ times a fixed nonzero form. The selection depends on the field variable: for $\beta \neq -\tfrac14$, $M_{\beta}$ is invertible, and for the field $\psi$ with $\delta g = M_{\beta}(\delta\psi)$ the $\psi$-derivative of $M_{\beta}(\mathcal{G} + \Lambda)$ has the self-adjoint symbol $M_{\beta}\,\sigma(\mathcal{G})\,M_{\beta}$, the Euler-Lagrange expression of the Einstein-Hilbert functional in $\psi$. So the route's Ricci form ($\beta = -\tfrac12$) is variational for a densitised metric; the trace-free form ($\beta = -\tfrac14$) is not of this kind.
\item[(ii)] \emph{($\Lambda$ for the metric alone; proved in the family, by Lovelock's theorem in general.)} $M_{-1/4}$ has rank $9$ (it drops the trace and $\Lambda$ with it), so the trace-free form is the only member of the family that keeps $\Lambda$ free; for the metric alone it passes the Helmholtz condition on trace-free variations (those fixing the volume element; there it is the Euler-Lagrange expression of the Einstein-Hilbert functional at fixed volume element) and fails it on all variations. With an enlarged field content it is variational with $\Lambda$ an integration constant: the Henneaux-Teitelboim form (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-henneaux-teitelboim-promotion}), which is the route's own variational form, consistent with the stored statements that on the route $N$ is initial data and the solution space is the promoted one (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-route-makes-n-initial-data}), the norm mode then being one global pair with no local mode (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.promoted-norm-one-global-pair}). For the metric alone: by Lovelock's theorem (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-lovelock-and-anderson-duchamp-natural-lagrangians}(a)) every natural Euler-Lagrange expression of order at most two in four dimensions is $a\mathcal{G} + b$, with the single vacuum value $\Lambda = b/a$, so the route's solution set with $\Lambda$ free is not that of any natural variational problem of order at most two for the metric, and a metric action needs a fixed $\Lambda$. The frozen point's constraint $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}) carries that value as an input, the registered input; it does not compute it. De Sitter fields of every $\Lambda'$ solve the trace-free form, and of them the Einstein form at $\Lambda = 3Q(I)$ keeps only $\Lambda' = \Lambda$. The order bound is needed: the Weyl-squared functional, of fourth order (its second variation at the flat background is fourth order in $p$), has every Einstein field of every $\Lambda$ among its solutions (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-conformal-gravity-bach-equations-and-conformal-gauge-form}(a)).
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Linearised Lovelock; proved.)} The covariant second-order symbols that are transverse, $p^{a}E_{ab} = 0$ for every $h$ (the linearised Noether identity of displacement-gauge invariance, which the route's Bianchi step uses with $\nabla\cdot T = 0$), form a plane spanned by the Einstein symbol and $(p_{a}p_{b} - \eta_{ab}p^{2})\tr h$, which is not self-adjoint; the transverse self-adjoint ones are the multiples of the Einstein symbol.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The metric action, up to terms the route does not see; given imported theorems.)} Assume a local, natural functional $S$ of the metric whose Euler-Lagrange expression has order at most two and is, with the matter source of (v), the route's equation at the fixed $\Lambda = 3Q(I)$. By Lovelock's theorem its gravitational part is a constant multiple of $\mathcal{G} + \Lambda$, and against the matter term of (v) the constant is the one with $G = G_{\mathrm{cl}} = 1/(4\eta)$; by the exactness of the variational complex and the classification of natural null Lagrangians (Anderson and Duchamp, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-lovelock-and-anderson-duchamp-natural-lagrangians}(b)), $S$ is the Einstein-Hilbert functional with $G_{\mathrm{cl}}$ and $\Lambda$ plus $c_{E}$ times the Euler density, $c_{P}$ times the Pontryagin density and a divergence, with $c_{E}$, $c_{P}$ free. The Euler density has zero second variation at the flat background (checked), as it has no field equations. The frozen-point MacDowell-Mansouri functional is the member with Euler coefficient $\alpha = -3/(4\Lambda)$ in $(R - 2\Lambda + \alpha E_{4})/16\pi G$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.euler-term-horizon-entropy-shift}(i)); the route does not fix $\alpha$. In first-order variables on the field space of connections preserving $I$, within the curvature-only class of the tractor gauge field (the classification of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.curvature-only-tractor-actions-are-macdowell-mansouri}(iii), granted here: $\kappa\,\epsilon(I, X, F, F) + \kappa' H + \kappa'' K$), the route fixes $\kappa$ by $G = G_{\mathrm{cl}}$ and leaves $\kappa'$ (the Holst-type density, whose frame equation vanishes on torsion-free curvatures, the only ones the route sees) and $\kappa''$ (the Chern-Weil density) free. On the normal tractor connections of torsion-free fields the same integrand is the Weyl square (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-integrand-on-tractor-transport-is-weyl-squared}(iii)), of fourth order, which the order bound excludes.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Matter; proved.)} Let the matter equations be $E_{\psi} = \delta S_{m}/\delta\psi$ for a local $S_{m}[g, \psi]$, with Hilbert stress $T_{H}$ normalised so that the frame equation of the Einstein-Hilbert functional plus $S_{m}$ is $\mathcal{G} + \Lambda + 8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}T_{H} = 0$. The system $(\mathcal{G} + \Lambda + 8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}T, E_{\psi})$ is the Euler-Lagrange system of a local functional (up to a constant factor on its first member) if and only if $T = T_{H} + \Theta[g]$ with $\Theta$ independent of the matter ($\Theta = 0$ if $T$ and $T_{H}$ both vanish in the matter vacuum). For a scalar field at the flat background the cross condition holds with the Hilbert stress for minimal coupling (background gradient, linear potential) and for the coupling $\xi\psi^{2}\mathcal{R}$ (constant background), and fails for a source with an altered trace term and for the minimal stress beside the matter equation of $\xi\psi^{2}\mathcal{R}$: the condition does not select minimal coupling, and on the torsion-free route it does not reach the spin coupling of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-einstein-cartan-matter-coupling}.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} For the three imports of the problem: (a) the route's equations are compatible with a local action at fixed $\Lambda$ (witness: the stored functional), and the route does not single one out, so (a) is not derived; (b) is not shrunk: the route fixes the Einstein-Hilbert and volume coefficients and leaves the Euler and Pontryagin coefficients, which are what distinguish the MacDowell-Mansouri functional from the Einstein-Hilbert functional; (c) its energy part is equivalent to the identification $T = T_{H}$ of the heat tensor with the Hilbert stress, and its spin part is untouched. The result is transport-absent: the frozen point enters only as the carrier of the input $\Lambda$.
synthesis.inverse-problem-for-the-clausi.technical: The Clausius route of the store gives Einstein's equations as a solution set and keeps $\Lambda$ as an integration constant. This result runs the inverse variational problem on that output, under the route's premise (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) and its hypotheses, and with the metric (or the frame) as the varied field. An operator can be the Euler-Lagrange expression of a local functional only if its linearisation is self-adjoint (the Helmholtz condition), which for second-order operators is tested on the principal symbol at a point; the five Lorentz-covariant second-order symbols on metric perturbations are written down and the conditions solved in exact arithmetic. Of the algebraic rewritings $M_{\beta}(\mathcal{G} + \Lambda)$, only the Einstein form passes when the metric is varied; for a reparametrised field ($\delta g = M_{\beta}\delta\psi$, $\beta \neq -\tfrac14$) the corresponding rewriting passes, so the route's Ricci form is variational for a densitised metric. The trace-free form, which leaves $\Lambda$ free, is not of that kind: for the metric alone it is variational only at fixed volume element, and its variational home with all variations is the Henneaux-Teitelboim form, an enlarged field content, which is the route's own variational form (on the route $N$ is initial data). Given Lovelock's theorem (an imported Fact), no natural variational problem of order at most two for the metric alone has the route's solution set with $\Lambda$ free, so a metric action needs a fixed $\Lambda$, which the frozen point's constraint carries as the registered input. The order bound matters: the Weyl-squared functional has every Einstein field among its solutions, and it is the frozen-point integrand on the tractor gauge field of torsion-free fields. Transverse self-adjoint symbols form one line, the linearised Einstein operator. Given Lovelock and Anderson-Duchamp (imported Facts), the metric action is Einstein-Hilbert with $G = 1/(4\eta)$ up to the Euler and Pontryagin terms; on the $I$-preserving first-order field space within the curvature-only class the Holst-type and Chern-Weil terms also stay free. With matter, the coupled system is variational if and only if the heat tensor is the Hilbert stress of the matter functional up to a matter-independent term; minimal coupling is not singled out and the spin coupling is not reached. None of the three imports of the open problem is derived: (a) and (b) are not, and (c) is restated as the identification of the heat tensor with the Hilbert stress. Transport-absent.
synthesis.inverse-problem-for-the-clausi.lay: Earlier work in the series showed, following Jacobson, that Einstein's equations follow if every small horizon has a temperature and an entropy proportional to its area, with heat raising that entropy. Gravity is usually written instead as the result of minimising an action. This result asks what the first picture, run backwards, says about the second. Equations come from an action only if a certain symmetry test passes, and the test depends on which variable is varied. With the usual choice of variable, the metric, only the standard Einstein form passes; with a rescaled variable other forms pass too, but the form in which the cosmological constant is left free passes only if the volume of space-time is held fixed, or in the known unimodular version of gravity with an extra field. So an ordinary action for the metric needs a definite cosmological constant, which the series carries in its frozen point as an input. Assuming two theorems from the literature, and that the equations involve at most two derivatives, the action is then fixed apart from terms that change no equations for fields without twisting, including the Euler term about which the two pictures disagree; so the route does not single out the series' action. With matter, the test holds exactly when the heat in the Clausius argument is the usual energy tensor obtained from the matter's own action. The result is conditional on the series' horizon premise.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} The route of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}, under Premise (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) and its hypotheses (H1) to (H4), shows that on its domain every admissible pair (field, conserved $C^{1}$ source $T$) satisfies its item (4), $\mathcal{R}(a) + 8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}T(a) = (\Lambda + 4\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}\tau)a$ with $\Lambda$ constant and $G_{\mathrm{cl}} = 1/(4\eta)$, the connection being torsion-free (a $C^{3}$ derived metric with its Levi-Civita connection). This is a statement about a solution set. The inverse variational problem asks for a local functional whose Euler-Lagrange equations have that solution set; any invertible operator applied to the equations has the same solution set, so the problem includes the choice of a multiplier. Throughout, $\tr S = \sum_{a} e^{a}\cdot S(e_{a})$ in an orthonormal frame, and in four dimensions $\tr\mathcal{G} = -\mathcal{R}$ (the scalar), $\tr(\Lambda a) = 4\Lambda$.

\emph{The Helmholtz condition and principal symbols.} If $E = \delta S/\delta\phi$ for a local functional $S$, the Fr\'echet derivative $DE$ is the second variation of $S$, a symmetric bilinear form: $\int \ip{k}{DE[h]} = \int \ip{h}{DE[k]}$ for compactly supported $h$, $k$ (the Helmholtz condition; its sufficiency on star-shaped domains is the Volterra-Vainberg theorem, cited from memory and not used here, since every sufficiency claim below has an explicit witness). For a linear operator $P = \sum a^{ij}(x)\partial_{i}\partial_{j} + (\text{lower order})$ on symmetric tensors, the formal adjoint has principal part $\sum (a^{ij})^{\top}\partial_{i}\partial_{j}$, so self-adjointness forces the principal symbol $\sigma(p)$ to be symmetric for the pairing $\ip{k}{h} = k_{ab}h^{ab}$ at every point and every $p$. For a natural second-order expression $E[g]$ the principal symbol of $DE$ at a point depends only on $g$ there; in a normal gauge at the point ($\hb = 1$, $\Omega = 0$ there, Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) it is the flat-background symbol. If $M$ is algebraic in $g$, $D(ME)[h] = M(DE[h]) + (DM[h])E$ and the second term has order zero in $h$, so the principal symbol of $D(ME)$ is $M\circ\sigma(DE)$. A Lorentz-covariant second-order symbol on symmetric $h$ is a combination of $A_{1}, \dots, A_{5}$ (the covariant quadratic forms in $p$ with values in symmetric tensors, linear in $h$: $h$ enters through $\tr h$, $p\cdot h\cdot p$, $hp$ or itself).

\emph{(i)} The check builds the linearised Riemann tensor from $h$ and $p$, $R_{abcd} = \tfrac12(p_{b}p_{c}h_{ad} + p_{a}p_{d}h_{bc} - p_{a}p_{c}h_{bd} - p_{b}p_{d}h_{ac})$ (sphere-positive convention; the overall sign is a common factor and does not affect symmetry, transversality or kernels), contracts it to the Ricci and Einstein symbols and expresses them in the basis, finding $\sigma(\mathcal{G}) = -\tfrac12(A_{1} + A_{2} - A_{3} + A_{4} - A_{5})$ and $\sigma(\Ric) = -\tfrac12(A_{1} + A_{4} - A_{5})$. Symmetry of $\ip{k}{\sigma h}$: $A_{3}$, $A_{4}$, $A_{5}$ are symmetric and $A_{1}$, $A_{2}$ are adjoint to each other ($\ip{k}{A_{1}h} = \tr h\;p\cdot k\cdot p$, $\ip{k}{A_{2}h} = \tr k\;p\cdot h\cdot p$), so the self-adjoint covariant symbols are those with equal $A_{1}$ and $A_{2}$ coefficients, a space of dimension $4$ (computed exactly on the ten basis tensors at two rational momenta). The Einstein symbol has equal coefficients and passes; the Ricci symbol has $-\tfrac12$ and $0$ and fails. Since $\tr\sigma(\mathcal{G})$ is built from $A$-terms whose trace contributes only to $A_{2}$ and $A_{3}$, $M_{\beta}\sigma(\mathcal{G}) = \sigma(\mathcal{G}) + \beta\eta\,\tr\sigma(\mathcal{G})$ changes the $A_{2}$ coefficient by $\beta$ times a nonzero number, so its asymmetry is $\beta$ times that of $M_{1}\sigma(\mathcal{G}) - \sigma(\mathcal{G})$, nonzero; the check confirms the linearity in $\beta$ at $\beta \in \{-\tfrac12, -\tfrac14, \tfrac37\}$, and that $M_{-1/2}\sigma(\mathcal{G}) = \sigma(\Ric)$. Algebraically, $M_{-1/2}(\mathcal{G} + \Lambda + 8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}T) = \mathcal{R} - \Lambda + 8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}(T - \tfrac12\tau)$, which is the route's item (4) (checked on a sample Ricci tensor and source). Hence $M_{\beta}(\mathcal{G} + \Lambda)$ fails the Helmholtz condition at every point of every field when $\beta \neq 0$. For $\beta = 0$ the Einstein-Hilbert functional with $\Lambda$ has metric Euler-Lagrange expression proportional to $\mathcal{G} + \Lambda$, and the stored functional has frame equation $2(\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a)I$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.macdowell-mansouri-principle-fixes-the-trace-free-part}(i)): the condition is met, by explicit witnesses. \emph{Field variable.} All of this is for the metric (or the frame) as the varied field with the pairing $\ip{k}{h}$. If $\beta \neq -\tfrac14$, $M_{\beta}$ is invertible ($1 + 4\beta \neq 0$) and $\psi$ with $\delta g = M_{\beta}(\delta\psi)$ is an equivalent field; the Euler-Lagrange expression of the Einstein-Hilbert functional in $\psi$ is $M_{\beta}^{\top}$ of that in $g$, that is $M_{\beta}(\mathcal{G} + \Lambda)$ up to a factor ($M_{\beta}$ is symmetric for the pairing), and its $\psi$-derivative has principal symbol $M_{\beta}\,\sigma(\mathcal{G})\,M_{\beta}$, symmetric. The check confirms the symmetry at $\beta \in \{-\tfrac12, \tfrac37, -2\}$ and that the Ricci symbol composed with $M_{-1/2}$ on the input is $M_{-1/2}\sigma(\mathcal{G})M_{-1/2}$: the route's Ricci form is the Einstein-Hilbert Euler-Lagrange expression of a densitised metric. So (i) is a statement about the varied field, not about the equations alone.

\emph{(ii)} $M_{-1/4}$ maps $\eta$ to $0$ and has rank $9$ on the ten-dimensional space (checked), so $M_{-1/4}(\mathcal{G} + \Lambda) = \mathcal{G} - \tfrac14\tr(\mathcal{G})$, the trace-free Ricci form, in which $\Lambda$ does not occur; for $\beta \neq -\tfrac14$, $M_{\beta}$ is invertible ($1 + 4\beta \neq 0$) and $M_{\beta}(\mathcal{G} + \Lambda) = 0$ fixes the trace $\mathcal{R}$ in terms of $\Lambda$, so $\Lambda$ is a parameter of the equation. So the trace-free form is the one member of the family with $\Lambda$ free, and by (i) it fails the Helmholtz condition on all variations of the metric. On trace-free $h$, $k$ (variations that fix the volume element; in Gauge Theory Gravity, frame variations at fixed $\det\hb$) the terms $A_{1}$, $A_{2}$, $A_{3}$ pair to zero ($\tr h = \tr k = 0$), so every covariant symbol is self-adjoint there; the check confirms this for the trace-free symbol on a basis of the nine-dimensional trace-free space, and the condition is met there by a witness: the Einstein-Hilbert functional at fixed volume element has $\delta S = \int\ip{\mathcal{G}}{h}$ with $\tr h = 0$, whose Euler-Lagrange expression is the trace-free part of $\mathcal{G}$. With an enlarged field content the trace-free equations are variational on all variations with $\Lambda$ a constant of integration: the Henneaux-Teitelboim form, Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-henneaux-teitelboim-promotion}. This is the route's own variational form: on the route $N$ is initial data and its solution space is the promoted one (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-route-makes-n-initial-data}), and under the promotion the norm mode is one global pair with no local mode (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.promoted-norm-one-global-pair}). For the metric alone a fixed value is needed (see the last paragraph of this step), and the frozen point's constraint carries it as an input, the registered input $N$ fixing $\Lambda$; it does not compute it: with $I = \nInf + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\nO$ in $\Cl(2,4)$ ($\nO = \tfrac12(e_{+} + e_{-})$, $\nInf = e_{+} - e_{-}$), $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}, checked in $\Cl(2,4)$). For de Sitter curvature at $\Lambda'$ the store's Ricci tensor is $\Lambda' g$ (the convention of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.macdowell-mansouri-principle-fixes-the-trace-free-part}); the trace-free form vanishes for every $\Lambda'$, and $\mathcal{G} + 3Q(I) = (\Lambda - \Lambda')g$ vanishes only at $\Lambda' = \Lambda$ (checked at two values of $\Lambda$ and three of $\Lambda'$). Beyond the family: Lovelock (1971, 1972; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-lovelock-and-anderson-duchamp-natural-lagrangians}(a)) proved that in four dimensions a symmetric tensor built naturally from the metric and its derivatives up to second order that is divergence-free (equivalently, for natural expressions, an Euler-Lagrange expression) is $a\mathcal{G} + bg$; its vacuum set has the single value $\Lambda = b/a$, so no natural variational problem of order at most two for the metric alone has the route's solution set with $\Lambda$ free. The order bound is needed: the Weyl-squared functional $\int W\cdot W$ is fourth order (the check finds its second variation at the flat background to be $2\,\Ric\cdot\Ric - \tfrac23 R^{2}$ in the linearised curvature, nonzero and homogeneous of degree four in $p$), and its Euler-Lagrange equations, the Bach equations, hold on every Einstein field of every $\Lambda$ in four dimensions (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-conformal-gravity-bach-equations-and-conformal-gauge-form}(a)), so its solution set contains the route's vacuum set with $\Lambda$ free and is larger. It is the frozen-point integrand on the normal tractor connection of a torsion-free field (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-integrand-on-tractor-transport-is-weyl-squared}(ii), (iii)).

\emph{(iii)} Invariance of a functional under displacement gauge transformations (diffeomorphisms) gives, by Noether's second theorem, $\nabla_{a}E^{ab} = 0$ identically; linearised at a flat point this is $p^{a}\sigma(p)_{ab} = 0$ for every $h$. On the route the same identity enters at the Bianchi step of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}(4), with $\nabla\cdot T = 0$ from (H3). Solving $p^{a}(\sum_{i} c_{i}A_{i})_{ab} = 0$ exactly gives a plane: $c_{1} = -c_{3}$ and $c_{2} = c_{4} = -c_{5}$; it contains the Einstein symbol and $A_{1} - A_{3} = (p_{a}p_{b} - \eta_{ab}p^{2})\tr h$, which is transverse and not self-adjoint. With self-adjointness ($c_{1} = c_{2}$) one line remains, spanned by the Einstein symbol. This is the linearised form of Lovelock's theorem, proved here without the import.

\emph{(iv)} Let $S$ be as stated. By (i) and (ii) (within the family) and by Lovelock's theorem (in general), its gravitational frame expression is $c(\mathcal{G} + \Lambda)$ with $\Lambda = 3Q(I)$; matching the route's coefficient $8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}$ in front of the source normalised as in (v) fixes $c$, that is $G = G_{\mathrm{cl}} = 1/(4\eta)$. If two local functionals have the same Euler-Lagrange expressions, their difference has identically vanishing Euler-Lagrange expression; by the exactness of the variational bicomplex it is locally a divergence, and for natural Lagrangians of a metric in four dimensions the variationally trivial ones are combinations of the Euler and Pontryagin densities plus divergences of natural currents (Anderson and Duchamp 1980, Anderson 1984; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-lovelock-and-anderson-duchamp-natural-lagrangians}(b)). Consistently, the check finds that the Euler density $E_{4} = \mathrm{Riem}\cdot\mathrm{Riem} - 4\Ric\cdot\Ric + R^{2}$ has zero second variation at the flat background, and that adding $R^{2}$ to it gives exactly the second variation of $R^{2}$. So in the metric reading $S$ is the Einstein-Hilbert functional with $G_{\mathrm{cl}}$ and $\Lambda$ plus $c_{E}E_{4} + c_{P}P_{4}$ plus a divergence, with $c_{E}$, $c_{P}$ not fixed by the route. The stored frozen-point functional is $(R - 2\Lambda + \alpha E_{4})/16\pi G$ with $\alpha = -3/(4\Lambda)$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.euler-term-horizon-entropy-shift}(i)), the member with $c_{E} = \alpha/16\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}$, $c_{P} = 0$; nothing on the route selects it. In first-order variables, on the field space of connections preserving $I$, the route sees only torsion-free fields, so a density whose Euler-Lagrange expressions vanish whenever the torsion does is invisible to it; the curvature-only classification (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.curvature-only-tractor-actions-are-macdowell-mansouri}(iii), granted for this first-order clause) finds the admissible densities $\kappa\,\epsilon(I, X, F, F) + \kappa' H + \kappa'' K$, with $K$ the Chern-Weil density (no field equations) and $H$ a Holst-type density whose frame equation vanishes on every curvature obeying the first Bianchi identity. Granting that classification, the route fixes $\kappa$ (by $G = G_{\mathrm{cl}}$; the frame equation of $\epsilon(I, X, F, F)$ is the Einstein form, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.macdowell-mansouri-principle-fixes-the-trace-free-part}(i)) and leaves $\kappa'$, $\kappa''$ free; within that class the Euler coefficient is the one carried by $\epsilon(I, X, F, F)$, fixed by $\Lambda$. On the normal tractor connections the same integrand is the Weyl square (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-integrand-on-tractor-transport-is-weyl-squared}(iii)), of fourth order, excluded by the order bound. \emph{For the imports of the open problem:} the route is compatible with a local action at fixed $\Lambda$ (witness: the stored functional) but does not single one out, so the existence of the action is not derived; the coefficients it leaves free, Euler and Pontryagin, are exactly those that distinguish the MacDowell-Mansouri functional from the Einstein-Hilbert functional, so its form is not derived either.

\emph{(v)} Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a local functional of $(g, \psi)$ with Euler-Lagrange system $(c(\mathcal{G} + \Lambda + 8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}T), E_{\psi})$, $c$ constant, and put $\mathcal{S}' = \mathcal{S} - S_{m}$. Its $\psi$-expression is $E_{\psi} - E_{\psi} = 0$ identically. The Hessian of $\mathcal{S}'$ is symmetric (Helmholtz), and its $(\psi, g)$ block is $D_{g}$ of the $\psi$-expression, which is $0$; so its $(g, \psi)$ block, $D_{\psi}$ of the $g$-expression, is $0$: $D_{\psi}\big(c(\mathcal{G} + \Lambda + 8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}T) - \delta S_{m}/\delta g\big) = 0$. With $\delta S_{m}/\delta g = 8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}\,c\,T_{H}$ (the normalisation of $T_{H}$ fixed by the same constant $c$) and $D_{\psi}(\mathcal{G} + \Lambda) = 0$, this is $D_{\psi}(T - T_{H}) = 0$ at every field; on a field space connected in $\psi$, $T - T_{H} = \Theta[g]$ does not depend on the matter, and $\Theta = 0$ if both vanish at $\psi = 0$. Conversely, if $T = T_{H}$ the system is the Euler-Lagrange system of $c$ times the Einstein-Hilbert functional plus $S_{m}$. The check verifies the cross condition $\ip{k}{K(p)} = L(-p)[k]$ for a scalar field with Lagrangian $\sqrt{g}(\tfrac12 g^{ab}\partial_{a}\psi\partial_{b}\psi - V(\psi)) - \tfrac12\xi\psi^{2}\sqrt{g}\,\mathcal{R}^{\circ}$ at the flat background, $K$ the $\psi$-derivative of the metric expression and $L$ the metric derivative of the matter equation, on the ten basis tensors at two momenta: with a background gradient $u$ and $V' = v_{1}$ constant ($\xi = 0$), $\ip{k}{K} = \tfrac12\tr k\,(u\cdot p - v_{1}) - u\cdot k\cdot p = L(-p)[k]$; with a constant background $s$, the $\xi$ terms $\xi s(p^{2}\tr k - p\cdot k\cdot p)$ appear on both sides (from $\sqrt{g}(-f\mathcal{G}^{\circ} - g\Box f + \nabla\nabla f)$, $f = -\tfrac12\xi\psi^{2}$, and from $-\xi\psi\,\delta\mathcal{R}^{\circ}$ with $\delta\mathcal{R}^{\circ} = p\cdot k\cdot p - p^{2}\tr k$). It fails when the source carries an altered trace term $-\tfrac12\lambda\,\tr k\,(u\cdot p)$, $\lambda = 1$, and when the source is the minimal stress while the matter equation carries $-\xi\psi\mathcal{R}^{\circ}$. So the condition ties the heat tensor to the matter functional, minimal or not; whether the matter couples minimally is not decided by it. So the energy part of the matter coupling is equivalent to the identification $T = T_{H}$, not derived from the route. The connection equation (spin density and torsion) does not occur on a torsion-free route, so the spin part of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-einstein-cartan-matter-coupling} is not reached.

\emph{Hypotheses that do the work.} Locality and naturality of the functional; the multiplier algebraic in $g$ (a multiplier depending on curvature or derivatives changes the principal symbol and is not covered); Euler-Lagrange expressions of order at most two (for (ii) beyond the family and for (iv)); the frozen point's $\Lambda$ (for the whole field; without it, unimodular variations); for (v), that the matter equations come from a local functional. The route's own premise (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) and (H1) to (H4) enter only through its output. Imported: Lovelock 1971 and 1972, and Anderson and Duchamp 1980 and Anderson 1984 on natural variationally trivial Lagrangians (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-lovelock-and-anderson-duchamp-natural-lagrangians}); Bach 1921 and the Bach-flatness of Einstein fields in four dimensions (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-conformal-gravity-bach-equations-and-conformal-gauge-form}). Literature cited from memory: the sufficiency of the Helmholtz conditions (Volterra-Vainberg), not used; Noether's second theorem.

synthesis.krein-quartet-drops-from-the-i.formal:
Let a gauge vector be gauge-fixed covariantly with parameter $\alpha > 0$ (the Nakanishi-Lautrup family; $\alpha = 1$ is the Gupta-Bleuler form of clause (K1) of Premise \claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields}), with its ghost and antighost, and call the \emph{weight} of a field its contribution to the induced Einstein-Hilbert coefficient in units of one minimally coupled real scalar (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-sakharov-induced-gravity-coefficients}(a), (b); a real scalar of curvature coupling $\xi_{R}$ has weight $1 - 6\xi_{R}$, a Weyl fermion $1$). The quartet is the time (or exact) component of the vector, its partner, the ghost and the antighost.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Energy cut-off on the Einstein static field; proved under the Krein premise, $\alpha = 1$.)} Under clause (K1) of the Krein premise, which fixes the zero-point energy of the negative-norm time component, on $\mathbb{R}\times S^{3}$ of unit radius in the Feynman gauge the time component, the exact part and the ghost pair all have frequencies $\sqrt{l(l+2)}$, with multiplicities $(l+1)^{2}$ ($l \ge 0$), $(l+1)^{2}$ ($l \ge 1$) and $2(l+1)^{2}$ of fermionic sign; the signed count vanishes at every $l \ge 1$ and is $-1$ at the zero frequency. So for every cut-off on energy the quartet contributes nothing to the zero-point sum, and the vector's weight is $-4$, that of its two helicities (the coexact one-forms, the attachment's helicity $\pm 1$ modules).
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Heat-kernel cut-off on the gauge-fixed operators; proved, in the Euclidean reading.)} On a closed Riemannian four-manifold (a Euclidean reading of the field equations, outside the flat background), with a proper-time cut-off on the gauge-fixed operator $P_{\alpha} = \delta d + \alpha^{-1}d\delta$ and on the ghost operator $\Delta_{0}$, the vector's weight is $\alpha - 5$ (transverse $-3$, longitudinal $\alpha$, ghosts $-2$) and its volume weight $1 + \alpha^{2}$; the two-helicity values $-4$ and $2$ hold only at $\alpha = 1$, and the Landau limit gives $-5$. On the unit four-sphere every term is computed exactly from the spectra.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Gauge-invariant reading; proved.)} The parameter-free product $\det_{T}(\Delta_{1})^{-1/2}\det{}'(\Delta_{0})^{1/2}$ under one cut-off has weight $-4$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The series' content; computed.)} With the twelve vectors of the connection-forced algebra (Theorem \claimref{standard-model.connection-forced}), forty-eight Weyl fields (three separate slot modules of sixteen, \claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components}) and the two elementary doublets (\claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}) of curvature coupling $\xi_{R}$, the induced coefficient is $B = 8(1 - 6\xi_{R})$ minimal-scalar units under the energy cut-off and $B = 12(\alpha - 1) + 8(1 - 6\xi_{R})$ under the heat-kernel cut-off on the gauge-fixed operators: zero at $\xi_{R} = \tfrac16$ in the first case and at $\xi_{R} = \tfrac16$, $\alpha = 1$ in the second, $-12$ at $\xi_{R} = \tfrac16$ in the Landau gauge, and $8$ at $\xi_{R} = 0$, $\alpha = 1$.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading (argued).} Under clause (K4) of the Krein premise the quartet has zero norm in the physical space (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-brst-kugo-ojima-strocchi-and-gribov}); still, a power-divergent coefficient sees it unless the regulator treats its four members alike, so the induced Einstein-Hilbert coefficient of the series' content is fixed by its physical content only together with the regulator and, for a covariant cut-off, the gauge. Under the Krein premise ($\alpha = 1$) the vector weight is $-4$ and the stored cancellation (\claimref{synthesis.attachment-modules-give-sakharov-weights-cancelling-at-three-separate-generations}) holds if the doublets are conformally coupled; schemes without a dimensionful cut-off induce no such term for massless fields (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-sakharov-induced-gravity-coefficients}(d)). Transport-absent.
synthesis.krein-quartet-drops-from-the-i.technical:
Count each field's contribution to the induced Einstein-Hilbert coefficient in units of one minimally coupled scalar: a scalar of curvature coupling $\xi_{R}$ gives $1 - 6\xi_{R}$, a Weyl fermion $1$ (with the Lichnerowicz term computed in geometric algebra), and a gauge vector in the Feynman gauge with its ghosts $-4$, the value of its two helicities.

Under the Krein premise, for a covariantly gauge-fixed vector the unphysical quartet (time or longitudinal component, its partner, ghost and antighost) has zero norm in the physical space, but whether it drops from a power-divergent coefficient depends on the regulator. On the Einstein static field with a cut-off on energy, in the Feynman gauge, all four members have the same frequencies $\sqrt{l(l+2)}$ and their signed multiplicities cancel at every level, leaving one zero-energy mode: the quartet drops and only the two helicities count. With a covariant heat-kernel cut-off on the gauge-fixed operator of gauge parameter $\alpha$ (computed in the Euclidean reading), the longitudinal eigenvalues are the scalar ones divided by $\alpha$ while the ghosts' are not, and the vector's weight becomes $\alpha - 5$: $-4$ only at $\alpha = 1$, $-5$ in the Landau gauge. On the unit four-sphere every term is computed exactly from the spectra.

With the series' content (twelve vectors, forty-eight Weyl fields, two Higgs doublets of curvature coupling $\xi_{R}$) the induced coefficient is $8(1 - 6\xi_{R})$ under the energy cut-off and $12(\alpha - 1) + 8(1 - 6\xi_{R})$ under the covariant one. The stored cancellation needs conformal coupling and, for the covariant cut-off, $\alpha = 1$, the Gupta-Bleuler value of the Krein premise. Reading, argued: the coefficient is fixed by the content only together with the regulator and the gauge. Transport-absent.
synthesis.krein-quartet-drops-from-the-i.lay: Sakharov's idea is that the strength of gravity could be induced by the quantum jitter of all the other fields. Each kind of field adds or subtracts a definite amount, and an earlier result showed that the series' force carriers and matter particles cancel exactly, at least for one way of cutting off the jitter at short distances. Force carriers come with extra bookkeeping modes that describe nothing physical and are removed in the end. This result checks, under the series' premise for these modes (an indefinite inner product), whether they really drop out of the count. With a cut-off on energy they do, level by level. With a cut-off that treats space and time alike, they do only for one particular choice of the bookkeeping, and otherwise each force carrier shifts the count. So the cancellation depends on the cut-off and the bookkeeping, not only on which particles exist. The series' own choice of bookkeeping is the one that keeps the cancellation, provided the Higgs fields couple to curvature in the special conformal way.

proofs.main:
\emph{Weights.} By Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-sakharov-induced-gravity-coefficients}(a), (b), a Laplace-type operator $D = -(\nabla^{2} + E)$ on a bundle of rank $r$ over a closed Riemannian four-manifold has heat trace $\mathrm{Tr}\,e^{-tD} = (4\pi t)^{-2}\bigl(\int r + t\int\mathrm{tr}(E + R/6) + O(t^{2})\bigr)$, and a term $\tfrac{\sigma}{2}\log\det D$ of the one-loop effective action, regulated by a heat-kernel (proper-time) cut-off $t \ge \epsilon$, contributes to the induced Einstein-Hilbert term in proportion to $\sigma\int\mathrm{tr}(E + R/6)\,\epsilon^{-1}$. We call $\sigma\,\mathrm{tr}(E + R/6)/(R/6)$ the \emph{weight} of the term: $1$ for a minimally coupled real scalar ($\sigma = 1$, $E = 0$), $1 - 6\xi_{R}$ for a real scalar of curvature coupling $\xi_{R}$ (we write $\xi_{R}$ for the curvature coupling; $\xi$ is the D-term level elsewhere in the store), and its $t^{-2}$ analogue $\sigma r$ the volume (quartic) weight. For a two-component fermion the Lichnerowicz term is $E = \tfrac12\sum_{a<b}e_{a}e_{b}\,\mathcal{R}(e_{a}\wedge e_{b})$ acting by left multiplication; on a field with $\mathcal{R}(B) = \kappa B$ on a set of planes the check computes it in $\Cl(4,0)$ as $-R/4$, so with $\sigma = -1$ on two components the weight is $-2(R/6 - R/4)/(R/6) = 1$. The Ricci map is $\Ric(a) = \sum_{b}e_{b}\cdot\mathcal{R}(e_{b}\wedge a)$; the check computes $\Ric = (0, 2, 2, 2)$ in a frame $(e_{0}, e_{i})$ with $R = 6$ on the Einstein static field $\mathbb{R}\times S^{3}$ of unit radius, and $\Ric = 3$, $R = 12$ on the unit four-sphere.

\emph{The vector and its quartet.} Write the gauge field as a one-form $A$ with field strength $dA$, gauge-fixed covariantly by the term $\tfrac{1}{2\alpha}(\delta A)^{2}$ ($\delta$ the codifferential; in Lorentzian signature the Nakanishi-Lautrup family, whose member $\alpha = 1$ has the Gupta-Bleuler commutator $[a(u), a(w)^{\dagger}] = -u\cdot w$ of clause (K1) of Premise \claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields}), with the Faddeev-Popov ghost and antighost, whose operator is $\delta d = \Delta_{0}$ on functions and which enter as $-\log\det\Delta_{0}$ (two real scalars of fermionic sign, weight $-2$). The quadratic operator on one-forms is $P_{\alpha} = \delta d + \alpha^{-1}d\delta = \Delta_{1} + (\alpha^{-1} - 1)d\delta$, with $\Delta_{1} = d\delta + \delta d$ the Hodge Laplacian; by the Weitzenb\"ock formula $\Delta_{1} = \nabla^{*}\nabla + \Ric$, so $E = -\Ric$ and $\mathrm{tr}(E + R/6) = -R + 4R/6 = -R/3$: the weight of $\tfrac12\log\det\Delta_{1}$ is $-2$, and with the ghosts the Feynman-gauge ($\alpha = 1$) vector has weight $-4$, the value of the stored count (\claimref{synthesis.attachment-modules-give-sakharov-weights-cancelling-at-three-separate-generations}(ii)). The unphysical quartet is the time component (in the static case) or the exact part of $A$, its partner, the ghost and the antighost; by clause (K4) of the Krein premise its states carry zero norm in the physical space (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-brst-kugo-ojima-strocchi-and-gribov}).

\emph{(i) Energy cut-off on the Einstein static field (under the Krein premise).} In the Feynman gauge on $\mathbb{R}\times S^{3}$ the field equation is $(\partial_{t}^{2} + \Delta)A = 0$ componentwise: since $e_{0}$ is parallel and $\Ric(e_{0}) = 0$ (computed), $A_{0}$ obeys the minimal scalar equation with $\Delta = \Delta_{0}$ on $S^{3}$, and the spatial part obeys it with the Hodge Laplacian $\Delta_{1}$ of $S^{3}$. The scalar harmonics of degree $l$ (restrictions of harmonic homogeneous polynomials of degree $l$ on $\mathbb{R}^{4}$) have $\Delta_{0} = l(l+2)$ and multiplicity $\binom{l+3}{3} - \binom{l+1}{3} = (l+1)^{2}$ (computed for $l < 40$; in general by the same binomial identity). The Hodge decomposition of one-forms on $S^{3}$ (no harmonic one-forms) is exact $\oplus$ coexact, and $\Delta_{1}d = d\Delta_{0}$, with $d$ injective on nonconstant functions; so the exact one-forms have the eigenvalues $l(l+2)$, $l \ge 1$, with multiplicity $(l+1)^{2}$. The ghost and antighost obey the minimal scalar equation. So all four members of the quartet have frequencies $\omega_{l} = \sqrt{l(l+2)}$, with multiplicities $(l+1)^{2}$ ($A_{0}$, $l \ge 0$), $(l+1)^{2}$ (exact part, $l \ge 1$) and $2(l+1)^{2}$ (ghosts, $l \ge 0$). A bosonic mode of either norm has zero-point energy $+\omega/2$: for the time component, quantised with $[a_{0}, a_{0}^{\dagger}] = -1$ as clause (K1) of the Krein premise requires, the symmetrised Hamiltonian $-\tfrac{\omega}{2}(a_{0}a_{0}^{\dagger} + a_{0}^{\dagger}a_{0}) = \omega N_{0} + \tfrac{\omega}{2}$ with $N_{0} = -a_{0}^{\dagger}a_{0}$; a real Grassmann mode has $-\omega/2$. The signed count at level $l$ is therefore $(l+1)^{2} + (l+1)^{2} - 2(l+1)^{2} = 0$ for $l \ge 1$ and $1 - 2 = -1$ at $l = 0$, where $\omega_{0} = 0$ (computed for $l < 40$, and identically from the multiplicities). For every cut-off function, $\tfrac12\sum\omega f(\omega/L)$ over the quartet is zero: the quartet drops level by level and the vector's zero-point sum is that of the coexact one-forms. These have $\Delta_{1} = (l+1)^{2}$, $l \ge 1$, and multiplicity $2l(l+2)$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-ikeda-taniguchi-spectra-of-the-hodge-laplacian-on-spheres}), which is $2(k^{2} - 1)$ at $k = l + 1$, the attachment's helicity $\pm 1$ modules of the stored count; the check confirms that the $S^{3}$ spectra reproduce the heat-kernel densities, $\tfrac{\sqrt{\pi}}{4}t^{-3/2}(1 + t)$ for $\Delta_{0}$ and $\tfrac{\sqrt{\pi}}{4}t^{-3/2}(3 - 3t)$ for $\Delta_{1}$ (with $\mathrm{tr}(E + R/6) = -6 + 3 = -3$ from the computed Ricci map), using $\int_{0}^{\infty}k^{2j}e^{-tk^{2}}\,dk = \Gamma(j + \tfrac12)/(2t^{j + 1/2})$ and the Euler-Maclaurin formula for an even summand (whose odd derivatives vanish at $0$, so the sum and the integral have the same polar part). So under an energy cut-off the vector's weight is $-4$ and comes from its two helicities alone. The energy cut-off and the heat-kernel cut-off give the same weights for the other fields: on an ultrastatic field the four-dimensional operator is $-\partial_{t}^{2}$ plus a Laplace-type spatial operator $D_{3}$, the frequencies are $\sqrt{D_{3}}$, and the curvature-linear heat coefficient of $D_{3}$ is $\mathrm{tr}(E + R_{3}/6)$ with $R_{3} = R$ there, so the $t^{-1}$ polar coefficient of the energy trace (the dictionary of \claimref{synthesis.attachment-modules-give-sakharov-weights-cancelling-at-three-separate-generations}(ii)) is the four-dimensional weight: $1$ per Weyl fermion and $1 - 6\xi_{R}$ per scalar. For $\alpha \neq 1$ the time and longitudinal components mix and have dipole solutions, but every frequency is still $\omega_{l}$; that the quartet then also drops is argued, not computed.

\emph{(ii) Heat-kernel cut-off on the gauge-fixed operators (Euclidean reading).} The computation is a Euclidean reading, outside the flat background on which the gravitational field lives: the weights it defines are the coefficients of the local curvature-linear density, which do not depend on the global field used to read them. On a closed Riemannian four-manifold, Hodge theory gives $\Omega^{1} = d\Omega^{0}\oplus\delta\Omega^{2}\oplus\mathcal{H}^{1}$, $P_{\alpha}$ preserves the decomposition, $P_{\alpha} = \Delta_{1}$ on coclosed forms, and $P_{\alpha}\,d\phi = \alpha^{-1}d\delta d\phi = \alpha^{-1}d\Delta_{0}\phi$. So the spectrum of $P_{\alpha}$ on exact forms is the nonzero spectrum of $\Delta_{0}$ divided by $\alpha$ (the flat momentum-space form, $P_{\alpha}(k)a = Q(k)a - (1 - \alpha^{-1})(k\cdot a)k$ with eigenvalue $Q(k)/\alpha$ on $k$ and $Q(k)$ on $k^{\perp}$, is checked in $\Cl(4,0)$), and the coclosed part of $\Delta_{1}$ has heat trace $\mathrm{Tr}\,e^{-t\Delta_{1}} - \mathrm{Tr}'e^{-t\Delta_{0}}$ (finitely many harmonic and zero modes contribute no pole). With the cut-off $t \ge \epsilon$ applied to $P_{\alpha}$ and to the ghost operator, the polar coefficients are additive: the coclosed part has $t^{-1}$ weight $-2 - 1 = -3$ and $t^{-2}$ weight $4 - 1 = 3$; $\mathrm{Tr}'e^{-t\Delta_{0}/\alpha}$ is $\mathrm{Tr}'e^{-t'\Delta_{0}}$ at $t' = t/\alpha$, so its $t^{-1}$ and $t^{-2}$ coefficients are multiplied by $\alpha$ and $\alpha^{2}$, weights $\alpha$ and $\alpha^{2}$; the ghosts give $-2$ and $-2$. Hence the vector's weight is $-3 + \alpha - 2 = \alpha - 5$ and its quartic weight is $3 + \alpha^{2} - 2 = 1 + \alpha^{2}$. The value $-4$ (and $2$) holds only at $\alpha = 1$; in the Landau limit the longitudinal modes become infinitely heavy and the weight is $-5$. On the unit four-sphere the check computes every term exactly from the spectra: $\Delta_{0} = l(l+3)$ with multiplicity $(l+1)(l+2)(2l+3)/6$ (checked against the harmonic-polynomial count for $l < 30$) and coexact $\Delta_{1} = (l+1)(l+2)$ with multiplicity $l(l+3)(2l+3)/2$, $l \ge 1$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-ikeda-taniguchi-spectra-of-the-hodge-laplacian-on-spheres}); with $\nu = l + \tfrac32$ both are odd polynomials in $\nu$ times $e^{-t\nu^{2}}$ on the half-integer grid, whose polar parts are those of the integrals, $\int_{0}^{\infty}\nu^{2j+1}e^{-t\nu^{2}}d\nu = j!/(2t^{j+1})$ (midpoint Euler-Maclaurin; the endpoint corrections are polynomial in $t$). They give $\tfrac16t^{-2} + \tfrac13t^{-1}$ and $\tfrac12t^{-2} - t^{-1}$, and the heat-kernel densities $\tfrac16(1 + 2t)t^{-2}$ for $\Delta_{0}$ and $\tfrac16(4 - 4t)t^{-2}$ for $\Delta_{1}$ (volume $8\pi^{2}/3$, $\mathrm{tr}(E + R/6) = -12 + 8 = -4$ from the computed Ricci map) are reproduced exactly; the weights $\alpha - 5$ and $1 + \alpha^{2}$ follow for $\alpha = 0, \tfrac12, 1, 2, 3$.

\emph{(iii) The gauge-invariant reading.} The product $\det_{T}(\Delta_{1})^{-1/2}\det{}'(\Delta_{0})^{1/2}$, which carries no gauge parameter (it is the result of (ii) at $\alpha = 1$, where the longitudinal factor and one ghost factor cancel), regulated by one cut-off, has weight $-3 - 1 = -4$ and quartic weight $3 - 1 = 2$, the two helicities.

\emph{(iv) The series' content.} The connection-forced algebra has dimension $8 + 3 + 1 = 12$ (Theorem \claimref{standard-model.connection-forced}), each generation sixteen Weyl components (\claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components}), three generations read as separate slot modules as in the stored count, and the rung field is two elementary doublets of hypercharge $\tfrac12$ (\claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}), eight real scalars, each of weight $1 - 6\xi_{R}$ by Fact (a). Summing, $B = 48 + 12\,w_{V} + 8(1 - 6\xi_{R})$ with $w_{V} = -4$ under the energy cut-off (by (i)) and $w_{V} = \alpha - 5$ under the heat-kernel cut-off on the gauge-fixed operators (by (ii)): $B = 8(1 - 6\xi_{R})$, respectively $B = 12(\alpha - 1) + 8(1 - 6\xi_{R})$. The check evaluates the sum for several $\alpha$ and $\xi_{R}$: it is $0$ at $\xi_{R} = \tfrac16$ for the energy cut-off and for $\alpha = 1$, $-12$ at $\xi_{R} = \tfrac16$ in the Landau gauge, $8$ at $\xi_{R} = 0$, $\alpha = 1$, and zero also at $(\alpha, \xi_{R}) = (\tfrac13, 0)$.

\emph{Reading (argued).} Under clause (K4) of the Krein premise the quartet has zero norm in the physical space (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-brst-kugo-ojima-strocchi-and-gribov}). The heat-kernel cut-off on $P_{\alpha}$ treats the longitudinal mode, whose eigenvalue is rescaled by $\alpha^{-1}$, differently from the ghosts, whose operator is not, so the quartet that (K4) removes from the physical space still contributes $\alpha - 1$ per vector to a power-divergent coefficient; a regulator applied alike to the four members (the energy cut-off, or any cut-off at $\alpha = 1$) removes it. The dependence of power-divergent terms on the gauge parameter is standard in kind; the weight $\alpha - 5$ is computed here. Schemes without a dimensionful cut-off (dimensional continuation, or the locally covariant renormalisation of the stress tensor) induce no such term for massless fields at all (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-sakharov-induced-gravity-coefficients}(d)). So the induced Einstein-Hilbert coefficient of the series' content is not fixed by its physical content alone: it is fixed by the content together with the regulator and, for a covariant cut-off, the gauge. Under the store's Krein premise, whose clause (K1) is the Gupta-Bleuler value $\alpha = 1$, the vector weight is $-4$ and the stored cancellation holds at $\xi_{R} = \tfrac16$; at $\xi_{R} = 0$ the content induces $B = 8$. The result does not use transport (transport-absent).

synthesis.loc-independent-of-clausius-an.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = G = 1$, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, $\mathrm{Ric}$ positive on spheres (the $\Ric^{\circ}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}), $S_{ab} = R_{ab} - \tfrac14 R\,g_{ab}$ the tracefree Ricci tensor, for a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime the trace-free part of the Ricci map of its field strength, read in components with the derived metric $g$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}). Fix a constant $c \neq 0$ and let $\mathcal{M}_{c}$ be the following assignment: every local Rindler horizon patch through $p$ changes its entropy as $\delta S = \eta(p)\,\delta A$ with
\[
\eta(p) \;=\; \tfrac14\bigl(1 + c\,S_{ab}S^{ab}(p)\bigr),
\]
the patch's boundary modes are in the state that (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise} prescribes, and the admissible pairs (gravitational field, matter) are those satisfying hypotheses (H1) to (H4) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius} with this density. (H1) thus holds in $\mathcal{M}_{c}$ by construction; the content is that the admissible class contains the $\Lambda$-vacua unchanged and a spacetime on which $\eta \neq \tfrac14$. On the integrated reading the class is small ($S_{ab}S^{ab}$ must be constant on each admissible field; Reissner-Nordstr\"om with its Maxwell field, $S_{ab}S^{ab} = 4Q^{4}/r^{8}$, is not admissible). The entropy here is decoupled from any mode count, as in version 2 of the premise, which dropped the mode-count reading: (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) is imposed on the state, and $\mathcal{M}_{c}$ is not a model of version 1, where the entropy of a fixed mode set in the (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) state would fix $\eta$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Vacuum data unchanged.)} On every field with $\mathrm{Ric} = \Lambda g$ (Ricci map $\Lambda$ times the identity), in particular the Schwarzschild, Kerr, Schwarzschild-de Sitter and de Sitter fields, $S_{ab} = 0$ and $\eta = \tfrac14$, and (H1) holds with $T = 0$. So every statement of the store about these geometries (horizon temperatures under (R) and (R$_{\Lambda}$), the Clausius integrals along the Schwarzschild and Schwarzschild-de Sitter families of Theorems \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-entropy-clause-curvature-independent-density}(ii) and \claimref{synthesis.sds-clausius-fixes-area-constant}, the cutoff counts of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.black-hole-data-do-not-fix-field-equations}(iii) on Schwarzschild) holds in $\mathcal{M}_{c}$ exactly as in the store; whatever tension those statements already have among themselves is inherited, not created (the literal cutoff count on Schwarzschild-de Sitter, identified with the horizon modes, already disagrees with $A_{b}/4$: filed alongside, synthesis.cutoff-count-is-not-a-local-density-on-sds), and the calibration of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-entropy-clause-curvature-independent-density}(ii) returns $\tfrac14$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(A spacetime where it fails.)} Let $a > 0$ and let $(g, T)$ be the Einstein static universe $-dt^{2} + a^{2}(d\chi^{2} + \sin^{2}\chi\,(d\theta^{2} + \sin^{2}\theta\,d\phi^{2}))$ with dust at rest of density $\rho$, $8\pi\rho = 2(1 + 3c/a^{4})/a^{2}$. Then $S_{ab}S^{ab} = 3/a^{4}$ everywhere, $\eta = \tfrac14(1 + 3c/a^{4}) \neq \tfrac14$, the dust is conserved, and for every point and every null $k$
\[
T(k,k) - \frac{\eta}{2\pi}\,\mathrm{Ric}(k,k) \;=\; 0 ,
\]
so the leading defect of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}(2) vanishes and (H1) holds on every local Rindler patch, on the differences reading and, since $\eta$ is constant on this spacetime, on the integrated reading. Its field equations are $G_{ab} + \Lambda_{J}g_{ab} = 8\pi G_{e}T_{ab}$ with $G_{e} = 1/(4\eta)$ and integration constant $\Lambda_{J} = 1/a^{2}$ (equal to a given $\Lambda$ for $a^{2} = 1/\Lambda$). Inside the Einstein static universe alone the density is constant; the density law of $\mathcal{M}_{c}$ depends on curvature: it is $\tfrac14$ on every $\Lambda$-vacuum and $\tfrac14(1 + 3c/a^{4})$ on the Einstein static universe, and (Loc), which forces one universal constant by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-entropy-clause-curvature-independent-density}(i), fails in $\mathcal{M}_{c}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Independence.)} Hence (Loc) does not follow from (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$), from (H1) to (H4) on either reading of (H1), or from the $\Lambda$-vacuum horizon data of the store.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Where the integrated reading confines it.)} If the entropy of a patch is $\int\eta\,dA$ with $\eta$ a $C^{1}$ function on the invertible region that depends only on the curvature scalars at the point (scalars of the field strength), and (H1) holds, then by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-entropy-clause-curvature-independent-density}(iv) $\eta$ is constant on each connected spacetime (a gravitational field on a connected invertible region); if the spacetime contains one point whose curvature scalars are those of a point of a Schwarzschild, Schwarzschild-de Sitter or de Sitter horizon (for example any region of exact de Sitter, or a vacuum exterior close enough to a horizon), then $\eta = \tfrac14$ throughout it. So on the integrated reading (Loc) can fail only in spacetimes with no such point, of which (ii) is one.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Beyond one flat chart.} The closed spatial slices of the Einstein static universe in (ii) are global and are not carried by a single gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime; the statements above that hold on the invertible region are in Gauge Theory Gravity (on any chart of the Einstein static universe that omits one point of each slice, the field strength, the dust and the Clausius balance at every point are as stated), and the closed spatial slices are read on the manifold assembled from the derived metric's charts.
synthesis.loc-independent-of-clausius-an.technical:
The local-horizon premise has two clauses; this result concerns (Loc), which says the entropy per unit area of a small horizon patch does not depend on the curvature or the matter at the point. The open problem asks either for a derivation of (Loc) from the series' structure or for a model of the other premises in which it fails. Here is such a model. Give every local horizon the density one quarter times $(1 + c\,S_{ab}S^{ab})$, where $S_{ab}$ is the tracefree part of the Ricci tensor. In every vacuum with a cosmological constant this tracefree part vanishes, so every vacuum black-hole and de Sitter horizon the store treats keeps its temperature, its entropy $A/4$ and every calibration built on them; the temperature clause is untouched. In the Einstein static universe filled with dust the density is $\tfrac14(1 + 3c/a^{4})$, not one quarter, and Jacobson's Clausius balance still holds on every local horizon there, with a correspondingly renormalised Newton coupling and the usual cosmological constant $1/a^{2}$.

So nothing in the Clausius relation, in the temperature clause or in the $\Lambda$-vacuum horizon data forces (Loc). The Clausius relation holds in the model by construction of its admissible class; what is shown is that this class keeps every vacuum and contains a spacetime where the density is not one quarter. The model needs the entropy decoupled from a mode count, as in the premise's second version. This is the store's exact form of a point known in substance from Jacobson-type derivations with curvature-dependent entropy (Eling, Guedens and Jacobson), not a new mechanism. A survey of the store's postulates finds none that fixes the entropy of non-Killing horizons or the coupling of matter in the field equations, so the model differs from the store's intended reading only where no postulate speaks; that part is a survey, not a theorem. The curvature-independence clause is therefore a genuine premise: it fixes $\eta$, hence, together with the temperature clause (whose independence is filed alongside, synthesis.r-loc-independent-sets-matter-coupling), the matter coupling of gravity, the separation the stored black-hole-data result locates. On the integrated reading, where entropy is the integral of the density, the stored constancy result does more: the density is constant on each connected spacetime, hence one quarter on any spacetime containing a single point with the curvature of a calibrated horizon, so failures are confined to spacetimes like the static universe that contain none. The static universe's closed spatial slices are global and are not carried by the store's one-chart fields, so they are read on several charts of flat spacetime, each carrying its own gravitational field, glued on overlaps by displacement and rotation gauge transformations. On the differences reading of the premise's second version even that confinement is absent. The first-order Euler-entropy rate on local patches, which excludes the Euler term on the integrated reading, is filed alongside, synthesis.euler-entropy-first-order-rate-on-local-patches.
synthesis.loc-independent-of-clausius-an.lay: To derive Einstein's equations from thermodynamics one assumes that every small piece of horizon carries the same entropy per unit area, whatever the gravitational field strength or matter there. Could that follow from the rest of the series? This result says no, by example. Imagine a world where the entropy per area is a quarter plus a small extra amount that grows with the matter-induced part of the gravitational field strength. Around black holes and in empty space with a cosmological constant that extra amount is zero, so every black-hole and cosmological-horizon fact the series relies on is unchanged. But in a universe uniformly filled with dust it is not zero, and the heat-balance argument still works there, just with a slightly different strength of gravity. So the equal-entropy-everywhere assumption is doing real work: it is what fixes how strongly matter sources the gravitational field, and the rest of the series does not supply it.
