synthesis.local-boost-temperature-is-loc.formal:
Signature $(-,+,+,+)$ in this statement and its proof; in signature $(+,-,-,-)$ with the Riemann tensor still positive on spheres every component $R_{abcd}$ with all indices down changes sign, so $k$ below is $-R_{0101}/3$ there, while with the store's curvature sign (minus that tensor) it is $R_{0101}/3$ unchanged. The clause numbers (i), (ii) and (iii) of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise} used here are those of its version 1 (clause (i) the mode count and entropy, clause (ii) the temperature, clause (iii) the modular flow); the current version states the entropy as (Loc), the temperature as (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$), and records the rest under ``Not part of this premise''. Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), $p$ a point of its invertible region, $\ell$ a future physically null direction at $p$, $n$ the other null direction of a boost plane through $p$ containing $\ell$, and $\mathcal{H}_{p,\ell}$ the local Rindler horizon of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise}; let $D$ be a causal diamond about $p$ of edge radius $L$. Leading order means leading order in the size of the patch against the scale of the field strength $\mathcal{R}$ at $p$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The geometric half, derived.)} In a normal gauge at $p$ (Riemann normal coordinates: a displacement gauge in which the straight background lines through $p$ are the geodesics of the derived metric, with $\hb(p) = 1$ and $\Omega(p) = 0$), the derived metric is $g_{ab} = \eta_{ab} - \tfrac13 R_{acbd}x^{c}x^{d} + O(x^{3})$, with $x$ the background displacement from $p$ and $R_{acbd}$ the curvature at $p$, read from the field strength in the signature of this statement. On the boost plane through $p$, with $x = \rho(\sinh\lambda, \cosh\lambda, 0, 0)$, the metric induced by the terms up to second order is
\[
d\rho^{2} - F(\rho)^{2}\,d\lambda^{2}, \qquad F(\rho)^{2} = \rho^{2} + k\rho^{4}, \quad k = \tfrac13 R_{0101},
\]
with no cross term and no dependence on the rapidity $\lambda$, for every field strength at $p$; the third-order terms $-\tfrac16\nabla_{e}R_{acbd}x^{c}x^{d}x^{e}$ add $O(\rho^{5})$ to $F^{2}$, with rapidity dependence. Hence $F(0) = 0$ and $F'(0) = 1$, and by Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-section-period} read with unit rate, the Euclidean section of the local boost is regular at its tip $\rho = 0$ (the bifurcation point $p$ of the local boost, its fixed point in the boost plane) exactly when the period of imaginary rapidity is $2\pi$. The static observer at $\rho$ has proper acceleration $a = F'/F$ and, at rapidity period $2\pi$, proper inverse temperature $2\pi F$, so $T = a/(2\pi F'(\rho))$; with $F'(\rho)^{2} = (1 + 2k\rho^{2})^{2}/(1 + k\rho^{2})$ from the second-order terms, $T = (a/2\pi)\bigl(1 - \tfrac32 k\rho^{2} + O(\rho^{3})\bigr)$, and $T = a/2\pi$ at leading order. Off the boost plane, at transverse distance $y$, the induced metric depends on $\lambda$ at order $|\mathrm{Riem}|\,y^{2}$, the size of the field strength times $y^{2}$, so these statements hold at leading order and not beyond. For a diamond of radius $L$ in the leading-order flat geometry of the normal gauge, $\zeta = \bigl((L^{2} - t^{2} - r^{2})\partial_{t} - 2t\,x^{i}\partial_{i}\bigr)/(2L)$ is conformal Killing, vanishes on the edge $\{t = 0, r = L\}$, is divergence-free there, and its derivative on the edge is the unit boost of the plane spanned by $\partial_{t}$ and the edge normal: surface gravity $1$, the normalisation of (i) for the wedge.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Clause (iii), read on the whole mode algebra, is clause (ii).)} Let $\mathfrak{A}$ be the CAR algebra over a mode set $\mathcal{J}$ (the Definition's mode set, renamed here so as not to clash with the unit $J$) with windows $\mathfrak{A}_{F}$ (Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics}), its numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$, $J = e_{2}e_{3}$ the complex unit of the radial atom from which the boundary modes descend (\claimref{synthesis.transverse-bivector-is-the-complex-unit-of-the-radial-atom}), and let $\tau_{\lambda}(a_{j}) = e^{-Jw_{j}\lambda}a_{j}$ be a quasi-free flow in rapidity with real weights $w_{j}$. For $\beta > 0$ a state $\omega$ is $(\tau, \beta)$-KMS if and only if, on every window, $\omega|_{\mathfrak{A}_{F}}$ is faithful and its modular group is $\sigma_{s} = \tau_{-\beta s}$; the faithful states with that modular group on a window are exactly one, the Gibbs state of $\sum_{j \in F} w_{j}N_{j}$ at $\beta$. With $\beta = 2\pi$ of rapidity, clause (iii) of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise}, read as a statement about the modular flow of the state on the patch's whole mode algebra, is therefore equivalent, on a patch carrying such modes, to KMS at rapidity period $2\pi$, which is clause (ii) at leading order, the conversion to $T = a/2\pi$ in proper time being (i) (exact only where $F' = 1$). The stronger geometric reading of clause (iii), a flow carrying the algebras of nested sub-patches properly into one another, cannot hold on a mode space where the boost acts by phases (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-modular-clause-moves-no-nested-patch}) and is not treated here.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The thermal half, assumed.)} Consequently, for a patch carrying a mode algebra on which the local boost (or the diamond flow) acts as such a quasi-free phase flow, an assumption and not a result, clauses (ii) and (iii) of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise} together are, at leading order, the single condition
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$)] for all elements $a, b$ of every window, the correlator $F_{a,b}(\lambda) = \omega\bigl(a\,\tau_{\lambda}(b)\bigr)$ continues in imaginary rapidity and its two orderings meet after one period of the regular Euclidean section of the local boost: $F_{a,b}(\lambda + 2\pi J) = \omega\bigl(\tau_{\lambda}(b)\,a\bigr)$, the continuation taken in $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$.
\end{enumerate}
This is joint KMS on whole windows: the local-boost form of the joint KMS condition that defines the I-state (Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state}), which the store obtains at a Schwarzschild horizon from Premise \claimref{singularity.r-regularity-fixed-locus} for the single-mode marginals together with the joint quasi-freeness of Premise \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave}, and at the de Sitter horizon from Premise \claimref{synthesis.r-lambda-regularity-cosmological-horizon} for the marginals. (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) is a new premise, stronger than the local form of (R) alone. Under it the state is the quasi-free state with symbol $(1 + e^{2\pi w})^{-1}$, the unique KMS state whatever the weights $w_{j}$, so the condition fixes the state without fixing which modes the patch carries. No condition on the pair $(\mathfrak{A}, \tau)$ alone can replace it: by Theorem \claimref{singularity.rate-rigidity-temperature-not-algebra-intrinsic} the value of $\beta$ is fixed only by a stipulation or by data outside the pair.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.local-boost-temperature-is-loc.technical: Premise (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) asks for three things on every small local horizon: an area density of entropy, the temperature $a/2\pi$ and a geometric modular flow. This result shows that the last two, with the modular flow read on the patch's whole mode algebra and the boost acting on the modes by phases, are one condition, and separates what in it is derived from what is assumed. Derived: the geometric half. In a normal gauge about any point of a gravitational field on flat spacetime ($\hb = 1$ and $\Omega = 0$ there, the Riemann normal coordinates of the derived metric; signature $(-,+,+,+)$), the second-order derived metric on a boost plane is $d\rho^{2} - (\rho^{2} + \tfrac13R_{0101}\rho^{4})\,d\lambda^{2}$, the same at every rapidity, so the Euclidean continuation is smooth at its tip, the bifurcation point of the local boost, exactly for rapidity period $2\pi$, whatever the field strength, and an observer of acceleration $a$ sees $T = a/2\pi$ up to a relative correction $-\tfrac32k\rho^{2}$ and terms of order $\rho^{3}$. The diamond's conformal Killing field has unit surface gravity at its edge, the same normalisation. On every finite window of a mode algebra, a state is thermal (KMS) at inverse temperature $\beta$ for the boost exactly when it is faithful and its modular flow is the boost run at $-\beta$ per unit modular parameter, so the modular-flow clause adds nothing to the temperature clause (a geometric action on nested sub-patches is a stronger reading, not treated here). Assumed: the thermal half, the condition (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) that the state of the patch's modes be jointly KMS for the local boost at rapidity period $2\pi$ on whole windows. At Killing horizons the series makes the corresponding assumption in two parts, (R) for each single mode and (Q) for the joint quasi-free state; (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) is the local form of both together, a new premise and stronger than the local form of (R). It fixes the state uniquely whatever modes the patch carries. Because the temperature is not intrinsic to the algebra and its flow, a condition referring to the geometry cannot be avoided. This is a reduction of two clauses to one premise, not a derivation of the temperature, and it uses no feature specific to the series.
synthesis.local-boost-temperature-is-loc.lay: The assumption that every small horizon is hot at the Unruh temperature and that its quantum state's internal clock runs along the horizon's own boost was stated as two separate requirements. This result shows that, read as statements about all the modes of the horizon together, they are one. The geometry part can be made local: near any point, however strong the gravitational field is, the smoothness condition that sets the temperature at a black hole gives the Unruh temperature, up to small corrections. For a quantum state on a finite set of modes, being thermal for a flow and having that flow as its internal clock are the same property. What is left is one assumption, that the modes of every small horizon are jointly thermal at that temperature. At black holes the series makes the corresponding assumption in two parts, one for each mode separately and one for how the modes combine; the local version needs both, so it is a new assumption, stronger than the black-hole smoothness rule alone. It is not derived here from anything weaker.

proofs.main:
Read in Gauge Theory Gravity, the Riemann normal coordinates below are the background coordinates of a normal gauge at $p$, with $\hb(p) = 1$ and $\Omega(p) = 0$, the metric is the derived metric and $R_{acbd}$ is read from the field strength (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}, clauses (i), (iii) and (iv)). \emph{(i), the boost plane.} Take Riemann normal coordinates at $p$ adapted to an orthonormal frame with $e_{0} \pm e_{1}$ along $\ell$ and $n$, so that to second order $g_{ab}(x) = \eta_{ab} - \tfrac13 R_{acbd}x^{c}x^{d}$ with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ (the third-order terms are treated at the end of this step). On the plane $x^{2} = x^{3} = 0$ put $x = \rho(\sinh\lambda, \cosh\lambda, 0, 0)$; then $\partial_{\rho}x = x/\rho$ and $u := \partial_{\lambda}x = \rho(\cosh\lambda, \sinh\lambda, 0, 0)$. The flat part gives $\eta(\partial_{\rho}x, \partial_{\rho}x) = 1$, $\eta(\partial_{\rho}x, u) = 0$ and $Q(u) = -\rho^{2}$. The curvature part is $R(V, x, W, x) = R_{acbd}V^{a}x^{c}W^{b}x^{d}$, antisymmetric in its first two and in its last two slots; it vanishes whenever $V$ or $W$ is $\partial_{\rho}x \propto x$, and for $V = W = u$, all four vectors lying in the $(e_{0}, e_{1})$ plane, it equals $R_{0101}(u^{0}x^{1} - u^{1}x^{0})^{2} = R_{0101}\rho^{4}(\cosh^{2}\lambda - \sinh^{2}\lambda)^{2} = R_{0101}\rho^{4}$. So the induced metric is $d\rho^{2} - (\rho^{2} + \tfrac13R_{0101}\rho^{4})\,d\lambda^{2}$ to this order, independent of $\lambda$. Writing $F^{2} = \rho^{2}(1 + k\rho^{2})$ with $k = R_{0101}/3$, $F(0) = 0$ and $F'(0) = 1$ for every $k$. Continuing $\lambda = -I_5\theta$, with $I_5 = I_4e$ the central unit of $\Cl(2,3)$, the unit of a continued coordinate of a spacetime vector (\claimref{std-algebra.complexification-is-the-odd-extension}), gives $d\rho^{2} + F^{2}d\theta^{2}$, which is the form of Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-section-period} with unit rate; that proposition's argument (smoothness at $\rho = 0$ iff the angle period times $F'(0)$ is $2\pi$) uses only $F(0) = 0$ and $F'(0)$, so the section is regular at the bifurcation point exactly for $\theta$-period $2\pi$. For the metric $d\rho^{2} - F^{2}d\lambda^{2}$ the curve of fixed $\rho$ has proper time $F\,d\lambda$ and proper acceleration $F'/F$; at rapidity period $2\pi$ the proper inverse temperature is $2\pi F$, so $T/(a/2\pi) = 1/F'$, and $F'^{2} = (F^{2})'^{2}/(4F^{2}) = (1 + 2k\rho^{2})^{2}/(1 + k\rho^{2}) = 1 + 3k\rho^{2} + O(\rho^{4})$ from the second-order terms. The third-order term $-\tfrac16\nabla_{e}R_{acbd}x^{c}x^{d}x^{e}$ of the normal-coordinate expansion contributes $-\tfrac16\nabla_{e}R(u, x, u, x)\,x^{e} = O(\rho^{5})$ to $F^{2}$, rapidity dependent through $x^{e}$, hence $O(\rho^{3})$ to $F'^{2}$; so $T = (a/2\pi)(1 - \tfrac32k\rho^{2} + O(\rho^{3}))$, the stated $T$. With a transverse offset $y = (x^{2}, x^{3})$ the term $R(u, x, u, x)$ acquires $2R(u, x_{\parallel}, u, y) + R(u, y, u, y)$, which depend on $\lambda$ through $u$; their size is $|\mathrm{Riem}|\,\rho^{3}|y|$ and $|\mathrm{Riem}|\,\rho^{2}|y|^{2}$, so the conical angle on the edge element at distance $|y|$ from $p$ is $2\pi$ up to relative order $|\mathrm{Riem}|\,|y|^{2}$, the leading-order statement and no more. The script checks the induced metric exactly at rational rapidities (rational $\cosh$, $\sinh$) for algebraic curvature tensors built as sums of Kulkarni-Nomizu products, the rational-function identity for $F'^{2}$, and, as a control, that the offset metric depends on $\lambda$.

\emph{(i), the diamond.} For $\zeta^{t} = (L^{2} - t^{2} - r^{2})/2L$, $\zeta^{i} = -t\,x^{i}/L$: $\partial_{t}\zeta^{t} = -t/L$, $\partial_{i}\zeta^{t} = -x^{i}/L$, $\partial_{t}\zeta^{i} = -x^{i}/L$, $\partial_{j}\zeta^{i} = -t\,\delta^{i}_{j}/L$. Lowering with $\eta$ ($\zeta_{t} = -\zeta^{t}$), the $tt$ entry of $\partial_{a}\zeta_{b} + \partial_{b}\zeta_{a}$ is $2t/L$, each spatial diagonal entry is $-2t/L$ and the mixed entries are $-x^{i}/L + x^{i}/L = 0$, so $\partial_{a}\zeta_{b} + \partial_{b}\zeta_{a} = -(2t/L)\eta_{ab} = \tfrac12(\partial\cdot\zeta)\eta_{ab}$ with $\partial\cdot\zeta = -4t/L$: conformal Killing. On the edge $t = 0$, $r = L$ the field vanishes and the divergence vanishes, and with $n = x/L$ the edge normal, $\partial_{t}\zeta = -n$ and $n^{i}\partial_{i}\zeta^{t} = -1$, so $\nabla\zeta$ there is minus the unit boost generator of the $(t, n)$ plane, surface gravity $1$. Fact \claimref{angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hypotheses} records that for the free massless field the modular group of a double cone is geometric; the statement that it is this flow at $2\pi$ per unit modular parameter is Hislop and Longo's, cited from memory \cite{HislopLongo1982}, and is not used. Only the geometric normalisation, surface gravity $1$ as for the wedge, enters the result.

\emph{(ii).} Fix a finite window $F$. The flow $\tau$ preserves $\mathfrak{A}_{F} \cong \End(\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{F})$, a matrix factor, and acts there as $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{J\lambda K})$, $K = \sum_{j \in F}w_{j}N_{j}$, with $J = e_{2}e_{3}$ the complex unit of the boundary modes (\claimref{synthesis.transverse-bivector-is-the-complex-unit-of-the-radial-atom}); this unit acts on the modes and their flows, the $I_5$ of the continued line element in (i) on a coordinate, and the two are not identified. If $\omega$ is $(\tau, \beta)$-KMS on $\mathfrak{A}$, its restriction to the invariant subalgebra $\mathfrak{A}_{F}$ is KMS (Theorem \claimref{hawking.kms-restricts-invariant-subalgebras}), hence equal to the Gibbs state $\varrho = e^{-\beta K}/\mathrm{tr}\,e^{-\beta K}$ (Theorem \claimref{singularity.kms-uniqueness-factor}, Theorem \claimref{hawking.gibbs-states-are-kms-conversely-finite}), which is faithful since $\varrho$ is invertible; its modular flow is $\sigma_{s}(x) = \varrho^{Js}x\varrho^{-Js}$ (Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-theory-matrix-factor-proved-outright}), which is $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{-J\beta Ks})$, the flow at $-\beta s$. Conversely let $\omega|_{\mathfrak{A}_{F}} = \mathrm{tr}(\varrho'\,\cdot\,)$ be faithful with $\operatorname{Ad}(\varrho'^{Js}) = \operatorname{Ad}(e^{-J\beta Ks})$ for all real $s$. Differentiating at $s = 0$, $[\ln\varrho' + \beta K, x] = 0$ for every $x \in \mathfrak{A}_{F}$, so $\ln\varrho' + \beta K$ is central; the centre of a matrix factor is the scalars, so $\varrho' = c\,e^{-\beta K}$, and normalisation gives $\varrho' = \varrho$, which is KMS (Theorem \claimref{hawking.gibbs-states-are-kms-conversely-finite}). If this holds on every window, $\omega$ is KMS on the dense union of windows and hence on $\mathfrak{A}$ (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-kms-passes-inductive-limits}). On the von Neumann algebra $\pi_{\omega}(\mathfrak{A})''$ the analogous equivalence is Takesaki's theorem (cited from memory, not used); the statement above is the window form. The script verifies, on a window of three modes in $\Cl(3,3)$ with rational Boltzmann factors $q_{k}$ standing for $e^{-2\pi w_{k}}$, that the Gibbs element $G$ implements the imaginary-time flow on the generators, $G v_{k} G^{-1} = q_{k}^{-1}v_{k}$ and $G v_{k}^{*}G^{-1} = q_{k}v_{k}^{*}$, which is $\tau_{J\beta}$ (the content of the KMS identity, which by cyclicity of the trace holds for $\operatorname{Ad}(\varrho')$ with any invertible $\varrho'$), the Fermi-Dirac occupations $q_{k}/(1 + q_{k})$, that the centre is the scalars (the commutator map with the six generators has rank $63$), and that two faithful non-Gibbs states (one Boltzmann factor changed; a hop term added) fail $\operatorname{Ad}(\varrho') = \tau_{J\beta}$ on the generators and the KMS identity with $\operatorname{Ad}(G)$, while $c\varrho$ passes both; and a correlated state with the same single-mode marginals ($G$ plus a small multiple of $\sigma_{0}\sigma_{1}$, $\sigma_{k} = 2N_{k} - 1$) keeps every single-mode expectation and fails the joint condition.

\emph{(iii).} By (ii) with $\beta = 2\pi$ of rapidity and (i) for the conversion to proper time, clause (ii) of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise} and its clause (iii) are each equivalent to: $\omega$ is $(\tau, 2\pi)$-KMS in rapidity. Spelled out on window elements, the KMS condition at $\beta = 2\pi$ is the displayed (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$), and $2\pi$ is the period of the regular Euclidean section by (i); the condition quantifies over all elements of every window, so it is joint KMS. Premise \claimref{singularity.r-regularity-fixed-locus} (where the period $2\pi/\kappa$ of Killing time is $2\pi$ of rapidity, Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-section-period}) and Premise \claimref{synthesis.r-lambda-regularity-cosmological-horizon} constrain only single-mode marginals; the joint KMS state at a Schwarzschild horizon, the I-state of Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state}, needs in addition the joint quasi-freeness of Premise \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave}. So (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) is the local-boost form of (R) and the joint part of (Q) together, and it is stronger than the local form of (R): a product of single-mode Gibbs states at one period satisfies both, but a state with the same marginals and correlated modes satisfies the local form of (R) and not (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$). For a quasi-free flow the KMS state is unique among all states and is the quasi-free state with symbol $(1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1}$, for any self-adjoint one-particle Hamiltonian (Corollary \claimref{hawking.full-uniqueness-given-dynamics}), so (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) fixes the state whatever the weights. Finally, Theorem \claimref{singularity.rate-rigidity-temperature-not-algebra-intrinsic}(iii)-(iv) shows that the KMS states of $(\mathfrak{A}, \tau)$ form a line on which automorphisms intertwining the flow act only by $\beta \mapsto -\beta$, and that $|\beta|$ is meaningful only relative to the parametrisation of the flow; a condition selecting $\beta = 2\pi$ of rapidity must therefore refer to the geometry of the flow, as (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) does through the regular Euclidean section.

\emph{Remark (a survey, not part of the theorem).} The store offers two other ways to obtain the temperature, and neither applies to the store's mode spaces. The Bisognano-Wichmann and Borchers mechanism delivers $2\pi$ from positivity of energy and covariance (Fact \claimref{angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hypotheses}), but on a mode space where the boost acts by phases it dilates no nontrivial translation group (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.point-spectrum-boost-admits-no-half-sided-translations}), so that route needs the continuum mode space and a local net that the store does not construct. The incidence vacua read boost-constantly have inverse temperature $-\ln|Q(x)|$, a function of the interval rather than a constant rapidity period (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boost-stationary-incidence-vacua-read-interval}(v)), so they do not give $a/2\pi$. Within the store, then, (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) is not derived from weaker premises.

synthesis.macdowell-mansouri-is-the-froz.formal:
Work in $\Cl(2,4)$ with $\nO$, $\nInf$ as in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}, $\Lambda \neq 0$, frozen point $I = \nInf + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\nO$ ($Q(I) = \Lambda/3$), canonical tractor $X = \nO$ and Stelle-West vector $V = X - \tfrac{3}{\Lambda}I$ ($Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$, $\ip{I}{V} = 0$), as in Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}; $W = \{I, V\}^{\perp}$, of signature $(1,3)$. Orientation as in the stored check of that theorem: generators $e_{0}$ ($+1$), $e_{1}, e_{2}, e_{3}$ ($-1$), $e_{4}$ ($+1$), $e_{5}$ ($-1$), $\nO = \tfrac12(e_{4} + e_{5})$, $\nInf = e_{4} - e_{5}$, $I_{6} = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}e_{4}e_{5}$; two-forms are combined by the exterior product of their form parts (a sum over ordered planes), so that $\epsilon(I, V, e\wedge e, e\wedge e) = 6$ times the volume form. Let $P(B_{1}, B_{2}, B_{3}) = \langle B_{1}B_{2}B_{3}\rangle_{6}\,I_{6}^{-1}$ be the Pfaffian (cubic invariant) of the bivectors, so that $\epsilon(I, V, F, G) = P(I\wedge V, F, G)$. On a five-dimensional base with coordinates $(x, y)$, let $\theta$ be a vector-valued one-form with values in $V^{\perp}$ (the frame), $E = \theta\wedge V/Q(V)$ (the translational part of the connection, in the normalisation $A = \Omega - \hb^{-1}\wedge V/\ell^{2}$, $\ell^{2} = -Q(V) = 3/\Lambda$ (negative for $\Lambda < 0$), of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west}), $K = E\times E$, and $R$ the curvature of the Lorentz part. The five-dimensional Chern-Simons form of $P$, written through its transgression from the Lorentz connection (Facts \claimref{synthesis.imported-five-dimensional-chern-simons-gravity} and \claimref{synthesis.imported-chern-weil-and-chern-simons-forms}(b)), is, modulo exact forms,
\[
L_{5} = 3\int_{0}^{1} P\big(E;\, (R + t^{2}K)\wedge(R + t^{2}K)\big)\,dt = P\big(E;\, 3\,R\wedge R + 2\,R\wedge K + \tfrac35\,K\wedge K\big).
\]
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Reduction; proved.)} On the ansatz $\theta = \theta_{4} + \lambda\,dy\,I$, with $\theta_{4}$ a frame of $W$ on the four-dimensional directions and $R$ valued in $\Lambda^{2}W$, $K_{4} = E_{4}\times E_{4} = \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\,\theta_{4}\wedge\theta_{4}$ and
\[
L_{5} = \frac{3\lambda}{Q(V)}\,\epsilon(I, V, F, F)\wedge dy, \qquad F = R + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\,\theta_{4}\wedge\theta_{4},
\]
the frozen-point MacDowell-Mansouri density of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(iii). The torsion never enters $L_{5}$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The ratio is the Chern-Simons locus; proved.)} The three five-dimensional Lovelock densities $P(E; R\wedge R)$, $P(E; R\wedge K)$, $P(E; K\wedge K)$ reduce to $Q(V)^{-1}\lambda$ times $1$, $3$, $5$ times $\epsilon(I, V, R, R)$, $\epsilon(I, V, R, K_{4})$, $\epsilon(I, V, K_{4}, K_{4})$. Hence $a\,P(E; RR) + b\,P(E; RK) + c\,P(E; KK)$ with $a \neq 0$ reduces to a multiple of a square $\epsilon(I, V, R + sK_{4}, R + sK_{4})$ if and only if $9b^{2} = 20ac$, and then $s = 3b/(2a)$; the solutions with $s = 1$ are exactly the multiples of the Chern-Simons coefficients $(3, 2, \tfrac35)$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Five-dimensional equations; proved.)} The Chern-Simons equations $P(J; F_{5}, F_{5}) = 0$, $J$ a bivector, evaluated on the torsion-free ansatz: for $J$ in $\Lambda^{2}(V^{\perp})$ they vanish identically; for $J = u\wedge V$, $u \in W$, they are the frame equation of the four-dimensional functional (wedged with $dy$), which vanishes on every Einstein field with the matching $\Lambda$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.macdowell-mansouri-principle-fixes-the-trace-free-part}); for $J = I\wedge V$ they are the additional four-form equation
\[
\epsilon(I, V, F, F) = \frac{Q(V)}{3}\,\frac{\partial L_{5}}{\partial\lambda} = 0,
\]
the equation of the scale $\lambda$ of the reduced direction. On an Einstein field with the matching $\Lambda$, $F$ is minus the Weyl map in the store's sign, $F = -\mathcal{W}$ (the Lorentz block of the tractor field strength, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}(iv)); at a point of Schwarzschild-de Sitter, $F(B) = W(B) = m(B + 3\sigma B\sigma)$ with $\sigma = e_{1}e_{0}$ and $m = -M/(2r^{3})$ (so $\mathcal{W}(\sigma) = +\tfrac{2M}{r^{3}}\sigma$), its value is $48m^{2} = \tfrac14 C_{abcd}C^{abcd} = 12M^{2}/r^{6} \neq 0$ for either sign of $\Lambda$ (in this orientation; the general identity $\epsilon(I, V, F, F) = \tfrac14 C_{abcd}C^{abcd}$ times the volume form on the tractor field strength of a torsion-free field is Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-integrand-on-tractor-transport-is-weyl-squared}(iii), in the same orientation), while for a type N Weyl field (plane waves) it is $0$. So the frozen-point functional is the consistent reduction of the five-dimensional one only with $\lambda$ held fixed; with $\lambda$ varied the black holes are not solutions. The same scalar equation is the equation of a released Stelle-West norm in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.stelle-west-norm-is-no-local-output}(iv): in both the Lagrangian is of degree one in the scale.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Signature of the parent; proved.)} The five-dimensional frame space $V^{\perp} = W \oplus \langle I\rangle$ has signature $(2,3)$ for $\Lambda > 0$ ($I$ timelike) and $(1,4)$ for $\Lambda < 0$. So within $\Cl(2,4)$ the de Sitter functional is the reduction of a parent on a $(2,3)$ base along a timelike direction, and the anti-de Sitter functional that of the ordinary anti-de Sitter Chern-Simons gravity along a spacelike one. A Lorentzian parent with a spacelike reduced direction for $\Lambda > 0$ is the Chern-Simons gravity of $SO(1,5)$, in $\Cl(1,5)$, the second repair of Theorem \claimref{rule2.rule-2-kaluza-klein-algebra}(iv).
\item[(v)] \emph{(Coupling; argued.)} With the Chern-Simons coefficient $k$ (a level, quantised for a compact form of the group; the quantisation for $SU(2,2)$ is not standard) the four-dimensional coefficient is $k$ times the integral of $\lambda\,dy$ times a fixed number, so $N^{2} = 3/(G\Lambda)$ is $k$ times the length of the reduced direction in units of the de Sitter radius, times a fixed number: the level does not fix Newton's constant, and the relation is a re-expression of $N$, not a prediction.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.macdowell-mansouri-is-the-froz.technical:
The open problem asks whether the frozen-point MacDowell-Mansouri functional $Q(I)^{-1}\int\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$ can be obtained from the series' objects. This result tests one outside route: five-dimensional Chern-Simons gravity, whose action is a functional of the $\Cl(2,4)$ connection alone (the Chern-Simons form of the cubic Pfaffian invariant, Chamseddine's, an imported Fact), so in five dimensions no reduction datum is needed.

Written through its transgression from the Lorentz connection, the five-dimensional form is $P(E; 3RR + 2RK + \tfrac35 KK)$, with $E$ the frame part and $K = \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\theta\wedge\theta$. Taking the frozen point as the fifth frame direction, $\theta = \theta_{4} + \lambda\,dy\,I$, it reduces exactly to $(3\lambda/Q(V))\,\epsilon(I, V, F, F)\wedge dy$: the three Lovelock terms come with multiplicities $1$, $3$, $5$, and the Chern-Simons coefficients are exactly the ones that make the result a perfect square. Any other five-dimensional Lovelock combination misses the MacDowell-Mansouri ratio. The multiplicities and the reduction of five-dimensional Chern-Simons gravity to a four-dimensional curvature-squared form are the standard reduction of Lovelock densities along a line (literature, recorded with the imported Fact); what is new here is that the reduced direction is the frozen point and the parent's vector is the Stelle-West vector $V = X - (3/\Lambda)I$, so the reduction lands exactly on the series' frozen-point functional.

Three limits. The five-dimensional equations on the ansatz contain, besides the four-dimensional frame equation, the equation of the scale $\lambda$, which is the MacDowell-Mansouri density itself, the same scalar equation as for a released Stelle-West norm (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.stelle-west-norm-is-no-local-output}); its value on a torsion-free field is a quarter of the Weyl square (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-integrand-on-tractor-transport-is-weyl-squared}), so it is nonzero at every point of Schwarzschild-de Sitter ($12M^{2}/r^{6}$ in the stored orientation), and the reduction is consistent only with that scale held fixed. For $\Lambda > 0$ the frozen point is timelike and the parent base has signature $(2,3)$; a Lorentzian parent needs $\Cl(1,5)$. The level does not fix the coupling (argued); the relation between level, length and $N$ is a re-expression, not a prediction. So the action is relocated, not derived; the form is explained by a gauge symmetry one dimension up; the matter coupling is untouched; and the Euler term comes with the square.
synthesis.macdowell-mansouri-is-the-froz.lay: The series borrows a formula for the action of gravity. This result tries a borrowed route from outside: in five dimensions there is a gravitational action built from the series' six-dimensional connection alone, needing no special direction. Squashing the fifth dimension along the series' frozen point gives back exactly the borrowed four-dimensional formula, and the five-dimensional symmetry explains its particular mix of terms. But the squashing only works if the size of the fifth dimension is held fixed; if it is allowed to vary, black holes stop being solutions. For a positive cosmological constant the parent space would need two time directions, and the route does not fix the strength of gravity.

proofs.main:
\emph{Language.} The proof is in geometric algebra throughout: the values of every form are multivectors of $\Cl(2,4)$, and the forms on the five-dimensional base are multivector fields of a flat five-dimensional background (the $d$-dimensional clause of Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}): $dx^{\mu}$, $dy$ are the background vectors $e^{0}, \dots, e^{4}$, the exterior product of the base parts is their outer product, $d$ is $\nabla \wedge$, and an exact form is a $\nabla \wedge$-derivative. The imported formulas below are read in this language; their content is unchanged.

\emph{Imported input.} Five-dimensional Chern-Simons gravity (Chamseddine 1989 and 1990, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-five-dimensional-chern-simons-gravity}), with the transgression and variation formulas of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-chern-weil-and-chern-simons-forms}(b), (c): for a connection $A$ with values in the bivectors of $\Cl(2,4)$ the Chern-Simons five-form of the cubic invariant $P$ satisfies $d\,\mathrm{CS}_{5}(A) = P(F, F, F)$ and $\delta\,\mathrm{CS}_{5} = 3P(\delta A; F, F)$ up to exact forms, and, with $A = \omega + E$ split by the Stelle-West vector $V$ ($\omega$ in the stabiliser of $V$), the transgression from $\omega$ gives $\mathrm{CS}_{5}(A) - \mathrm{CS}_{5}(\omega) = 3\int_{0}^{1}P(E; F_{t}, F_{t})\,dt$ modulo exact forms, with $F_{t} = R + t\,DE + t^{2}K$. The invariant $P$ needs the vector $V$ exactly once among its six legs, $E$ carries $V$, and $\omega$, $R$ and $K$ do not while $DE$ does; so $\mathrm{CS}_{5}(\omega)$ and every term with $DE$ vanish and $L_{5} = 3\int_{0}^{1}P(E; (R + t^{2}K)^{2})\,dt$. Expanding $(R + t^{2}K)^{2} = R^{2} + 2t^{2}RK + t^{4}K^{2}$ (two-forms commute, and the grade-six part of a product of three bivectors is their outer product, symmetric in them) and integrating, $3\int_{0}^{1}(1, 2t^{2}, t^{4})\,dt = (3, 2, \tfrac35)$; the check computes these three integrals with the series' polynomial routines. In particular torsion does not enter $L_{5}$.

\emph{Orientation and standard input.} The chart is that of the stored check of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}: $\nO = \tfrac12(e_{4} + e_{5})$, $\nInf = e_{4} - e_{5}$, $I_{6} = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}e_{4}e_{5}$, and the base parts of two-forms multiply by the outer product of background vectors (a sum over ordered planes; the background blades multiplied are disjoint, so their outer product is the Grassmann product of the checks, whatever the background signature); the opposite orientation of the null pair flips the sign of every $\epsilon(I, V, \cdot, \cdot)$ value below. The multiplicities $1$, $3$, $5$ in (i) and the passage from five-dimensional Chern-Simons gravity to a four-dimensional curvature-squared density are the standard reduction of Lovelock densities along a line (the note of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-five-dimensional-chern-simons-gravity}); the content specific to the series is the choice of the frozen point as the reduced direction and of the Stelle-West vector as the parent's vector.

\emph{The translational square.} For $u, w \in V^{\perp}$, $(u\wedge V)\times(w\wedge V) = -Q(V)\,u\wedge w$ (commutator product; the term in $\ip{u}{w}$ cancels). With $E = \theta\wedge V/Q(V)$ this gives $K = E\times E = -Q(V)^{-1}\theta\wedge\theta = \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\theta\wedge\theta$, the shift of the Lorentz block in Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west} and Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(ii); the check confirms $K_{4} = \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\theta_{4}\wedge\theta_{4}$ on samples, with $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$ and $\ip{I}{V} = 0$.

\emph{(i)} On the ansatz, $E = E_{4} + \lambda\,dy\,(I\wedge V)/Q(V)$ and $K = K_{4} + K_{\times}$, where $K_{\times} = \lambda\sum_{\mu}(E_{4,\mu}\times(I\wedge V)/Q(V))\,dx^{\mu}\wedge dy$ is linear in $dy$ and carries $I$ once. The top form of $L_{5}$ contains $dy$ exactly once, and its value needs $I$ and $V$ exactly once each, so the surviving terms are: $dy$ from $E$, with $R$ and $K_{4}$ in the other slots; or $dy$ from one factor $K_{\times}$, with $E_{4}$ in the first slot. By multilinearity and the reordering of the four vector legs $\theta_{\mu}, V, \theta_{\nu}, I$ (the form sign and the Clifford sign compensate) the second kind reproduces the first with multiplicity $2$ per occurrence of $K$: $P(E; RR)$, $P(E; RK)$, $P(E; KK)$ reduce to $(\lambda/Q(V))$ times $\epsilon(I, V, R, R)$, $3\,\epsilon(I, V, R, K_{4})$, $5\,\epsilon(I, V, K_{4}, K_{4})$, wedged with $dy$. With the coefficients $(3, 2, \tfrac35)$ the sum is $(3\lambda/Q(V))\big(\epsilon(I, V, R, R) + 2\epsilon(I, V, R, K_{4}) + \epsilon(I, V, K_{4}, K_{4})\big) = (3\lambda/Q(V))\,\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$, with $F = R + K_{4}$. The check verifies the multiplicities and the identity exactly on pseudo-random rational frames and curvatures at $\Lambda \in \{3, -\tfrac32, 12\}$ and $\lambda \in \{1, \tfrac23\}$, with all three pieces nonzero.

\emph{(ii)} By (i), $aP(E; RR) + bP(E; RK) + cP(E; KK)$ reduces to $(\lambda/Q(V))(a\,r + 3b\,k + 5c\,q)$ with $r, k, q$ the three four-dimensional densities. This is $a$ times $\epsilon(I, V, R + sK_{4}, R + sK_{4}) = r + 2s\,k + s^{2}q$ exactly when $3b = 2as$ and $5c = as^{2}$, that is $s = 3b/(2a)$ and $9b^{2} = 20ac$. At $s = 1$ (the Lorentz block of the frozen-point functional) $(a, b, c) = a(1, \tfrac23, \tfrac15)$, a multiple of $(3, 2, \tfrac35)$. Other five-dimensional Lovelock combinations (for example Einstein-Hilbert with volume, $a = 0$) do not reduce to the square.

\emph{(iii)} By the imported variation formula the equations are $P(J; F_{5}, F_{5}) = 0$ for every bivector $J$. On the torsion-free ansatz $F_{5} = R + K_{4} + K_{\times}$ has no leg along $V$, so for $J \in \Lambda^{2}(V^{\perp})$ the six legs cannot contain $V$ and the equation is empty. For $J = u\wedge V$ with $u \in W$, the legs must contain $I$ once, which only $K_{\times}$ supplies: the equation is $2P(u\wedge V; F, K_{\times})$, linear in $F$ and in the frame, the frame equation of the four-dimensional functional wedged with $dy$; on an Einstein field with the matching $\Lambda$, $F$ is (minus) the Weyl curvature (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}) and the frame equation vanishes (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.macdowell-mansouri-principle-fixes-the-trace-free-part}). For $J = I\wedge V$, no further $I$ or $V$ may appear, so only $F\wedge F$ contributes and the equation is $\epsilon(I, V, F, F) = 0$; since $L_{5}$ is linear in $\lambda$ by (i), this is $(Q(V)/3)\,\partial L_{5}/\partial\lambda$, and it remains the $\lambda$ equation when $\lambda$ depends on $x$, because $d\lambda\wedge dy$ enters only the translational block, which $L_{5}$ does not contain. The check evaluates all fifteen equations at a point with the frame the identity, for $W(B) = m(B + 3\sigma B\sigma)$, $\sigma = e_{1}e_{0}$ (the Schwarzschild Weyl curvature at radius $r$ along $e_{1}$, $m = -M/(2r^{3})$; trace-free and satisfying the first Bianchi identity, both checked) at $m \in \{1, -\tfrac23\}$ and $\Lambda \in \{3, -\tfrac32\}$: the frame and $V$-free equations vanish, and $\epsilon(I, V, F, F) = 48m^{2}$, a quarter of the Kretschmann invariant $192m^{2} = C_{abcd}C^{abcd}$, so $12M^{2}/r^{6}$, independent of $\Lambda$; this agrees with the general identity $\epsilon(I, V, F, F) = \tfrac14 C_{abcd}C^{abcd}$ times the volume form of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-integrand-on-tractor-transport-is-weyl-squared}(iii) (same orientation), and the scalar equation is the one a released Stelle-West norm obeys (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.stelle-west-norm-is-no-local-output}(iv)), the Lagrangian being of degree one in the scale in both cases. For the type N field $W(B) = \langle BN_{1}\rangle_{0}N_{1} - \langle BN_{2}\rangle_{0}N_{2}$, $N_{i} = (e_{0} + e_{3})\wedge e_{i}$ (also checked Weyl), the value is $0$. On generic sample curvatures the check confirms that the $I\wedge V$ equation equals the four-dimensional density and $(Q(V)/3)\,\partial L_{5}/\partial\lambda$, and that the frame equations are not identically zero. (In components, a labelled reading: $\epsilon(I, V, F, F) \propto \epsilon_{abcd}\epsilon^{efgh}F^{ab}{}_{ef}F^{cd}{}_{gh}$, which for a Weyl tensor is proportional to $C_{abcd}C^{abcd}$ since its double dual is minus itself.)

\emph{(iv)} $V^{\perp}$ is spanned by $e_{0}, \ldots, e_{3}$ and $I$, on which the Gram form is $\mathrm{diag}(1, -1, -1, -1) \oplus (\Lambda/3)$; its signature is $(2,3)$ for $\Lambda > 0$ and $(1,4)$ for $\Lambda < 0$, and $I^{\perp}$ has signature $(1,4)$, $(2,3)$ respectively (computed by congruence at $\Lambda \in \{3, \tfrac34, -3, -\tfrac97\}$). For $\Lambda > 0$ the four-dimensional group is the stabiliser of the reduced direction, $SO(1,4)$, as the frozen-point functional requires, but the five-dimensional frame space contains the timelike $I$. In $\Cl(1,5)$, two orthogonal unit vectors of square $-1$ give a Lorentzian $(1,4)$ frame space and a de Sitter $(1,4)$ complement of the reduced direction (checked). $\Cl(1,5)$ is the repair with $\nu^{2} = -1$ of Theorem \claimref{rule2.rule-2-kaluza-klein-algebra}(iv).

\emph{(v) (Argued.)} If the five-dimensional action is $\kappa_{5}\int L_{5}$, then by (i) the four-dimensional coefficient of $\int\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$ is $3\kappa_{5}Q(V)^{-1}\int\lambda\,dy = -\kappa_{5}\Lambda\int\lambda\,dy$; with the proper length $P = |Q(I)|^{1/2}\int\lambda\,dy$ of the reduced direction this is $\mp 3\kappa_{5}P/\ell$. The four-dimensional coefficient is proportional to $1/(G\Lambda)$, so $N^{2} = 3/(G\Lambda)$ equals a fixed number times $\kappa_{5}P/\ell$. A quantised level fixes $\kappa_{5}$ up to an integer (for a compact form of the group; for $SU(2,2)$ the standard argument does not apply), and $P/\ell$ is free, so the level does not fix the coupling. No value of the level is compared with $N$: the relation re-expresses $N$ through $\kappa_{5}$ and $P/\ell$ and predicts nothing.

synthesis.macdowell-mansouri-principle-f.formal:
Units $c = 1$, signature $(1,3)$ (store), the store's curvature sign (the components $R_{abcd}$ are minus those of the round-sphere-positive Riemann tensor, so that de Sitter space has $\Ric = \Lambda g$ and $F_{abcd} = 0$), read from the field strength of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime with derived metric $g$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}); the Ricci map $\Ric(b) = \partial_{a}\cdot\mathcal{R}(a\wedge b)$ and scalar $\mathcal{R} = \partial_{a}\cdot\Ric(a)$, the Einstein map $\mathcal{G}(a) = \Ric(a) - \tfrac12 a\,\mathcal{R}$, the Schouten map $\Sch(a) = \tfrac12(\Ric(a) - \tfrac{\mathcal{R}}{6}a)$ and $J = \partial_{a}\cdot\Sch(a)$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}; in components $\Ric_{bd} = g^{ac}R_{abcd}$, $\mathcal{R} = g^{bd}\Ric_{bd}$, $\Sch = \tfrac12(\Ric - \tfrac{\mathcal{R}}{6}g)$, $J = g^{ab}\Sch_{ab}$). Let $\Lambda \neq 0$, and let $S_{\mathrm{MM}}$ be the series' MacDowell-Mansouri functional of the de Sitter (anti-de Sitter) connection $A(a) = \Omega(a) - \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\,\hb^{-1}(a)\wedge V$ (that is $\Omega(a) + \hb^{-1}(a)\wedge V/Q(V)$, so that $D_{a}V = \hb^{-1}(a)$ on both branches) (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west}), in the frozen-point presentation $S \sim Q(I)^{-1}\int\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$ of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(iii), whose field space is the whole pair $(\hb, \Omega)$ with $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ and $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$ fixed. Its Lorentz block is the operator $F(B) = \mathcal{R}(B) - \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}B$ on bivectors (in components $F_{abcd} = R_{abcd} - \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}(g_{ac}g_{bd} - g_{ad}g_{bc})$), as in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.series-wald-entropy-changes-without-flux-on-local-horizons}. At a point, with an orthonormal frame $e_{a}$ of $g$, reciprocal frame $e^{a}$, pseudoscalar $I = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}$, $\epsilon_{abcd}$ defined by $e_{a}\wedge e_{b}\wedge e_{c}\wedge e_{d} = \epsilon_{abcd}\,I$ and $F^{cd} = \tfrac12 F^{cd}{}_{ef}\,e^{e}\wedge e^{f}$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The frame equation; proved.)} The variation of $S_{\mathrm{MM}}$ with respect to the frame $\hb^{-1}$ is the trivector-valued linear function $E(a) = 2\big(\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a\big)I$. In components (a labelled reading), the three-form of the Fact's second Euler-Lagrange equation is
\[
E_{a} := \epsilon_{abcd}\,e^{b}\wedge F^{cd} = 2\,\big(\mathcal{G}(e_{a}) + \Lambda e_{a}\big)\,I .
\]
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Ten conditions; proved.)} As a linear map on the twenty-dimensional space of algebraic curvature tensors at a point, $R \mapsto (E_{a})$ has rank $10$ and kernel exactly the Weyl tensors: it is injective on the Ricci part, and the nine trace-free components of $\Ric$ enter as nine independent conditions. In particular a vacuum stationary point has $\Ric = \Lambda g$: the trace-free part vanishes.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Restricted to dilations: the one equation of the scale-only no-go; proved.)} If the frame is varied only by pure dilations, $\delta\hb^{-1}(a) = \delta w\,\hb^{-1}(a)$ at fixed conformal class, the frame equation is contracted with the frame: $e^{a}\wedge E_{a} = 2(4\Lambda - \mathcal{R})\,I$, a map of rank $1$ on the curvature, the single trace equation $\mathcal{R} = 4\Lambda$ (the Yamabe equation of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-structure-and-natural-scale-actions-do-not-select-the-almost-einstein-scale}(ii)). The one equation of every scale-only principle and the ten of this one come from the same functional; the nine trace-free conditions are supplied exactly by varying the conformal class.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(With matter; the algebra proved, the coupling standard.)} Add a matter functional $S_{m}[\hb, \psi]$ whose frame variation defines $T$, with $S_{\mathrm{MM}}$ normalised so that the frame equation reads $\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a + 8\pi G\,T(a) = 0$ ($G$ the normalisation constant of the functional, a free constant, as $1/(4\eta)$ is on the Clausius route). This is exactly clause (7) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-condition-is-infinity-vacuum-incidence}, $\Ric + 8\pi G\,T = (\Lambda + 4\pi G\,\tau)\,g$, $\tau = g^{ab}T_{ab}$. On shell
\[
\Sch = \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\,g - 4\pi G\,\big(T - \tfrac{\tau}{3}\,g\big), \qquad \Sch^{\circ} = -4\pi G\,T^{\circ}, \qquad \Lambda = 6\cdot\tfrac{J}{4} - 2\pi G\,\tau ,
\]
which is the content of $\nabla_{a}I' = 4\pi G\,(0, T^{\circ}_{ab}, \tfrac{1}{12}\nabla_{a}\tau)$ with $\rho_{I'} = J/4$ in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.infinity-vacuum-incidence-is-a-property-of-the-scale}(4). In vacuum $\Sch = \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}g$, the Schouten slot of the Stelle-West Cartan connection, so the scale tractor $I'$ is parallel: the own-ray incidence of the infinity vacua (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-condition-is-infinity-vacuum-incidence}) is the vacuum case of the field equations of $S_{\mathrm{MM}} + S_{m}$, and with matter the stored derivative of the scale tractor is a law, because $T$ is given by $S_{m}$ independently of the vacuum field.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} $S_{\mathrm{MM}}$ is a dynamical principle for the whole gauge field, not for the scale within a fixed conformal class: its field space is every pair $(\hb, \Omega)$, its field equations are second-order equations with an independently given source, and its zero set is not the parallel-tractor condition, so it is not a rewording of that condition. It is imported (MacDowell-Mansouri, Stelle-West), and the series supplies only its frozen-point presentation, in which the frozen point enters as the constant prefactor $1/Q(I) = 3/\Lambda$; adopting it is adopting Einstein's equations as a variational premise. So it answers the question of a principle for the whole gauge field only given that imported action principle: transport-absent, and a principle derived from the series' objects, from which the incidence would follow rather than being assumed in variational form, remains open. The Stelle-West field $V$ here is a variable of the action ($Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$, $\ip{V}{I} = 0$), not a selected point. Compared with the Clausius route of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}, the two principles give the same field equations (the Euler term of $S_{\mathrm{MM}}$ is topological in four dimensions), with $\Lambda$ a parameter of the functional here and an integration constant there, and they differ in the entropy: the Wald entropy of $S_{\mathrm{MM}}$ on a local edge carries the Euler density $-\tfrac{3}{4\Lambda}$ times the Cartan curvature of the edge plane, which the clause (Loc) excludes (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.series-wald-entropy-changes-without-flux-on-local-horizons}). The statements hold for $\Lambda \neq 0$; at $\Lambda = 0$ the curvature-squared presentation has a pole and the functional is the Einstein-Cartan limit of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}, with the same frame equation at $\Lambda = 0$. With spinning matter the torsion equation of the Fact is sourced by the spin density and its contact term enters $T$; the trace-free count of (ii) is unchanged.
synthesis.macdowell-mansouri-principle-f.technical:
The open problem asks for a principle of the series for the whole gravitational gauge field, not for the scale inside a fixed conformal class, whose field equations fix the trace-free part of the curvature, so that the Einstein condition (the own-ray incidence of the infinity vacua, equivalently a parallel scale tractor) follows rather than being restated. Given an imported action principle, the store already contains one, in the dark-energy part of the series: the MacDowell-Mansouri functional (MacDowell-Mansouri, Stelle-West), the square of the de Sitter curvature seen from the frozen point, with the Stelle-West vector built from the frozen point and the canonical tractor. It varies $\hb$ and $\Omega$ together.

The frame variation of that functional, as a three-form, is exactly twice the dual of $\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a$. As a linear map of the curvature at a point it has rank ten and kernel the Weyl tensors, so it imposes the nine trace-free conditions and the trace. Restricting the variation to pure dilations of the frame contracts it with the frame and leaves only the trace, the Yamabe equation: the stored no-go for scale-only principles is this same functional with the conformal class frozen, and the missing nine conditions are exactly what varying the class supplies. With a matter functional the field equations are the store's clause (7), and on shell the Schouten tensor is $\tfrac{\Lambda}{6}g - 4\pi G(T - \tfrac{\tau}{3}g)$, which is the stored formula for the derivative of the scale tractor; in vacuum it is the Schouten slot of the Stelle-West connection, so the scale tractor is parallel. The principle is imported, with the standard Einstein-Cartan matter coupling, and transport-absent: adopting it adopts Einstein's equations as a variational premise, so a principle derived from the series' objects remains open. It agrees with the Clausius route on the field equations and disagrees on the entropy, since its Wald entropy carries the Euler term that (Loc) excludes. The algebra is checked exactly in $\Cl(1,3)$ on fixed rational curvature tensors and on a spanning set of the curvature space.
synthesis.macdowell-mansouri-principle-f.lay: Einstein's equations say how matter bends spacetime, and ten numbers per point must match. Earlier work showed that any rule which only adjusts the overall size of rulers, keeping the light cones fixed, yields just one of the ten. This result points out that the series already holds, borrowed from the literature, a rule that adjusts everything: the MacDowell-Mansouri action, which the series writes as the square of the curvature seen from its frozen point. Varying it gives all ten equations, with matter entering as an independent source, and when matter is absent it reproduces exactly the series' geometric statement of Einstein's condition. Freezing the light cones in this same action leaves only the one equation found before. The action is taken from the literature rather than derived from the series' transport, and it disagrees with the series' entropy premise about one geometric term in horizon entropy.

proofs.main:
Everything is computed in Gauge Theory Gravity (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}): the curvature is the store-sign operator $\mathcal{R}(B) = -R(\hb(B))$ on physical bivectors, with Ricci map $\mathcal{R}(a) = \partial_{b}\cdot\mathcal{R}(b\wedge a)$, scalar $\mathcal{R} = \partial_{a}\cdot\mathcal{R}(a)$, Einstein map $\mathcal{G}(a) = \mathcal{R}(a) - \tfrac12 a\mathcal{R}$, and Schouten map $\Sch(a) = \tfrac12(\mathcal{R}(a) - \tfrac{\mathcal{R}}{6}a)$; $I$ is the pseudoscalar of the physical frame, $I^{2} = -1$.

\emph{(i)} The Lorentz block of the field strength of the Fact is, as an operator, $F(B) = \mathcal{R}(B) - \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}B$ up to its overall sign ($-\mathcal{F}$ of the dictionary, row 13; it vanishes for the de Sitter field). The Fact's second Euler-Lagrange equation is the frame variation, a trivector-valued linear function of the frame direction $a$:
\[
E(a) \;=\; 2\,\partial_{b}\wedge F\bigl(I(a\wedge b)\bigr),
\]
whose component form is the three-form $\epsilon_{abcd}\,e^{b}\wedge F^{cd}$ with $e^{b}\wedge e^{e}\wedge e^{f}$ read as the trivector $e^{b}\wedge e^{e}\wedge e^{f}$ and $\epsilon_{abcd}$ from $e_{a}\wedge e_{b}\wedge e_{c}\wedge e_{d} = \epsilon_{abcd}I$ (the check computes both on three rational curvature operators at $\Lambda \in \{0, \tfrac37, -2\}$ and finds them equal). Two GA identities evaluate it. For the identity operator, $\partial_{b}\wedge(I(a\wedge b)) = -3\,aI$ (in four dimensions the dual of the bivectors through $a$, wedged back with the frame, returns three copies of the dual of $a$). For every curvature operator,
\[
\partial_{b}\wedge\mathcal{R}\bigl(I(a\wedge b)\bigr) \;=\; \mathcal{G}(a)\,I .
\]
Both sides are linear in $\mathcal{R}$, so it suffices to check it on the two parts of $\mathcal{R} = \mathcal{W} + \Sch\wedge\mathrm{id}$, where $(\Sch\wedge\mathrm{id})(a\wedge b) = \Sch(a)\wedge b + a\wedge\Sch(b)$. On the Weyl part the duality $\mathcal{W}(IB) = I\mathcal{W}(B)$ (dictionary row 5) gives $\partial_{b}\wedge\mathcal{W}(I(a\wedge b)) = \partial_{b}\wedge(I\,\mathcal{W}(a\wedge b))$, which is $I$ times the contraction $\partial_{b}\cdot\mathcal{W}(a\wedge b)$ up to sign, zero because $\mathcal{W}$ is trace-free, while its Einstein map is zero. On the Kulkarni-Nomizu part both sides are linear in the symmetric map $\Sch$, and the check verifies the identity on the ten basis symmetric maps, which span. Hence
\[
E(a) = 2\,\mathcal{G}(a)I - \tfrac{2\Lambda}{3}(-3\,aI) = 2\bigl(\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a\bigr)I .
\]
For the de Sitter field ($\mathcal{R}(B) = \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}B$) $F = 0$ and $E = 0$, and $E \neq 0$ at a wrong $\Lambda$; the check confirms this on the de Sitter gauge field in the flat slicing, the Weyl duality and $\partial_{b}\wedge\mathcal{W}(I(a\wedge b)) = 0$ on the Weyl operators of three gauge fields (Schwarzschild, a Kasner vacuum, a non-vacuum synchronous field), and $\partial_{b}\wedge(I(a\wedge b)) = -3aI$.

\emph{(ii)} By (i), $\mathcal{R} \mapsto E$ factors through the Einstein map, which vanishes on the Weyl part and is injective on the Ricci part (in four dimensions $\mathcal{G}$ determines $\mathcal{R}(a) = \mathcal{G}(a) - \tfrac12 a\,\partial_{b}\cdot\mathcal{G}(b)$, and the Ricci part $\Sch\wedge\mathrm{id}$ is determined by the Ricci map). The algebraic curvature operators form a twenty-dimensional space, the Weyl operators ten of it and the Ricci part ten; so the map has rank $10$ and kernel exactly the Weyl operators, and the nine trace-free components of the Ricci map enter as nine independent conditions. The GTG check finds rank $10$ on the images of the ten Kulkarni-Nomizu operators; the earlier check computes the rank on a spanning set of the twenty-dimensional space in components. A vacuum stationary point has $\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a = 0$, that is $\mathcal{R}(a) = \Lambda a$.

\emph{(iii)} A pure dilation $\delta\hb^{-1}(a) = \delta w\,\hb^{-1}(a)$ (the conformal class fixed) changes the functional by $\int\delta w\,\partial_{a}\wedge E(a)$, so the restricted Euler-Lagrange equation is the pseudoscalar $\partial_{a}\wedge E(a)$. In four dimensions $a\wedge(vI) = (a\cdot v)I$ for vectors, so $\partial_{a}\wedge E(a) = 2\,\partial_{a}\cdot(\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a)\,I = 2(4\Lambda - \mathcal{R})I$, the trace of $\mathcal{G}$ being $-\mathcal{R}$. The GTG check confirms this on the FLRW and Schwarzschild gauge fields at $\Lambda = 0, \tfrac53$, and the earlier check that the map has rank $1$ on the curvature. This is the trace $\mathcal{R} = 4\Lambda$, the single Euler-Lagrange equation of the Einstein-Hilbert action restricted to a conformal class in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-structure-and-natural-scale-actions-do-not-select-the-almost-einstein-scale}(ii) (the Einstein-Cartan term of $S_{\mathrm{MM}}$ is that action and the Euler term is topological).

\emph{(iv)} The coupling to matter is the standard one for the Einstein-Cartan functional: the frame variation of $S_{m}$ is the energy-momentum three-form, and with the normalisation stated the frame equation becomes $\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a + 8\pi G\,T(a) = 0$, $T$ a symmetric linear map on physical vectors (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-einstein-cartan-matter-coupling}(a): Kibble 1961, Sciama 1964, Hehl, von der Heyde, Kerlick and Nester 1976; in Gauge Theory Gravity Lasenby, Doran and Gull 1998; the sign is the store's, matching clause (7)). The rest is algebra, checked exactly with $k = 8\pi G$ as a rational symbol on fixed rational $T$ and several $(\Lambda, k)$: given $T$, define $\Ric$ by clause (7); then $\mathcal{G} + \Lambda g + kT = 0$ identically, and conversely, since the map $\Ric \mapsto \mathcal{G}$ is invertible in four dimensions. From clause (7), $\mathcal{R} = 4\Lambda + 8\pi G\,\tau$ and, with the Schouten tensor of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}, $\Sch = \tfrac12(\Ric - \tfrac{\mathcal{R}}{6}g) = \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}g - 4\pi G(T - \tfrac{\tau}{3}g)$; its trace-free part is $-4\pi G\,T^{\circ}$ and $J = \tfrac{\mathcal{R}}{6}$ gives $6\cdot\tfrac{J}{4} - 2\pi G\,\tau = \Lambda$. These are the middle slot $-\Sch^{\circ}$ and the relation $\Lambda = 6\rho_{I'} - 2\pi G\,\tau$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.infinity-vacuum-incidence-is-a-property-of-the-scale}(4), whose $\nabla_{a}I' = (0, -\Sch^{\circ}_{ab}, \tfrac14\nabla_{a}J)$ then equals $4\pi G(0, T^{\circ}_{ab}, \tfrac{1}{12}\nabla_{a}\tau)$. In vacuum $\Sch = \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}g$ exactly (checked), so $\Sch^{\circ} = 0$ and $J$ is constant, and by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.infinity-vacuum-incidence-is-a-property-of-the-scale}(3) the scale tractor is parallel, which is the own-ray incidence of the infinity vacua of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-condition-is-infinity-vacuum-incidence}. The value $\tfrac{\Lambda}{6}g$ is the Schouten slot of the Cartan connection $\Omega(a) - \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\,\hb^{-1}(a)\wedge V$, whose Lorentz curvature block vanishes exactly on the de Sitter field (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(ii)).

\emph{Reading.} The field space of $S_{\mathrm{MM}}$ is the pair $(\hb, \Omega)$ (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west}); in the frozen-point form the constraints $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, $\ip{V}{I} = 0$, $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$ fix $\Lambda$ and do not restrict $(\hb, \Omega)$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(iii)). The functional is not a Lagrange-multiplier or nonnegative-functional rewording of the parallel-tractor condition: its Euler-Lagrange equations are (i) to (iv), and the matter law has $T$ from $S_{m}$. The comparison with the Clausius route uses Theorem \claimref{synthesis.series-wald-entropy-changes-without-flux-on-local-horizons}: on a local edge the Jacobson-Myers density of the series' action is $-\tfrac{3}{4\Lambda}$ times the Cartan curvature of the edge plane, curvature-dependent, while (Loc) asks for a curvature-independent density with no Euler term; so (Loc) is not the Wald entropy of $S_{\mathrm{MM}}$, though both routes give the same field equations. Literature from memory: MacDowell and Mansouri 1977 and Stelle and West 1980 as in the Fact; the Einstein-Cartan coupling is the imported Fact cited in (iv); the Yamabe reading as in the stored no-go.

\emph{In components} (a labelled reading). With $F^{cd} = \tfrac12 F^{cd}{}_{ef}\,e^{e}\wedge e^{f}$ and $F_{abcd} = R_{abcd} - \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}(g_{ac}g_{bd} - g_{ad}g_{bc})$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.series-wald-entropy-changes-without-flux-on-local-horizons}), the frame equation is $E_{a} = \tfrac12\epsilon_{abcd}F^{cd}{}_{ef}\,e^{b}\wedge e^{e}\wedge e^{f}$; the contraction of $\epsilon$ with the curvature is the one that gives the Einstein tensor, $E_{a} = 2(\mathcal{G}_{a}{}^{h} + \Lambda\delta_{a}^{h})e_{h}I$. The earlier checks evaluate this on rational curvature tensors (sums of Kulkarni-Nomizu products of rational symmetric matrices), on all fifty-five Kulkarni-Nomizu products of the ten basis symmetric matrices (a spanning set of rank $20$), and the ranks $10$, $9$ (trace-free) and $1$ (dilations), and the matter algebra of (iv) with $k = 8\pi G$ as a rational symbol.

synthesis.parallel-frozen-point-on-matte.lay: The series has a fixed reference direction, the frozen point, whose length is the cosmological constant. It is known to stay fixed in empty space. The prediction that dark energy never changes asks for it to stay fixed where there is matter too, and the gravitational action gives Einstein's equations only if it is allowed to vary just those fields that keep the frozen point fixed. This result shows that, measured in the actual spacetime's own scale, the frozen point stays fixed in the presence of matter only for the connection that the action's field space prescribes; the series' own transport rule differs from it by exactly the matter present. So choosing that field space secures the prediction's condition. The reverse holds only if the condition is taken to say which connection carries the frozen point; taken only as a statement about solutions, it is weaker. It also shows that with this field space the cosmological constant is simply a fixed number, so "dark energy never changes" is the same as the standard cosmological model's assumption and is not separate evidence for the frozen point. Neither question is answered here.

synthesis.positive-structure-and-natural.technical:
The open problem asks for a principle of the series that selects the scale within the conformal class, so that the infinity vacua's incidence, and with matter the field equations, follow rather than being restated. It proposed two lines: the sesquilinear (non-conformally invariant) structure, where the rung unit is seen, and a variational principle for the scale tractor. The first is blocked by an exact symmetry argument, and the two natural forms of the second by exact counter-models; the general variational case is only argued.

The positive structure is invariant under the centraliser of the conformal energy $Z$: a circle times the rotations of the four negative directions. That group fixes no tractor. Its circle fixes exactly the tractors of negative cosmological constant, the wrong sign, and no null (flat) tractor is fixed by either factor. So the structure can at most fix two numbers of a tractor, the norms of its two projections, and with them $\Lambda$; it cannot fix the scale tractor itself, which also carries a position and a direction.

A variational principle in the scale alone, with the conformal class held fixed, has one Euler-Lagrange equation. The Einstein-Hilbert action restricted to a conformal class gives the trace of the field equations and nothing else, the Yamabe equation; its stationary scales include harmonic conformal factors such as $1 + x_{1}x_{2}$, whose metric has zero scalar curvature and nonzero trace-free Ricci tensor. The tractor Dirichlet functional gives the biharmonic equation, again with $1 + x_{1}x_{2}$ stationary; and in Lorentzian signature the scale $(t + x_{1})^{2}$, whose trace-free Hessian is a null square, has zero action density without being parallel. The trace-free part of the field equations, nine conditions, is what a selecting principle must supply. These two functionals do not supply it, and a count (argued, by Cauchy-Kovalevskaya) says that no local functional of one scalar with a somewhere noncharacteristic Euler-Lagrange equation does; everywhere-characteristic equations and nonvariational principles are not treated. What remains is a principle that varies the whole gauge field $\hb$, on the series' route the Clausius relation with the local-horizon premise, or a Lagrange-multiplier restatement, which the problem excludes. The computations are exact in $\Cl(2,4)$ (commutant ranks, the Cayley rotation, tabulated scales) and in rational arithmetic (Ricci from the Christoffel symbols of $\varphi^{2}\eta$ at rational points, polynomial Euler-Lagrange operators).
synthesis.positive-structure-and-natural.lay: In the series, the step from quantum data to Einstein's equations stops at one choice: of all the ways to put a ruler on spacetime that agree about light rays, which one is the physical one. This result tests two natural ways of making that choice from inside the series and shows that neither works in the forms tested. The series' notion of positive probability has a symmetry, and that symmetry moves every possible ruler, so it cannot pick one out; at most it could pick the size of the cosmological constant. And the natural actions built from the ruler alone give only one equation, while Einstein's equations need ten; simple examples satisfy the one equation and are not solutions of Einstein's. A counting argument suggests the same for any such action, though it is not proved for every kind. The missing nine must come from something that moves the light cones as well, which is gravity's own dynamics.
