synthesis.r-loc-independent-sets-matter-.formal:
Units with $\hbar$ and the speed of light equal to one, signature $(1,3)$; write $\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}$ as in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}. Read the premises on finite windows as in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boundary-mode-premises-finite-models}, and the local-horizon premise (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) as its two clauses (Loc) and (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$), with the modes of a local horizon's patch labelled by its generating null direction. Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}). For $c > 0$ let (R$_{c}$) be (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) with the rapidity period $2\pi$ replaced by $2\pi c$ for the local horizons through points of a region $U$, open in the invertible region, that meets no Killing horizon locus.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Model.)} Keep every Killing-horizon structure of the store as it is (the windows, (P), (R), (L$_E$), (I), (Q), (R$_{\Lambda}$), the counting premises and the identification of horizon and cutoff modes), and give the modes of each local horizon through a point of $U$ the gauge-invariant quasi-free state with occupations $e^{-2\pi c w}/(1 + e^{-2\pi c w})$ at rapidity weight $w$. This state is even, stationary under the boost and under every number-diagonal generator, KMS at rapidity period $2\pi c$, and for $c \ne 1$ it is not KMS at $2\pi$ at any nonzero weight. No premise of the store other than (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) constrains the state of local-horizon modes at points of $U$, so the model satisfies every other present premise and (Loc), and violates (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) exactly when $c \neq 1$. Hence (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$), with the labelling above, is independent of the present premises, (Loc) included. The region $U$ must be nonempty: for the exact de Sitter field every local Rindler horizon is, at leading order, a patch of some observer's cosmological horizon, so if (R$_{\Lambda}$) is read for every observer there is no such $U$; generic gravitational fields, and the exterior and interior of a hole away from its horizon, supply one.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Clausius at the local temperature.)} Under (R$_{c}$), $T_{\chi} = \kappa/(2\pi c)$ in the time of the approximate boost field $\chi$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.local-boost-temperature-is-local-regularity}, with the period rescaled), and on a thin pencil about the generator through $p$
\[
\delta Q - T_{\chi}\,\eta\,\delta A \;=\; \frac{\kappa}{2}\Big(T(k,k) - \frac{\eta}{2\pi c}\,\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}(k,k)\Big)\Big|_{p}\,\lambda_{0}^{2} + O(\lambda_{0}^{3}).
\]
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Field equations.)} With (Loc), the Clausius hypothesis (H1) at the temperature of (ii), and (H2) to (H4) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}, the gravitational field on $U$ satisfies Einstein's equations, $\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a = -8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}\,T(a)$ in the store's sign, with $\Lambda$ an integration constant and
\[
G_{\mathrm{cl}} \;=\; \frac{c}{4\eta}.
\]
If the period $2\pi c$ is used also for the local horizons through points of a Killing horizon locus other than the one generated by the Killing generator, the null-null equation along that generator reads $0 = 0$ for every $c$, so the jump of the period at Killing patches obstructs nothing.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(What the clause adds.)} The density of (Loc) is calibrated on the Schwarzschild family with the Killing temperature of (R), $\eta = \tfrac14$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-entropy-clause-curvature-independent-density}(ii), through Theorem \claimref{synthesis.quarter-from-temperature}), which (R$_{c}$) leaves unchanged. Then $G_{\mathrm{cl}} = cG$: the coupling of matter in the field equations equals the $G$ of black-hole thermodynamics exactly when the local period equals the Killing period, $c = 1$. The field-equation route determines only $\eta/c$, the entropy density per unit of local temperature normalisation.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.r-loc-independent-sets-matter-.technical:
The temperature clause of the local-horizon premise asks the modes of every small horizon to be thermal at rapidity period $2\pi$. To see whether the rest of the store already implies it, take a model that keeps everything the store says about Killing horizons (black-hole and de Sitter horizons, their windows and their states) and changes only the local horizons through a region that meets no Killing horizon, where the modes are put in the thermal state at period $2\pi c$. With the modes labelled by null direction, the labelling under which the clause is consistent at nonzero weight, this state is even and stationary, and it is thermal at $2\pi$ only if $c = 1$. A survey of the store's postulates finds that only the local-horizon premise speaks about the state of local-horizon modes, so every other premise holds in the model: the entropy clause (Loc) because its present version does not tie the entropy to the state of the modes, and Indifference in its declared, scoped reading. The temperature clause is therefore independent of the present premises. The region where the period is changed must exist: for the exact de Sitter field every local horizon is a patch of some observer's cosmological horizon, so if (R$_{\Lambda}$) is read for every observer there is none, but generic gravitational fields and black-hole exteriors and interiors away from the horizon supply it. Independence is relative to the present premise set: the positive-null-energy premise filed alongside (synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises) would fix the period at $2\pi$ and so imply the clause.

The model is not idle. Rerunning Jacobson's argument at the temperature $\kappa/(2\pi c)$ changes only one coefficient of the leading-order Clausius defect, and polarisation over all null directions still gives a field equation for the gravitational field on flat spacetime, now with $G_{\mathrm{cl}} = c/(4\eta)$. The density $\eta = \tfrac14$ is calibrated with the Killing temperature, which the model keeps, so $G_{\mathrm{cl}} = cG$. Read the other way, the temperature clause, beyond what (R) and (R$_{\Lambda}$) say at Killing horizons, is the statement that matter gravitates with the same $G$ that appears in the area law; the field equations alone measure only the ratio of the entropy density to the local temperature normalisation. At a Killing horizon the clause is not new: its generator has vanishing null-null Ricci and stress components, so the jump of the period there costs nothing.
synthesis.r-loc-independent-sets-matter-.lay: The series needs two assumptions about tiny horizons to derive Einstein's equations: their entropy grows with area at a fixed rate, and they are warm at a definite temperature. This result shows the temperature assumption is extra, given the series' present assumptions: one can keep everything else the series says, including everything about black holes and the cosmological horizon, and give the tiny horizons, with their modes labelled by the light-like direction they belong to, a different temperature, and nothing breaks. What changes is the strength of gravity felt by ordinary matter. If tiny horizons were half as warm as assumed, matter would gravitate twice as strongly as the black-hole formulas say. So the temperature assumption is what ties the gravity of everyday matter to the gravity that appears in black-hole entropy.

proofs.main:
Read in Gauge Theory Gravity, the geometric steps below (Ricci curvature, the local boost field, the field equations) are those of the gravitational field on flat spacetime through its derived metric and field strength (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}, clauses (iv) and (vi)). \emph{(i)} Let $\mathfrak{A}_{F}$ be a window of the modes of a local horizon through a point of $U$, with the boost acting by $a_{j} \mapsto e^{-Jsw_{j}}a_{j}$ in rapidity $s$ ($J = e_{2}e_{3}$ the complex unit of the boundary modes, numbers on the window read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$, \claimref{synthesis.transverse-bivector-is-the-complex-unit-of-the-radial-atom}), and let $\varrho_{c} = \bigotimes_{j}\operatorname{diag}(1, e^{-2\pi cw_{j}})/(1 + e^{-2\pi cw_{j}})$ in the occupation basis. It is diagonal in the number basis, so it commutes with every number-diagonal generator and with the parity operator (even, stationary, compatible with (L$_E$)); it is the Gibbs state of $2\pi c\sum_{j}w_{j}N_{j}$, hence KMS at rapidity period $2\pi c$ and quasi-free with diagonal symbol. A single mode is KMS at period $2\pi$ only with $n/(1 - n) = e^{-2\pi w}$; the model has $n/(1 - n) = e^{-2\pi cw}$, so for $c \neq 1$ every mode with $w \neq 0$ violates (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$). The check verifies this with $u = e^{-2\pi}$ as an exact rational-function symbol at weights $1, 2, 3$ and $c = 2$, and that the array weights $-1, 0, 1$ keep the period-$2\pi$ state on a Killing window.

The labels by null direction are used so that the local-horizon clause and its variant are satisfiable at nonzero weight at all: on modes shared by the two sheets of an edge the variant fails for the same reason as the clause (a state KMS at $2\pi c$ for a flow and for its inverse is the trace), and the result filed alongside shows the labels remove that obstruction for every period. With labels, the states of different directions are independent and the product above restricts correctly to every local horizon through the point.

That every other premise holds: the premises (P), (R), (L$_E$), (I), (Q) and the counting premises are statements about the windows of the singular boundary or of a Killing horizon (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boundary-mode-premises-finite-models} gives their finite readings), and (R$_{\Lambda}$) concerns the cosmological horizon; the model leaves all of these as the store has them. Of the store's 51 postulates only (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) and sheaf tameness mention local horizons, diamonds, accelerated observers or all points (search of the postulate texts), and tameness is a regularity condition at points of the degeneration locus, which carries no state. (Loc) fixes the entropy differences $\delta S = \eta\,\delta A$ and says nothing about the state's period: version 2 of the premise does not tie the entropy to the state of the modes (the mode-count reading is excluded there), which is why it holds in the model; under that excluded reading the entropy density would change with $c$. The structural premise of indifference (scrambling.indifference-structural-premise-series) forbids assignments that nothing in the framework determines, but it is applied at the declared level and flagged where it is used; the model's change of period between Killing patches and $U$ is such an assignment, so the premise holds in its declared, scoped reading and not under an unrestricted one. The identification of horizon and cutoff modes concerns the modes of a hole and is kept. So the model satisfies every present premise except (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$), which it violates for $c \ne 1$; this is independence from the present premises. It needs $U \ne \emptyset$: in exact de Sitter space every local Rindler horizon is at leading order a patch of some observer's cosmological horizon (null hyperplanes of the embedding, edges moved by null rotations), so if (R$_{\Lambda}$) is read for every observer no such $U$ exists there; generic spacetimes and the exterior or interior of a hole away from $r = 2M$ supply one. A premise fixing the state of local-horizon modes, such as the positive-null-energy premise of the result filed alongside (synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises), would make the model fail in $U$ and imply (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$). Imported field-theory theorems that would give period $2\pi$ (Bisognano-Wichmann, Unruh, in Fact \claimref{angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hypotheses}) apply to a field theory meeting their hypotheses; they are not premises about the store's modes, and the model is not such a theory.

\emph{(ii)} The geometric half of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.local-boost-temperature-is-local-regularity} is unchanged: the boost field $\chi$ has surface gravity $\kappa$ and rapidity $\kappa$ times its parameter, so a state of rapidity period $2\pi c$ has temperature $\kappa/(2\pi c)$ in the time of $\chi$. On the past half of the generator through $p$, with $\chi = -\kappa\lambda k$ (hypothesis (H2) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}) and $\theta = -\lambda\,\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}(k,k)|_{p} + O(\lambda^{2})$ (step (2) there),
\[
\delta Q = \int_{\lambda_{0}}^{0}T(k,k)\,(-\kappa\lambda)\,d\lambda = \frac{\kappa}{2}T(k,k)\,\lambda_{0}^{2}, \qquad
\delta A = \int_{\lambda_{0}}^{0}\theta\,d\lambda = \frac12\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}(k,k)\,\lambda_{0}^{2},
\]
per unit cross-section area, with the error terms of that theorem. So $\delta Q - T_{\chi}\eta\,\delta A = \tfrac{\kappa}{2}\bigl(T(k,k) - \tfrac{\eta}{2\pi c}\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}(k,k)\bigr)\lambda_{0}^{2} + O(\lambda_{0}^{3})$. The check integrates the two polynomials exactly at three rational parameter sets, carrying $2\pi$ as an independent rational symbol so that no step uses its value, and confirms that the defect vanishes exactly when $T(k,k) = (\eta/2\pi c)\,\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}(k,k)$.

\emph{(iii)} (H1) at leading order requires $\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}(k,k) = (2\pi c/\eta)\,T(k,k)$ for every null $k$ at every $p \in U$. The symmetric tensor $S = \mathrm{Ric}^{\circ} - (2\pi c/\eta)T$ then vanishes on all null vectors, so $S = f g$ for a function $f$: the map $S \mapsto (S(k,k))_{k}$ on the ten-dimensional space of symmetric tensors has the one-dimensional kernel spanned by $g$, which the check confirms exactly (rank $9$ over twelve rational null vectors, $g$ in the kernel). From here the argument of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius} applies word for word with $\eta$ replaced by $\eta/c$: the contracted Bianchi identity and $\nabla^{a}T_{ab} = 0$ then give Einstein's equations with $\Lambda$ an integration constant and $8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}} = 2\pi c/\eta$, that is $G_{\mathrm{cl}} = c/(4\eta)$. On a Killing horizon the generator $\ell$ has $\theta = \sigma = 0$ along it, so $\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}(\ell,\ell) = 0$ by the Raychaudhuri equation, and the equation at $k = \ell$ forces $T(\ell,\ell) = 0$ at any period; the null-null equation there is $0 = 0$ whatever $c$ is assigned, and the equations for $k \neq \ell$ determine $S$ by continuity in $k$, so a period that jumps between the Killing patch and the others obstructs nothing.

\emph{(iv)} Theorem \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-entropy-clause-curvature-independent-density}(ii) fixes $\eta = \tfrac14$ from the Schwarzschild family through Theorem \claimref{synthesis.quarter-from-temperature}, which uses the Hawking temperature of (R) at Killing horizons; the model keeps (R), so the calibration is unchanged and $G_{\mathrm{cl}} = c/(4 \cdot \tfrac14) = c$ in units of the $G$ that defines the Planck cell. The check reads $G_{\mathrm{cl}}$ off the defect: it computes the coefficient of $\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}(k,k)$ in the exactly integrated defect, sets the defect to zero to get $\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}(k,k) = \mu\,T(k,k)$, and finds $\mu = 8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}$ with $G_{\mathrm{cl}} = c$ at $\eta = \tfrac14$ for $c = 1, 2, 3$ (with $2\pi$ carried as a rational symbol). Since only $\eta/c$ enters (ii) and (iii), the field equations do not separate the two clauses: any change of the local period can be compensated by a change of the density, and the Killing calibration is what separates them.

synthesis.r-loc-needs-sheet-labelled-mod.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$, signature $(1,3)$. Let $p$ be a point, $\Sigma$ a small spacelike two-surface element through $p$, and $\ell$, $n$ its two future null normals. The local Rindler horizons $\mathcal{H}_{p,\ell}$ and $\mathcal{H}_{p,n}$ of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise} built on $\Sigma$ (generated by $\ell$ and by $n$) share the edge $\Sigma$; call them the two sheets of the edge. Take as a hypothesis, not assumed, the temperature clause (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) of that premise: the state of a patch's boundary modes is KMS at rapidity period $2\pi$ for the patch's future-directed local boost. A \emph{shared algebra} at $p$ is a unital $*$-algebra $\mathfrak{A}$ of modes contained in the mode algebras of both patches, the inductive limit of finite matrix factors (windows) each invariant under both boost flows, on which each flow acts on a window as $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{JsH})$ with $H = H^{*}$, as the phase-acting boost of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics} does. The windows' numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$, $J = e_{2}e_{3}$ the complex unit of the completed pair of the radial plane, which commutes with its mode operators (\claimref{synthesis.transverse-bivector-is-the-complex-unit-of-the-radial-atom}); in (iii) this $J$ is the windows' scalar, not the rotation generator $e_{2}e_{3}$ in the domain of $D$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Opposite boosts.)} At leading order in the patch size the future-directed approximate boost fields of the two sheets are $\chi$ and $-\chi$, each of unit surface gravity; on the past halves $\chi = -\lambda k$ along the generators ($k = \ell, n$), the form used in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Shared modes carry no temperature.)} Assume (N): the action of a boost on modes it fixes depends only on its vector field, so the flow of the sheet $n$ on a shared algebra is the inverse of that of the sheet $\ell$, $\alpha^{n}_{s} = \alpha^{\ell}_{-s}$. If a state satisfies (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) for both sheets, then on every window $\alpha^{\ell}$ is trivial and the state is the normalised trace. Hence at any nonzero weight no state satisfies (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) on both sheets of an edge on a shared algebra.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Covariant lifts carry nothing.)} A Lie algebra homomorphism $D$ from the Lorentz algebra into the $*$-derivations of a finite window (every one inner, $D(B) = J[h_{B}, \cdot\,]$ with $h_{B}$ self-adjoint) is zero: the Lorentz algebra is simple and noncompact, $\operatorname{ad}$ of a boost having the real eigenvalues $\pm 2$, while $\operatorname{ad}$ of every element of the image has purely imaginary eigenvalues, in $J\R$. So a Lorentz-covariant action of the local boosts on finite windows is trivial, independently of (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$), and carries no boost temperature.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The completed pair is shared.)} The completed pair of Theorem \claimref{hawking.modular-structure-completed-pair} has ladder $v = \tfrac12(e_{0} + e_{1})$, $v^{*} = \tfrac12(e_{0} - e_{1})$, the two null directions of the plane of $\sigma = e_{0}e_{1}$, that is the generators of the two sheets of the edge orthogonal to that plane, and relabelling the pair reverses the orientation. Under (N) the two sheets ask its weight-$w$ mode for the occupations $1/(1 + e^{2\pi w})$ and $1/(1 + e^{-2\pi w})$, equal only at $w = 0$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Sheet labels suffice.)} Let the modes at $p$ be labelled by future null directions, one window algebra $\mathfrak{A}_{p,[\ell]}$ for each direction, the algebras of different directions commuting, and let a local boost with bivector $B$ whose horizon is generated by $\ell$ act on $\mathfrak{A}_{p,[\ell]}$ through the weight $c_{\ell}(B)$ defined by $\tfrac12(B\ell - \ell B) = c_{\ell}(B)\,\ell$. Then $c_{\ell}$ is a character of the stabiliser of the direction $[\ell]$ (it vanishes on the null rotations fixing $\ell$, on the rotation about $\ell$ and on all brackets), every future boost of a horizon generated by $\ell$, whatever its edge, has the same weight $c_{\ell} = -1$ in the past-half orientation of (i), and the product over directions of the states $e^{-2\pi h_{\ell}}/\operatorname{tr}e^{-2\pi h_{\ell}}$ satisfies (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) for every local Rindler horizon through $p$, at every weight.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Consequences.} (a) Read the stored Definition, as a hypothesis, as placing the hole's modes at the bifurcation surface of the Killing horizon, where Premise \claimref{singularity.r-regularity-fixed-locus} imposes its condition, with those modes in the patches of both sheets through each of its points. Then at such a point the other sheet through that point is a local Rindler horizon whose future boost is $-\xi$ for the Killing field $\xi$; under the one-mode-set identification of (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) and (N), (R) and (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) on that sheet have no common state at the frequencies $\omega_{j} > 0$ of the Definition. (b) Antipodal de Sitter observers share the bifurcation sphere of their static patches, with Killing fields $\xi$ and $-\xi$ in the stabiliser of the frozen point (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-static-boost-frozen-point}); (R$_{\Lambda}$) imposed for every observer on modes of that sphere meets (ii). (c) So, under (N), (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) quantified over every local Rindler horizon is consistent at nonzero weight only if no mode is shared by the two sheets of an edge: the modes a patch carries at its edge must be labelled by the patch's sheet (its generating null direction), not by the point or by the plane of the edge. The per-direction windows of (v) are point spectrum, so the positive-null-energy premise of the result filed alongside (synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises) cannot be posed on them; the continuum carrier of that result, modes along each generator with the edge a null set carrying no mode, is the other resolution and supplies the labels automatically.
synthesis.r-loc-needs-sheet-labelled-mod.technical:
Clause (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) of the local-horizon premise asks the boundary modes of every local Rindler horizon to be thermal at rapidity period $2\pi$ for that horizon's future boost. This result tests the clause against itself. A small spacelike surface element through a point has two future null normals, and each generates a local Rindler horizon with that element as its edge; in local inertial coordinates both have the same flat boost as approximate Killing field, future pointing on one sheet and past pointing on the other, so their future boosts are $\chi$ and $-\chi$. On a mode set where the boost multiplies modes by phases, as in the store's Definition, the boost fixes its modes, and modes at the edge belong to both patches. If a boost's action on fixed modes depends only on its vector field, the two sheets act on such modes by mutually inverse flows; a state thermal at period $2\pi$ for a flow and for its inverse is thermal at $2\pi$ and at $-2\pi$, and on a matrix factor that forces the generator to be a scalar and the state to be the trace (KMS uniqueness). A Lorentz-covariant action on finite windows is no way out: the Lorentz algebra is simple and noncompact and has no nonzero homomorphism into the compact algebra of self-adjoint generators of a window, so such an action is trivial whatever the state.

The store's completed pair is such a shared algebra: its two ladder operators are the two null directions of one timelike plane, the generators of the two sheets of the orthogonal edge, and the two sheets ask its mode for reciprocal occupations. If, reading the stored Definition, the hole's modes sit at the bifurcation surface of a Killing horizon, where (R) is imposed, and belong to the patches of both sheets, then the other sheet through the surface is a local Rindler horizon with future boost $-\xi$, so with one mode set the two premises ask one mode for two occupations. The same happens for two antipodal de Sitter observers, which share a bifurcation sphere. Labelling modes by null direction removes the conflict: every horizon generated by a given null direction, whatever its edge, has a future boost that dilates that direction with the same weight, a character of the direction's stabiliser, so one thermal state per direction satisfies the clause for every local horizon. In quantum field theory the conflict does not arise because the two sheets carry the algebras of the right and left wedges, which commute (a remark, literature from memory); on the continuum of field modes along generators the labels are automatic, and the positive-null-energy carrier filed alongside is of that kind, while the per-direction windows here, being point spectrum, cannot carry it. The null directions at a point form a sphere, which in the series' twistor correspondence is, after complexification, the incidence line of the point; this identification of the labels is a remark, argued and not proved here.
synthesis.r-loc-needs-sheet-labelled-mod.lay: The series assumes that every small horizon, the kind an accelerated observer sees anywhere in spacetime, is warm at a definite temperature. This result shows a hidden snag. Any small patch of surface has two light-like directions leaving it, and each defines such a horizon, with the same edge. The two horizons have opposite notions of which way their boost runs. If the quantum modes that carry the temperature sit on the shared edge, do not know which of the two horizons they belong to, and each boost acts on them only through its own flow, the two horizons demand opposite temperatures from the same modes, and the only state that satisfies both is one with no temperature at all. The store's basic two-mode building block has exactly this ambiguity, and the same clash appears at the meeting surface of a black hole's horizon, if the hole's modes are read as sitting there, and at the horizons of opposite observers in de Sitter space. The fix is to label the modes by the light-like direction they belong to, which is what happens automatically in ordinary quantum field theory.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i)} At leading order in the patch size the metric at $p$ is flat and the approximate boost Killing field of a local Rindler horizon with edge $\Sigma$ is the flat boost that fixes $\Sigma$ (as in hypothesis (H2) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}). In inertial coordinates $(t, x, y, z)$ at $p$ with $\Sigma = \{t = x = 0\}$ take $\ell = \partial_{t} + \partial_{x}$, $n = \partial_{t} - \partial_{x}$ and $K = x\,\partial_{t} + t\,\partial_{x}$. On the null hypersurface through $\Sigma$ generated by $\ell$, at the point $\lambda\ell$ with affine parameter $\lambda$, $K = \lambda\ell$; on the one generated by $n$, at $\lambda n$, $K = (-\lambda)\partial_{t} + \lambda\partial_{x} = -\lambda n$. On the past halves ($\lambda < 0$) $K$ is therefore past pointing on the $\ell$ sheet and future pointing on the $n$ sheet, and the future-directed boosts are $\chi_{\ell} = -K = -\lambda\ell$ and $\chi_{n} = K = -\lambda n$: the same field up to sign, each of the form $\chi = -\kappa\lambda k$ with $\kappa = 1$. On the future halves the orientations are reversed. The patches of a Killing horizon are local Rindler horizons (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-is-a-second-placement-of-the-count}(ii)), so the same holds at a bifurcation surface with $K$ replaced by the Killing field. The check verifies the orientations and $|\chi| = |\lambda|$ on both halves of both sheets at three rational parameters.

\emph{(ii)} Fix a window $\mathfrak{A}_{F}$ of the shared algebra; it is a matrix factor, invariant under both flows, so the restriction of the state is KMS at the same period for the restricted flows (Proposition \claimref{hawking.kms-restricts-invariant-subalgebras}). Write $\alpha^{\ell}_{s} = \operatorname{Ad}(e^{JsH})$ on $\mathfrak{A}_{F}$; by (N), $\alpha^{n}_{s} = \operatorname{Ad}(e^{-JsH})$. By KMS uniqueness at a factor (Theorem \claimref{singularity.kms-uniqueness-factor}, with Lemma \claimref{hawking.gibbs-states-are-kms-conversely-finite}) the density is $e^{-2\pi H}/\operatorname{tr}e^{-2\pi H}$ and also $e^{2\pi H}/\operatorname{tr}e^{2\pi H}$. So $e^{-4\pi H}$ is a positive multiple of the identity; $H$ being self-adjoint, its eigenvalues are all equal, $H$ is a scalar, $\alpha^{\ell}$ is trivial on $\mathfrak{A}_{F}$ and the density is the identity divided by its trace, the normalised trace. Equivalently, by Theorem \claimref{singularity.rate-rigidity-temperature-not-algebra-intrinsic}(2), a flow-reversing identification carries the $2\pi$-KMS state to the $(-2\pi)$-KMS state, and on a factor these coincide only when the flow is trivial. Since every window is trivial for the flow and carries the trace, so does the inductive limit (the flow is trivial on a dense subalgebra, hence everywhere by continuity, and the state agrees with the trace on a dense subalgebra). For the phase-acting boost of the Definition, $H = \sum_{j \in F} w_{j}N_{j}$ on a window, scalar only if every weight $w_{j}$ vanishes. The check solves the linear KMS conditions $E^{-1}\varrho\,A\,E = A\varrho$ (all matrix units $A$, $E = e^{-\beta H}$ with a rational Boltzmann symbol) on a two-mode window with weights $1, 2$: one flow alone has a one-dimensional solution space, the Gibbs density; the flow and its inverse together have only $\varrho = 0$; a scalar $H$ admits the trace.

\emph{(iii)} On a window $\Mat_{n}(\C)$ every derivation is inner, and the derivations of a flow of $*$-automorphisms are $J[h, \cdot\,]$ with $h$ self-adjoint, determined up to a scalar; modulo scalars they form the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{su}(n)$ (identified with $J$ times the traceless self-adjoint matrices), on which $\operatorname{ad}$ of every element has purely imaginary eigenvalues, in $J\R$: $[Jh, E_{ab}] = J(\lambda_{a} - \lambda_{b})E_{ab}$ in an eigenbasis of $h$. Let $D$ be a Lie algebra homomorphism from the Lorentz algebra into it. In $\Cl(1,3)$ with the commutator bracket, the boost $B = e_{0}e_{1}$ has $[B, X_{\pm}] = \pm 2X_{\pm}$ for $X_{\pm} = e_{0}e_{2} \mp e_{1}e_{2}$ (computed in the check). Then $[D(B), D(X_{+})] = 2D(X_{+})$, so $D(X_{+})$ is zero or an eigenvector of $\operatorname{ad}_{D(B)}$ with the real nonzero eigenvalue $2$, which a purely imaginary spectrum excludes; hence $D(X_{+}) = 0$. The kernel of $D$ is an ideal containing $X_{+}$, and the ideal generated by $X_{+}$ is the whole six-dimensional bivector space (computed exactly in the check; this is the simplicity of the real Lie algebra $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$, the realification of $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\C)$). So $D = 0$: a Lorentz-covariant action on finite windows is trivial whatever the state, and no condition on states, (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) included, is needed for this conclusion.

\emph{(iv)} By Theorem \claimref{hawking.modular-structure-completed-pair}(1) the completed pair is $v = \tfrac12(e_{0} + e_{1})$, $v^{*} = \tfrac12(e_{0} - e_{1})$ with $\sigma = e_{0}e_{1}$, and relabelling the pair reverses the orientation; $e_{0} \pm e_{1}$ are null and are the two generators $\ell$, $n$ of the sheets of the edge orthogonal to the plane of $\sigma$. A mode of weight $w$ has, for a flow $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{Jsw(N - 1/2)})$, the $2\pi$-KMS occupation $e^{-2\pi w}/(1 + e^{-2\pi w}) = 1/(1 + e^{2\pi w})$, and for the inverse flow $1/(1 + e^{-2\pi w})$; these agree only at $w = 0$. This is (ii) on the single-mode algebra $\Mat_{2}(\C)$.

\emph{(v)} In $\Cl(1,3)$ with $Q(e_{0}) = 1$, $Q(e_{i}) = -1$, the map $v \mapsto \tfrac12(e_{0}e_{1}v - v\,e_{0}e_{1})$ sends $te_{0} + xe_{1}$ to $-(xe_{0} + te_{1})$, so $B = e_{0}e_{1}$ is the bivector of $-K$, the future boost of the past half of the $\ell$ sheet, and $\tfrac12(B\ell - \ell B) = -\ell$. The edges orthogonal to $\ell$ are permuted transitively by the null rotations fixing $\ell$, the rotors $\Lambda_{a} = 1 + \tfrac{a}{2}\ell e_{j}$ ($j = 2, 3$; $(\ell e_{j})^{2} = 0$, $\Lambda_{a}\widetilde{\Lambda}_{a} = 1$, $\Lambda_{a}\ell\widetilde{\Lambda}_{a} = \ell$), which preserve the time orientation; the future boost of the horizon generated by $\ell$ with edge $\Lambda_{a}\Sigma$ is $B' = \Lambda_{a}B\widetilde{\Lambda}_{a}$, and $\tfrac12(B'\ell - \ell B') = \Lambda_{a}\tfrac12(B\ell - \ell B)\widetilde{\Lambda}_{a} = -\ell$. So $c_{\ell} = -1$ for every such boost. The stabiliser algebra of $[\ell]$ is spanned by $B$, $\ell e_{2}$, $\ell e_{3}$ and $e_{2}e_{3}$, with weights $-1, 0, 0, 0$ on $\ell$; $c_{\ell}$ is linear, and it vanishes on brackets because $\tfrac12\operatorname{ad}_{[X,Y]} = [\tfrac12\operatorname{ad}_{X}, \tfrac12\operatorname{ad}_{Y}]$ and both act on the line of $\ell$ by scalars; so it is a character. The check verifies, for three null rotations, that $B' \neq B$, $B'^{2} = 1$, that $B'$ moves $e_{j}$ (a different edge) and that its weight on $\ell$ is $-1$, the weights of the stabiliser basis, and that the brackets of that basis have weight zero; and that the opposite sheet's boost $-B$ gives $n$ the weight $-1$ and $\ell$ the weight $+1$. With the action $\alpha^{B}_{s} = \operatorname{Ad}(e^{-Jsc_{\ell}(B)h_{\ell}})$ on $\mathfrak{A}_{p,[\ell]}$ every horizon generated by $\ell$ acts on its modes at $p$ by the one flow $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{Jsh_{\ell}})$, whose $2\pi$-KMS state is $e^{-2\pi h_{\ell}}/\operatorname{tr}$; a horizon generated by $\ell$ contains no other direction's label at $p$, the algebras of different directions commute, and the product state restricts to each of these, so (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) holds for every local horizon through $p$ at every weight. At the other points $q$ of an edge the same construction applies with the null normal at $q$.

\emph{Consequences.} (a) Take as a hypothesis the reading of the stored Definition in which the hole's modes sit at the fixed locus of the Killing flow, the bifurcation surface, where Premise (R) asks each single-mode marginal to be KMS for the Killing flow with frequency $\omega_{j} > 0$ at $2\pi/\kappa$, rapidity period $2\pi$. A point of that surface is the edge of the two sheets of the bifurcate horizon, local Rindler horizons by (i) and the cited theorem, with future boosts $\xi$ and $-\xi$ on the past halves. Under that reading and the identification of (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) (one mode set) the hole's modes at the point are modes of both patches; each single-mode algebra is invariant, so (ii) applies to it with $H = \omega_{j}(N_{j} - \tfrac12)$ and gives $\omega_{j} = 0$, against the Definition. (b) In the conventions of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-static-boost-frozen-point}, the static Killing field of an observer is generated by an element of the stabiliser of the frozen point; in the embedding $-X_{0}^{2} + X_{1}^{2} + X_{2}^{2} + X_{3}^{2} + X_{4}^{2} = 1$ (unit radius) it is $\xi = X_{4}\partial_{0} + X_{0}\partial_{4}$, future pointing on the worldline $X_{4} > 0$ and past pointing on the antipodal worldline $X_{4} < 0$, and both observers' flows fix the sphere $X_{0} = X_{4} = 0$; the check verifies this at three rational points of each worldline and two of the sphere. If (R$_{\Lambda}$) is imposed for both observers on modes of that sphere, (ii) applies as in (a). (c) is (ii) and (v) together; (iii) shows that a covariant lift cannot replace the sheet labels. The per-direction windows of (v) are point spectrum, so by the stored no-go for half-sided translations on point spectrum the positive-null-energy premise of the result filed alongside (synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises) cannot be posed on them; its continuum carrier is the other resolution.

\emph{Remarks.} The hypothesis that the patch's modes include modes at its edge is a reading of the stored Definition, not stored text; it is how the store places modes for a phase-acting boost: such a boost maps each mode to itself, and in the store the modes it acts on sit at its fixed locus ((R) at the bifurcation surface, the completion's pair over the exceptional set). On the continuum mode space with the boost dilating the affine parameter of the generators, modes away from the edge belong to one generator, so the labels of (v) are automatic there; in quantum field theory the algebras of the two sheets are those of the right and left wedges, which are each other's commutants (Bisognano and Wichmann; from memory). The null directions at a point form a two-sphere, which after complexification is the projective line of spinors $\pi$ with $\ell \propto \pi\bar\pi$, the incidence line of the point in the chart of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.incidence-relation-chart}; reading the labels of (v) as points of that line is a remark and is not used.

synthesis.series-content-induces-a-newto.formal:
Let each field carry its weight $w$ in units of one minimally coupled real scalar (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-sakharov-induced-gravity-coefficients}(a), (b): $1 - 6\xi_{R}$ for a real scalar of curvature coupling $\xi_{R}$, $1$ for a Weyl fermion, $-4$ for a gauge vector with its ghosts in the Feynman (Gupta-Bleuler) gauge, as in \claimref{synthesis.attachment-modules-give-sakharov-weights-cancelling-at-three-separate-generations}) and its mass $m$, and regulate the one-loop effective action by a proper-time cut-off $t \ge \Lambda^{-2}$, in the Feynman gauge.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The form; proved, given the Fact.)} $1/G_{\mathrm{ind}} = \tfrac{1}{12\pi}\bigl[B\Lambda^{2} - \sum_{j}w_{j}m_{j}^{2}\ln(\Lambda^{2}/m_{j}^{2}) - (1 - \gamma)\sum_{j}w_{j}m_{j}^{2} + O(m^{4}/\Lambda^{2})\bigr]$, $B = \sum_{j}w_{j}$ over the fields lighter than $\Lambda$; the coefficient of $\ln\Lambda^{2}$ is the $m^{2}$-part of the $t^{2}$ heat-kernel coefficient and does not depend on the regulator, while $B\Lambda^{2}$ and the constant do. For a massive vector at $\xi_{R} \neq 0$ that coefficient depends on the gauge parameter: its weight is $-(3 + 6\xi_{R}\alpha)$, $-4$ at $\xi_{R} = \tfrac16$ and $\alpha = 1$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The content at the cut-off; computed.)} Under Hypothesis (S), for a cut-off between $M_{I}$ and $M_{U}$ of the chain (Theorem \claimref{standard-model.chain}: twenty-one vectors, forty-eight Weyl fields, the bidoublet, the complex $(10,1,3)$ and optionally the complex $(15,2,2)$), $B = -36 + \sum_{j}(1 - 6\xi_{R,j})$ over the chain's real scalars: $-36$ if all are conformally coupled, $28$, $32$ or $152$ if all are minimally coupled. The content above $M_{U}$ is not stored.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The logarithmic remainder; computed.)} (a) If the content below $\Lambda$ is the weak-scale content alone (twelve vectors, forty-eight Weyl fields, the two elementary doublets of \claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}) and $B = 0$ ($\xi_{R} = \tfrac16$), then for every cut-off $\Lambda \ge 10\,m_{t}$ the remainder $\sum_{j}w_{j}m_{j}^{2}\ln(\Lambda^{2}/m_{j}^{2})$ is positive, the top quark outweighing the $W$ and $Z$, so $1/G_{\mathrm{ind}} < 0$ at this order; the doublets' tree term $-8\pi\xi_{R}v^{2} = -\tfrac{4\pi}{3}v^{2}$ has the same sign; both are below $10^{-31}M_{P}^{2}$ at $\Lambda = M_{P}$. (b) Under (S), for a cut-off above $M_{I}$, the nine vectors at $M_{I}$ (weight $-4$ each), the chain's scalars and, under Premise (M) (\claimref{neutrino.m-framework-realises-majorana-term-scale}), the Majorana neutrinos enter with both signs, so the sign of the remainder is not fixed by the store; for masses up to $6 \times 10^{11}$ GeV and scalar weights of size at most $1$ these fields contribute below $10^{-12}M_{P}^{2}$ at $\Lambda = M_{P}$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Matching; computed.)} If $B > 0$, the observed $G$ is reproduced at leading order exactly when $\Lambda^{2} = 12\pi M_{P}^{2}/B$ (for $B = 8$, $\Lambda^{2} = \tfrac{3\pi}{2}M_{P}^{2}$).
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading (argued).} The store supplies no cut-off scale in Planck units: $N$ is initial data (\claimref{programme.n-parameter-of-the-laws}), the weak scale's constant is a second free number (\claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-second-free-number}), the descent's duration, which would set the deposit's ultraviolet end, is not fixed and is a datum of the state, which enters the stress tensor only through smooth state-dependent terms (\claimref{synthesis.hadamard-condition-leaves-the-deposit-spectrum-free-on-bounded-bands}), the floors are frame dependent, the Krein premise's Pauli-Villars masses are free, and the locally covariant scheme leaves a free coefficient times $m^{2}$ (Fact (d)). So the induced-gravity route reaches $G$ only by choosing one dimensionful regulator datum, and $G$ stays an input. Transport-absent.
synthesis.series-content-induces-a-newto.technical:
In Sakharov's induced gravity with a proper-time cut-off $\Lambda$, in the Feynman gauge, each field contributes to $1/G$ its weight times $\Lambda^{2}$, minus its weight times $m^{2}\ln(\Lambda^{2}/m^{2})$, over $12\pi$. The weights are $1 - 6\xi_{R}$ per real scalar of curvature coupling $\xi_{R}$, $1$ per Weyl fermion and $-4$ per gauge vector. The logarithmic coefficient is fixed by the heat-kernel coefficient and does not depend on the regulator, though for massive vectors at $\xi_{R} \neq 0$ it depends on the gauge; the quadratic one depends on both.

The quadratic coefficient $B$ counts every field lighter than the cut-off. If the cut-off lies above the chain's intermediate scale, under Hypothesis (S) the Pati-Salam content has twenty-one vectors, and $B = -36$ plus the scalars' weights: negative if the scalars are conformally coupled, $28$ to $152$ if they are minimally coupled. Nothing in the store fixes these couplings or the content above the unification scale.

Where $B = 0$ and only the weak-scale content lies below the cut-off, the remainder is logarithmic and has the wrong sign: the top quark outweighs the $W$ and $Z$ bosons, and the Higgs doublets' classical curvature coupling adds a term of the same sign, so the induced $1/G$ is negative and far too small. Under (S), with a cut-off above the intermediate scale, the heavy vectors there pull the other way and the sign is not fixed by the store; the size stays far below $1/G$. Where $B > 0$, the observed $G$ fixes the cut-off, for instance $\Lambda^{2} = \tfrac{3\pi}{2}M_{P}^{2}$ at $B = 8$: a fit. Reading, argued: no stored datum supplies the cut-off in Planck units, so $G$ stays an input. Transport-absent.
synthesis.series-content-induces-a-newto.lay: Sakharov's idea is that gravity's strength could be produced by the quantum jitter of all other fields, up to some shortest length where the jitter is cut off. The result is the cut-off energy squared times a count of the fields, plus a much smaller term from the particle masses. If the series' larger unified symmetry is real at high energies, the count depends on how its many extra Higgs fields couple to curvature, which nothing in the series decides. If only the everyday particles lie below the cut-off and their count is zero, the small mass term is left, and it has the wrong sign: it would make gravity repulsive, and it is far too weak. With the series' unified symmetry, heavy force carriers pull the other way and the sign is undecided, but the term is still far too weak. Where the count is positive, gravity's observed strength can be matched, but only by choosing the cut-off to match it, a little above the Planck energy. The series has no number that would set that cut-off, so on this route the strength of gravity remains an input.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i) The form.} By Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-sakharov-induced-gravity-coefficients}(a), (b), a field of weight $w$ (in units of one minimally coupled real scalar: $1 - 6\xi_{R}$ for a real scalar of curvature coupling $\xi_{R}$, $1$ for a Weyl fermion, $-4$ for a gauge vector with its ghosts in the Gupta-Bleuler gauge, as in \claimref{synthesis.attachment-modules-give-sakharov-weights-cancelling-at-three-separate-generations}) and mass $m$ has heat trace $(4\pi t)^{-2}e^{-tm^{2}}\bigl(\int r + t\int\mathrm{tr}(E + R/6) + \dots\bigr)$, and with a proper-time cut-off $t \ge \Lambda^{-2}$ its contribution to the coefficient of the induced Einstein-Hilbert term is proportional to $w\int_{\Lambda^{-2}}^{\infty}t^{-2}e^{-tm^{2}}\,dt$; for $m = 0$ this is $w\Lambda^{2}$, which with the normalisation of Fact (b), $-(192\pi^{2}\epsilon)^{-1}B\,R$ at $\epsilon = \Lambda^{-2}$ against $R/(16\pi G)$, gives $1/G_{\mathrm{ind}} = B\Lambda^{2}/(12\pi)$, $B = \sum_{j}w_{j}$. With masses, the substitution $t = u\Lambda^{-2}$ gives $\int_{\Lambda^{-2}}^{\infty}t^{-2}e^{-tm^{2}}dt = \Lambda^{2}E_{2}(x)$, $x = m^{2}/\Lambda^{2}$, $E_{n}(x) = \int_{1}^{\infty}u^{-n}e^{-xu}\,du$. The exponential integrals satisfy $E_{2}' = -E_{1}$, $E_{1}'(x) = -e^{-x}/x$, $E_{2}(0) = 1$, and $E_{1}(x) = -\gamma - \ln x + \sum_{k \ge 1}(-1)^{k+1}x^{k}/(k\,k!)$; the check verifies these relations exactly on the truncated series, with $\ln x$ and $\gamma$ kept symbolic, and reads off $E_{2}(x) = 1 + x(\ln x + \gamma - 1) + O(x^{2}\ln x)$. Hence
\[
\frac{1}{G_{\mathrm{ind}}} = \frac{1}{12\pi}\Bigl[B\Lambda^{2} - \sum_{j}w_{j}m_{j}^{2}\ln\frac{\Lambda^{2}}{m_{j}^{2}} - (1 - \gamma)\sum_{j}w_{j}m_{j}^{2} + O(m^{4}/\Lambda^{2})\Bigr].
\]
The logarithm comes from the $t^{2}$ term of the heat trace, whose part linear in $m^{2}$ and $R$ is the cross term $-m^{2}\,\mathrm{tr}(E + R/6)$ of $e^{-tm^{2}}$ with $t\,\mathrm{tr}(E + R/6)$ (checked on the product of the two series); a $t^{2}$ coefficient produces a logarithm under every regulator with one scale (for dimensional continuation, the pole of the same coefficient), so the coefficient $-\sum w_{j}m_{j}^{2}/(12\pi)$ of $\ln\Lambda^{2}$ does not depend on the regulator, while $B\Lambda^{2}$ and the constant do; in particular a covariant cut-off on the gauge-fixed operators of a vector at gauge parameter $\alpha \neq 1$ changes the vector's weight in $B$.

\emph{Gauge.} All weights below are Feynman-gauge values ($\alpha = 1$, the Gupta-Bleuler form of clause (K1) of the Krein premise): under a covariant cut-off on the gauge-fixed operators a vector's weight is $\alpha - 5$ (\claimref{synthesis.krein-quartet-drops-from-the-induced-einstein-hilbert-coefficient-only-under-a-regulator-that-treats-it-alike}, which owns the weak-scale coefficient $B = 8(1 - 6\xi_{R})$ of the twelve vectors of the forced gauge algebra (Theorem \claimref{standard-model.connection-forced}), forty-eight Weyl fields and the two doublets, used here as an input). For a massive vector the logarithm's coefficient is regulator independent but, at $\xi_{R} \neq 0$, gauge dependent: in the $R_{\alpha}$ gauge the transverse part ($-3$) has mass $m_{V}$, while the longitudinal part (weight $\alpha$, its eigenvalues $(\lambda + \alpha m_{V}^{2})/\alpha$), the Goldstone mode (weight $1 - 6\xi_{R}$) and the ghosts ($-2$) have mass squared $\alpha m_{V}^{2}$, so the coefficient of $m_{V}^{2}\ln\Lambda^{2}$ has weight $-3 + \alpha + (1 - 6\xi_{R})\alpha - 2\alpha = -(3 + 6\xi_{R}\alpha)$ (computed): the Proca value $-3$ for every $\alpha$ at $\xi_{R} = 0$, and $-(3 + \alpha)$ at $\xi_{R} = \tfrac16$, $-4$ at $\alpha = 1$. The gauge dependence at $\xi_{R} \neq 0$ is that of an off-shell quantity: the term $\xi_{R}Rv\,h$ makes the vacuum not stationary at order $R$ (the Nielsen identity, cited from memory).

\emph{(ii) The content at the cut-off.} A field of mass above $\Lambda$ is suppressed by $e^{-tm^{2}}$ for $t \ge \Lambda^{-2}$; a field below it contributes its full weight to $B$ whatever its mass. Under Hypothesis (S), the chain of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.chain} has between $M_{I}$ (about $10^{10}$ to $10^{11}$ GeV) and $M_{U}$ (about $10^{16}$ GeV) the Pati-Salam algebra, of dimension $15 + 3 + 3 = 21$, the three generations of sixteen, the bidoublet $(1,2,2)$ (four real scalars if real, eight if complex), the complex $(10,1,3)$ ($60$ real) and, where named, the complex $(15,2,2)$ ($120$ real). So for a cut-off in that window $B = 48 - 84 + \sum_{j}(1 - 6\xi_{R,j}) = -36 + \sum_{j}(1 - 6\xi_{R,j})$: $-36$ if every scalar is conformally coupled, and $28$, $32$ or $152$ for the three scalar contents if every scalar is minimally coupled (computed). Above $M_{U}$ the store does not fix the content. So the sign and size of $B$ at a cut-off above $M_{I}$ are set by the curvature couplings of the chain's scalars, which no stored result fixes. The chain runs with one Higgs doublet from $M_{Z}$ to $M_{I}$, while the rung field is two elementary doublets (\claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}); this tension between stored results is named here and not resolved, and the scales $M_{I}$, $M_{U}$ quoted are the chain's.

\emph{(iii)(a) The remainder for the weak-scale content alone.} Suppose the content below $\Lambda$ is the weak-scale content and $B = 0$ ($\xi_{R} = \tfrac16$). The scalars have weight $0$; a Dirac fermion of mass $m$ is two Weyl fields of mass $m$; a massive vector has weight $-4$ (the Gauge paragraph, $\alpha = 1$). With $L = \ln(\Lambda^{2}/m_{t}^{2})$ and $\ell_{V} = \ln(m_{t}^{2}/m_{V}^{2}) \le m_{t}^{2}/m_{V}^{2} - 1$,
\[
S = \sum_{j}w_{j}m_{j}^{2}\ln\frac{\Lambda^{2}}{m_{j}^{2}} \;\ge\; \bigl(6m_{t}^{2} - 4(2m_{W}^{2} + m_{Z}^{2})\bigr)L - 4\bigl(2m_{W}^{2}\ell_{W} + m_{Z}^{2}\ell_{Z}\bigr),
\]
since every other fermion adds a positive term when $\Lambda$ exceeds its mass. With the stored values of $m_{t}$, $m_{W}$, $m_{Z}$ the coefficient of $L$ is positive and the constant is less than three times it (computed exactly), and for $\Lambda \ge 10\,m_{t}$, $L \ge \ln 100 > 4$ (as $e < 3$ and $3^{4} < 100$); so $S > 0$ and the loop term $-S/(12\pi)$ is negative. At other $\alpha$ the coefficient of $L$, $6m_{t}^{2} - (3 + \alpha)(2m_{W}^{2} + m_{Z}^{2})$, stays positive up to $\alpha = 5$ (computed). At $\xi_{R} = \tfrac16$ the doublets' classical coupling $-\xi_{R}R\,|\phi|^{2}$ with $|\phi|^{2} = v^{2}/2$ shifts $1/(16\pi G)$ by $-\xi_{R}v^{2}/2$, that is $\Delta(1/G) = -8\pi\xi_{R}v^{2} = -\tfrac{4\pi}{3}v^{2}$ at tree level, of the same sign (computed from the stored $v$; numerically $-2.5 \times 10^{5}$ GeV$^{2}$, about $1.3$ times the loop term at $\Lambda = M_{P}$). For the size at $\Lambda = M_{P}$: $m^{2}\ln(\Lambda^{2}/m^{2})$ increases with $m$ below $\Lambda/\sqrt{e}$, so $|S| \le 48\,m_{t}^{2}\ln(M_{P}^{2}/m_{t}^{2})$ (twenty-four Dirac fermions, the neutrinos included, none heavier than the top; the vectors subtract), and with $\ln y$ below the bit length of $y$ and $\pi > 3$ the check bounds the loop term by $10^{-31}M_{P}^{2}$ and the tree term by $10^{-32}M_{P}^{2}$ (computed); numerically, from the top, $W$ and $Z$ alone, $S/(12\pi M_{P}^{2})$ is about $2 \times 10^{-33}$ (computed, in the proof text only).

\emph{(iii)(b) Under (S).} For a cut-off above $M_{I}$ the remainder contains the fields at $M_{I}$: the $21 - 12 = 9$ vectors that the vev along the Majorana element makes massive, of weight $-4$ each, so $-4 \cdot 9\,M_{I}^{2}\ln(\Lambda^{2}/M_{I}^{2})$ in $S$, of the attractive sign; the chain's scalars near $M_{I}$, whose weights are those that $B = 0$ would need ($36$ units of nonconformal weight) and are not fixed; and, under Premise (M) (\claimref{neutrino.m-framework-realises-majorana-term-scale}), the three right-handed neutrinos, of weight $+1$ and Majorana mass $M$, of the repulsive sign. The fermion argument of (a) does not cover the heavy vectors, so the sign of the remainder is not fixed by the store. Its size is: with total weight at most $4 \cdot 9 + 188 + 3 = 227$ in absolute value (scalar weights of size at most $1$, that is $0 \le \xi_{R,j} \le \tfrac13$), masses up to $6 \times 10^{11}$ GeV (the largest stored $M_{I}$), $\Lambda = M_{P}$ and the same bounds, the check bounds these fields' contribution by $10^{-12}M_{P}^{2}$ (computed). Fields at or above $M_{U}$ are not stored and are not bounded here.

\emph{(iv) Matching.} If $B > 0$, $1/G_{\mathrm{ind}} = M_{P}^{2}$ at leading order exactly when $\Lambda^{2} = 12\pi M_{P}^{2}/B$; for the weak-scale content with minimally coupled doublets ($B = 8$) this is $\Lambda^{2} = \tfrac{3\pi}{2}M_{P}^{2}$, $\Lambda \approx 2.17\,M_{P}$ (computed). The cut-off is then chosen to give $G$, which is a fit, not a prediction.

\emph{Reading (argued).} A prediction of $G$ on this route needs a cut-off scale in Planck units from the series, and the store has none: $N = M_{P}/H$ is initial data (\claimref{programme.n-parameter-of-the-laws}); the weak scale's constant is a second free number (\claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-second-free-number}); the descent's duration $\tau$, which would set the deposit's ultraviolet end $k_{\mathrm{UV}} \sim 1/\tau$, is not fixed, and in any case is a datum of the state, which by the Hadamard property enters the stress tensor only through smooth state-dependent terms, not through the local $G_{ab}$ coefficient that the regulator sets (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-microlocal-hadamard-condition}; \claimref{synthesis.hadamard-condition-leaves-the-deposit-spectrum-free-on-bounded-bands}); the floors are a frame-dependent cut-off with no scale in Planck units (\claimref{synthesis.floor-regulator-keeps-the-charge-and-the-central-term-below-the-cut-off}); the Pauli-Villars regulators of the Krein premise replace $\Lambda^{2}$ by $\sum_{i}c_{i}M_{i}^{2}\ln M_{i}^{2}$ with free regulator masses; and the locally covariant scheme has no Einstein-tensor freedom for massless fields and a free coefficient times $m^{2}$ for massive ones (Fact (d)). So every route in the store reaches $G$ only by fixing one dimensionful regulator datum to the observed value, and $G$ stays an input. The mechanism is standard one-loop physics (transport-absent); what is new here is its evaluation on the series' content at and above the weak scale.

synthesis.series-wald-entropy-changes-wi.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = G = 1$, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, Riemann tensor positive on spheres, read from the field strength of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime with derived metric $g$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}). Let $\Lambda > 0$, $\alpha = -3/(4\Lambda)$, and let the gravitational Lagrangian of the field be the series' $(R - 2\Lambda + \alpha E_{4})/16\pi$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.euler-term-horizon-entropy-shift}(i), from Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west}). Let (W$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) be the hypothesis (W) of that theorem extended to the local Rindler horizons of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise}: the entropy of a cut $\Sigma$ of a local horizon is the Jacobson-Myers functional $S[\Sigma] = \tfrac14\int_{\Sigma}(1 + 2\alpha\,R_{\Sigma})\,dA$ of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-wald-noether-charge-entropy}(c), $R_{\Sigma}$ the scalar curvature of $\Sigma$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The density on a local edge.)} At a point of $\Sigma$ where the second fundamental form along one null normal $k$ vanishes, $R_{\Sigma} = 2K$ with $K$ the sectional curvature of the tangent plane, and the density is
\[
s \;=\; \tfrac14\bigl(1 - 3K/\Lambda\bigr) \;=\; -\frac{3}{4\Lambda}\,F(e_{2}, e_{3}, e_{2}, e_{3}),
\]
with $F_{abcd} = R_{abcd} - \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}(g_{ac}g_{bd} - g_{ad}g_{bc})$ the Cartan curvature of the MacDowell-Mansouri square (minus the Lorentz block of its field strength, $-\mathcal{F}(B) = \mathcal{R}(B) - \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}B$ in the store's sign, the Lorentz block of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west} being $-(\mathcal{R}(B) - B/l^{2})$, evaluated on the edge plane) and $e_{2}, e_{3}$ an orthonormal basis of the plane. For the de Sitter field every plane has $K = \Lambda/3$, so $s = 0$ on every local edge. Integrated over a cross-section $\{t = t_{0},\ r = r_{b}\}$ of the horizon locus of a Schwarzschild-de Sitter hole in the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand chart ($\hb = 1 - \beta P$, $\beta^{2} = 1 - f(r)$ with $f$ as in (ii)), of area $A = 4\pi r_{b}^{2}$, on which the Killing field $\xi = \hb^{-1}(e_{t})$ is null and normal to the horizon with $(\xi \cdot D)\xi = \kappa_{b}\xi$, $\kappa_{b} = f'(r_{b})/2$ its surface gravity, $s$ gives $A/4 - 3\pi/\Lambda$, the value of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.euler-term-horizon-entropy-shift}(ii).
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Radial generators of Schwarzschild-de Sitter.)} Let $f(r) = 1 - 2M/r - \Lambda r^{2}/3$ with $M > 0$, the metric function of the Schwarzschild-de Sitter field, $p$ a point of the static region $f > 0$ at radius $r_{0}$, and $k_{\pm} = f^{-1}\partial_{t} \pm \partial_{r}$ (in the static coordinates of the derived metric), the affinely parametrised radial future null directions at $p$. For either sign and for every cut through $p$ orthogonal to $k_{\pm}$ with vanishing expansion and shear at $p$ (any tilt of its tangent plane along $k$, any normalisation of $k$ along it): $R(k, A, k, B) = 0$ and $R(k, A, B, C) = 0$ along the generator $\gamma$ through $p$ for transverse $A, B, C$; hence the expansion and shear vanish along all of $\gamma$, the area per unit cross-section is constant along it, and no matter crosses ($\delta Q = 0$). Along $\gamma$, $r(\lambda) = r_{0} \pm \lambda$ and the density of (i) is
\[
s(\lambda) \;=\; -\frac{3M}{2\Lambda\,r(\lambda)^{3}} .
\]
So per unit cross-section area, in the thin-pencil limit of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}(H2), the patch $\lambda \in [\lambda_{0}, 0]$ changes its (W$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) entropy by
\[
\Delta S \;=\; -\frac{3M}{2\Lambda}\Bigl(\frac{1}{r_{0}^{3}} - \frac{1}{(r_{0} \pm \lambda_{0})^{3}}\Bigr) \;=\; \pm\frac{9M}{2\Lambda r_{0}^{4}}\,|\lambda_{0}| + O(\lambda_{0}^{2}),
\]
positive for the outgoing and negative for the ingoing horizon, while $\delta A = 0$ and $\delta Q = 0$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Consequences.)} Under (W$_{\mathrm{loc}}$): the entropy change of the radial local horizons of every Schwarzschild-de Sitter hole is not $\eta\,\delta A$ for any $\eta$, which is refutation condition (a) of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise}; the Clausius relation (H1) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius} fails at first order in $\lambda_{0}$ in vacuum, the defect being that theorem's integrated-reading term $(k\cdot\nabla s)\lambda_{0}$ with $k\cdot\nabla s = \pm 9M/(2\Lambda r_{0}^{4})$; and since the entropy falls along the ingoing horizon with no flux, no reading $dS = \delta Q/T + d_{i}S$ with $d_{i}S \ge 0$ restores it. The same holds for every entropy functional that differs from the Jacobson-Myers one by terms vanishing where the $k$-extrinsic curvature vanishes, or by functions of the Ricci tensor. The area term alone, $A/4$, is constant along these generators and consistent with (H1). The change is the value at $p$ of a divergence on the cut: it cancels over any closed cut (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.euler-term-horizon-entropy-shift}(ii)), so the failure is of the Clausius relation on open patches, as (H1) and (H2) require it, with the entropy of a patch the integral of the density over the patch (a functional of the cut) taken per unit cross-section area in the thin-pencil limit.
\end{enumerate}
Hence, with entropy a functional of the cut and (H1) imposed on open patches, (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) and (W$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) cannot both hold, nor can (H1) and (W$_{\mathrm{loc}}$). The general first-order rate of the Euler entropy on any local patch is filed alongside, synthesis.euler-entropy-first-order-rate-on-local-patches; on radial Schwarzschild-de Sitter generators it reduces to the curvature-gradient term evaluated in (ii). With (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) adopted, horizon entropy on local horizons is not the Wald functional of the series' action: the Euler term must be left out of the entropy functional, while it stays in the action, where it is topological. Together with Theorem \claimref{synthesis.sds-clausius-fixes-area-constant}(v), which excludes its constant shift on closed horizons, this gives the de Sitter entropy $3\pi/\Lambda = \pi N^{2}$ and the Einstein-Hilbert nucleation exponent $-1$, not $0$ and $-4$. The bifurcation surface itself, where the boost flow has its fixed points, lies beyond one flat chart (it is the meeting of the four regions of the maximal extension); the chart contains the future horizon, on whose cross-sections the area, the surface gravity and the boost flow are those stated.
synthesis.series-wald-entropy-changes-wi.technical:
The series' gravitational action, the MacDowell-Mansouri square, contains the Euler density with coefficient $-3/(4\Lambda)$. If horizon entropy were its Wald (Jacobson-Myers) functional, the stored result shows the extra term is a constant on closed horizons, invisible to every Clausius relation between closed cuts; it left open whether it matters on the small open patches of a local Rindler horizon, which is where the local-horizon premise (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) and Jacobson's argument live. It does. On a local edge the Jacobson-Myers density equals $-3/(4\Lambda)$ times the Cartan curvature of the edge plane, so it depends on the curvature (the field strength) at the point and vanishes identically for the de Sitter field.

The cleanest test is the store's own vacuum solution, Schwarzschild-de Sitter. Along a radial null generator, ingoing or outgoing, the curvature components that focus or shear the generators vanish identically, so for every admissible cut the area stays constant and, in vacuum, no energy crosses. Yet the density changes, as $-3M/(2\Lambda r^{3})$: the Wald entropy grows along outgoing and falls along ingoing local horizons with nothing crossing them. That violates the curvature-independence clause (Loc) of the premise (the change is not proportional to the area change, which is zero), violates the Clausius relation at first order, and cannot be absorbed into an entropy production because it has both signs. The change is the value at the point of a divergence on the cut, so it cancels over any closed cut, as the stored result requires; what fails is the Clausius relation on each open patch, which is how Jacobson's argument and the store's hypotheses impose it, with the entropy of a patch the integral of its density (a functional of the cut). The general first-order rate on any patch is filed alongside, synthesis.euler-entropy-first-order-rate-on-local-patches; this result supplies the exact radial value and the all-orders, two-signed change. The result does not depend on the choice of cut, on the normalisation of the generators, or on the usual ambiguity of the Wald entropy away from stationary horizons, since the terms that ambiguity adds vanish where the expansion and shear vanish.

So the Euler term must be excluded from the horizon entropy functional (not from the action): with (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) adopted, the entropy of local horizons is the area term. With the stored result on closed horizons, the de Sitter entropy is $\pi N^{2}$, not zero, and black-hole nucleation keeps its Einstein-Hilbert exponent. Whether the entropy is, in addition, exactly the boundary-mode count is not decided here.
synthesis.series-wald-entropy-changes-wi.lay: The series writes gravity's action as the square of a curvature built from its frozen point. That action contains an extra term which does not change Einstein's equations but, in the standard Wald recipe, does change the entropy assigned to horizons. Earlier work showed the change is a fixed constant for closed horizons such as a black hole's, so it cannot be seen in the usual heat-balance arguments. This result looks at the small pieces of horizon that Jacobson's derivation of Einstein's equations uses. Around a black hole in a universe with a cosmological constant, a light front moving straight inward or outward keeps its area and has nothing crossing it, yet the Wald entropy of the extra term changes: it goes up on the way out and down on the way in. A horizon whose entropy changes with no heat crossing it, and that can even lose entropy, breaks the heat balance and the assumption that entropy grows with area at the same rate everywhere. So if the local-horizon assumption is kept, the extra term has to be left out of the entropy, while it can stay in the action.

proofs.main:
Everything is computed in Gauge Theory Gravity (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}, clauses (i), (ii) and (iv)) in the store's signature $(+,-,-,-)$ and curvature sign, $\mathcal{R}(B) = -R(\hb(B))$. The statement's signature $(-,+,+,+)$ with Riemann positive on spheres is kept for its formulas; every quantity the proof uses is the same in both conventions: the sectional curvature of a spacelike plane with unit bivector $B$, taken with the plane's positive-definite induced metric ($-g$ restricted to the plane in the store's signature, $g$ in the statement's), is $K = \langle\mathcal{R}(B)B^{-1}\rangle$; this holds because the vectors of a spacelike plane of $\Cl(1,3)$ square to $-1$, so $B^{2} = -1$ (on a plane whose vectors square to $+1$, as on $\Cl(4,0)$, the store's sign gives $-K$), and it is $\Lambda/3$ on de Sitter and positive on round spheres, $F(e_{2}, e_{3}, e_{2}, e_{3}) = K - \Lambda/3 = \langle(\mathcal{R}(B) - \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}B)B^{-1}\rangle$ on the edge plane, and $R(k, A, k, B) = 0$, $R(k, A, B, C) = 0$ are the vanishing of $(k\wedge B)\cdot\mathcal{R}(k\wedge A)$ and $(B\wedge C)\cdot\mathcal{R}(k\wedge A)$ (dictionary C11).

\emph{Setting.} By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.euler-term-horizon-entropy-shift}(i) the series' Lagrangian is $(R - 2\Lambda + \alpha E_{4})/16\pi$ with $\alpha = -3/(4\Lambda)$; in four dimensions $E_{4}$ is topological, so its field equations are those of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west} torsion-free, $G_{ab} + \Lambda g_{ab} = 0$ in vacuum, and Schwarzschild-de Sitter is a solution. The GTG check builds the Schwarzschild-de Sitter field in the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand chart, $\hb = 1 - \beta P$ with $\beta^{2} = 2M/r + \Lambda r^{2}/3 = 1 - f$, and finds its Ricci map $\mathcal{R}(a) = \Lambda a$ at three points of the static region. Under (W$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) the entropy of a cut is the Jacobson-Myers functional of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-wald-noether-charge-entropy}(c), with density $s = \tfrac14(1 + 2\alpha R_{\Sigma})$.

\emph{(i)} For a spacelike two-surface with null normals $k, n$, $k\cdot n = -1$, and null second fundamental forms $\chi^{(k)}, \chi^{(n)}$, the Gauss equation (standard, cited from memory) gives $R_{\Sigma} = h^{ac}h^{bd}R_{abcd} + Q(\chi^{(k)}, \chi^{(n)})$, where $Q$ is a sum of terms each bilinear in one $\chi^{(k)}$ and one $\chi^{(n)}$ (explicitly $2\theta_{k}\theta_{n} - 2\chi^{(k)}_{AB}\chi^{(n)AB}$ up to the sign convention for $n$). Where $\chi^{(k)} = 0$, $R_{\Sigma} = h^{ac}h^{bd}R_{abcd} = 2K$, with $K$ the sectional curvature of the tangent plane, $K = \langle\mathcal{R}(B)B^{-1}\rangle$ for its unit bivector $B$. Then $s = \tfrac14(1 + 4\alpha K) = \tfrac14(1 - 3K/\Lambda) = -\tfrac{3}{4\Lambda}(K - \Lambda/3)$, and $K - \Lambda/3 = F(e_{2}, e_{3}, e_{2}, e_{3})$ for $F_{abcd} = R_{abcd} - \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}(g_{ac}g_{bd} - g_{ad}g_{bc})$, the curvature of the Cartan connection whose square is the series' action (it vanishes on the de Sitter model, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.euler-term-horizon-entropy-shift}(i)). On de Sitter space $\mathcal{R}(B) = \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}B$ for every bivector, so every spacelike plane has $K = \langle\tfrac{\Lambda}{3}BB^{-1}\rangle = \Lambda/3$ and $s = 0$; the GTG check computes the field strength of the de Sitter gauge field in the flat slicing and finds $K = \Lambda/3$ on the transverse plane and on a generic spacelike plane. On a cross-section $\{t = t_{0},\ r = r_{b}\}$ of the horizon locus in the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand chart the second fundamental form along the generator $\xi$ vanishes ($\xi$ is the Killing field, normal to the horizon, so its expansion and shear vanish there; the GTG check computes $\chi^{(\xi)}(e_{A}, e_{B}) = e_{B}\cdot((e_{A}\cdot D)\xi) = 0$ for $A, B \in \{2, 3\}$), which is the condition of the formula above; the one along the other null normal does not vanish (for $n = e_{0} - e_{1}$ its expansion is $-4/r_{b}$, also computed by the check; both vanish only on the bifurcation surface, which lies beyond the chart), and $K = 2M/r_{b}^{3} + \Lambda/3$ (from (ii) below); there $\xi = \hb^{-1}(e_{t}) = e_{0} + \beta e_{1}$ is null ($\beta = 1$) and $(\xi\cdot D)\xi = \kappa_{b}\xi$ with $\kappa_{b} = f'(r_{b})/2$, both computed by the GTG check from the gauge field at three rational horizons, so $\int s\,dA = 4\pi r_{b}^{2}\cdot(-3M/(2\Lambda r_{b}^{3})) = -6\pi M/(\Lambda r_{b})$, and $f(r_{b}) = 0$, i.e. $6M/r_{b} = 3 - \Lambda r_{b}^{2}$, turns this into $\pi r_{b}^{2} - 3\pi/\Lambda = A/4 - 3\pi\chi/(2\Lambda)$ with $\chi = 2$, the value of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.euler-term-horizon-entropy-shift}(ii). The check confirms this value at the same three horizons, with $M$ solved from $f(r_{b}) = 0$.

\emph{(ii) Curvature along radial generators.} In the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand gauge the field strength of the Schwarzschild-de Sitter field is, in the store's sign, $\mathcal{R}(B) = \tfrac{M}{2r^{3}}(B + 3\sigma B\sigma) + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}B$ with $\sigma = e_{1}e_{0}$ the radial plane (the Schwarzschild operator of the dictionary plus the de Sitter one; the check computes it from the gauge field). On the transverse plane, $\sigma$ commutes with $e_{2}e_{3}$, so $\mathcal{R}(e_{2}\wedge e_{3}) = (2M/r^{3} + \Lambda/3)\,e_{2}\wedge e_{3}$ and $K = 2M/r^{3} + \Lambda/3$, with $dK/dr = -6M/r^{4}$. The radial future null directions are those of $e_{0} \pm e_{1}$: in the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand labels the static $k_{\pm} = f^{-1}\partial_{t} \pm \partial_{r}$ are the physical vectors $k_{+} = (e_{0} + e_{1})/(1 - \beta)$ and $k_{-} = (e_{0} - e_{1})/(1 + \beta)$, using $f = (1 - \beta)(1 + \beta)$, with $dr/d\lambda = \pm 1$. For $k$ in the radial plane and $A$ transverse, $\sigma$ anticommutes with $k$ and commutes with $A$, so $\sigma(k\wedge A)\sigma = -k\wedge A$ and $\mathcal{R}(k\wedge A) = (\Lambda/3 - M/r^{3})\,k\wedge A$; then $(k\wedge B)\cdot\mathcal{R}(k\wedge A) \propto \langle kBkA\rangle = -Q(k)\langle BA\rangle = 0$, so $R(k, A, k, B) = 0$ for all $r$ ($k_{\pm}$ is a principal null direction), and $(B\wedge C)\cdot\mathcal{R}(k\wedge A) = 0$ because $k$ is orthogonal to $A$, $B$, $C$, so $R(k, A, B, C) = 0$. The rotation-gauge field of the chart has $\Omega(\hb(e_{0})) = 0$ and $\Omega(\hb(e_{1})) = -\beta'\,e_{1}e_{0}$, which commutes with $e_{2}$ and $e_{3}$, so the transverse physical frame $e_{2}, e_{3}$ is $D$-parallel along both radial null directions. The check confirms the Ricci map, the transverse eigenvalue, the vanishing of $(k\wedge B)\cdot\mathcal{R}(k\wedge A)$ and $(B\wedge C)\cdot\mathcal{R}(k\wedge A)$ for both signs and all transverse $A, B$, and the parallelism of $e_{2}, e_{3}$, at three rational points of the static region.

\emph{Every admissible cut gives the same data on $\gamma$.} Let $\Sigma$ be a cut through $p$ orthogonal to $k$ with $\chi^{(k)}(p) = 0$. Its tangent plane at $p$ lies in $k^{\perp} = \mathrm{span}(k, E_{\theta}, E_{\phi})$ and is spacelike, so it is $\mathrm{span}(E_{\theta} + a k, E_{\phi} + b k)$ for some $a, b$. Propagate $\Sigma$ along its null generators with affine parameter $\lambda$ (any normalisation of $k$ along $\Sigma$, fixed to $k_{\pm}$ at $p$). By the Raychaudhuri and Sachs equations of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-raychaudhuri-null-congruence}, along the generator $\gamma$ through $p$ the second fundamental form obeys $d\chi_{AB}/d\lambda = -\chi_{AC}\chi^{C}{}_{B} - R(k, A, k, B)$ (zero twist); with $\chi(0) = 0$ and $R(k, A, k, B) = 0$ along $\gamma$, uniqueness for this ordinary differential equation gives $\chi^{(k)} = 0$ on all of $\gamma$, so the expansion and shear vanish there and the area element along $\gamma$ is constant. A connecting vector $Z$ of the generators obeys $\nabla_{k}Z = \nabla_{Z}k = \chi^{(k)}(Z) + \omega(Z)k$, with $\omega$ the rotation one-form of the slicing; along $\gamma$ this is $\omega(Z)k$, so the tangent plane of $\Sigma_{\lambda}$ at $\gamma(\lambda)$ is the parallel transport of the plane at $p$ tilted further along $k$. Since $R(k, A, B, C) = 0$ and $R(k, A, k, B) = 0$, the sectional curvature of $\mathrm{span}(E_{\theta} + a k, E_{\phi} + b k)$ equals that of $\mathrm{span}(E_{\theta}, E_{\phi})$ for all $a, b$ (in GTG: the tilted plane's bivector is $e_{2}\wedge e_{3} + b\,e_{2}\wedge k + a\,k\wedge e_{3}$, and the vanishing above leaves $\langle\mathcal{R}(B')B'^{-1}\rangle = K$; the check confirms this at three tilts each way); and since $E_{\theta}, E_{\phi}$ are parallel, the latter is $R_{\hat\theta\hat\phi\hat\theta\hat\phi}(r(\lambda)) = 2M/r(\lambda)^{3} + \Lambda/3$ with $r(\lambda) = r_{0} \pm \lambda$. By (i), with $\chi^{(k)} = 0$ on $\gamma$, the density on $\gamma$ is $s(\lambda) = -\tfrac{3}{4\Lambda}\cdot 2M/r(\lambda)^{3} = -3M/(2\Lambda r(\lambda)^{3})$, independent of the cut, of $a, b$, of $\omega$ and of $\chi^{(n)}$.

\emph{The change.} For a pencil of generators about $\gamma$ with cross-section area $a_{0}$ at $\lambda = 0$, $S_{\lambda} = \int s\,dA$ over the cross-section at $\lambda$. As $a_{0} \to 0$ with $\lambda$ fixed, $S_{\lambda}/a_{0} \to s(\lambda)\cdot\exp\int_{0}^{\lambda}\theta\,d\lambda' = s(\lambda)$ by continuity of $s$ and of the expansion. This is the thin-pencil limit of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}(H2). So per unit cross-section area $\Delta S = s(0) - s(\lambda_{0}) = -\tfrac{3M}{2\Lambda}(r_{0}^{-3} - (r_{0} \pm \lambda_{0})^{-3})$. With $\lambda_{0} < 0$: outgoing, $r(\lambda_{0}) < r_{0}$ and $\Delta S > 0$; ingoing, $r(\lambda_{0}) > r_{0}$ and $\Delta S < 0$. Expanding, $ds/d\lambda = \alpha\,dK/d\lambda = (-3/4\Lambda)(\mp 6M/r_{0}^{4}) = \pm 9M/(2\Lambda r_{0}^{4})$. The area change is zero (constant area element along $\gamma$), and $\delta Q = \int T_{ab}\chi^{a}k^{b} = 0$ in vacuum. The check evaluates $\Delta S$ against the closed form at three points and two values of $\lambda_{0}$, the signs, and the rate from the jets.

\emph{(iii)} Refutation condition (a) of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise} asks for a class of local horizons whose entropy change is not a universal constant times the area change at leading order. Under (W$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) the radial local horizons of a Schwarzschild-de Sitter hole have $\delta A = 0$ and $\Delta S \neq 0$ at first order, so no $\eta$ works; and the change depends on the curvature at the point through $M/r^{4}$. The Clausius relation (H1) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius} requires $\delta Q = T_{\chi}\,\delta S$ at leading order; here $\delta Q = 0$ and $T_{\chi}\Delta S = (\kappa/2\pi)(\pm 9M/(2\Lambda r_{0}^{4}))|\lambda_{0}| + O(\lambda_{0}^{2})$, which is that theorem's step (6) defect for the integrated reading with $k\cdot\nabla s \neq 0$, so (H1) fails at first order. (Under the differences reading of (H1) the density is to be constant; the Jacobson-Myers functional is an integrated functional whose density varies, so it is not of that form either.) An entropy-production reading $dS = \delta Q/T + d_{i}S$, $d_{i}S \ge 0$ (Eling, Guedens and Jacobson, cited from memory) requires $\Delta S \ge 0$ when $\delta Q = 0$, which the ingoing horizon violates. Robustness: a functional differing from the Jacobson-Myers one by terms that vanish where $\chi^{(k)} = 0$ (the extrinsic terms by which the Wald and Jacobson-Myers forms differ off stationary horizons, the Jacobson-Kang-Myers ambiguity, cited from memory) takes the same values on $\gamma$; one differing by functions of the Ricci tensor differs on $\gamma$ by a constant, since $\mathrm{Ric} = \Lambda g$. synthesis.stelle-west-norm-is-no-local-o.technical:
The Stelle-West vector of the series' MacDowell-Mansouri functional is not an independent datum: by the stored lemma $Q(V)Q(I) = -1$, so its norm is $-3/\Lambda$ automatically. Asking for the norm as an output means releasing it: varying $V$ over all of $I^{\perp}$ in $\int(c_{1}\epsilon(I,V,F,F) + c_{3}\epsilon(I,V,
abla V,
abla V,F) + c_{5}\epsilon(I,V,(
abla V)^{4}))$ with constant couplings, the polynomial family of Cartan gravity with a dynamical symmetry-breaking vector. Because every derivative term puts $V$ into two slots of $\epsilon$, the equation along $V$ is exactly $c_{1}L_{1} + 3c_{3}L_{3} + 5c_{5}L_{5}$, and the tangential components vanish on torsion-free fields. On a torsion-free Einstein block $\mathcal{W} + \kappa\,e\wedge e$ with $V = tV_{c}$ the three densities are $t(\kappa^{2} + |W|^{2}/24)$, $\kappa t^{3}$ and $t^{5}$ times one constant ($6$ in the stored chart): the Weyl part enters only through the MacDowell-Mansouri term. So with that term alone no Stelle-West vector is stationary on the Schwarzschild-de Sitter connection, where $|W|^{2} = 48M^{2}/r^{6}$, while de Sitter is stationary for every norm; with that term and the others, a constant-norm solution needs $|W|^{2}$ constant; without it, the norm is tied to the curvature by $c_{5}/c_{3}$. Couplings depending on the norm are not treated. The Henneaux-Teitelboim promotion is the global version, where the same density is the advance of the conjugate time. Within this family the norm is an input, a global label or a coupling ratio, never a local output.
synthesis.stelle-west-norm-is-no-local-o.lay: In the series' version of a known gravitational action, a fixed vector of a given length (the Stelle-West vector) breaks the symmetry, and its length encodes the cosmological constant. One might hope that letting this vector move freely would make its length, and so the cosmological constant, come out of the equations rather than being put in. This result shows it does not, for the family of actions with fixed coefficients built in the same way. First, in the series the vector's length is not a separate number at all: it is fixed by the length of the frozen point. Second, if the length is allowed to vary from point to point, the new equation demands that a particular measure of tidal curvature vanish everywhere, which rules out black holes while allowing empty expanding space with any length. Adding the two other terms of this family either keeps that problem or ties the length to a ratio of new constants. Coefficients that themselves depend on the length are not covered. Treating the length as one constant for the whole universe is the version that keeps black holes.

The canonical pair solves the stored functional's equations (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west}, Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}), in which variations of $V$ are restricted to the level set of the norm, that is to $\{I, V\}^{\perp}$, where by (ii) they give nothing on torsion-free fields; releasing the norm adds the equation along $V$, which fails. For the de Sitter field $F = 0$, so $L_{1} = 0$ for every $V = tV_{c}$; and the connection equation of the bare functional, $\epsilon(I, 
abla V, F, \cdot) = 0$ (the term $\epsilon(I, V,

abla V = t\,e$ has derived metric $t^{2}g$, whose cosmological constant is $\Lambda/t^{2}$, and $Q(tV_{c}) = -3t^{2}/\Lambda = -3/\Lambda_{t}$ (checked). (b) With $c_{1}
