synthesis.twistor-flat-fields-give-nords.formal:
Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a torsion-free gravitational field on four-dimensional flat spacetime, signature $(+,-,-,-)$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), with store curvature $\mathcal{R}$, Schouten map $\Sch$ and Weyl curvature $\mathcal{W}(A \wedge B) = \mathcal{R}(A \wedge B) - \Sch(A) \wedge B - A \wedge \Sch(B)$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}), and let $F_{T}$ be the field strength of its tractor gauge field $\Omega_{T}(a) = \Omega(a) - 
Inf \wedge \hb^{-1}(a) + 
O \wedge \Sch(\hb^{-1}(a))$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}). Call the field \emph{twistor-flat} on an open region if $F_{T} = 0$ there; by Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-tractor-connection-local-twistor-transport} this is the condition that local twistor transport, the tractor connection acting on the conformal spinor space $\CS$, is path independent on simply connected subregions, so that the one space $\CS$ of the twistor attachment (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment}) is carried unchanged to every point.
 egin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] The field is twistor-flat on a region if and only if $\mathcal{W} = 0$ there, if and only if (Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-weyls-theorem}) about each point there is a gauge with $\hb^{-1}(a) = \phi\,a$, $\phi > 0$; then the scalar curvature is $\mathcal{R} = 6\,\Box\phi/\phi^{3}$ with $\Box = \partial_{t}^{2} - \partial_{x}^{2} - \partial_{y}^{2} - \partial_{z}^{2}$.
\item[(ii)] On a twistor-flat field suppose Einstein's equations $\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a = -8\pi G\,T(a)$ hold with a symmetric stress map $T$ of trace $	au$. Then $S(a) = T(a) - 	frac{	au}{3}a$ has vanishing covariant curl, $(D_{A}S)(B) = (D_{B}S)(A)$ for all vectors $A$, $B$. Hence (a) if $T(a) = (ho + p)(a \cdot u)u - p\,a$ is a conserved perfect fluid ($Q(u) = 1$), then $
ablaho = u\,(u \cdot 
ablaho)$: the density is constant on each rest space of the fluid, for every pressure and every $\Lambda$; (b) if $T = 0$ then $\mathcal{R}(B) = 	frac{\Lambda}{3}B$, constant curvature. So no static perfect-fluid body whose density varies in space, and no vacuum field of nonzero field strength at $\Lambda = 0$ (the Schwarzschild field, gravitational waves), is twistor-flat under Einstein's equations.
\item[(iii)] On the same class Nordstr"om's pair, $\mathcal{W} = 0$ and $\mathcal{R} = -24\pi G\,	au$, is the single equation $\Box\phi = -4\pi G\,	au\,\phi^{3}$ for one function. For every trace $	au$ and Cauchy data $\phi$, $\partial_{t}\phi$ on $t = t_{0}$ its Taylor coefficients are determined order by order with no condition on $	au$, and the Bianchi identities of the gravitational side hold identically, so the coupled system with matter conserved by its own equations is consistent with no condition beyond that conservation. Its static weak field obeys $
abla^{2}(\phi - 1) = 4\pi Gho$, the Newtonian field; the trace of Einstein's equations on the class, $\mathcal{R} = 8\pi G	au + 4\Lambda$, gives at $\Lambda = 0$ instead $
abla^{2}(\phi - 1) = -	frac{4\pi}{3}Gho$, repulsive at one third of Newton's strength.
\item[(iv)] Hence the consistency conditions of a coupled system of matter and a twistor-flat gravitational field (Bianchi identities, conservation of the stress, gauge covariance, second order, the Newtonian static limit) are met by Nordstr"om's equations, which are not Einstein's; by Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-lovelock-and-anderson-duchamp-natural-lagrangians}(a), Einstein's equations with free $G$ and $\Lambda$ follow only once a divergence-free natural map of the field of second order is equated to the whole stress map, that is, under the clause that the whole stress map is the source, which these conditions do not supply. The classification of the points with $\mathcal{W} 
eq 0$ by Petrov type, with the subspaces of $\CS$ that stay parallel there, is the result \claimref{synthesis.attachment-transport-is-flat-only-where-weyl-vanishes}.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.twistor-flat-fields-give-nords.technical:
Work with a torsion-free gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on four-dimensional flat spacetime and its tractor gauge field $\Omega_{T}$, the $\Cl(2,4)$ connection whose action on conformal spinors is local twistor transport. Call the field twistor-flat where the field strength $F_{T}$ of $\Omega_{T}$ vanishes: there the one conformal spinor space $\CS$ used by the twistor attachment is carried unchanged from point to point.

(i) A field is twistor-flat exactly where its Weyl curvature vanishes, that is, locally $\hb^{-1}(a) = \phi\,a$, and then $\mathcal{R} = 6\,\Box\phi/\phi^{3}$.

(ii) If such a field satisfies Einstein's equations with stress $T$, the Cotton block of $F_{T}$ forces $T - \tfrac{\tau}{3}g$ to have vanishing covariant curl. For a conserved perfect fluid this means the density is constant on each rest space; in vacuum the field has constant curvature. Isolated perfect-fluid bodies, inhomogeneous static perfect fluids, the Schwarzschild field and gravitational waves are all outside the class.

(iii) Nordstr\"om's equations, $\mathcal{W} = 0$ and $\mathcal{R} = -24\pi G\tau$, reduce on the class to $\Box\phi = -4\pi G\tau\phi^{3}$, which can be solved order by order for every trace, so they impose nothing on the matter beyond its own conservation; their static weak field is Newton's. The trace of Einstein's equations on the class has the opposite sign and gives a repulsive field of one third of Newton's strength. Nordstr\"om's theory is excluded by observation (no light deflection, a perihelion shift of minus one sixth of Einstein's); it serves as a consistent counter-model.

(iv) So the consistency conditions of the coupled system on twistor-flat fields (Bianchi identities, conservation, second order, Newtonian limit) hold for Nordstr\"om's equations, which are not Einstein's; with Lovelock's theorem, Einstein's equations follow only under the clause that the whole stress map, not its trace, is the source.
synthesis.twistor-flat-fields-give-nords.lay: The series attaches its quantum particles to spacetime through twistors, a space that is the same at every point only where the gravitational field has no tidal part of a particular kind (the Weyl curvature, the part that bends light around a star and travels as gravitational waves). Such fields are rescalings of flat spacetime. If Einstein's equations hold on them, the matter they contain must be spread evenly in its own rest frame: a star or a lumpy dust cloud cannot sit in such a field, and empty space can curve only uniformly, so the space outside a body is not of this kind. On the same fields an older theory of gravity, Nordstr\"om's, in which only the trace of the matter's stress-energy sources gravity, works for any matter at all, satisfies every consistency requirement, and reproduces Newton's law. It is ruled out by observation (it bends no light, and it gives the wrong advance of Mercury's perihelion, minus one sixth of Einstein's), so it is a counterexample to the logic, not a viable theory. So requiring the coupled system of matter and gravity to be consistent on the fields where the twistors attach does not single out Einstein's equations; something more is needed: the rule that the whole stress-energy, not only its trace, is the source, or an attachment of the particles that works where the Weyl curvature is nonzero.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} Conventions are those of Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields} and Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}: signature $(+,-,-,-)$, store curvature $\mathcal{R}(B) = -R(\hb(B))$, Ricci map $\mathcal{R}(b) = \partial_{a} \cdot \mathcal{R}(a \wedge b)$, scalar $\mathcal{R} = \partial_{a} \cdot \mathcal{R}(a)$, Einstein map $\mathcal{G}(a) = \mathcal{R}(a) - 	frac12 a\,\mathcal{R}$, field equation $\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a = -8\pi G\,T(a)$ (de Sitter has $\mathcal{R}(B) = 	frac{\Lambda}{3}B$, $\mathcal{R} = 4\Lambda$), Schouten map $\Sch(a) = 	frac12(\mathcal{R}(a) - 	frac16 a\,\mathcal{R})$, and $\mathcal{R}(A \wedge B) = \mathcal{W}(A \wedge B) + \Sch(A) \wedge B + A \wedge \Sch(B)$. $D_{A}$ is the covariant derivative along $A$; for a map $S$ of vectors, $(D_{A}S)(B) = D_{A}(S(B)) - S(D_{A}B)$.

\emph{(i).} By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}(iv) the field strength $F_{T}$ of $\Omega_{T}$ has three blocks: the spacetime (Lorentz) block $-\mathcal{W}(A \wedge B)$, the $
Inf$ block the torsion, zero here, and the $
O$ block the Cotton term $(D_{A}\Sch)(B) - (D_{B}\Sch)(A)$. So $F_{T} = 0$ implies $\mathcal{W} = 0$. Conversely let $\mathcal{W} = 0$ on a region. By Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-weyls-theorem} about each point there is a gauge with $\hb^{-1}(a) = \phi\,a$. By Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-tractor-connection-local-twistor-transport}(i) the tractor connection is a connection of the conformal class: a change of scale acts on $\Omega_{T}$ as a gauge transformation by a rotor of the parabolic subgroup, under which $F_{T}$ transforms by conjugation. In the flat scale $\phi = 1$ ($\Omega = 0$, $\Sch = 0$) one has $\Omega_{T}(a) = -
Inf \wedge a$, constant, so $F_{T}(a \wedge b) = \Omega_{T}(a) 	imes \Omega_{T}(b)$; since $
Inf$ is null and orthogonal to $a$ and $b$, $(
Inf \wedge a)(
Inf \wedge b) = 
Inf a 
Inf b = -
Inf^{2}ab = 0$ and likewise in the other order, so the commutator vanishes and $F_{T} = 0$; hence $F_{T} = 0$ in every scale of the class. The twistor attachment works with one conformal spinor space $\CS$ (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment}). Part (ii) of the same Fact makes local twistor transport the spin action of $\Omega_{T}$ on $\CS$, a bivector $B$ acting by left multiplication $\psi \mapsto 	frac12 B\psi$; this is the defining representation of $\su(2,2)$ on the four-dimensional space $\CS$, which is faithful (left multiplication by a nonzero bivector of $\Cl(2,4)$ is nonzero on $\CS$), so twistor transport is flat exactly where $F_{T} = 0$; a flat connection has trivial transport around every contractible loop, and a nonzero field strength gives a nontrivial transport around small loops in its plane at second order (the standard relation between curvature and holonomy, cited from memory). The points with $\mathcal{W} 
eq 0$ are classified by Petrov type in the result \claimref{synthesis.attachment-transport-is-flat-only-where-weyl-vanishes}; only the flat case is used here. The check computes $F_{T}$ in all blocks at two rational points of two conformally flat fields with nonzero scalar curvature and finds it zero, and on a field that is not conformally flat finds $F_{T} 
eq 0$ with spacetime block $-\mathcal{W}$. The formula $\mathcal{R} = 6\,\Box\phi/\phi^{3}$ is the standard conformal-change formula of the scalar curvature in the store's sign; the check computes $\mathcal{R}$ from the field strength by exact Taylor jets at four points of two fields and confirms it.

\emph{(ii).} From the field equation, taking the trace ($\partial_{a} \cdot a = 4$, $\partial_{a} \cdot \mathcal{G}(a) = -\mathcal{R}$), $\mathcal{R} = 4\Lambda + 8\pi G	au$, so $\mathcal{R}(a) = -8\pi G\,(T(a) - 	frac{	au}{2}a) + \Lambda a$ and
\[
\Sch(a) = 	frac12 igl(-8\pi G\,(T(a) - 	frac{	au}{2}a) + \Lambda a - 	frac16 a\,(4\Lambda + 8\pi G	au) igr) = -4\pi G\,S(a) + 	frac{\Lambda}{6}a, \qquad S(a) = T(a) - 	frac{	au}{3}a .
\]
By (i) the field is twistor-flat, so the Cotton block vanishes: $(D_{A}\Sch)(B) = (D_{B}\Sch)(A)$. Since $D_{A}\,\id = 0$ (the covariant derivative is metric and torsion-free) and $\Lambda$ is constant, this is $-4\pi G\,((D_{A}S)(B) - (D_{B}S)(A)) = 0$, the curl condition.

(a) In the index reading ($S_{bc} = w\,u_{b}u_{c} - 	frac{ho}{3}g_{bc}$ with $w = ho + p$, which is $S$ for the perfect fluid since $	au = ho - 3p$), contract the curl $
abla_{a}S_{bc} - 
abla_{b}S_{ac}$ with $u^{b}u^{c}$. Using $u^{c}
abla_{a}u_{c} = 0$ (from $Q(u) = 1$), $u^{b}u^{c}
abla_{a}S_{bc} = 
abla_{a}f$ with $f = 	frac23ho + p$, and $u^{b}u^{c}
abla_{b}S_{ac} = u^{b}
abla_{b}(f u_{a}) - S_{ac}\dot u^{c} = \dot f u_{a} + f\dot u_{a} + 	frac{ho}{3}\dot u_{a} = \dot f u_{a} + w\dot u_{a}$, where a dot is $u \cdot 
abla$. So
\[
u^{b}u^{c}(
abla_{a}S_{bc} - 
abla_{b}S_{ac}) = 
abla_{a}f - u_{a}\dot f - w\,\dot u_{a} .
\]
This is an identity among first derivatives of covariant quantities, so it holds on every field once it holds at a point of the flat field for arbitrary first jets (at any point one may choose the gauge in which the connection vanishes there); the check verifies it exactly at a rational point for two sets of polynomial $ho$, $p$ and a unit $u$ given by a rational parametrisation. Conservation of $T$, $
abla^{b}T_{ab} = u_{a}
abla^{b}(w u_{b}) + w\dot u_{a} - 
abla_{a}p = 0$, projected orthogonally to $u$, gives $w\dot u_{a} = 
abla_{a}p - u_{a}\dot p$. Substituting, the contraction equals $	frac23(
abla_{a}ho - u_{a}\dotho)$; the check verifies this combination as well. The curl condition makes it zero, so $
ablaho = u\,(u \cdot 
ablaho)$. For static dust with varying density the curl is nonzero: with $u = e_{t}$, $p = 0$ on the flat field its contraction has spatial components $	frac23
ablaho$, as the check confirms. This agrees with Stephani's classification of conformally flat perfect fluids (cited from memory), whose densities are constant on the rest spaces.

(b) If $T = 0$ then $\Sch = 	frac{\Lambda}{6}\id$ and $\mathcal{W} = 0$ give $\mathcal{R}(A \wedge B) = 	frac{\Lambda}{6}(A \wedge B + A \wedge B) = 	frac{\Lambda}{3}A \wedge B$; the check confirms this on the conformally flat de Sitter fields $\phi = 1/(1 - \Lambda Q(x)/12)$ for two values of $\Lambda$ at two points each. At $\Lambda = 0$ the field strength vanishes. The Schwarzschild field has vanishing Ricci map and $\mathcal{R}(\sigma_{r}) = 	frac{2M}{r^{3}}\sigma_{r}$ (dictionary, store sign), so $\mathcal{W} = \mathcal{R} 
eq 0$; a gravitational wave at $\Lambda = 0$ is a vacuum field of nonzero field strength, hence $\mathcal{W} 
eq 0$ by (b). Neither is twistor-flat.

\emph{(iii).} On $\hb^{-1}(a) = \phi\,a$, $\mathcal{W} = 0$ identically by (i), and by (i) $\mathcal{R} = -24\pi G	au$ reads $6\,\Box\phi/\phi^{3} = -24\pi G	au$, that is $\Box\phi = -4\pi G	au\phi^{3}$. Solving for $\partial_{t}^{2}\phi$, the Taylor coefficient of $\phi$ with time exponent $k + 2$ is fixed by coefficients of time exponent at most $k + 1$ (the spatial Laplacian keeps the time exponent, and the product $	au\phi^{3}$ involves only coefficients of $\phi$ with time exponent at most $k$), so from Cauchy data every coefficient is determined, and no equation constrains $	au$, since there is one equation for one unknown and no differential identity links it to the matter. The check carries this out to total order four for a trace depending on $t$, $x$, $y$, $z$, builds the field, computes its scalar curvature from the field strength as a jet, and finds $\mathcal{R} + 24\pi G	au = 0$ through jet order two (with $4\pi G$ carried as a rational formal value), while a different trace fails; the field's tractor field strength is zero at a second point. For analytic data the formal solution converges (Cauchy-Kovalevskaya), and for smooth data local existence holds by the standard theory of semilinear wave equations (both cited from memory); only the formal statement is used for consistency. The Bianchi identities hold for the field strength of every gauge field. The matter is conserved by its own equations, as for any matter coupled through the derived metric (displacement-gauge invariance of the matter action); the gravitational equations add no condition, unlike Einstein's, whose contracted Bianchi identity requires $
abla \cdot T = 0$ of the source. For a static weak field $\phi = 1 + \psi$, to first order $\Box\phi = -
abla^{2}\psi$, so Nordstr"om's equation gives $
abla^{2}\psi = 4\pi Gho$ (dust, $	au = ho$), and since $g_{tt} = \phi^{2} = 1 + 2\psi + \dots$ a slow test body moves in the Newtonian potential $\psi$. The trace of Einstein's equations, $\mathcal{R} = 4\Lambda + 8\pi G	au$ from (ii), gives at $\Lambda = 0$ instead $-6
abla^{2}\psi = 8\pi Gho$, $
abla^{2}\psi = -	frac{4\pi}{3}Gho$. These equations are Nordstr"om's theory in the form of Einstein and Fokker (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-nordstrom-scalar-theory-einstein-fokker-form}); the computation above re-derives what is used.

\emph{(iv).} By (iii), Nordstr"om's equations on twistor-flat fields satisfy the Bianchi identities, are compatible with the conservation of every stress, are covariant (both equations are statements about the field strength and the stress trace), are of second order in $\phi$, and have the Newtonian static limit; by (ii) they are not Einstein's equations, which on this class have no solution with a perfect-fluid source of varying rest density, whereas Nordstr"om's equations are solvable for every trace. So these consistency conditions do not imply Einstein's equations. Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-lovelock-and-anderson-duchamp-natural-lagrangians}(a) gives the step that does: a natural symmetric map of the field, of second order and divergence-free for every field, is $c_{1}\mathcal{G}(a) + c_{2}a$; equating such a map to a multiple of $T(a)$ gives Einstein's equations with free $G$ and $\Lambda$. Nordstr"om's equations are not of that form (the Weyl condition is unsourced and the scalar equation sees only $	au$), so the clause that the whole stress map is the source is what separates the two, and it is not among the consistency conditions. Nordstr"om's theory is excluded by observation (null geodesics are conformally invariant, so it deflects no light; its perihelion shift is minus one sixth of Einstein's; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-nordstrom-scalar-theory-einstein-fokker-form}): it serves here as a consistent counter-model, not as a candidate theory.

synthesis.vacuum-field-stress-tensor-is-.formal:
Let $g$ be the derived metric, of signature $(1,3)$, of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), $x$ a point of its invertible region, and use the tractor connection of Fact \claimref{interior.imported-tractor-connection} (on flat spacetime the $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field $\Omega_{T}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}) in the splitting of $g$. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-condition-is-infinity-vacuum-incidence}(2) the pairing classes of the canonical tractors along a physical vector $v \in T_xM$ are
\[
\omega_v(I_g, w) = -\Sch(v, w), \qquad \omega_v(X, w) = g(v, w),
\]
for $w$ in the $\mu$ slot, independent of how the vacua are extended off $x$. Call a symmetric tensor $\Theta$ at $x$ a \emph{first-order vacuum-field tensor} if $\Theta = L(\Sch) + c\,g$ with $L$ linear and $c$ a number (that is, $\Theta$ is an affine function of these classes) and $L$ is equivariant under the stabiliser of $(I_g, X)$ in the tractor orthogonal group, which acts on the $\mu$ slot as $O(1,3)$. Write $\kappa := 4\pi G$ for a constant $G > 0$ and $J = g^{ab}\Sch_{ab}$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Form.)} $\Theta = a\,\Sch + b\,J g + c\,g$ for numbers $a, b, c$.
\item \emph{(Dichotomy.)} The matter clause of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-condition-is-infinity-vacuum-incidence}(7) with source $\Theta$, $\omega_{\ell}(I_g, \ell) = \kappa\,\Theta(\ell, \ell)$ for every real null $\ell$ at $x$, is $(1 + \kappa a)\,\Sch(\ell, \ell) = 0$ for every real null $\ell$. Hence either (a) $a = -1/\kappa$, and the clause holds for every $\Sch$; or (b) $a \neq -1/\kappa$, the clause holds only where $\Sch = \tfrac{J}{4}g$ ($x$ an Einstein point), and there $\Theta = (\tfrac{a}{4} + b)J\,g + c\,g$ is pure trace, with $\Theta(\ell,\ell) = 0$ for every null $\ell$.
\item \emph{(Conservation.)} If $\Theta$ is built this way at every point of a region, then $\nabla^a\Theta_{ab} = (a + b)\nabla_b J$, by the contracted Bianchi identity $\nabla^a\Sch_{ab} = \nabla_b J$. In case (a), $\Theta$ is conserved for every metric if and only if $b = 1/\kappa$, and then
\[
\Theta = -\frac{1}{8\pi G}\Bigl(\Ric - \tfrac12 R\,g\Bigr) + c\,g, \qquad \Ric + 8\pi G\,\Theta = \Bigl(\tfrac12 R + 8\pi G\,c\Bigr)g
\]
identically in the store's convention: the Einstein equation of clause (7) holds for every metric with $T := \Theta$, which is a definition of the source.
\item \emph{(Consequence.)} If the source $T$ in clause (7) can take, at a point with given $\Sch$, values with different $T(\ell,\ell)$ (so that the clause is a relation between independent data and can fail), or can have $T(\ell,\ell) \neq 0$ for some null $\ell$, then $T$ is not a first-order vacuum-field tensor. A matter law in the form of clause (7) needs a symmetric tensor that is not a covariant affine function of the canonical classes, together with a hypothesis tying it to them. The statement concerns first-order classes only: a source that is not a function of them, such as an independent $T(k,k)$ given as the density of the generator of null translations of a field theory on the patch, is not excluded by it.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.vacuum-field-stress-tensor-is-.technical: The incidence theorem reads Einstein's equations as a condition on the vacua annihilated by the pure-scale tractor: along its own light ray each such vacuum is excited by an amount that should equal $4\pi G$ times the matter's null energy. An earlier remark argued that a stress tensor defined on the CAR side, linearly, would need a second algebra; this result makes that precise. The first-order data of the vacuum field that do not depend on how the field is extended off a point are the classes of the two canonical tractors: $-\Sch(v,w)$ for the infinity vacua and $g(v,w)$ for the point vacua. A symmetric tensor built from them linearly and covariantly, that is equivariantly for their common stabiliser, which acts on the tangent space as the Lorentz group, must be $a\Sch + bJg + cg$: an exact computation shows that the linear maps of symmetric two-tensors commuting with a rational boost, two rational rotations and two reflections form a two-dimensional space, spanned by the identity and the trace map, which is Schur's lemma for the Lorentz group here. Since a null vector has $g(\ell,\ell) = 0$, the matter clause with such a source is $(1 + 4\pi G a)\Sch(\ell,\ell) = 0$ on the null cone. Either $a = -1/4\pi G$ and the clause holds in every metric, or it forces $\Sch$ to be pure trace at the point, where the source is pure trace too and no null energy flows. In the first branch, asking the source to be conserved in every metric fixes $b$ by the contracted Bianchi identity $\nabla^a\Sch_{ab} = \nabla_b J$, and the source is the Einstein tensor over $8\pi G$ (in the sphere-positive convention, minus the store-convention one) plus a cosmological term: Einstein's equation then holds identically because it is how the source was defined. In neither branch is the matter clause a law relating matter to geometry. (The conservation step is the linear case of Lovelock's theorem; the form is Schur's lemma.) So a source that can vary independently of the curvature at a point, the kind a matter law needs, is not a function of the vacuum field's first-order classes: it needs a further datum, a state on some algebra (for the series, the field theory's tower algebra, which is a different object from the tractor Clifford bundle that carries the vacua) or a second algebra, and a hypothesis tying it to the classes, which on the Clausius route is the hypothesis (H1) of the Einstein derivation. The classes of non-canonical vacuum sections are excluded because they depend on how the vacuum field is extended, a choice, not on the metric. The result is limited to sources read off the first-order classes; an independent null energy density, such as the density of the generator of null translations of a field theory on the patch, is not excluded and is an instance of the further datum. The checks verify the class formulas, the commutant dimension, the dichotomy on eleven null directions for three sample triples $(a,b,c)$ and for $a = -1/\kappa$, the contracted Bianchi identity at a point of a metric with generic second and third derivatives, and the Einstein-tensor identity of the conserved branch.
synthesis.vacuum-field-stress-tensor-is-.lay: In the series, Einstein's equations can be read as a statement about certain quantum vacuum states: along its own light ray each of them is disturbed by exactly the energy that matter carries along that ray. A natural hope is to find the matter's energy on the same quantum side, built from how those vacua are disturbed. This result shows that this cannot work if the matter's energy is built linearly, and without singling out a direction, from those disturbances. Any such recipe gives one of two things. Either the "matter" is just the curvature itself relabelled, so Einstein's equations hold automatically because they define the matter, or the recipe allows no matter flowing along light rays at all, only a cosmological-constant-like term. In neither case do the equations say anything about how real matter sources the gravitational field. A real matter law needs something the vacuum disturbances do not carry: a separate quantum state of matter, or a second quantum system, and a rule linking it to the geometry.

synthesis.weyl-flat-variations-carry-onl.formal:
Let $V$ be the vectors of $\Cl(1,3)$, signature $(+,-,-,-)$, with frame $\{e_{a}\}$ and reciprocal frame $\{e^{a}\}$, and consider gravitational fields $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}; only its clauses (i) to (e) are used, not the field equation (f)) at first order about $\hb = \id$, $\Omega = 0$: the derived metric is $g(a, b) = a \cdot b + h(a) \cdot b$ with $h$ a symmetric linear map of $V$. Fix a nonzero $p \in V$ and the field $h(x) = \tfrac12 (p \cdot x)^{2} h_{0}$, $h_{0} \in \mathrm{Sym}$ (the symmetric maps, dimension $10$); its first-order curvature is the constant map $\mathcal{R}_{p}[h_{0}](B) = -\tfrac12\,p \wedge h_{0}(B \cdot p)$ (up to the overall sign of the curvature convention, on which nothing below depends), with Ricci map, scalar $\mathcal{R}_{p}$, Schouten map and Weyl map $\mathcal{W}_{p}[h_{0}]$ formed as in Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}. A displacement $x \mapsto x + \tfrac12 (p \cdot x)^{2}\xi$ changes $h_{0}$ by $a \mapsto (a \cdot p)\xi + (a \cdot \xi)p$; these form the gauge space $G_{p}$. Write $L = \R\,\id$ (the conformal direction, $\hb^{-1}(a) = \phi\,a$ at first order). A \emph{conserved source at $p$} is $T_{0} \in \mathrm{Sym}$ with $T_{0}(p) = 0$; pair $h_{0}$ with $T_{0}$ by $\ip{h_{0}}{T_{0}} = \sum_{a} e^{a} \cdot h_{0}(T_{0}(e_{a}))$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Kernels; proved.)} $\ker \mathcal{R}_{p} = G_{p}$ (dimension $4$) and $\ker \mathcal{W}_{p} = G_{p} \oplus L$ (dimension $5$), for every nonzero $p$, null or not. The kernel of the scalar $h_{0} \mapsto \mathcal{R}_{p}[h_{0}]$ has dimension $9$ and contains $G_{p}$; the scalar of $\id$ is $3\,Q(p)$, so for $Q(p) \neq 0$ this kernel is $G_{p} \oplus C_{p}$ with $C_{p} \cap L = 0$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Exactly four covariant classes; proved for $Q(p) \neq 0$.)} The stabiliser of $p$ in the Lorentz group preserves $G_{p}$, and its commutant on the six-dimensional quotient $\mathrm{Sym}/G_{p}$ has dimension $2$. Hence $\mathrm{Sym}/G_{p}$ is the sum of two inequivalent irreducible pieces, the images of $L$ (dimension $1$) and of $C_{p}$ (dimension $5$), and the subspaces of $\mathrm{Sym}$ that contain $G_{p}$ (closed under displacements) and are invariant under the stabiliser are exactly $G_{p}$, $G_{p} \oplus L$, $G_{p} \oplus C_{p}$ and $\mathrm{Sym}$. The second is the tangent space of the Weyl-flat fields; by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.twistor-flat-fields-give-nordstrom-not-einstein}(i) these are the twistor-flat fields, the domain on which the twistor attachment is carried by transport. At null $p$ the stabiliser is not reductive and the count fails (computed at $p = e_{0} + e_{1}$): with $N_{p}$ the two transverse trace-free (helicity-two) directions, $G_{p} \oplus N_{p}$ and $G_{p} \oplus L \oplus N_{p}$ are further invariant classes, and the scalar-flat kernel contains $L$, so there are at least six. Clauses (iii) and (iv) do not use (ii).
\item[(iii)] \emph{(What each class sees of a conserved source; proved.)} The conserved sources at $p$ form a space of dimension $6$; the pairing vanishes on $G_{p}$ and is nondegenerate between $\mathrm{Sym}/G_{p}$ and the conserved sources. A conserved source annihilates $G_{p} \oplus L$ if and only if its trace $\tau = \tr T_{0}$ vanishes, and (for $Q(p) \neq 0$) annihilates $G_{p} \oplus C_{p}$ if and only if $T_{0}(a) = \lambda\,(Q(p)\,a - (a \cdot p)\,p)$. So a field equation obtained by varying the field only within the Weyl-flat class, $\ip{\delta h_{0}}{E_{0} + \kappa T_{0}} = 0$ for $\delta h_{0} \in G_{p} \oplus L$, is one condition on the trace of the source and leaves its five trace-free components free (Nordstr\"om's coupling, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-nordstrom-scalar-theory-einstein-fokker-form}); varying within $\mathrm{Sym}$ gives all six.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The null flux is the trace-free channel; proved.)} A symmetric map $T$ is determined by its null fluxes $k \cdot T(k)$, $Q(k) = 0$, up to adding $c\,\id$. A conserved source at $p \neq 0$ that is a multiple of $\id$ is zero. Hence if $X = E_{0} + \kappa T_{0}$ is conserved at $p \neq 0$ and its trace-free part vanishes, then $X = 0$: the trace-free channel together with conservation fixes the whole conserved source at every nonzero momentum, leaving only a constant multiple of $\id$ (a cosmological term) at $p = 0$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Response of minimally coupled matter; proved, standard.)} If a matter Lagrangian density depends on the gravitational field only through $\hb$ applied to its derivatives (as an outermorphism on a field strength) and the factor $(\det \hb)^{-1}$, its derivative along $\hb = \id + t\,\delta$ at $t = 0$ is $\sum_{a} \delta(e_{a}) \cdot T(e^{a})$ with $T$ its $\hb$-response stress map. For a scalar field this is the canonical stress of displacements. For Maxwell matter, with density $\tfrac12\br{\hb(F)^{2}}/\det\hb$ for a field strength bivector $F = \nabla \wedge A$ held fixed, it is the symmetric gauge-invariant stress $T(a) = -\tfrac12 FaF$, the Belinfante-improved canonical stress (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-maxwell-stress-spacetime-algebra}) and its response to $\delta = \id$ vanishes; for a scalar field it is $(a \cdot \nabla\phi)\nabla\phi - a\,\mathcal{L}$, of trace $-Q(\nabla\phi) + 2m^{2}\phi^{2}$. More generally a density that depends on $\hb$ algebraically and is unchanged under $\hb \mapsto c\,\hb$ for constant $c$ has zero response along $\id$ at each point, so such matter (the Maxwell field) does not couple at first order to variations within the Weyl-flat class; for the massless Dirac field the same holds classically, on shell, since its stress has trace proportional to the mass (standard, cited from memory, not checked here); at the quantum level the trace anomaly contains a scheme-dependent $\Box\mathcal{R}$ term, first order in $h$ and nonzero on $L$ (the scalar of $\id$ is $3\,Q(p)$), so this decoupling is classical.
\item[(vi)] \emph{(One coupling; computed, standard.)} For point sources coupled through the field with strengths $\kappa_{n}\,p_{n} \cdot h_{0}(p_{n})$, invariance under $h_{0} \mapsto h_{0} + q \otimes \xi + \xi \otimes q$ requires $\sum_{n} s_{n}\kappa_{n}\,p_{n} = 0$ ($s_{n} = \pm 1$ for incoming and outgoing), which on the momentum-conserving configuration of five momenta spanning $V$ computed here (one linear relation among them) forces all $\kappa_{n}$ equal; with more momenta the condition must be imposed on every conserved configuration, as in Weinberg's argument; a source with $Q(p_{n}) = 0$ has zero coupling to $L$.
\item[(vii)] \emph{(Reading; argued.)} Displacement gauge invariance does not give the whole-stress clause: the Weyl-flat class is closed under displacements and gives the trace coupling. Under an action principle in which matter is minimally coupled and the field is varied in the five directions $C_{p}$ that leave the Weyl-flat class, the source is the whole response of (v), and by (iv) its trace-free part already fixes it up to the cosmological term; with Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-lovelock-and-anderson-duchamp-natural-lagrangians}(a) the second-order field equations are then Einstein's. The clause is therefore equivalent, at first order and under that action principle, to the matter theory being defined and varied off the attachment's domain; the Maxwell field (and, classically, the massless Dirac field) confined to that domain does not gravitate at first order. For matter with spin, $\Omega$ is varied independently (the Einstein-Cartan choice of the definition): the $\hb$-response is then the canonical stress, whose antisymmetric part enters the antisymmetric part of the $\hb$ equation, while the $\Omega$ equation ties the torsion to the spin density; after the torsion is eliminated the symmetric source is the Belinfante stress plus a spin-spin contact term of order $\kappa$, second order in the coupling, so at first order the channels of (iii) and (iv) apply to the Belinfante stress (standard, cited from memory). The quantum stress must stay conserved for (iv) to apply: for chiral matter this needs the mixed gravitational anomaly to cancel (argued).
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.weyl-flat-variations-carry-onl.technical: The open problem asks for the clause that the whole stress map, not its trace, is the gravitational source, to be derived from the field theory. This result works at first order about flat spacetime in Gauge Theory Gravity and asks which variations of the position-gauge field $\hb$ see which parts of the stress. At a momentum $p$ the symmetric perturbations $h_{0}$ (ten) split into the displacement gauge directions $G_{p}$ (four), the conformal line $L$ (one) and five further directions. Exact computations at the Lorentz-orbit representatives of every nonzero momentum show that the first-order curvature vanishes exactly on $G_{p}$ and the first-order Weyl curvature exactly on $G_{p} \oplus L$; the commutant of the stabiliser of $p$ on the six non-gauge directions is two-dimensional, so at every non-null momentum there are exactly four classes of fields closed under displacements and covariant under that stabiliser: gauge only, Weyl-flat (Nordstr\"om), scalar-flat, and all fields. At null momentum, the momentum of radiation, the stabiliser is not reductive and there are further classes, among them gauge plus the two helicity-two directions; the pairing statements below hold there too. The Weyl-flat class is the domain of the twistor attachment (stored). Pairing with a conserved source, the Weyl-flat class sees only its trace and leaves its five trace-free components free; all fields see all six. The null fluxes $k \cdot T(k)$ that the Clausius route uses determine $T$ up to a multiple of the identity, so they are exactly the trace-free channel, and a conserved source with no trace-free part is zero at nonzero momentum (the unimodular mechanism), which is why that route returns $\Lambda$ as an integration constant. The response of minimally coupled matter to $\hb$ is its $\hb$-response stress: for the Maxwell field the symmetric gauge-invariant (Belinfante) stress $-\tfrac12 FaF$, with zero response to the conformal direction, and for a scalar the canonical stress, with nonzero trace. For Dirac matter, under the Einstein-Cartan choice, the first-order symmetric source is the Belinfante stress and the spin contact term is second order; its decoupling from the conformal direction when massless is classical, the trace anomaly being first order there. Point sources coupled through the field must share one coupling, and massless ones do not couple to the conformal line. The reading: gauge invariance does not give the clause, since the Weyl-flat class is closed under displacements and yields Nordstr\"om's coupling; under an action principle with minimal coupling the clause is equivalent to varying the field off the attachment's domain, where the Maxwell field (and, classically, the massless Dirac field) would otherwise not gravitate at first order. Standard pieces (the spin-zero and spin-two split, Einstein-Fokker, unimodular gravity, Weinberg's universality) are re-derived in the spacetime algebra; new is their placement against the attachment's domain and the Clausius route.
synthesis.weyl-flat-variations-carry-onl.lay: Einstein's theory says that everything about matter's energy, momentum and pressure is a source of the gravitational field. An older rival, Nordstr\"om's, used only one number made from them, their trace, and is ruled out because it does not deflect light. The series wants to derive Einstein's rule from its own field theory. This result shows what that requires. If gravity's field is only allowed to change in the ways that keep the derived metric a rescaling of the flat one, which are exactly the fields where the series' twistors can be attached, then it responds only to the trace, as in Nordstr\"om's theory, and light and other massless fields do not affect it at all, even though this restricted theory respects every change of coordinates. The full rule needs the field to be able to change in five further ways that leave those fields. (For waves moving at the speed of light the bookkeeping has a few more cases, but the conclusion is the same.) The light-ray form of Einstein's equations used elsewhere in the series sees exactly the part that the trace misses, and energy conservation then fills in the rest, up to a cosmological constant. So the missing step is not a symmetry; it is that the matter theory must work, and be varied, beyond the fields where the twistors attach.

\emph{(i)} $\ker \mathcal{R}_{p} \supseteq G_{p}$ because a pure displacement has zero curvature; directly, $h_{0} = p \otimes \xi + \xi \otimes p$ gives $h_{0}(B \cdot p) = ((B \cdot p) \cdot \xi)\,p$ since $(B \cdot p) \cdot p = 0$, so $p \wedge h_{0}(B \cdot p) = 0$. The check finds $\dim\ker\mathcal{R}_{p} = 4 = \dim G_{p}$ at the representatives, so equality holds (computed exactly, proved for every $p$ by covariance). \emph{(ii)} Let $H_{p}$ be the stabiliser of $p$. eq 0$. By (i), $G_{p} \oplus L = \ker\mathcal{W}_{p}$ is the first-order tangent space of the Weyl-flat fields, which by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.twistor-flat-fields-give-nordstrom-not-einstein}(i) are the twistor-flat fields.

\emph{(iii)} $T_{0}(p) = 0$ is four linear conditions of rank $4$, so the conserved sources form a space of dimension $6$ (computed). For $h_{0} = p \otimes \xi + \xi \otimes p$, $\ip{h_{0}}{T_{0}} = 2\,\xi \cdot T_{0}(p) = 0$. The check finds the pairing matrix of $\mathrm{Sym}$ against the conserved sources of rank $6$, so the induced pairing of the six-dimensional $\mathrm{Sym}/G_{p}$ with the conserved sources is nondegenerate. Since $\ip{\id}{T_{0}} = 	r T_{0} = 	au$, the conserved sources annihilating $G_{p} \oplus L$ are those with $	au = 0$, a space of dimension $5$ (computed: the annihilator has dimension $5$ and consists of trace-free maps). For $Q(p) 
eq 0$ the annihilator of $K_{p}$ has dimension $6 - 5 = 1$; the map $T_{0}(a) = Q(p)\,a - (a \cdot p)\,p$ is conserved ($T_{0}(p) = 0$) and invariant under $H_{p}$, and the check finds the computed annihilator equal to its span. A field equation from varying within a class $U \supseteq G_{p}$, $\ip{\delta h_{0}}{X} = 0$ for $\delta h_{0} \in U$ with $X = E_{0} + \kappa T_{0}$ conserved (the gravitational side conserved by the Noether identity of displacements, the matter side by its own equations), constrains $X$ exactly modulo the annihilator of $U$: for $U = G_{p} \oplus L$ it is the single condition $	r X = 0$, and the trace-free part of $T_{0}$ (five components) does not enter, which is Nordstr"om's coupling (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-nordstrom-scalar-theory-einstein-fokker-form}, $\mathcal{R} = -24\pi G	au$ with $\mathcal{W} = 0$); for $U = \mathrm{Sym}$ it is $X = 0$, all six.

\emph{(iv)} The map $T \mapsto (k \cdot T(k))_{k}$ over twelve rational null vectors $k$ (among them $e_{0} \pm e_{i}$ and Pythagorean quadruples) has kernel of dimension $1$, spanned by $\id$, computed exactly; since $k \cdot \id(k) = Q(k) = 0$ the kernel always contains $\id$, and twelve directions already reach the bound, so the null fluxes determine $T$ modulo $\R\,\id$ for all null directions. If $X = \lambda\,\id$ is conserved at $p 
eq 0$ then $X(p) = \lambda p = 0$ forces $\lambda = 0$ (the check also finds the conserved sources and $\id$ independent at three momenta). So for conserved $X$ at $p 
eq 0$, vanishing trace-free part implies $X = 0$; at $p = 0$ a constant $\lambda\,\id$ survives, the cosmological term (the unimodular mechanism).

\emph{(v)} Let $\mathcal{L}(\hb) = (\det\hb)^{-1}\Phi(\hb(\partial\psi), \psi)$ where $\hb$ enters only through the derivatives of the matter field (applied as a linear map, or as its outermorphism on a field strength) and the volume factor. Along $\hb = \id + t\,\delta$: $ rac{d}{dt}(\det\hb)^{-1}|_{0} = -	r\delta$ and $ rac{d}{dt}\Phi|_{0}$ is, by the chain rule, $\partial\Phi/\partial(
abla\psi)$ contracted with $\delta(
abla\psi)$, so the derivative is linear in $\delta$, of the form $\sum_{a} \delta(e_{a}) \cdot T(e^{a})$, with $T(a)$ the contraction of $\partial\Phi/\partial(
abla\psi)$ with $a \cdot 
abla\psi$ minus $a\,\mathcal{L}$, the $\hb$-response stress. When $\Phi$ depends on $
abla\psi$ directly (the scalar) this is the canonical Noether stress of displacements (the current of global translations); when $\hb$ acts on a field strength built from a potential (the Maxwell field, $F = 
abla \wedge A$ held fixed) it is the symmetric gauge-invariant stress, which differs from the canonical Noether stress of $A$ by the Belinfante term. For the scalar, $\Phi = 	frac12 Q(\hb(
abla\phi)) - 	frac12 m^{2}\phi^{2}$ gives $T(a) = (a \cdot 
abla\phi)
abla\phi - a\,\mathcal{L}$ and $	r T = Q(
abla\phi) - 4\mathcal{L} = -Q(
abla\phi) + 2m^{2}\phi^{2}$. For the Maxwell field, $\Phi = 	frac12 r{\hb(F)^{2}}$ with $\hb(a \wedge b) = \hb(a) \wedge \hb(b)$; at first order $\hb(F) = F + t\,\delta_{\wedge}F$ with $\delta_{\wedge}(a \wedge b) = \delta(a) \wedge b + a \wedge \delta(b)$, so the derivative is $ r{F\,\delta_{\wedge}F} - 	frac12	r\delta\, r{F^{2}}$, which equals $\sum_{a}\delta(e_{a}) \cdot T(e^{a})$ with $T(a) = -	frac12 FaF$, the stress of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-maxwell-stress-spacetime-algebra}, symmetric and gauge invariant (the Belinfante-improved canonical stress). The check does not use these formulas: it evaluates the full nonlinear densities exactly at six rational $t$ for each of the sixteen elementary $\delta$ and takes the derivative at $0$ of the interpolating polynomials (both numerator and $\det\hb$ are polynomials of degree at most $4$ in $t$), then compares with the two stress maps at a rational field strength and a rational gradient; it also confirms that the Maxwell response is symmetric and trace-free and the scalar trace formula. A first-order Weyl-flat variation is $\delta = \sigma(x)\,\id$ plus a displacement; the displacement part pairs to zero with the conserved stress after integration by parts, and the conformal part gives $\int \sigma\,	r T = 0$. So the Maxwell field does not couple at first order to variations within the Weyl-flat class. For the Dirac field the response is not algebraic in $\hb$ when $\Omega$ is eliminated, and with $\Omega$ independent it is the canonical stress (see (vii)); the classical on-shell trace of its stress is proportional to $m$ times the scalar spin product, so for $m = 0$ it vanishes on shell (not pointwise off shell, as for the Maxwell density), by conformal invariance with weight $-	frac32$ for the spinor (standard, cited from memory, not checked). At the quantum level the renormalised stress has a state-independent trace anomaly containing a scheme-dependent $\Box\mathcal{R}$ term, which is first order in $h$ and nonzero on $L$ (the scalar of $\id$ is $3\,Q(p)$), so the decoupling of the massless Dirac field from the Weyl-flat class is classical only.

\emph{(vi)} For point sources with momenta $p_{n}$ coupled to the field at a soft momentum $q$ through $\kappa_{n}\,p_{n} \cdot h_{0}(p_{n})/(p_{n} \cdot q)$ (the classical radiated field of a scattering at a point, or Weinberg's soft factor), the change under $h_{0} \mapsto h_{0} + q \otimes \xi + \xi \otimes q$ is $2\,\xi \cdot \sum_{n} s_{n}\kappa_{n}p_{n}$, which must vanish for every $\xi$. On the configuration of the check (five rational momenta, $\sum s_{n}p_{n} = 0$, spanning $V$, so one linear relation among them) the solution space of $\sum s_{n}\kappa_{n}p_{n} = 0$ is computed to be the line of constant $\kappa$: one coupling for all five sources. With six or more momenta a single configuration leaves a kernel of dimension $n - 4$, and universality follows only by imposing the condition on every momentum-conserving configuration, which is Weinberg's argument; that general step is standard and not computed here. Within $G_{p} \oplus L$ the coupling of a source is $\sigma\,p_{n} \cdot p_{n} = \sigma\,Q(p_{n})$, zero for a massless source (the stored absence of light deflection in Nordstr"om's theory).

\emph{(vii), argued.} By (i) and (ii) the Weyl-flat class is one of the four displacement-closed covariant classes, so displacement gauge invariance alone does not exclude it, and by (iii) it couples to the trace only; the Einstein-Fokker form of Nordstr"om's theory is generally covariant, the nonlinear counterpart. If the gravitational field equations are the Euler-Lagrange equations of an action $S_{g} + S_{m}$ with $S_{m}$ minimally coupled and $\hb$ varied in all directions, the source of the $\hb$ equation is the response of (v), and by (iii) and (iv) varying in the directions $C_{p}$ supplies its trace-free part, which with conservation fixes it at every nonzero momentum. With Lovelock's theorem (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-lovelock-and-anderson-duchamp-natural-lagrangians}(a)) a natural divergence-free second-order gravitational side is $c_{1}\mathcal{G} + c_{2}$, which gives Einstein's equations. The directions $C_{p}$ leave $\ker\mathcal{W}_{p}$, the tangent of the attachment's domain, so the clause holds under that action principle exactly when the matter theory is defined and varied there. For matter with spin, the definition's note makes $\Omega$ independent; then the $\hb$-response of (v) is the canonical stress, whose antisymmetric part equals the divergence of the spin density on shell; it enters the antisymmetric part of the $\hb$ equation, and the $\Omega$ equation ties the torsion to the spin density (Einstein-Cartan, standard, cited from memory). Eliminating the torsion, the symmetric source is the Belinfante stress plus a spin-spin contact term of order $\kappa$, which is second order in the coupling; at first order the pairings of (iii), which involve only symmetric $h_{0}$, therefore see the Belinfante stress. Conservation of the source, used in (iii) and (iv), must survive quantisation; for chiral matter that is the cancellation of the mixed gravitational anomaly (argued, not used). This step is a reading of (i) to (vi) at first order; the nonlinear statement and the action principle itself are not derived.

\emph{Circularity.} The uses are the twistor-flat result (for the identification of the Weyl-flat class with the attachment's domain), the Maxwell stress Fact, Nordstr"om's Fact, Lovelock's Fact and the dictionary Fact; none assumes that the whole stress is the source. Einstein's equations enter only in (vii), through Lovelock's theorem, after the clause.
